quest:1135.text: Highperch Venom. From Theramore, Fiora Longears sends hunters west for wyvern venom. At Highperch in Thousand Needles, the wyverns carry venom sacs buyers value across Kalimdor. In Theramore, Fiora Longears seeks hunters willing to travel far for a trade beyond the Horde’s use of wyverns as flying mounts. Buyers across Kalimdor value the creatures’ lethal venom, often more than the beasts themselves. The journey means dangerous heights and a hunt for fresh venom sacs. Highperch lies west of Dustwallow Marsh, among the sandstone mesas of Thousand Needles. Its wyverns carry unusually concentrated toxin, but reaching their nests means crossing Horde territory and climbing treacherous ground. You must slay the wyverns and take their venom sacs intact, then carry them back to Theramore.

quest:1136.text: Frostmaw. In the Alterac Mountains, a rare yeti hunt calls you far from home. Melor Stonehoof sends you after Frostmaw and awaits his mane in Thunder Bluff. Melor Stonehoof sends you far from home to hunt Frostmaw in the Alterac Mountains. The yeti’s white coat blends with the mountain snow, and he rarely shows himself. Melor gives you a scroll explaining how to lure him. Bring Frostmaw’s mane back to Melor in Thunder Bluff, and your journey will be complete.

quest:1137.text: News for Fizzle. In the Badlands, Martek the Exiled has news for Fizzle Brassbolts about indurium. You carry his message to the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Martek says indurium withstands heat remarkably well, so it may suit Fizzle's pistons. Flakes will not do; Fizzle needs real indurium ore, dug from deep within Uldaman at the Badlands' northern edge. Martek names Uldaman as indurium's true source. He sends his regards and asks you to repeat all he has told you to Fizzle Brassbolts.

quest:1140.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. From Maestra's Post, Delgren's crusade reaches its sixth chapter. He deciphers Orcish writings recovered from the cult's emissaries and learns Athrikus Narassin hid two trapped Highborne soulgems in satyr strongholds deep in Ashenvale. Champions are sent to Night Run and Satyrnaar to shatter the vessels, free the tormented spirits, and weaken Athrikus's power. After Ilkrud Magthrull, an orcish courier, is cut down, Delgren the Purifier puts his study of Orcish to use. His peers in the Holy Light often scoffed at learning an adversary's tongue. Yet Delgren's practical wisdom lets him decipher notes recovered from the cult's emissaries. They reveal that Athrikus Narassin hid two potent soulgems containing ancient Highborne essences far to the northeast, in the defiled groves of Night Run and Satyrnaar.

quest:1142.text:
Mortality Wanes. In Razorfen Kraul, Heralath Fallowbrook has one last plea for the living. He asks you to carry his wife's stolen pendant to Darnassus and tell her he has died. Heralath Fallowbrook lies mortally wounded among the brambles of Razorfen Kraul. Savage quilboar and dark magic have overrun the stronghold, far from Alliance lands. His strength is fading, and he can manage only broken whispers.

He speaks of Lonebrow, a brave dwarf sent ahead to warn Falfindel. Heralath knows he will not leave the Kraul alive. Heralath asks you to recover the pendant that marks his marriage to Treshala Fallowbrook. One of the lair's aggressors tore it from him. He asks any traveler who stops beside him to carry it across Kalimdor to Darnassus, so Treshala learns of his death and does not wait in vain.

quest:1143.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Dark rites at the Tower of Althalaxx threaten northern Darkshore. Balthule Shadowstrike leads an Alliance assault on Athrikus Narassin, the ancient sorcerer who commands the cult from the tower’s peak. In northern Darkshore, the ruined Tower of Althalaxx shelters demonic rites. Balthule Shadowstrike watches from nearby and sees the danger must be faced now. Athrikus Narassin, an ancient night elf warlock, dwells at the summit. Beneath the shattered roof, he directs the dark rituals.

quest:1147.text:
The Swarm Grows. At Ironstone Camp, Moktar Krin says Belgrom wants the silithid driven back underground. His war party is too weakened to fight, so you are sent to the dig site south of camp to face them. Moktar Krin says Belgrom considers the silithid a threat and wants them driven back into the depths they came from. Moktar's war party has already killed the dwarves sent by the Explorers' League, but the fighters are in no state for another battle.

The dig site lies south of Ironstone Camp, and Moktar expects no more dwarves there. You are to kill the silithid Searchers, hive drones and invaders. Moktar's party cannot leave until the work is done.

quest:1148.text: Parts of the Swarm. In Thousand Needles, you find a cracked silithid carapace and see how tightly its plating is woven. Korran at the Crossroads wants to study more of these creatures. You find silithid chitin woven tighter than anything you have seen. The creature's body shows great strength and advanced development. Korran at the Crossroads wants to learn more about the creatures and their origins. He asks for one silithid heart, five silithid talons and three intact silithid carapaces.

quest:1149.text: Test of Faith. At Dorn Plainstalker's camp above Thousand Needles, Horde adventurers face a test of faith. The hermit asks them to step from a wooden plank into the chasm and trust their resolve. Above Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker reflects on the mind, body, and spirit. He sets trials to measure what lies within an adventurer instead of relying on simple tribal traditions. Conviction takes many forms, he believes. At its heart is faith strong enough to risk one's life.

quest:115.text: Shadow Magic. Marshal Marris needs the midnight orbs taken from Blackrock shadowcasters in Redridge. Their dark power threatens Lakeshire's defenders and the town's line. The Blackrock clan has long relied on brute force. Now its raids in the Redridge Mountains bring a darker threat. Shadowcasters wield dark powers and channel fel and shadow energies through demon-tainted midnight orbs. These relics have dealt terrible losses to the local militia, and the war is turning against the defenders. Marshal Marris directs Lakeshire's strained defense from the town center. He knows ordinary steel cannot easily overcome dark relics. If Blackrock orcs keep their midnight orbs, Redridge's eastern borders may collapse. Marris orders the shadowcasters slain and the orbs seized, so the demonic relics can be destroyed instead of put to use.

quest:1150.text: Test of Endurance. In Thousand Needles, challengers face the second rite in Dorn Plainstalker's spiritual trials. After proving their courage of spirit, they enter Roguefeather Den to test their physical endurance and draw out its fierce leader, Grenka Bloodscreech. At the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker prepares young warriors for a wider, harsher world. This trial tests the body's strength. Dorn believes readiness calls for spiritual devotion, mental discipline, and the stamina to endure sustained brutality. Roguefeather Den lies within Screeching Canyon, west of Freewind Post. Hostile harpies fill the cavern, making it perilous to wander in alone. Challengers fight deep into the roost and vandalize the harpies' gathered provisions. Then they endure the flock's fierce retaliation until its matriarch, Grenka Bloodscreech, enters the fight.

quest:1151.text: Test of Strength. In Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker asks you to prove your strength. Your trial brings you against Rok'Alim the Pounder, an ancient rock elemental, and calls for pieces of his shattered form. Long ago, primordial elementals covered the world and served the Old Gods. When those powers were overthrown and sealed beneath the earth, the spirits lost their hold on this realm. Most faded from the physical world unless modern spellcraft bound and summoned them. A few were strong enough to remain on Azeroth without such magic. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one of them, wandering the arid canyons of Thousand Needles as an echo of that age. The centaur clans named Rok'Alim for the deafening crashes of his stone fists against the canyon floor. Anyone who crosses his path risks being hammered into dust. Dorn Plainstalker sends initiates to face this force of raw might and prove their warrior spirit. They return with fragments of the elemental's stony heart as proof of victory.

quest:1152.text: Test of Lore. In Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker sends Horde champions north to face a trial of the world's history. Braug Dimspirit waits in Stonetalon Mountains to test what they know of Azeroth and its shared suffering. At the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker tests initiates in faith, endurance, and combat. Yet strength and faith alone do not make a true Horde champion. Dorn knows the bounds of what he can teach, so he sends those who have proved themselves to Stonetalon Mountains. There, an elder shaman will test their minds and knowledge of the world. The road runs north over the Barrens' dry scrub and into the crags of Stonetalon. High in the mountains, near the entrance to Talondeep Path, Braug Dimspirit keeps his hermitage. The cavern cuts through the rock toward Ashenvale. From there, Braug looks upon a frontier at war: goblin logging ventures despoil the forests, while hostile night elves fiercely defend their ancestral borders.

quest:1153.text: A New Ore Sample. At Camp Taurajo, Tatternack Steelforge seeks ore in Thousand Needles to strengthen the Horde’s arms. He sends you south for a sample to test. Tatternack Steelforge is a blacksmith in Camp Taurajo, watched closely by Orgrimmar. He has already made weapons from local centaur armaments. Yet he still hopes to prove his craft to Warchief Thrall. Travelers passing through showed him strange ore taken from a kobold to the south. When they refused to sell it, he took the refusal as an insult to his craft and the Horde. You leave the southern Barrens’ flat plains for the towering canyon maze of Thousand Needles. Kobold diggers tunnel through its crags and cliffs. Bring back chunks of unrefined ore taken directly from them. Then Tatternack can judge whether the raw mineral can be forged into weapons for Thrall’s war effort.

quest:1154.text: Test of Lore. At Talondeep Path, Horde seekers face the Test of Lore. Braug Dimspirit asks them to find and study a tome of dragon history before he tests what they remember. After trials across Thousand Needles' salt flats and plateaus, Dorn Plainstalker's candidates travel north to Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. He waits near the mouth of Talondeep Path. Braug counts those earlier trials as tests of body and faith. Yet the Horde also needs disciplined minds and knowledge of ancient history, not only skill against beasts. Braug sends seekers through Talondeep Path into southern Ashenvale. Beneath the trees south of Splintertree Post lies Dor'Danil Barrow Den, a dangerous ruin haunted by fallen night elf druids and the creatures that slaughtered them. Deep in its lower chambers, a stone podium holds 'Legacy of the Aspects'. The rare manuscript tells of the ancient creation and corruption of the great Dragon Aspects.

quest:1159.text: Test of Lore. Across the Great Sea, Horde seekers now carry the Test of Lore to the ruins of Lordaeron. You have answered Braug Dimspirit's first riddle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Now he sends you to a former human scholar among the Forsaken in Undercity. After you prove your mettle and learn the Dragon Aspects' history in the Legacy of the Aspects, Braug Dimspirit admits his knowledge has limits. The trial now reaches beyond Kalimdor and shows the Horde's far-reaching ties. So Braug sends you toward the undead capital beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Parqual Fintallas lives in the damp corridors of the Apothecarium. Once a respected human chronicler of the northern kingdoms, he kept seeking knowledge through the Scourge and his transformation into one of the Forsaken. You arrive as an outsider, claiming to have completed the spiritual and physical trials of Thousand Needles. Parqual doubts you are more than an opportunistic mercenary, and expects you to prove your worth to him.

quest:1164.text: To Steal From Thieves. Genavie Callow in Undercity asks you to confront the Dabyrie family at their farmstead in Arathi. Her grievance turns a dispute over stolen belongings into a demand for vengeance. Genavie Callow says the plague took her family and the war left her estate looted and burned. She accuses Kenata and her children of taking the few belongings she still treasured. Now she asks you to bring her the heads of Kenata, Fardel, and Marcel Dabyrie from the Dabyrie Farmstead in Arathi.

quest:1167.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Before you face Athrikus Narassin, Delgren sends you north to speak with Balthule Shadowstrike. The scout has watched the Tower of Althalaxx and can tell you what has changed there. Delgren the Purifier sends you north to meet Balthule Shadowstrike, his sentinel partner. You have purified corrupted relics and weakened the cult's hold along Darkshore's border. Before you confront Athrikus, Delgren wants fresh intelligence from Balthule. The sentinel has kept watch from the ruins overlooking the tower.

quest:1175.text:
A Bump in the Road. At the Mirage Raceway, Trackmaster Zherin needs the growing beasts kept from the track. You are asked to thin the Saltstone Basilisks, Crystalhides and Gazers before they wander onto it. A basilisk once struck the goblins' racer, the Red Thunder. After the crash, Kronkrider hired Zherin to watch over the Mirage Raceway track. Zherin does not know what the beasts on the Shimmering Flats are eating. He knows only that they have grown too big.

Their numbers must be kept down before one strays onto the course during a race. Clearing wreckage is bad enough. Zherin would rather not pick burnt animal parts out of it as well.

quest:1176.text: Load Lightening. At the Mirage Raceway, Pozzik’s goblin crew seeks lighter parts for its racers. Hollow vulture bones may strengthen the steering and frame without adding heavy metal. Across the Shimmering Flats, goblin and gnome engineers race to win by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust matters little if a car carries too much weight. Gnome teams favor intricate gears and brass fittings. Pozzik’s goblins strip away dense iron framing and replace it with lighter hollow parts wherever they can. Pozzik looks to the salt wastes around Thousand Needles instead of importing costly composites. Salt Flats vultures are plentiful, and their bones are hollow, honeycombed, strong under strain, and light. His mechanics work them into the racers’ steering rigs and smaller braces. They hope the machines can outmaneuver the gnomes without shaking apart at top speed.

quest:1177.text: Hungry!. Mudcrush Durtfeet is hungry in northern Dustwallow Marsh and wants food from you. Bash the fishy Mirefin and bring back their heads, or Mud will eat you. Mudcrush Durtfeet, an ogre called Mud, makes a plain bargain. Bash the fishy Mirefin and bring him their heads for food. Feed Mud, or he will eat you.

quest:1178.text:
Goblin Sponsorship. The goblin racers are waiting on a promised part as the gnomes gain ground. Pozzik sends you to Ratchet to ask Gazlowe what happened. Pozzik calls the racing team the pride of goblins. Many people help it in one way or another. Gazlowe searches the world for parts and once came to work on one of its rigs.

Weeks ago, Gazlowe promised a new prototype fuel regulator, but it has not arrived. He is usually prompt, so Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and learn what happened. The gnomes are gaining.

quest:1179.text: The Brassbolts Brothers. Pilot Longbeard in Ironforge needs a traveler to carry helmets to the Brassbolts Brothers. Their test drivers keep crashing rocket cars at the Shimmering Flats, so the gnomes need head protection. Pilot Longbeard, a dwarven aviator in Ironforge, has an urgent request from the Shimmering Flats in southern Kalimdor. His friends, the inventive gnome Brassbolts brothers, have settled on its vast salt pans to race experimental machines. Longbeard's military and piloting duties keep him busy, so he cannot carry their supplies himself. The Brassbolts' rocket car races across the salt beds at extraordinary speed. Yet its test drivers keep crashing and suffering severe concussions. Longbeard has gathered a crate of heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets to protect them. You carry the crate across the sea to Kalimdor, giving the gnomes the protection they need to bring reluctant pilots back behind the wheel.

quest:1180.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Gazlowe in Ratchet still waits for the fuel regulator he promised Pozzik. Revilgaz in Booty Bay said he would ship it, but it has not arrived. So Gazlowe sends you to Wharfmaster Lozgil at the far northwestern end of the Booty Bay docks to check the cargo records. Gazlowe promised Pozzik a new fuel regulator, but it has not reached Ratchet. Revilgaz in Booty Bay said he would ship it over. Perhaps the part slipped through the cracks. If it never left, there may be little to do. Still, you can find out whether it departed Booty Bay. Wharfmaster Lozgil, at the far northwestern end of the docks, can search the cargo records.

quest:1181.text: Goblin Sponsorship. At the Mirage Raceway, the goblin racers still need their missing fuel regulator. Wharfmaster Lozgil sends you to Baron Revilgaz in Booty Bay for help. Wharfmaster Lozgil can do little more to trace the missing shipment bound for Ratchet. He sends you to Baron Revilgaz, since the Baron knows his own business best. You will find him on the top floor of the tavern across the harbor in Booty Bay.

quest:1182.text:
Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz is seeking the Venture Company’s new fuel regulator plans for Pozzik at Lake Nazferiti. Foreman Cozzle has outsmarted him, so the Baron sends you after the blueprints. Baron Revilgaz says the Venture Company’s shredders at Lake Nazferiti in northern Stranglethorn carry a new model of fuel regulator. Pozzik could use its details, but Foreman Cozzle has proved cleverer than the Baron expected. So Revilgaz believes you may have better luck finding the plans.

The blueprints are kept in Cozzle’s house, almost certainly under lock and key. The Venture Company’s base lies around Lake Nazferiti, in the vale’s north-eastern corner. Cozzle keeps the key in his cabin atop the oil tower. The box of blueprints is in the small house near the tower’s base. Revilgaz admits the gnome team there is good, and his team needs every advantage it can find.

quest:1183.text: Goblin Sponsorship. At the Shimmering Flats, Baron Revilgaz's regards reach Pozzik with the Fuel Regulator Blueprints. The Baron invites Pozzik to ask for anything he needs. Baron Revilgaz sends you to the Shimmering Flats with the Fuel Regulator Blueprints and his regards for Pozzik. The Baron says Pozzik should ask if he ever needs anything. Revilgaz waits to hear that Pozzik breaks the track record.

quest:1184.text: Parts of the Swarm. From Thousand Needles, Korran sends word to Orgrimmar about Moktar and his studies. Korran sends you to Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar with word from Thousand Needles. The cracked carapaces came from silithid at the Rustmaul Digsite. Tell Belgrom that Moktar is doing his bidding well and that Korran's studies are progressing. Korran hopes to learn more soon.

quest:1186.text: The Eighteenth Pilot. On the Shimmering Flats, Pozzik sends you to find Razzeric while he works on the racers. Razzeric is the team's eighteenth pilot, and he enjoys modifying the racers. Pozzik is fitting a new fuel regulator into the racer designs. He sends you to Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats, the team's eighteenth pilot. Razzeric likes to modify the racers. Pozzik says he is a little off his rocker, so try not to look too surprised.

quest:1195.text: The Sacred Flame. Zangen Stonehoof sends you after a sacred flame and an ancient relic. To aid Rau Cliffrunner in Thousand Needles, you seek a moonwell phial in Ashenvale. The Galak centaur guard an ancient relic in Thousand Needles. The artifact dates to the beginning of their race, and sacred flames protect it. Zangen Stonehoof needs water blessed by the moon to quench those flames. He sends you north to Ashenvale, where the old forests hold the moonwell water he seeks. Pure moonwell water needs a vessel that will not taint it. You seek an etched phial carried by the Laughing Sisters, dryads near Raynewood Retreat. Submerge the phial in a moonwell along the western banks of the Falfarren River, then carry it back to Mulgore.

quest:1196.text: The Sacred Flame. A phial of moonwell water travels south from Ashenvale to Freewind Post. Rau Cliffrunner needs it to break the eternal flame guarding an ancient centaur relic in Thousand Needles. Zangen Stonehoof sends you south across central Kalimdor with an etched phial of purified moonwell water. You cross the sun-baked Barrens, descend the Great Lift, and continue to Freewind Post. Rau Cliffrunner waits on the high mesa above the canyon floor. From there, he watches the centaur clans below.

quest:1197.text: The Sacred Flame. At Splithoof Hold, Rau Cliffrunner seeks to silence the Galak centaur's sacred fire. You carry blessed water into their stronghold, quench the brazier, and take the Cloven Hoof. North of Freewind Post, Splithoof Crag lies at the heart of Galak territory in Thousand Needles. Deep in its cavern, Splithoof Hold shelters a fire the centaur hold sacred. Rau Cliffrunner prepares an etched phial of purified water for his allies. You enter the hold and use the water to quench the flame for a moment. Then you take the Cloven Hoof relic guarded within.

quest:1198.text: In Search of Thaelrid. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass sends you into Blackfathom Deeps to find a missing scout. The Argent Dawn fears naga and Twilight's Hammer cultists have joined forces in the flooded ruins. The Argent Dawn watches for threats across Kalimdor, as well as the Scourge in Lordaeron. In Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass gathers reports of dangers beyond the natural world. Word reaches him that naga have made a pact with the doomsday zealots of Twilight's Hammer in Blackfathom Deeps. The flooded ruins lie along the Ashenvale shore, and the order fears what this alliance may bring. Argent Guard Thaelrid entered the caverns to investigate rumors from the coast. Weeks have passed without word, and Shaedlass's other scouts are away on separate operations. He fears Thaelrid has fallen or been taken by the dark powers beneath the waves. So he sends you into Blackfathom Deeps to bring the missing scout back alive.

quest:1199.text: Twilight Falls. At Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight's Hammer cultists have joined the naga beneath the Ashenvale coast. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus calls on Alliance champions to gather pendants from fallen cultists and hinder their plans to awaken ancient evils. Beneath Ashenvale's Zoram Strand, Blackfathom Deeps lies in ruins. Once a sacred night elf temple to Elune, it held a powerful moonwell. The Sundering shattered the temple and plunged it beneath the sea. Now naga and cultists fill its halls. The waters have turned foul, and the cultists revere powers darker than the sea. Twilight's Hammer worships the chaotic Old Gods and seeks their return. Its followers hope to spread madness and ruin across the world. Reports in Darnassus say the cultists have joined the naga in Blackfathom Deeps. There they perform rituals in the submerged halls and use the temple's tainted waters to feed their dark masters' resurgence. Argent Guard Manados watches over threats to Azeroth from Darnassus on behalf of the Argent Dawn. He sees danger in Blackfathom Deeps, where horrors could reach every civilized race. The order offers aid and recognition to heroes who enter the flooded labyrinth, cull the cultists, and bring back the Twilight Pendants from their necks as proof of defeat.

quest:1200.text: Blackfathom Villainy. At Blackfathom Deeps, Argent Guard Thaelrid calls the Alliance to stop Twilight Lord Kelris. The cult leader sacrifices captives to Aku'mai, and Thaelrid asks you to bring Kelris's severed head to the Argent Dawn in Darnassus as proof. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple devoted to Elune. Corruption from an ancient Old God rose through the rock and fouled the Moon Well. From the tainted waters beneath the depths, Aku'mai crawled forth, a voracious servant of that darkness. After the temple was defiled, the Twilight's Hammer joined forces with local naga. Its holy halls became a place of ritual murder. Argent Guard Thaelrid entered Blackfathom Deeps on behalf of his order. There, he was grievously wounded and drained of strength. Surrounded by enemies, he knows he cannot finish his mission alone. So he pleads with brave Alliance travelers who reach him to kill Twilight Lord Kelris. Kelris leads the cultists in sacrificing innocents to Aku'mai for dark power.

quest:1201.text:
Theramore Spies. In Dustwallow, Horde and Alliance keep an uneasy truce, though skirmishes and covert deeds continue. Nazeer Bloodpike wants Alliance infiltrators east of Brackenwall Village hunted down and slain. Alliance spies watch Brackenwall Village from the islands to its east. They send word of Horde movements back to Theramore.

Nazeer Bloodpike, the village spymaster, sends you to find and kill them. Their superiors must know such spies are unwelcome.

quest:1202.text: The Theramore Docks. At Theramore Docks, papers taken from a ship lie beneath the water. Nazeer Bloodpike sends you to recover them after two spies were discovered and cast them into the sea. After dealing with the Theramore spies, you hear from Nazeer Bloodpike again. Two spies went to a ship by the Theramore docks and took its papers. They were discovered and threw the papers into the sea. One spy escaped and reported the failure, unable to retrieve what they had cast away. The Captain's Documents lie in a footlocker beneath the water by the Theramore docks. You are sent to recover them and bring them to Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village. He says the papers matter greatly to the Alliance's stability. That makes them important to the Horde's security, too.

quest:1203.text: Jarl Needs a Blade. In Dustwallow Marsh, Jarl needs a blade for urgent cutting. “Swamp Eye” Jarl wants a moonsteel broadsword and warns you not to dawdle. “Swamp Eye” Jarl has cutting to do, but keeps its purpose to himself. He asks for a particular blade, called a moonsteel broadsword by some and a swing blade by Jarl. You might find one in town, or ask a blacksmith to make one special. Jarl warns you not to sleep on it; whatever needs cutting will not keep forever.

quest:1204.text: Mudrock Soup and Bugs. In Theramore, Morgan Stern hopes to win Stormwind City over with a new dish. The trek through Dustwallow Marsh is too much for Morgan Stern, so you gather Mudrock tongues for Mudrock Soup and Bugs. Morgan Stern is gathering ingredients for a new dish in Theramore. A long trek through Dustwallow Marsh is more than Morgan Stern expects to survive, so you hunt Mudrock turtles. Their tongues are needed first. Mudrock turtles roam the coast of Dustwallow Marsh, mostly around the bay. Morgan Stern wants forked tongues in particular, having heard they bring a distinct flavor to the dish.

quest:1206.text: Jarl Needs Eyes. At Swamplight Manor, Jarl seeks forty unpopped Darkmist eyes for their smooth, salty juice. The spiders live in Darkmist Cavern, west of the manor. After Soothing Spices, Jarl turns to eye juice, a drink they enjoy. Most creatures have only two eyes, but spiders have many. Jarl likes the taste of Darkmist eye juice. The Darkmist spiders live in Darkmist Cavern, west of the manor. Jarl wonders whether the cave took its name from the spiders, or the spiders from the cave.

quest:1218.text: Soothing Spices. In Dustwallow Marsh, "Swamp Eye" Jarl needs three Soothing Spices for a stew. "Swamp Eye" Jarl loves swamp cooking, including fried green frog legs. Now Jarl plans a stew and needs soothing spice for the pot. Bring three Soothing Spices, and Jarl will share the stew with you. Does stew suit your taste?

quest:1219.text: The Orc Report. In Dustwallow Marsh, you find a severed orc hand gripping a bone tube. Inside lies a dirt-stained parchment in Orcish, meant for a Theramore Lieutenant. In the loose dirt, you find a severed orc hand gripping a tube carved from bone. Inside is a dirt-stained parchment written in Orcish. It seems significant, and a Theramore Lieutenant is the one to show it to.

quest:1220.text: Captain Vimes. Near Theramore, Lieutenant Aden sends you to Captain Garran Vimes with an orc report and word of Horde spies. Lieutenant Aden sends you to Captain Garran Vimes with the orc report you found. Vimes reads orcish better than most, so Aden wants him to know that Horde spies are close to Theramore. You’ll find Vimes at the barracks on the northeastern side of Theramore Isle.

quest:1221.text: Blueleaf Tubers. Mebok Mizzyrix sends trained gophers into Razorfen Kraul to find Blueleaf Tubers. The Ratchet merchant seeks the buried delicacy for trade. In the southern Barrens, Blueleaf Tubers lie deep beneath the roots of Razorfen Kraul. Their rarity makes them a delicacy prized across the world. They grow far from open fields and ordinary wild groves, so foragers must search underground. Mebok Mizzyrix, a merchant in Ratchet, has devised a way to find buried tubers. He trains snufflenose gophers to catch a tuber's scent from fifty paces away. Foragers receive a command stick, a ventilated crate, and an instruction manual to guide the creatures through quilboar territory. The harvest lies in the lands of the hostile Death's Head quilboar tribe. In the Kraul, you must guard your trained gopher from feral beasts and thorny briars, then command it to dig up the buried bulbs. The tubers go back to Ratchet, where Mizzyrix's foreign buyers await.

quest:1222.text: Stinky's Escape. In the swamp, "Stinky" Ignatz is searching for bogbean leaves for a cook in Theramore. Critters have surrounded him, and he asks you to guard him while he looks for a plant. When he is done, Morgan Stern is waiting in Theramore. "Stinky" Ignatz is glad to find someone who does not see him as a meal. Morgan Stern, a cook in Theramore, sent him to gather bogbean leaves for a new recipe. Ignatz guesses Stern finds them tasty. Now critters have surrounded him, and he asks you to guard his back while he searches for a bogbean plant. Morgan Stern, a cook in Theramore, is anxious. Ignatz went into the swamp a while ago and has not returned.

quest:1238.text: The Lost Report. In Dustwallow Marsh, you uncover a spy's report bound for Brackenwall Village. An orc's severed hand grips a bone tube holding a dirt-stained account of weeks spent watching Theramore. You find an orc's severed hand in loose dirt, its fingers closed around a tube carved from bone. Inside lies a dirt-stained parchment. It reports on Theramore after weeks of spying and is meant for Nazeer Bloodpike, the orcs' spymaster at Brackenwall Village.

quest:1239.text: The Severed Head. In Dustwallow Marsh, you uncover a male orc's severed head. Bring it to Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village. Your digging turns up a male orc's head, ragged where it was cut from the neck. Its lips curl in a snarl, and dark eyes glare defiantly. Bring the head to Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village.

quest:124.text: A Baying of Gnolls. Gnolls have reached Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs already threaten the region. Verner asks you to drive away the brutes and mystics that endanger his horses. Verner Osgood’s stable in Lakeshire has grown dangerous to tend. Blackrock orcs hold the heights, while gnoll packs roam the ridges around town. Now gnoll raiders have reached the northern edge of Verner’s paddocks. They prey on horses that stray too close to the bluffs.

quest:1240.text: The Troll Witchdoctor. Nazeer Bloodpike seeks the truth about Marg Nighteye's death through troll witch-magic. You carry Marg's head to Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Nazeer Bloodpike insists the truth about Marg's death must come to light. He says only troll witch-magic can reveal what happened. So you carry Marg's head to Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. No Darkspear witchdoctor is mightier than Kin'weelay, and Nazeer believes Kin'weelay can reach Marg's spirit.

quest:1241.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Stormwind, the inquiry begins urgently when a diplomat fails to reach Theramore Isle. Bishop DeLavey suspects Defias foul play and sends trusted operatives to Jorgen, a discreet contact in the Valley of Heroes. A high-ranking diplomat sailed from the Eastern Kingdoms to meet Lady Jaina Proudmoore in Theramore Isle for sensitive talks. The diplomat never arrived. Royal investigators search Stormwind for clues. The disappearance remains secret to prevent panic and keep conspirators from learning the crown is watching. Bishop DeLavey believes the Defias Brotherhood abducted the diplomat, but he does not rely only on the king’s guard. He turns to discreet contacts and seeks out Jorgen, an old acquaintance who keeps a low profile fishing in the Valley of Heroes. Jorgen is just inside the city gates.

quest:1242.text: The Missing Diplomat. Jorgen sends trusted operatives across Stormwind with a sealed note for Elling Trias. From the Valley of Heroes to Trias' Cheese in the Trade District, the delivery carries the search for the missing diplomat. After the first inquiries into the diplomat's disappearance, Jorgen asks trusted operatives to keep silent and carry a sealed note across Stormwind. It is bound for Trias' Cheese in the Trade District, not a barracks or magistrate's office. As concern spreads beyond the palace, the handoff avoids the usual guard channels.

quest:1243.text: The Missing Diplomat. Elling Trias sends you south from Stormwind to seek news of the missing diplomat. His lead points toward Duskwood and Watcher Backus, a contact near Darkshire who may know of Defias activity. After a frustrating exchange with Jorgen, Elling Trias, the cheesemonger, turns to his wider circle of informants. To save his own coin, he sends you to do the fieldwork instead of hiring agents. You carry a sealed missive across the border into Duskwood, where beasts and the undead make travel dangerous. Watcher Backus patrols the northern approach to Darkshire as a member of the Night Watch. Trias trusts him to report illicit movements through Duskwood. Show Backus the sealed dispatch, and he can share guard records and local gossip about Defias Brotherhood operations in the south.

quest:1244.text: The Missing Diplomat. Watcher Backus has brought the search for Stormwind’s missing diplomat to Duskwood. A gathering of Defias bandits at Addle’s Stead may hold a lead. Watcher Backus of the Night Watch brings you to Duskwood. Several weeks ago, an unusually large gathering of Defias bandits came to Addle’s Stead. They usually keep to themselves across the border in Westfall, so their presence in the dark woods is a troubling change. Now you search the abandoned farmstead for the papers they left behind.

quest:1245.text: The Missing Diplomat. You bring the recovered Defias Docket to Stormwind, where the search for a missing diplomat grows more dangerous. Watcher Backus in Duskwood wants no part of the Defias Docket you recovered. Its papers lay out plans too intricate for simple banditry or a diversion. Fearing royal punishment and wary of his Night Watch superiors, Backus asks you to keep his part quiet. The schemes could end careers or cost lives, so you carry the papers to Stormwind.

quest:1246.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Old Town, Elling Trias sends you after a name tied to the missing diplomat’s case. Dashel Stonefist may know more about suspicious papers, and the search leads into Stormwind’s rough streets. Elling Trias recalls Dashel Stonefist, known as Fist, among the names tied to the coded notes and leads. A rough street fighter, Stonefist keeps to the cramped alleys of Old Town. Finding him takes the search from Stormwind Keep’s grand halls into the city’s criminal circles.

quest:1247.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Old Town, Dashel Stonefist gives up a warning for Elling Trias. His confession names a backup abduction plot and a contact in Menethil Harbor. Dashel Stonefist gives in when he fears for his health. In an Old Town alley, he admits the conspirators' first plan to kidnap the envoy failed, and his part in it fell apart. To shift blame, he tells you of a secret meeting weeks ago at Addle's Stead in Duskwood. He also names a lead in their backup plan: an insider in Menethil Harbor known only as Slim.

quest:1248.text: The Missing Diplomat. You follow the trail of a kidnapped Stormwind diplomat to Menethil Harbor. An intercepted docket confirms the abduction but leaves the diplomat's identity and the conspirators' destination unknown. You have a docket that confirms a diplomat was taken from Stormwind. It names neither the diplomat nor the conspirators' destination. So the trail leads beyond Stormwind's gates to Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands, where you can search among the harbor crowds and their secret dealings.

quest:1249.text: The Missing Diplomat. Stormwind's envoy is missing, and you follow the trail from the capital to Menethil Harbor. There, the inquiry crosses paths with underworld figures and operatives tied to Stormwind's intelligence network. You follow the missing Stormwind envoy's trail north to Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Its docks and taverns hide shady dealers and covert runners, all working under the local guard's nose. To follow the leads through this port, you must deal with people who know the darker side of Alliance territory.

quest:1250.text: The Missing Diplomat. Jahn says the Defias took the king from his ship while it lay moored. You are sent to Mikhail in the Wetlands as the search for Hendel continues. Jahn says the Defias put a man named Hendel aboard the king's ship while it was moored. The king was bound for Theramore to meet Jaina Proudmoore. Jahn believes the Defias worked with someone else, so you are asked to speak with Mikhail in the Wetlands as the search for Hendel begins.

quest:1251.text: The Black Shield. At the burned Shady Rest Inn, a black shield clings to the crumbling chimney. Krog at Brackenwall Village waits to see it. Fire swept through the Shady Rest Inn and left little behind. An iron shield, charred black, is fixed to the crumbling chimney. You can work it free of the brick and bring it to Krog at Brackenwall Village. He will ask whether it counts as evidence from the inn’s remains.

quest:1253.text: The Black Shield. At the burned Shady Rest Inn, a fire-blackened shield hangs from the crumbling chimney. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore awaits evidence from the ruins. Few parts of the burned Shady Rest Inn remain beyond a crumbling chimney. A fire-blackened iron shield is still fixed to its brick, and can be removed. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore awaits evidence from the inn site.

quest:126.text: Howling in the Hills. Gnoll cries trouble the hills around Lakeshire, where Verner Osgood offers a bounty on Yowler. With Stormwind's forces stretched thin by the Blackrock orcs, the town relies on visitors to face the gnolls. Gnoll cries still echo through the Redridge hills, though lesser gnolls have been driven from the paths around Lakeshire. Verner Osgood, the town's farrier, knows the pack will keep raiding while its leader lives. Yowler is a huge, cunning gnoll whose calls direct the pack across the hills. Verner asks for Yowler's paw as proof of the kill and of the calls' silence. Stormwind's eastern border towns face danger with little help from the kingdom's army. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and disputes over the regency have paralyzed high command. Royal soldiers focus on the Blackrock orc clans in the north, leaving Lakeshire without defenders against gnolls. So townsfolk such as Verner Osgood arrange their own bounties to keep their homes from being overrun.

quest:1260.text: Morgan Stern. In Theramore, Angus Stern waits for word from Morgan Stern, who is gathering recipes for a new menu. Angus Stern wants customers at the Blue Recluse to taste rural dishes in the bayou style. He sent his nephew Morgan to Theramore, the city beside Dustwallow Marsh, to gather recipes from the locals. The journey is too long for Angus, so he asks you, a young traveler, to speak with Morgan.

quest:1264.text: The Missing Diplomat. A tavern keeper sends you to Commander Samaul in Theramore, where Hendel may still be stationed. The tavern keeper believes Hendel is among the Kul Tiras Marines who visit regularly. They are paid at the beginning of each month and usually leave Theramore afterward. Commander Samaul may know if Hendel is still stationed there. Mention Elling's name, and Samaul may help discreetly. Commander Samaul is the officer in charge of Miss Proudmoore's forces in Theramore. He is busy, but offers to answer your questions. The marsh beyond the city holds ogres, orcs and murlocs. Black dragons dwell in its southern reaches.

quest:1265.text: The Missing Diplomat. Elling sends you to find Private Hendel, and a local officer fears the reason may be troubling. Hendel was stationed at Sentry Point, the first tower outside Theramore, where you are asked to seek signs of him. A local officer knows Private Hendel and says he was stationed at Sentry Point, the first tower outside Theramore. The officer fears Elling sent you there first because your business may be troubling. Tell the officer what you can share. The watch must protect these lands, so any disturbance matters.

quest:1268.text: Suspicious Hoofprints. At the Shady Rest Inn, hoofprints lead into the marsh. Its bare frame still smokes, and the tracks fade across the soft ground. Krog at Brackenwall Village should hear of them. The Shady Rest Inn is a smoking frame, with hoofprints stretching away into the marsh. Some impressions show clearly, while others are nearly lost in the soft ground. You carry word of the tracks to Krog at Brackenwall Village.

quest:1269.text: Lieutenant Paval Reethe. At Brackenwall Village, Krog awaits Lieutenant Paval Reethe's badge and news of the Shady Rest Inn. Beneath rubble and brush, you find a badge marked with Theramore's sign. Ash and debris cover it, but Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name is embossed below the golden anchor. Krog waits at Brackenwall Village. He asks whether you have learned what befell the Shady Rest Inn.

quest:127.text: Selling Fish. Dockmaster Baren needs spotted sunfish from Lake Everstill. The fish feed Lakeshire, but murlocs along the shore make them dangerous to gather. Spotted sunfish are prized around Lake Everstill, and townspeople and passing merchants keep demand high. Yet Lakeshire's supplies often run thin, though the fish swim below the surface. Local threats stretch the town's strength, so even basic trade depends on travelers. Anglers nearby could once fill Dockmaster Baren's orders with ease. Now aggressive murloc tribes haunt the shallows and banks, keeping ordinary townsfolk from the water. You can fish while watching for danger, or take sunfish from the foraging murlocs that trouble the shore.

quest:1270.text: Stinky's Escape. In the swamp, “Stinky” Ignatz is trapped by critters before he finds bogbean. Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet needs the leaves for a potion, so Ignatz asks you to free and guard him as he searches. Then find Mebok in Ratchet. “Stinky” Ignatz is glad to meet someone who will not eat him. Mebok Mizzyrix, a goblin from Ratchet, needs bogbean leaves for a potion. Ignatz says the reason does not matter; the pay was good, and he knows the swamp. But before he found the plant, critters surrounded him. He asks you to help him escape and guard him while he searches.

quest:1271.text: Feast at the Blue Recluse. In Dustwallow Marsh, you finish your work for Morgan Stern with ... and Bugs, then return to Angus Stern at the Blue Recluse. Angus Stern is Morgan Stern's uncle. You return to Angus at the Blue Recluse after helping Morgan research recipes in Dustwallow Marsh.

quest:1273.text: Questioning Reethe. Ogron has found Reethe at last and asks you to help question him. He says Reethe hid well for a human, though the days in the swamp may have driven him mad. Afterward, you return to Krog at Brackenwall Village. Ogron has found Reethe after a long search. By Ogron's reckoning, Reethe hid well for a human. Yet Ogron fears the days in the swamp may have left Reethe mad, and wants you beside him for answers. Once you have spoken with Reethe, you return to Krog at Brackenwall Village.

quest:1274.text: The Missing Diplomat. A quiet request in Stormwind draws you to Bishop DeLavey at Stormwind Keep. The Church and crown need help with a matter too perilous for public channels. As you travel through Stormwind, Thomas, an altar boy, approaches with a quiet request. Bishop DeLavey, a respected cleric of the Church of the Holy Light, needs an outsider's help at Stormwind Keep. He calls the matter delicate and urgent. You must keep it discreet, lest the people panic.

quest:1275.text: Researching the Corruption. In Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper seeks corrupted brain stems from Blackfathom Deeps. Blood elves across the sea are said to be turning to demonic magic. He hopes the naga and satyr can teach him how to keep history from repeating itself. Night elves across Kalimdor still remember the ruin of their ancient kin. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne gave in to demonic energies and became satyrs or naga. Now the high elves call themselves blood elves and embrace dark magic. Gershala Nightwhisper sees the old disaster taking shape again. Blackfathom Deeps gives Gershala a place to study the corruption. Its temple ruins lie beneath the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, where satyr cultists and naga dwell. He asks you to gather brain stems from both. He hopes to trace the link between arcane addiction, demonic corruption, and the body's ruin.

quest:1276.text: The Black Shield. In Thunder Bluff, Krog brings a blackened iron shield to a smith for answers. Reethe gave him nothing useful, leaving Mosarn as his only lead. Krog remembers Mosarn as a highly regarded blacksmith in Thunder Bluff. The Earthen Ring once thanked Krog with armor Mosarn had crafted, and Krog speaks well of that work. He believes Mosarn made the shield too and may know more. It is a slim lead. Reethe yielded nothing useful, so Krog brings the blackened iron shield to Mosarn in Thunder Bluff.

quest:128.text: Blackrock Bounty. In Lakeshire, Blackrock Bounty draws fighters as Blackrock forces gather in northern Redridge. Stormwind sends no royal soldiers, so Magistrate Solomon and Guard Howe offer payment to independent fighters who strike at Blackrock Champions and disrupt the clan’s assault. Redridge belongs to the Kingdom of Stormwind, yet the Blackrock clan ignores human borders. Orcs pour through mountain passes from the Burning Steppes and fortify camps across northern Redridge. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and Stormwind’s regency withholds royal soldiers. As Lakeshire’s coffers dwindle, Magistrate Solomon and other local leaders offer bounties to protect the town. Guard Howe names the Blackrock Champions as the backbone of the invading vanguard. These squad leaders are battle-hardened veterans who coordinate their warbands and drive lesser grunts forward. Lakeshire’s defenders hope a bounty on the Champions will break the clan’s tactical leadership and stall a full-scale push south. The town’s outer defenses may soon collapse.

quest:1282.text: They Call Him Smiling Jim. Guard Byron sends you to Theramore for the story of They Call Him Smiling Jim. He hints that Jim's life was not always this way. Guard Byron remembers the fine inn Smiling Jim once kept in the marsh. He pities Jim, but would rather not speak of what changed. For the full story, ask Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore.

quest:1284.text: Suspicious Hoofprints. Smoke rises from the Shady Rest Inn, and Suspicious Hoofprints cross the marsh. Some prints are clear; others fade in the soft mud. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore needs the report. Hoofprints lead from the smoking ruin of the Shady Rest Inn into the marsh. Some are easy to see, while others nearly vanish in the soft mud. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore needs to hear about them.

quest:1285.text: Daelin's Men. Adjutant Tesoran has found Lieutenant Paval Reethe in the guard's records. They trace Reethe's service from enlistment in the Kul Tiras marines at sixteen, through promotions for distinguished service, to the Theramore guard with Lady Proudmoore's recruits. The final entry marks Reethe missing, and Captain Garran Vimes is to hear the news. Captain Garran Vimes sent you to Adjutant Tesoran, who searched the books and found Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Reethe enlisted in the Kul Tiras marines at sixteen, and distinguished service brought him promotions. Later, he joined the Theramore guard with most of the recruits who sailed over with Lady Proudmoore. The record ends by listing him as missing. Vimes, in Theramore, is to hear the news.

quest:1286.text: The Deserters. At Lost Point, Captain Garran Vimes questions deserters who took Theramore’s abandoned tower. Captain Garran Vimes struggles to hold the marsh, yet his people keep several watchtowers standing. Scouts have found deserters in an abandoned tower at Lost Point, southeast of the inn. A man named Jacken leads them. Vimes asks you to learn what Jacken knows about Reethe, though the man may not give up the information easily.

quest:1287.text: The Deserters. Reethe has been driven from the deserter band, and Balos Jacken calls him a coward. Jacken asks you to forget the meeting. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is waiting to hear about Reethe. Balos Jacken says the deserters drove Reethe out for repeatedly plundering the ogres’ stores at Brackenwall Village. The band is too small to face those ogres, he says, and Reethe crossed the line once too often. They left Reethe to manage alone. In return for the answer, Jacken asks you to forget the meeting.

quest:1288.text: Vimes's Report. Captain Garran Vimes praises your work as the finest he has seen from an amateur. Now you carry his report to Theramore for Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore asked Captain Vimes to keep her informed about a delicate situation. He has not spoken with her for some time. He planned to deliver the report later, but now sends you in his place. You may have better answers to her questions than he does.

quest:1289.text: Vimes's Report. Lady Jaina Proudmoore has read Vimes's Report and thanks you for aiding Captain Garran Vimes's investigation. She sends you back to Vimes in Theramore to help uncover the mystery. Lady Jaina Proudmoore thanks you for helping Captain Vimes's investigation. His report eases her mind because the matter is in capable hands. She sends you back to him in Theramore to help uncover the mystery.

quest:1302.text: James Hyal. Across the Great Sea, James Hyal's family waits for word from Kalimdor. He sailed there with Lady Jaina Proudmoore's expedition and set out to open an inn on the frontier. Now his family looks to Theramore's records for news. During the Third War, many left their homes in the Eastern Kingdoms to follow Lady Jaina Proudmoore across the Great Sea. James Hyal went with them, known at home for his gift in the kitchen. After the fighting ended and Theramore Isle was founded, he sought a living on Kalimdor. He planned to open an inn for travelers and fellow settlers. Back in the Eastern Kingdoms, James's brother grows worried. No letters have come from across the sea, though he hopes James is busy running a roadside taproom. He asks travelers to seek his brother out. The search begins in Theramore, where Clerk Lendry keeps records of expedition members who have ventured into the wilderness.

quest:1319.text: The Black Shield. At Theramore's smithy, Captain Garran Vimes sends a shield to a smith who may know its maker. Captain Garran Vimes knows little about the shield. So he sends you to Caz Twosprocket, one of the best blacksmiths around. Caz tends the forge in Theramore's smithy and may be able to tell you more.

quest:1320.text: The Black Shield. Caz Twosprocket studies the black shield tied to the Shady Rest Inn mystery. One detail nearly escapes notice, and Caz sends you to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore with what was found. A last detail nearly escapes Caz Twosprocket while looking over the black shield. The leather strap on its back has burned away, yet it seems to have been made for a large person. Caz guesses a tauren. That is all Caz can tell, so you are sent to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore with the word and Caz's apology for not being more help.

quest:1321.text: The Black Shield. Krog sends you to Brackenwall Village to ask Do'gol about the Blackened Iron Shield. Krog finds nothing unusual about the Blackened Iron Shield. Still, he thinks Do'gol, the blacksmith in Brackenwall Village, may see something more. He urges you not to expect much.

quest:1322.text: The Black Shield. In Brackenwall Village, Do'gol seeks venom for a shield whose writing is hidden by burned residue. Six sacs from the marsh's Darkfang spiders hold acid that can clear its rim. At Brackenwall Village, Do'gol studies the lettering around a shield's rim. Burned grime makes it hard to read, but acid can clear the residue. Darkfang spiders in the marsh carry venom fit for the work, so Do'gol asks you for six of their venom sacs.

quest:1323.text: The Black Shield. In Brackenwall Village, Do'gol sends you to Krog to learn a name on the shield. The writing seems to say Mosarn, but Do'gol does not know the name. Do'gol has rubbed the shield with too much acid, yet its writing remains hard to read. The name seems to be Mosarn, but Do'gol does not know it. Krog knows many people in Brackenwall Village, so Do'gol sends you to speak with Krog.

quest:133.text: Ghoulish Effigy. In Duskwood, the dead press against Abercrombie’s shack. He asks you for ghoul ribs to make a grim scarecrow and guard his home. Beyond Darkshire’s guarded bounds, Abercrombie lives alone among Duskwood’s shadowed trees. Flesh Eaters and Bone Chewers roam the wilds freely. He says ravenous corpses recently battered down his walls, so he asks you to bring him their ribs. He hopes a grisly effigy will keep the hungry dead from his home. For his wooden shack, Abercrombie trusts a grim plan over the Night Watch or stronger walls. He believes an effigy made from ghoul remains will frighten off other scavenging dead. A scarecrow built from slain undead is unsettling. Yet travelers in Duskwood often do as the hermit asks to earn needed coin.

quest:134.text: Ogre Thieves. In western Duskwood, Abercrombie sends travelers to the ogres’ stronghold at Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. He says they ambushed him while he foraged and took a crate of irreplaceable herbs and tools. On the damp roads of western Duskwood, Abercrombie says he was attacked while gathering supplies. Brutes from the southern ogre mound drove the aged hermit off. He left behind a sturdy wooden crate filled with precious herbs and delicate instruments. In southern Duskwood, Vul'Gol Ogre Mound is a danger to unwary wanderers. Hostile ogres harass travelers there, and Abercrombie's crate rests near the entrance among roaring brutes and spell-weaving magi.

quest:1361.text: Regthar Deathgate. In the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate calls seasoned Horde fighters west. He is gathering volunteers for a campaign across the mountains into Desolace, where centaur clans terrorize the frontier. Horde leaders watch their borders for threats. In the Barrens, Regthar Deathgate has raised a defensive post to guard the western passes. So Horde officers send proven fighters west of the Crossroads to answer his call. Regthar Deathgate waits in a fortified redoubt along the ridges west of the Crossroads. From there, he watches the mountain trails into Desolace. He is gathering a vanguard to cross hostile ground and strike the Kolkar and other warring centaur clans before their expansion threatens Horde territory.

quest:1362.text: The Kolkar of Desolace. Regthar Deathgate sends Horde champions west into Desolace to reinforce scout Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post. The Kolkar threaten Horde lands from their stronghold there. Centaur raiders keep pressing into the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate knows the fighting will not end there while the Kolkar draw strength from their ancestral lands on Kalimdor's western coast. Their stronghold remains beyond Horde control, and raiders keep pouring through the mountain passes. The Horde must strike at their home. Ghost Walker Post gives the Horde a foothold deep in Desolace. Scout Felgur Twocuts watches the rival centaur clans from the outpost. Regthar sends seasoned fighters from the Barrens to serve under Felgur. From this camp, the Horde carries its campaign west, from defense to direct action.

quest:1365.text: Khan Dez'hepah. After The Kolkar of Desolace, Felgur Twocuts turns against Khan Dez'hepah. Many centaur clans fight across Desolace, and Felgur wants the Kolkar weakened before they unite. Across Desolace, centaur clans fight one another. The Kolkar are one of many, roaming the dry plains and killing their own. Felgur Twocuts does not mourn their losses. Centaur are strong and brutal, and united they would be a fierce foe for the Horde. Felgur wants the Kolkar weakened before that can happen. Felgur Twocuts begins by disrupting the Kolkar. Their village lies northeast of where Felgur stands. Felgur wants Khan Dez'hepah's head brought back.

quest:1366.text: Centaur Bounty. In Desolace, Felgur Twocuts calls for blood after Khan Dez'hepah. He wants fifteen ears from centaur of any clan. Felgur Twocuts says the centaur clans have been scared. Now, he says, it is time to bleed them. As you travel across Desolace, hunt centaur from any clan and gather fifteen ears. Felgur wants to thin their numbers and weaken their resolve. He means to end any thoughts of expansion.

quest:1367.text: Magram Alliance. In Desolace, Gurda Wildmane urges you to turn the centaur clans' hatred against them. Befriend one clan to learn how all can be beaten. If you side with the Magram, slay the Gelkis, then speak with Warug at the edge of Magram Village in southeast Desolace. Gurda Wildmane urges you to turn the centaur clans' hatred against them. Choose one clan as an ally and learn from it how all can be beaten. If you side with the Magram, slaying their foes, the Gelkis, earns their respect. Warug, the Magram spokesman, waits on the outskirts of Magram Village in southeast Desolace once you have earned enough respect. Before then, he has nothing to say to you. The Magram have no words for the weak. They kill them instead. To prove your strength, Warug sends you to face many Gelkis.

quest:1368.text: Gelkis Alliance. In southwest Desolace, Gurda Wildmane turns the centaur clans' hatred toward their defeat. Befriend one clan to learn how the others may be beaten. The Gelkis demand that you kill their hated enemies, the Magram, before you meet Uthek the Wise at Gelkis Village. Gurda Wildmane means to turn the centaur clans' hatred against them. Befriend one clan, and what you learn may show how to defeat them all. Choose the Gelkis. To earn their respect, kill the Magram, the clan they hate most. Once the Gelkis respect you, meet Uthek the Wise, their shaman, on the outskirts of Gelkis Village in southwest Desolace. Until then, you are not welcome there. Uthek says you tread on Gelkis earth. Prove your friendship by killing Magram centaur, then return when their blood has soaked the ground.

quest:1369.text: Broken Tears. In the Gelkis village cave, Warug wants you to break the crystals they call the tears of Theradras. He asks for three broken pieces, claiming the centaur mother cannot protect them. Warug mocks the Gelkis for trusting Theradras, mother of the centaur, to protect them. He says no one protects the centaur, while the Magram are strongest and need no protection. In a cave in the Gelkis village, the Gelkis hoard crystals called the tears of Theradras. Warug sends you to smash them and bring him three broken pieces. He trusts you with this only if you are no enemy of the Magram.

quest:1370.text: Stealing Supplies. In Desolace, Uthek the Wise sends you east after the Magram’s stores. The Gelkis believe meat gives them strength, while the Magram keep supplies for the days between hunts. Uthek the Wise says the Gelkis draw strength from meat. A full belly fights harder than an empty one. The Magram keep extra stores for the days between hunts. So you are sent to their village to the east for six bags of crudely dried meat, to bring back to Uthek at the Gelkis Village.

quest:1371.text:
Gizmo for Warug. In Magram Village, Warug now wants a new target dummy to replace the wooden human he broke. Warug remembers a gnome who came to Desolace long ago with horses and a cart. Inside were curious things: some burned in different colors, while others moved though they were not alive. Warug killed the gnome, but not before the gnome made him laugh.

Warug kept his favorite thing from the cart, a wooden human that waved at him. He hit it and broke it. Now he wants an advanced target dummy to take its place, and expects one from anyone who is no enemy of the Magram.

quest:1373.text:
Ongeku. Uthek sends you from Desolace to find a shard of draenethyst. The earth has whispered of the red crystal to him, and Ongeku holds a shard in the Swamp of Sorrows. After Stealing Supplies, Uthek the Wise sends you far from Desolace for a red crystal called draenethyst. He says the earth shares its secrets with those who listen. The crystal has only recently come to this land, carried from a place of flying mountains ruled by demons.

Uthek says a shard will make the magic strong. Ongeku, the lost one, holds one in the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. When you return, Uthek will seek proof that the Gelkis can still call you friend.

quest:1374.text: Khan Jehn. At Gelkis Village, Uthek the Wise says Khan Jehn must fall as the Magram grow weak. He asks you to bring the Khan's head back. At Gelkis Village, Uthek the Wise listens to what the earth tells him. The Magram are growing weak, and their Khan, Jehn, is the one to strike down. Uthek asks you to bring back the Magram Khan's head. He expects you to return as a friend of the Gelkis.

quest:1375.text: Khan Shaka. Warug of the Magram now sends you after Khan Shaka, the Gelkis Khan. Bring him Shaka’s head so he can stare at it and laugh at his enemy. In Magram Village, Warug says your help has pleased him and served the Magram well. Now he wants Khan Shaka, the Gelkis Khan, killed, and his head brought back. Warug means to stare at it and laugh at his enemy. He expects you to stay on good terms with the Magram.

quest:1382.text: Strange Alliance. Captain Pentigast seeks an alliance with the Gelkis in Desolace. They are at war with the Magram, and he sends you southwest to Uthek the Wise. Captain Pentigast sees a chance in the centaur clans’ quarrels. Joined together, they could not be stopped. He hopes their division will serve the Alliance. The Gelkis and Magram are locked in a brutal war, so striking at the Magram might persuade the Gelkis to join the Alliance. Uthek the Wise is where the Gelkis camps begin in southwestern Desolace. Pentigast hopes she can help secure an alliance. At first, she sends you away. She tells you to return after killing many Magram.

quest:1384.text: Raid on the Kolkar. In Desolace, Uthek the Wise sends you northeast against the Kolkar centaurs. After Strange Alliance, he wants ten of their charms brought back. Uthek scorns the Kolkar centaurs for trusting in their magic. To him, they know nothing of such things. So you head northeast, kill Kolkar, and take their charms. Uthek wants ten Crude Charms to cast into the fire and laugh as they burn.

quest:1385.text: Brutal Politics. Captain Pentigast fears Desolace’s victorious centaur clan will threaten Alliance strongholds. He seeks a clan’s friendship so the Alliance can learn how to defeat the centaurs. Centaur clans wage war across Desolace. Captain Pentigast fears the victor will turn against Alliance strongholds, so he seeks a way to prevent that danger. The Alliance needs a centaur clan as a friend to learn how to defeat the others. The Magram fight the Gelkis, so attacking the Gelkis may win the Magram’s favor. Earn that favor, then find Warug in the Magram village in southeastern Desolace. Warug says killing Gelkis is how you become a friend to the Magram.

quest:1386.text: Assault on the Kolkar. In Magram Village, Warug wants you to prove you can kill Kolkar as the Magram do. After Brutal Politics, you head north to face Kolkar centaurs, scouts and maulers. Warug mocks the Kolkar and their belief that they are strong. The Magram laugh as they kill them, and Warug wants you to prove you can do the same. Head north and slay twelve Kolkar centaurs, twelve scouts and six maulers.

quest:1387.text: Centaur Bounty. At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins sends you after Desolace's centaur clans. He asks for fifteen ears, believing peace cannot come while they remain. At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins speaks of Desolace's centaur clans. Each has its own leader and plans. Yet all share the same cruelty. Melkins says peace can come only when the centaur are gone. As you wander Desolace, you hunt centaur and take their ears. Melkins asks you to bring fifteen. He calls this service to the Alliance, bringing the war's end nearer.

quest:1389.text: Draenethyst Crystals. At the Harborage, Magtoor asks you to recover six draenethyst crystals stolen from the Fallow Sanctuary. Sacred to his people, the crystals are bound to their fear of losing their way. The lost ones of the Fallow Sanctuary resemble Magtoor's people. The journey to Azeroth drove them mad. Once brethren, they now dwell in the Sanctuary to the east, where they seize or kill anyone who strays close. They have also stolen draenethyst crystals, sacred to Magtoor's people. Magtoor's people lack the strength to enter the Fallow Sanctuary and reclaim the draenethyst among its huts and campfires. Without the crystals, they fear they too may lose their way. So Magtoor asks you to bring back six.

quest:1392.text: Noboru the Cudgel. At the Harborage, the Draenei have endured Noboru the Cudgel’s torment for months. You carry his cudgel to their leader, a token of the cruelty the lost ones have dealt them. For months, Noboru has tormented the Draenei who live at the Harborage. His cudgel recalls the cruelty the lost ones have dealt them. You carry it to their leader.

quest:1393.text: Galen's Escape. In the Fallow Sanctuary, Galen Goodward calls for help as creatures close around him. He offers a great treasure from his camp north of Stonard. Galen Goodward calls out from the Fallow Sanctuary, afraid the creatures around him will eat him. He promises a great treasure to anyone who gets him out. It lies in a strongbox at his camp in the swamp north of Stonard. Only Galen knows the trick to open it, and he will teach it to whoever rescues him.

quest:1394.text: Final Passage. You have passed Parqual Fintallas's test and all that came before it. Now he sends you to Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles, who will judge whether your mind, body and spirit have grown strong enough to earn honour. Dorn Plainstalker began the Test of Faith, and its trials now reach their final step. He waits in the Weathered Nook, in a cave reached by a ramp north of Freewind Post. Parqual Fintallas urges you to keep the balance you have shown through the trials.

quest:1396.text: Encroaching Wildlife. After Lost Ones wreck Watcher Biggs's caravan, wild creatures prowl near his camp. Biggs alone survives and asks you to help defend the supplies that remain. This follows Help Watcher Biggs. Watcher Biggs's caravan set out for the eastern coast, but never arrived. Lost Ones attacked, killing the guards and smashing the supplies. Biggs alone survived, and he has sworn to protect what remains. Now wild creatures skulk near the camp, and Biggs asks you to help defend it. Young sawtooth crocolisks, sorrow spinners and swamp jaguars press close to the camp. Biggs names eight crocolisks, ten spinners and ten jaguars to be slain.

quest:1418.text: Neeka Bloodscar. In Stonard, Helgrum the Swift sends you to Kargath, where his messages often fail to arrive. In the Badlands, harsh country near Alliance-held Loch Modan, messages between Stonard and Kargath often fail. Helgrum asks you to prove yourself by traveling to Kargath and speaking with Neeka Bloodscar, its head scout. Then you carry Neeka's report back to Helgrum.

quest:1421.text: The Lost Caravan. Watcher Biggs needs the caravan's reagents recovered after the Lost Ones carry a wagon north to the Fallow Sanctuary. The chest holds supplies for the wizards of Nethergarde Keep. Watcher Biggs was knocked senseless when the Lost Ones attacked the caravan. Before he fell, he saw them drag one of its wagons north to the Fallow Sanctuary, their village. A chest of reagents was aboard, prized by the wizards of Nethergarde Keep for their studies. Biggs asks you to find the chest and carry its contents back.

quest:1431.text: Alliance Relations. Thrall seeks a careful hand to keep peace with the Alliance. In Orgrimmar, Craven Drok sends seasoned Horde adventurers to Keldran, near the western exit. Quiet diplomacy and intelligence may help protect Thrall’s fragile peace. Thrall fears that war with the Alliance could ruin his young nation. Raised in human captivity, the Warchief learned human statecraft and military strategy. So Craven Drok watches for warriors and champions who can look beyond raw force and choose a subtler path. Near Orgrimmar’s western exit, Keldran keeps a humble dwelling. He practices magic and covert arts, working with appearances, perception, and statecraft. As the Horde faces a tense standoff with its bitter rivals, Keldran seeks discreet operatives to serve the Warchief.

quest:1432.text: Alliance Relations. In Orgrimmar, Alliance advances across Kalimdor put the Horde under pressure. Thrall's people send orders to Desolace to purge demons before the Alliance can accuse them of renewed ties to the Burning Legion. Alliance scouts and expeditions cross Kalimdor, leaving the Horde in a delicate position. Demonic remnants in central Kalimdor could confirm old suspicions that the orcs and their allies still serve the Burning Legion. With Warchief Thrall's sanction, Keldran oversees the effort from Orgrimmar. They must clear those remnants before hostile Alliance factions use them to justify war. The orders lead south through the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains and onward into Desolace. Ghost Walker Post stands just north of the vast Kodo Graveyard. Horde agents such as Takata Steelblade watch over these wastes. Rampant centaur tribes and spreading demonic corruption both threaten the region.

quest:1437.text: Vahlarriel's Search. In Desolace, Vahlarriel Demonslayer searches for two missing nobles of House Malem. Their father fears the worst, and the siblings were last reported crossing the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks ago. Vahlarriel asks you to find their wagon. Vahlarriel Demonslayer seeks Tyranis and Dalinda Malem. Their father has charged Vahlarriel with doing everything possible to find them. The search has only begun, and Vahlarriel hopes it will not keep them in Desolace long. The siblings were last reported crossing the Stonetalon Mountains some weeks ago. You are asked to find their wagon in Desolace and return at once. Its charred remains lie there, with a chest among them.

quest:1438.text: Vahlarriel's Search. At the fortress, Vahlarriel Demonslayer sends you to find Dalinda and Tyranis Malem. Their search begins there as Vahlarriel alerts superiors in Darnassus. They put Dalinda’s safe return first and question Tyranis’s motives. Vahlarriel Demonslayer asks you to seek Dalinda and Tyranis at the fortress and bring back what you learn. Vahlarriel will contact superiors in Darnassus at once. In private, they share their concern about why Tyranis came to Desolace. Above all, they want Dalinda brought home safe. Tyranis’s return can wait until they know more about him.

quest:1439.text: Search for Tyranis. At Thunder Axe Fortress, Dalinda Malem waits to learn what became of Tyranis. Orcs killed their guards and servants before bringing the siblings there. Tyranis tried to speak with his captors, and Dalinda asks you to find him and return once you know his fate. Orcs killed every guard and servant before dragging Dalinda and Tyranis to Thunder Axe Fortress. She expected them to die at once, but their captors had other designs. Tyranis tried speaking with the orcs, perhaps hoping his arcane learning would impress them. Dalinda cannot say why. She will not escape until she knows his fate, so she asks you to find him and return. He is in the building left of the fortress entrance. Dalinda fears Tyranis will seek the Burning Blade's secrets and join them if he can. Power has always drawn him, as magic draws those it seduces. To Dalinda's people, even studying such things is a grave crime. She doubts she could face her family knowing her brother had toyed with that danger.

quest:1440.text: Return to Vahlarriel. At Thunder Axe Fortress, Dalinda Malem is ready to leave when you choose. She thanks you for helping her and her family. Escort her out, then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer. Dalinda Malem is ready to leave Thunder Axe Fortress when you judge the moment right. She thanks you for all you have done for her and her family, in case things do not go as hoped. Nothing else keeps her there. She will leave when you choose the time. Escort her out of the fortress, then find Vahlarriel Demonslayer in Desolace.

quest:1442.text: Seeking the Kor Gem. You cross the sea to Darkshore seeking a Kor gem for Jordan Stilwell. Thundris Windweaver sends an Alliance paladin initiate into Blackfathom Deeps, where naga have corrupted the potent stone. Jordan needs it for his craft. Paladins in training travel across the sea to Darkshore for materials Jordan Stilwell needs. In Auberdine, the night elf Thundris Windweaver remembers the human blacksmith with respect. Night elves keep their distance, and some fallen humans have betrayed their trust. Yet Thundris believes paladins can still follow a righteous path. He tells them where ancient gems may be found. Blackfathom Deeps lies beneath Ashenvale's foggy northwestern coast. Twilight's Hammer cultists and treacherous sea-dwellers dwell in its submerged halls. Naga priestesses channel foul magic through ancient Kor gems. The gem you seek lies deep within the temple complex, among its dark halls and dangerous inhabitants.

quest:1447.text: The Missing Diplomat. In Stormwind, you seek the missing diplomat and find Dashel Stonefist in Old Town. You need answers from a man who would rather keep them to himself. In Old Town, your search leads through cutpurses and shady brokers, beyond the Cathedral’s watchful eye. Dashel Stonefist is a local contact with ties to Stormwind’s criminal factions. He knows about the abduction, but has no wish to share what he knows with investigators asking sensitive questions.

quest:1454.text:
The Karnitol Shipwreck. After sea giants strike his ship in Desolace, Karnitol flees with his servants by teleporting away. Kreldig Ungor sends you to find the noble's chest. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor sends you to find Karnitol's lost chest. Karnitol is a mage and some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck his ship in the northwest waters of Desolace.

He and his servants tried to bring one of his costlier chests ashore, but the giants swarmed them. Karnitol left the chest behind and teleported away with his servants. Find the chest and its contents, then return them to Karnitol in Stormwind. It lies along the northern coastline, in the Ethel Rethor stretch.

quest:1455.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. At Karnitol's wreck, you find the chest open and empty. Deep scratches score its sides and top, so you return to Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point. The chest lies empty, its sides and top scored with long, deep scratches. The marks suggest neither man nor giant forced it open. They look unlike cuts from a dagger or sword. With nothing more to learn, you close the chest and prepare to leave. Kreldig Ungor will be disappointed.

quest:1456.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Near Ranazjar Isle, Kreldig Ungor still hopes Karnitol's belongings can be found. The Slitherblade naga live among night elf ruins beneath the sea, where Kreldig thinks the satchel is most likely to be. Kreldig Ungor says there is still hope of finding Karnitol's belongings. Farther north along the coast, sunken night elf ruins lie on the ocean floor near Ranazjar Isle. The Slitherblade naga live there, and Kreldig believes it is the likeliest place to find Karnitol's satchel. He gives you a Recovery Diver's Potion. Kreldig believes the scouting party that traveled so far south must have been strong. He would search the mightier naga first: the tidehunters and sea witches.

quest:1457.text: The Karnitol Shipwreck. Karnitol's satchel waits in Ironforge for Roetten Stonehammer, who will pay you to carry it there. Kreldig Ungor sends you to take Karnitol's things to Roetten Stonehammer in Ironforge. Roetten will pay you for the work. With a laugh, Kreldig says Roetten may be so pleased that he asks you to join the Reclaimers full time. Travel carefully and without delay. Karnitol has little patience, though he is generous.

quest:1458.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. In Desolace, Kreldig Ungor gathers reagents for Leftwitch, a gnome mage in Kharanos. The Reclaimers are short-handed, so he begins with claws and horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor takes on another job. He gathers reagents for Leftwitch, a gnome mage who lives in Kharanos. Roetten calls it easy coin because the Reclaimers are already in Desolace. The crew is short-handed, but Kreldig says he does not care. Kreldig begins with ten claws and ten horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east. They dwell in the Sargeron ruins, due east of Nijel's Point. Once you have the claws and horns, the rest of Leftwitch's list can begin.

quest:1459.text: Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. In Desolace, Leftwitch's list sends Kreldig Ungor after scorpashi venom and aged kodo hides. He barely knows the land and cannot point you toward either creature. Kreldig Ungor reaches the next items on Leftwitch's list. She asks for seven vials of venom from any scorpashi and three hides from aged kodo. Dying and ancient kodo will not do. The instructions are plain, though Kreldig muses that mages ask for odd things. Kreldig cannot tell you where the kodo or scorpashi roam. He barely knows Desolace and has had no time to explore it.

quest:1465.text: Vahlarriel's Search. In Desolace, Vahlarriel's Search follows a trail south from the Malems' wagon. A pendant lies there, and smoke rises from a large fort in the distance.
