At Nijel's Point, Vahlarriel Demonslayer needs the pendant and word that the Malems may still be alive. You find a pendant in the Malems' wagon and footprints leading south. Smoke rises from a large fort in the distance. A tended fire feeds it, rather than burning buildings. If the Malems are alive, the tracks suggest they were taken toward the fort. At Nijel's Point, Vahlarriel Demonslayer needs to see the Malem Pendant. Tell her about the footprints leading south.

quest:1472.text: Devourer of Souls. In the Temple of the Damned, Carendin Halgar teaches Forsaken warlocks to bind a succubus. Godrick Farsan knows how to draw one from the Twisting Nether with the hearts of pure, loving mortals. Carendin Halgar teaches that a succubus must be lured across the threshold, not called by command. The demon hungers to ruin virtue and consume mortal essence. Offer the hearts of genuinely virtuous, loving men as bait. Halgar sends you to Godrick Farsan, who knows where such rare quarry can be found. Deep in the Temple of the Damned, Godrick Farsan helps Carendin prepare for demonic binding. Farsan has lost his physical sight, but says this has given him a deeper one. He claims to perceive spiritual currents and distant souls with uncanny clarity. With that sight, he can guide you to the pure hearts needed to draw out the demon.

quest:1474.text: The Binding. In the Undercity, Carendin Halgar puts an initiate's command of a succubus to the test. Pure Hearts draw the demon from the Twisting Nether into a ritual circle, where the warlock must master it through combat. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks learn to command demons. Summoning a succubus marks a hard passage in that training. A voidwalker depends on brute force, and an imp on lesser malice. A succubus can turn seductive and mental enchantments against its summoner. So Carendin Halgar requires each initiate to prove mind and magic unshakable before granting lasting dominion over such a demon.

quest:1476.text: Hearts of the Pure. In the Undercity, Godrick Farsan sets a trial for Carendin Halgar’s succubus binding. You seek two righteous human men whose pure hearts will tempt a demon. Carendin Halgar, master summoner in the Temple of the Damned, gives Godrick Farsan the groundwork for binding a succubus. Succubi prey on desire and ruin. Yet untainted virtue draws them from the Twisting Nether, where they are ripe for corruption. So Godrick searches human lands for souls whose goodness remains pristine and unbroken. Godrick Farsan names two men whose virtue marks them for sacrifice. Dalin Forgewright cares for desperate Lordaeron refugees barred from sanctuary outside the sealed Greymane Wall in southern Silverpine. Comar Villard tirelessly searches the perilous marshlands of the Wetlands for any trace of his lost wife. Their devotion, empathy and loyalty make them prime sacrifices to a Forsaken warlock.

quest:148.text: Supplies from Darkshire. Abercrombie in western Duskwood asks you to fetch a rare thread from Darkshire. He says he is too frail to cross the haunted woods and asks for Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva. North of Raven Hill Cemetery, you find Abercrombie alone in a shack in western Duskwood. Age and frailty keep him from making the dangerous journey through the woods to buy goods in Darkshire. So he asks you to go to the township's town square and speak with Madame Eva for a spool of Ghost Hair Thread.

quest:1480.text: The Corrupter. At Thunder Axe Fortress, a flayed strip from the Burning Blade bears red markings and a signature-like symbol. It smells rotten, yet bends easily. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may know more. The flayed skin smells of rot, yet bends easily despite its dry, fragile feel. Unrolled, it shows red markings on one side, written in some kind of language. A plain symbol at the bottom looks like a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may know more about the skin. Maurin believes the Burning Blade are coming to see how weak they are. Their magic is poor and their strength slight. Whatever power they hold comes from those they serve, not from any grasp of true power or knowledge.

quest:1481.text:
The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter searches for a way to find The Corrupter, though its wards may foil scrying. He needs a Hatefury shadowstalker scalp from the old ruins in northeast Desolace, near Sargeron. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the right reagents can reveal the demon lord. If Maurin is right about its power, those reagents must come from deadly creatures. He trusts you to face that danger in the Warchief's name.

First, the demon lord's wards against scrying must be broken. Maurin asks you for a satyr's scalp, and only a Hatefury shadowstalker's will serve. Search the old ruins in northeast Desolace, near Sargeron. Maurin warns you to bring back the right scalp. Wrong reagents could get people killed, for the demon lord may have contingency spells meant to slay anyone who tries to scry on him. Fate has already dealt out enough pain, he says.

quest:1482.text: The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter seeks an oracle crystal to find the demon lord Azrethoc. Northwest along the coast, the Slitherblade naga dwell in a vast coral reef, and they will take your intrusion badly. Maurin Bonesplitter needs an oracle crystal to find the demon lord Azrethoc. The skin you brought him bore Azrethoc's signature. Naga craft these crystals for their oracles, who dwell in a vast coral reef northwest along the coast. The Slitherblade naga live there near the shore. They are deadly and will take your intrusion badly, so Maurin urges you to move carefully and quickly. Maurin says finding and destroying Lord Azrethoc would earn you both much favor with the Warchief. Working together and moving swiftly serves each of your aims.

quest:1483.text: Ziz Fizziks. On Windshear Crag’s western ridge, Ziz Fizziks has left the Venture Company for the Tinkers' Union. A gnome engineer’s arrival drove him away, though his new superior works him just as hard. The Venture Company hired Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a gnome engineer, and Ziz Fizziks took it as an insult. He could not bear to work beside a gnomish rival, so he sought a way out. Ziz contacted Sputtervalve, a representative of the Tinkers' Union, and begged for a transfer away from Gerenzo’s oversight. The Tinkers' Union gave Ziz Fizziks a new position, but the easy life he expected never came. On Windshear Crag’s western edge, he found that Sputtervalve drove him as hard as any Venture Company foreman. Still, Ziz would rather labor under a demanding goblin superior than share an engineering workshop with a gnome.

quest:1484.text:
The Corrupter. Near Maurin Bonesplitter, the demon lord has proved more dangerous than he expected. Maurin believes Takata Steelblade doubts his skill, and that withholding what happened would dishonor Takata. So he sends you to speak with the swordsman nearby. The demon lord has proved more dangerous than Maurin Bonesplitter expected. Maurin believes Takata Steelblade doubts he can handle the creature, and keeping Takata uninformed would insult the swordsman's honor.

Maurin asks you to speak with Takata and offer to slay the demon, if Takata allows it. He cautions you not to press too hard, for he thinks Takata should believe the idea is his own. Takata Steelblade is nearby, across the path from Maurin. He stands on a cliff overlooking the Kodo Graveyard.

quest:1487.text: Deviate Eradication. In the Wailing Caverns, Ebru sends you to thin the deviate beasts. The night elf druid watches over the caverns while other disciples try to wake Naralex. His twisted vision has spawned mutated creatures whose numbers threaten to carry corruption beyond the underground springs and into the Barrens. Naralex brought his followers to the Barrens' underground springs, hoping to draw on the Emerald Dream and restore the dry plains as woodland. Instead, the Dream ensnared him, and his sleep turned to nightmare. Power coursing through the caverns warped native plants and animals into aggressive mutants called deviate beasts. Ebru watches from a cliffside cave above the entrance with the few Disciples of Naralex who remain. Their numbers dwindle. Some work to wake their fallen leader, but Ebru sees danger in the deviate vipers, shamblers, ravagers, and dreadfangs. They multiply quickly and may spread into the Barrens. So Ebru asks you to enter the deep tunnels and cull the monsters at their source.

quest:149.text: Ghost Hair Thread. In Duskwood, Madame Eva seeks ghost hair to spin into Ghost Hair Thread for Abercrombie. She sends you south of Darkshire to Blind Mary at an abandoned farmhouse, where an ethereal comb can gather hair from the tormented spirit. Madame Eva needs ghost hair to spin thread for Abercrombie. Linen and wool cannot serve Duskwood's rituals, so she gives you a Spectral Comb to gather strands from a spirit. The comb passes through the veil of death and catches loose spectral hair without violence. South of Darkshire, Blind Mary haunts an abandoned farmhouse. The tormented spirit despairs over her appearance and screams at intruders to look away. In anguish over what she had become, she tore out her own eyes. The Spectral Comb offers brief comfort: she can groom her ghostly hair, though her torment continues.

quest:150.text: Murloc Poachers. Along Lake Everstill, murlocs are stripping Lakeshire's waters of fish. Dockmaster Baren asks you to thin their ranks before the town loses its main food supply. Dockmaster Baren asks you to protect the fish that feed Lakeshire. Lake Everstill supplies the mountain town and its market with fresh catches. Large murloc tribes now crowd the shallows and scour the water for food. Left unchecked, they could wipe out the local fish and leave Lakeshire without its main food supply. Murlocs usually scavenge along the coast, so their numbers high in the Redridge Mountains are hard to explain. Dockmaster Baren wonders why they have come so far from the open ocean. They may be fleeing predators at sea, losing territorial fights, or drawn by Lake Everstill's plentiful waters. Whatever brought them inland, their presence points to trouble elsewhere in the region.

quest:1505.text: Veteran Uzzek. Just south of Far Watch Post, recruits turn to Veteran Uzzek for lessons in combat. His years of experience teach young Horde warriors that strength calls for discipline and study. Strength alone cannot make a Horde warrior a champion. The finest fighters stay humble students of their craft. Through discipline and study, they sharpen their instincts. Young warriors ready to pass beyond basic training seek veterans who have survived the trials of war. Between Durotar and the Barrens, young fighters seek deeper guidance in combat. Far Watch Post watches the eastern frontier. Just south of the orc garrison, Veteran Uzzek teaches promising recruits combat and survival tactics. He has endured countless bloody conflicts and now guides the next generation.

quest:1507.text: Devourer of Souls. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye sends an aspiring Horde warlock to seek Cazul's counsel. There, the warlock begins learning how to lure and bind a succubus. Horde warlocks who master lesser demons such as imps and voidwalkers may seek a succubus next. Beneath Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye oversees the dark arts and judges when a warlock is ready to call one from the Twisting Nether. A succubus can turn the frail against themselves, so binding one takes subtlety as well as strength. A succubus preys on mortal desire, so raw incantations alone cannot call one. The summoner must lure it with an object filled with pure love and devotion. Gan'rul cannot or will not provide such a relic, so he sends the warlock across the Cleft of Shadow to Cazul. The ancient warlock knows the arcane and demonic rites needed for the next part of the ritual.

quest:1508.text: Blind Cazul. In the Cleft of Shadow, Blind Cazul guides an initiate seeking to summon a succubus. He points toward an object charged with mortal emotion. A succubus answers to longing, sorrow, and desire. To draw one across the veil, a summoner needs more than willpower; the demon is known to devour souls. Blind Cazul understands what the initiate seeks. He knows where to find a fitting lure. Though blind, Blind Cazul senses the lives and sorrows within Orgrimmar’s red ramparts. He sends the initiate to Zankaja, an orc woman who lives atop the bluffs near the wind rider roost. She anxiously awaits her mate Dogran’s return. Her despair can draw a demon’s attention.

quest:1509.text: News of Dogran. Zankaja waits in Orgrimmar for word of Dogran, her mate, who has been gone for days. She sends you to ask Gazrog at the Crossroads. On the bluffs of Orgrimmar, Zankaja fears for Dogran, her mate. He went to the Crossroads after an honorable promotion, but his return is overdue and she has heard nothing for days. So she asks you to seek news from his commander, Gazrog.

quest:1510.text: News of Dogran. In Stonetalon, News of Dogran sends you into the foothills for a healing draught. The first runner never returned, and Ken'zigla at Malaka'jin may still have the medicine Dogran needs. Dogran lies badly wounded at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens. He was hurt fighting quilboar who had dug in, and the grunts who carried him back found his wounds festering. They feared the journey would harm him more before he could be treated. So Taurajo sent word north to the Crossroads for a healing draught made by the jungle trolls of Malaka'jin.

quest:1511.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. On the road to Camp Taurajo, Dogran's life depends on Ken'zigla's Draught. The troll apothecary prepared it in the Stonetalon Mountains for the missing operative. After the first courier failed to return, Ken'zigla prepared another dose. The troll apothecary had sent that emissary to find medicine for the missing scout Dogran. His draught is volatile and powerful. Half a dose gives a mortally wounded soldier strength to move without making the wounds bleed anew. The rest must wait until the next day, when it completes the recovery.

quest:1512.text: Love's Gift. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye waits for a pendant to draw a succubus. In the Barrens, Dogran gives up a treasured keepsake after he is found and revived. A warlock needs a talisman charged with strong, unblemished emotion to summon and control a succubus. These demons feed on mortal desire, twisting true affection into anguish. Dogran's pendant holds his devotion and the memory of their parting. Bring it to Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar's shadowy clefts, where he cleans and polishes it. Its bright emotional force can draw the soul-devourer across the Twisting Nether.

quest:1513.text: The Binding. At Neeru Fireblade's circle in Orgrimmar, you face the trial of binding a succubus. Dogran's Pendant draws the demon from the Twisting Nether, where you must overcome it by spellcraft and force of arms. Beneath the clefts of Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade keeps a tent with a circle prepared for dangerous rites. Under Gan'rul Bloodeye's guidance, you activate its runes and face the summoned succubus in battle. Calling a demon is only the beginning. You must overpower it alone and bend its spirit to your will.

quest:1515.text: Dogran's Captivity. At Camp Taurajo, a warlock faces a vital trial in Horde training: rescue a captured orc warrior. With Ken'zigla's Draught, you must find battered Grunt Dogran and give him strength to escape. Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo will not risk Horde soldiers in a costly attack on the entrenched quilboar. So Grunt Dogran's fate rests with you, an aspiring warlock armed only with Ken'zigla's Draught. Travel north through the brambles and hostile camps to find where the quilboar hold him captive.

quest:1519.text: Call of Earth. The earth calls a shaman to begin a patient trial of communion. By accepting an earthen sapta, the seeker steps onto a path of spiritual rebirth and learns to hear the foundation of life. A shaman learns to commune with the primal force of earth through a formative rite. Earth is the most stubborn and wise of the elements, the steady bedrock beneath existence. It moves through slow cycles of erosion and rebirth. Mountains wear into deserts, and rivers carve canyons over ages. To hear the earth's voice, an initiate needs that same patience. Answering the call changes a seeker beyond return to former ignorance. When the initiate proves readiness and respect for the laws of the Earth Mother, they receive an earthen sapta. The elixir opens a new way of seeing, and the shaman begins to grasp earth's secrets of strength, stamina, and elemental protection.

quest:1522.text: Call of Fire. A shaman sees your strength in earth and sends you north to Kranal Fiss. There, you can learn the ways of fire. Kranal Fiss lives north of the Crossroads. The shaman says he is easy to find, but warns you not to go too far, lest you reach the elves' lands.

quest:1529.text: Call of Water. In Thunder Bluff, your training turns toward water and a journey to the Barrens shore. You travel east to meet Islen Waterseer and begin the path toward the Water Totem. You have mastered earth and fire, and your trainers now judge you ready to study water. In Thunder Bluff, Xanis Flameweaver sees that you have the discipline to approach this cleansing element. So you leave Mulgore's mesas and cross the dry plains of the Barrens to the east. Islen Waterseer lives in a fishing shack on the Barrens' eastern coast, south of Ratchet and the mouth of the Southfury River. She keeps apart from the settlements beside the open ocean. Islen reads your readiness in the elements around you. Earth, wind, and fire already touch your spirit, and she prepares trials to teach you the purity of water.

quest:1530.text: Call of Water. Horde shamans journey south through the Barrens at Islen Waterseer's bidding, seeking Brine. There, they learn how water cleanses and heals. Islen Waterseer teaches that water brings rebirth. It carves rock, washes away impurities, and mends flesh, but only when it is pure. Polluted water brings blight instead of life. Before seeking communion with water, every shaman must understand this balance. You travel far south through the arid Barrens to find Brine. Quilboar raids trouble the wastes, yet Brine lives alone, without guards or fear. She holds the knowledge and trials that will help you bind yourself to water.

quest:1531.text: Call of Air. At Grommash Hold, Searn Firewarder sends seasoned shamans south for the Air Totem. Prate Cloudseer guides them through the final element of their craft. You have earned the favor of earth, fire, and water. Now you travel south from Orgrimmar across the Barrens, then down into the canyons of Thousand Needles to learn the last element: air. Troll trainer Searn Firewarder sends you when he sees you are ready for this final step in your early training. Prate Cloudseer waits in a high cave among the sandstone mesas of Thousand Needles. She lives quietly with her partner, far from Horde encampments, and expects you to show deference before she shares the secrets of the wind. Meet her with proper respect, and she teaches you the knowledge and focus to manifest the Air Totem. Then your circle of elemental craft is complete.

quest:1532.text: Call of Air. Xanis Flameweaver sends seasoned Horde shamans south from Thunder Bluff to seek Prate Cloudseer in Thousand Needles. There, they seek communion with the wind and the Air Totem, which channels its swift forces. You have attuned to earth, fire, and water. Now Xanis Flameweaver guides you from Thunder Bluff through a trial of humility, focus, and respect for the sky. Air is the final element, and its winds are fickle. They are harder to control than the elements you have already learned. Your path leads south, past the Barrens and into the canyons of Thousand Needles. Far to the east, Prate Cloudseer dwells in a secluded cave on the cliffs, where canyon drafts howl day and night. She tests your preparedness before giving you the Air Totem. It channels gusts, lightning, and swift wind spirits.

quest:1534.text: Call of Water. Brine sends a shaman north from the Barrens to gather water for Call of Water. This final essence comes from an ancient fountain in Ashenvale. After gathering water from the pool below Brine’s hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, you need one final essence. Brine sends you north across the dry plains and into Ashenvale, an ancient woodland sacred to the night elves. The Barrens give way to Ashenvale’s deep canopy, where water takes another form. To live in harmony with the element, a shaman must understand its many forms. Past the shimmering waters of Mystral Lake, near the mountain pass between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains, lie the Ruins of Stardust. An ancient fountain rests among quiet waters and old stones in this secluded elven sanctum. Untamed elemental and nature spirits guard the ruins and resent intruders. Tread carefully as you draw water from the fountain.

quest:1535.text: Call of Water. Brine sends shamans across the Barrens to gather water for a sapta. Below her hill, a guarded pool provides the first sample, and water means survival. Brine asks shaman initiates to study water in all its forms before she grants the water sapta. The sapta opens an initiate’s perception and lets them commune with the spirits. In the dry Barrens, water means survival. Forests flourish where it flows, while deserts starve without it. Living beings will kill to protect even the humblest spring. Quilboar fiercely guard the watering hole beneath Brine’s hill. They treat every pool as a priceless hoard and feast when rain comes. Brine regrets the violence their hoarding brings. Yet their greed and divided clans keep their threat contained, leaving the other races on the plains in a precarious balance.

quest:1536.text: Call of Water. You leave the Barrens for a pure spring in Forsaken-held Tarren Mill. Its water will help Brine prepare the Water Sapta, and its survival offers hope. Brine sends you across the sea to Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills. She needs water there to prepare the Water Sapta. Human resistance and the newly allied Forsaken surround the town, yet its small central well gives pure spring water. To Brine, it is a sacred remnant of cleanliness in an unhallowed land. For Brine, the pure well in Tarren Mill is more than an ingredient. She sees its endurance in Warchief Thrall, who bore hardship, captivity, and sorrow before rising to lead the orcish people. Thrall gives the Horde hope. The well shows that life and purity can endure through tragedy and corruption.

quest:154.text: Return the Comb. In Darkshire, Madame Eva waits for the comb Blind Mary has returned. Its ghostly strands can be spun into Ghost Hair Thread. Blind Mary waits in a shack south of Darkshire, grieving the death that changed her. Madame Eva’s comb recalls the grooming of her mortal life, and deepens her sorrow. She sees only a wraith, a monster stripped of mortal grace. Certain no one can love her again, she thrusts the comb and the ghostly hair tangled in its teeth back into your hands. Madame Eva awaits the comb in Darkshire, knowing the work was grim. With the ghostly hair, the fortune teller can spin a spool of Ghost Hair Thread. She pays you for any strands left after the delicate work.

quest:156.text: Gather Rot Blossoms. In Duskwood, Tavernkeep Smitts needs rot blossoms for his zombie juice. They grow inside the skulls of skeletal horrors and fiends in the graveyards. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Tavernkeep Smitts sometimes brews a strange drink. His zombie juice calls for rot blossoms, which root inside the empty skulls of animated skeletons. Smitts avoids the undead, so passing mercenaries gather the blossoms for him. Rot blossoms grow on skeletal horrors and fiends in the overgrown plots of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery and Raven Hill Cemetery. The Night Watch militia is stretched thin against the terrors creeping through the woods. Smitts commends those who hunt the dead to Commander Althea Ebonlocke, helping thin the restless ranks that threaten Darkshire.

quest:157.text: Deliver the Thread. In Darkshire, Madame Eva sends Ghost Hair Thread west through Duskwood to Abercrombie near Raven Hill Cemetery. The hermit says he needs it to guard his hut from restless spirits. Madame Eva gives you a spool of Ghost Hair Thread, spun from hair gathered from the ghost Blind Mary. You carry it west through Duskwood, where spiders and undead roam. Abercrombie waits in his ramshackle shack just north of Raven Hill Cemetery.

quest:158.text: Zombie Juice. Abercrombie sends travelers from his lonely shack in Duskwood to Darkshire for Zombie Juice. He says the night’s chill leaves him cold. Abercrombie lives alone among the horrors of Duskwood’s shadowed woods and often sends travelers on strange errands. He says the creeping dusk drains his warmth and vitality, then asks you to travel east to Darkshire. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Tavernkeep Smitts sells the potent drink Abercrombie seeks. Its ominous name is Zombie Juice, and Abercrombie says it will put fire back in his veins. Tavernkeep Smitts serves weary guards and frightened townsfolk at Darkshire’s tavern, but few ask for Zombie Juice. The drink is known for its dangerous strength, and Smitts recognizes the vintage. Abercrombie’s taste for such a morbid brew raises quiet eyebrows in a region besieged by the restless dead.

quest:159.text: Juice Delivery. In Darkshire, you carry Zombie Juice west to a hermit on Duskwood’s edge. Tavernkeep Smitts says the brew is stout enough to raise the dead. It is meant to warm Abercrombie, though its potency raises questions. Tavernkeep Smitts brews a legendary draught in Darkshire. When the Zombie Juice is ready, he hands you the bottle and warns you to handle it gently. He says the concoction is stout enough to raise the dead. You carry it across the haunted forest to an eccentric loner, in what seems a simple act of charity.

quest:160.text: Note to the Mayor. In western Duskwood, Abercrombie sends a message to Darkshire, where the mayor awaits an unexpected delivery. He calls himself an old friend of Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke, but the note raises questions. You return Abercrombie’s stolen chest from the ogres at Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, then carry his message down the misty roads to town. The hermit laughs with delight. He says he and Mayor Lord Ello Ebonlocke are old friends, and insists the mayor will be just as thrilled by what you have done.

quest:163.text: Raven Hill. In far western Duskwood, a light flickers in a ruined window at Raven Hill. Elaine Carevin sends travelers from Darkshire to learn what has taken shelter there. The Night Watch has long left Duskwood’s far west to the dead and the wilderness. Yet signs of life there demand attention. Calor, a watcher on the gloomy roads, saw movement among Raven Hill’s silent houses two nights in a row. A lantern flickered in a window. With ghouls, skeletons, and beasts across the land, the Night Watch cannot ignore what stirs among the ruins.

quest:164.text: Deliveries to Sven. In Darkshire, Elaine Carevin sends supplies to Sven Yorgen's camp in northwestern Duskwood. Sven and his few followers face the dangers of the blighted woods. Sven Yorgen and a few companions keep a camp on Duskwood's northwestern frontier. Wolves, spiders, and restless dead threaten Darkshire, yet Sven's band holds its ground beyond the town's walls. Danger keeps them from sparing anyone for the perilous journey back to town for provisions. Elaine Carevin arranges for travelers to carry supplies so the fighters can hold on. The Carevin family respects Sven and sees his stand as devotion to the Light. Elaine organizes supplies and sends them to his camp. When Sven receives the crate, he knows the Carevins are supporting him. His attention stays on the battle at hand.

quest:1642.text:
The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides the first steps of paladin training. Its teachings call champions of the Holy Light to humility, compassion, and patience, not godhood or strength alone. The Tome of Divinity’s sacred texts teach paladin initiates what it means to serve the Light. Divinity means neither seeking godhood nor claiming rule over others. Instead, champions reflect the Light’s grace through pure intent and goodness in every deed. Paladins take up arms against evil, but strength without moral purpose means little. Their true distinction lies in how they treat ordinary people across Azeroth, keeping power bound to righteousness and humility. Scripture is only the beginning of a paladin’s service. After an initiate studies the Tome of Divinity, Duthorian Rall in Stormwind tests whether its lessons have taken root in the candidate’s heart and mind. The Light asks for more than the slaying of beasts. It calls for patience, bravery, and understanding.

In the city and the surrounding lands, people suffer and humble tasks go without glory. By aiding the less fortunate and comforting those in despair, an initiate proves they have the sound mind and selfless spirit to bear the Light’s blessings responsibly.

quest:1643.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, initiates of the Light are sent to help someone in need. They seek a citizen of pure heart and noble motive, and find Stephanie Turner in the Trade District. Initiates of the Light begin this sacred trial by walking Stormwind’s streets. They seek someone of noble intent and pure motive who depends on the kindness of strangers. Before deeper instruction in holy duties, they learn that service to the vulnerable matters more than glorious combat. In Stormwind’s Trade District, Stephanie Turner makes clothing for children in the city’s orphanage with her husband. More tradesmen have come to the city, and competition for cloth and leather has made donations harder to find. Her husband has gone to Ironforge to seek support. Stephanie remains in Stormwind, carrying on their work.

quest:1644.text: The Tome of Divinity. Stephanie Turner in Stormwind needs help clothing children orphaned by the Scourge. Her husband John is gathering supplies as an aspiring paladin brings linen cloth to her home. Stephanie Turner cares for children whose families were lost to the Scourge in the northern lands over the last decade. Her husband John is away gathering supplies. So Stephanie must keep the children fed, warm, and sheltered while finding time to make them clothes. An aspiring paladin proves compassion by bringing linen cloth to Stephanie. With the cloth, she can sew shirts and pants for the children while tending to their food and shelter. Such humble aid shows how the Light's protectors guard the weak. Stephanie says this year has grown harsher. John must make long, difficult journeys as far as Ironforge to gather supplies. Even within Stormwind's high stone walls, the pain of recent tragedies in the north is still felt.

quest:1646.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge teaches young paladins what the Light asks of them. The Tome of Divinity says devotion calls for patience, compassion, and humble service to the needy, alongside martial strength. For a paladin, strength in battle must serve a higher purpose. Tiza Battleforge in Ironforge gives initiates the Tome of Divinity to teach them why they wield their arms. It turns their thoughts from dominion and godhood toward moral goodness. A paladin's calling is to serve as a steady instrument of the Light. The tome teaches that smiting evil is not enough to make a paladin. Compassion, patience, and humility set these warriors apart from common combatants. After studying its words, initiates undertake trials in Ironforge and nearby lands. Through charity and service, they show sound judgment and unwavering devotion.

quest:1647.text: The Tome of Divinity. At Ironforge's temple, an initiate seeks a lesson in the Light through service. Sent by a mentor into the outer ring, you search for someone with pure intent and a genuine need. There, John Turner shows how compassion and selfless work belong on the path of the Light. Initiates of the Light stationed in Ironforge face a trial of compassion. Their mentor sends them into the dwarven city to find someone truly in need of aid. The search calls for discernment: you must recognize a pure heart, noble intent, and a real need for kindness. Humble service lies at the heart of this calling. In Ironforge's outer ring, a humble worker named John Turner plies his trade. Startled by your approach, he calls out about the Orphanage of Stormwind, then tells you why he works so hard. Separated from his beloved wife by long hours of toil, Turner labors so orphaned children can have clothes and food. Help him, then return to the temple to continue your journey in the Light.

quest:1648.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, The Tome of Divinity calls servants of the Light to show compassion. John Turner seeks aid for the Stormwind orphanage he runs with his wife, caring for children left parentless by the Scourge. The trial asks an initiate to choose charity over martial glory. For an initiate walking the path of the Light, the trial in Ironforge calls for charity rather than arms. John Turner has come to the dwarven halls seeking help. He and his wife oversee an orphanage in Stormwind, where they care for children left without parents by the Scourge's rampages over the past decade. His journey to Ironforge speaks to the hardships shared by the Alliance's common folk. Provisions are hard to gather across borders. More tradesmen have come to work across Azeroth, and local supplies have grown scarce. John Turner has spent weeks in Ironforge appealing to civic groups and citizens, with little to show for it. His wife needs linen cloth to make clothes for the children. Giving it freely shows the selfless devotion at the heart of a servant of the Light.

quest:1649.text: The Tome of Valor. In Stormwind, The Tome of Valor calls paladins to prove their faith and courage. Duthorian Rall awaits those ready to petition the Church. The Tome teaches that valor is forged through hardship. Its sacred text likens virtues to precious ores, valuable when found but refined to endure. Through hard trials and true commitment, a paladin binds faith, compassion, and courage into strength against the evils threatening Azeroth. After reading the Tome, you are directed to Duthorian Rall, a respected paladin leader in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. He hears petitions from those seeking the trials of valor. The tests are no mere ritual. Defending the innocent and upholding the Church may cost your life, and only the steadfast earn recognition in the order.

quest:165.text: The Hermit. In Darkshire, Elaine Carevin asks you to check on Abercrombie, an elderly recluse who has stopped coming for provisions. His rickety shack stands at the edge of Raven Hill Cemetery. Elaine Carevin recalls an old man who once came to Darkshire for provisions, then stopped appearing. With danger on Duskwood’s roads, she asks you to visit his shack by Raven Hill Cemetery and find out whether he is safe. At the shack, you find Abercrombie alive. He chuckles at the Carevins’ concern and says age and the monsters in the woods have kept him from town. Glad to have an able traveler at his door, he quickly asks for help with a few errands.

quest:1650.text: The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall sends you to guard Daphne Stilwell on Westfall’s distant shore. Her husband is away, and Defias bandits threaten their homestead. At Stormwind’s Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall tests those who seek to become paladins. He asks them to defend the people of the realm. Now you have taken up the mantle of valor, and must put those ideals to work where law and authority have failed. Daphne Stilwell and her husband Jordan keep an outpost at Westfall’s isolated Longshore. Jordan is away in Ironforge, consulting dwarven blacksmiths, while Defias Brotherhood activity runs rampant. So Duthorian sends you west to protect Daphne before thieves overwhelm her homestead.

quest:1651.text: The Tome of Valor. At her Westfall farm, Daphne Stilwell calls for aid as the Defias Brotherhood closes in. A paladin must answer her plea. The Defias Brotherhood still contests the land around Daphne's homestead. Earlier clashes have not ended the danger, and another assault is expected. You are sent to hold the ground beside her house. There is no retreat. Your pursuit of the virtues in the Tome of Valor now faces a test of courage. Daphne has only her own firearm, while you can call on the blessings of the Holy Light. Wave after wave of Defias raiders attacks, and the fight tests whether you can protect someone vulnerable under crushing pressure. True valor means standing between innocent civilians and ruthless violence, even when danger bears down on you.

quest:1652.text: The Tome of Valor. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, you tell Duthorian Rall that Daphne Stilwell is safe after the defense of her Westfall homestead. Your courage fulfills the Church's trials of valor and its charge to shield the innocent without thought for yourself. Your defense shows you can stand between danger and the defenseless, as the Church expects of an aspiring paladin. The homestead holds firm, and Daphne is safe from the bandits who threatened her. Jordan Stilwell, Daphne's husband, remains in Ironforge, lending his renowned craftsmanship to the Alliance. Duthorian Rall prepares to send word north, so Jordan can focus on his work knowing his family is protected.

quest:1653.text: The Test of Righteousness. In Cathedral Square, Duthorian Rall sends you to Ironforge with news for Jordan Stilwell. His wife Daphne survived the Defias attack in Westfall. You guarded Daphne Stilwell at her Westfall homestead when Defias outlaws attacked, and she survived. Her husband had left for Ironforge, fearing his family was in danger. Now Rall sends you to tell Jordan in person, so he can learn what happened to Daphne. Jordan Stilwell once hoped to join the paladins, but chose his father's craft and became a master weaponsmith. He works at an anvil outside Ironforge's gates, holding fast to his faith as he shapes weapons. When you tell him Daphne survived, gratitude moves him to help you forge a blessed weapon of righteousness.

quest:1654.text: The Test of Righteousness. Jordan Stilwell has a sacred weapon in mind for a paladin worthy of the Light. The Ironforge smith needs rare materials from distant lands, including his lost family hammer. Outside Ironforge's gates, Jordan Stilwell cannot forge the paladin's weapon on his own. You gather the materials his craft demands. Jordan Stilwell needs four things for the weapon: Whitestone Oak lumber, refined ore from master prospectors, a purified Kor Gem, and his smithing hammer. He left the hammer behind while escaping Shadowfang Keep. Finding all four means facing dangers across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond.

quest:1655.text: Bailor's Ore Shipment. In Loch Modan, Bailor's Ore Shipment is bound for Jordan Stilwell's sanctified weapon. Mo'grosh ogres plundered the alloy on the road from the Wetlands. Jordan Stilwell awaits ore refined by his old friend Bailor Stonehand, but the shipment never reaches Ironforge. As the caravan travels south from the Wetlands into Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres ambush it and slaughter its guards. One wounded guard reaches a camp, then dies soon after. The shipment is left in ogre territory. Bailor Stonehand camps in Loch Modan and sends paladins across the Loch toward the northeastern hills. The stolen crate of alloy lies abandoned among the Mo'grosh camps. Recovering it means entering hostile territory, and will let Bailor keep his agreement with Jordan Stilwell.

quest:1656.text: A Task Unfinished. On Red Cloud Mesa, a young tauren cannot finish a family chore alone. Their coming-of-age trials and their father's request leave them too exhausted to carry furs to Innkeeper Kauth in Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren on Red Cloud Mesa face rites that prove they are ready for the wider world. The trials demand strength, while tribal chores still need doing. One youth must finish the Rite of Strength and answer an urgent request from their father. Too tired to carry a bundle of furs down the mesa, they ask you for help. Bloodhoof Village lies in the open plains below, where Innkeeper Kauth receives the furs. He intends to make them into warm blankets for weary wanderers. The plains tauren welcome travelers, and their support helps those facing solitary trials of strength.

quest:166.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood still keeps the farmlands in fear. Gryan Stoutmantle has found its stronghold beneath Moonbrook and calls for a final blow against its leader. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia have fought the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall for months. Now its stronghold lies exposed beneath Moonbrook. Stoutmantle orders Edwin VanCleef killed, believing his death will end the rebellion at last.

quest:167.text: Oh Brother. . .. In Stormwind, Wilder Thistlenettle waits after escaping a cave-in beneath Moonbrook. His brother, Foreman Thistlenettle, and the rest of the crew remain behind the rubble, and Wilder asks you to find his brother or recover the dwarf's Explorers' League Badge. Wilder Thistlenettle and his brother worked for a mining company in the tunnels beneath Moonbrook. Then thieves swarmed the mines, and a cave-in sealed the lower passages. Wilder escaped to Stormwind. His brother and the rest of the crew remained trapped behind the rubble.

quest:1678.text: Vejrek. In the foothills south of Frostmane Hold, you face Vejrek to prove your mettle. Muren Stormpike wants proof you can handle real foes. Your success begins a lesson in strong defense. Muren Stormpike says you need toughness before he can teach you new moves. Vejrek is the toughest troll in these parts, and his hut lies in the foothills south of Frostmane Hold. Muren asks you to bring back Vejrek’s head as proof you can handle real foes.

quest:1680.text: Tormus Deepforge. In Ironforge, Tormus Deepforge waits for fighters sent by Muren Stormpike. Before he forges a weapon for them, he asks them to face a perilous trial. Tormus Deepforge is a master dwarven weaponsmith in Ironforge. Warriors who show their growing skill to Muren Stormpike are sent across the city to consult him. Tormus is known for sturdy, potent arms, but he does not give fine blades or bludgeons to every passerby. A warrior must earn his work through action. Before Tormus agrees to forge a weapon, he asks the adventurer to promise him a favor. He speaks plainly about the danger ahead and warns that it could cost a life. To him, peril is no reason to turn back. It is the proper test of a warrior's mettle.

quest:169.text: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg. In Redridge, Magistrate Solomon offers a bounty for Gath'Ilzogg, the warlord behind Blackrock's invasion of Stonewatch. Anyone who storms the conquered keep and brings back the commander's severed head may claim it. Gath'Ilzogg leads Blackrock raids across the Redridge Mountains. His orcs seized Stonewatch Keep, once a human bastion, and turned it into a stronghold for attacks on nearby settlements. From its highest ramparts, he plans further strikes against Lakeshire. Redridge may be cut off from the rest of the kingdom. Stormwind's royal army has sent no reinforcements to the border, so Magistrate Solomon acts on his own. Lakeshire lacks the soldiers to retake Stonewatch Keep by force. Solomon offers a public bounty on Gath'Ilzogg, hoping to break Blackrock's leadership and begin reclaiming the keep for the crown.

quest:1698.text: Yorus Barleybrew. At the Lakeshire Inn, Yorus Barleybrew awaits bold Alliance warriors with an eccentric challenge. Trainers across Alliance capitals send seasoned fighters from Stormwind toward the Redridge borderlands to meet the dwarf and face his test of arms. Across Alliance capitals, warrior trainers watch fighters outgrow their first drills. When an apprentice proves their mettle around their twentieth season, Kelv Sternhammer, Wu Shen, and Darnath Bladesinger pass along word of Yorus Barleybrew. The dwarf offers no standard military order. Instead, he has issued an open wager and a test of arms to any Alliance warrior bold enough to answer. Yorus Barleybrew waits at the tavern in Lakeshire, on the front lines of Redridge's struggle against encroaching gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Those who find him meet a boastful dwarf with a hearty drink in hand, ready to judge any challenger who claims true fighting spirit. For warriors seeking to prove themselves beyond the capital's safe cobbled streets, his trial opens onto the harsher battles of the frontier.

quest:1699.text: The Rethban Gauntlet. In Lakeshire, Yorus Barleybrew sends runners north toward Rethban Caverns and back. They drink his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder, then race to return within an hour. Lakeshire's inn is full of grim talk about gnoll raids and missing town guards. Yorus Barleybrew offers travelers another diversion: a test of speed, courage, and endurance. Before they set out on foot for the northern foothills, they drink a draught of his family's Barleybrew Scalder. Redridge gnolls roam the hills between Lakeshire and Rethban Caverns. Runners must fight through their packs or slip past, reach the first fork in the dark tunnels, then hurry back to Yorus within an hour. The fiery drink makes the run harder, and challengers stagger through the hills.

quest:1700.text: Grimand Elmore. In Stormwind City, Grimand Elmore receives Furen Longbeard's technical notes. Their brief exchange carries intricate findings between two headstrong weaponsmiths who share the city. Furen Longbeard forged the specialized Fire Hardened Mail and uncovered intricate heat-treating techniques and elemental principles. He records his findings on parchment, then asks you to deliver them straight to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned crafter at a nearby weapon shop. Grimand Elmore bristles at the manuscript. He insists he taught Furen everything the younger dwarf knows, and the thought that his former pupil could teach him wounds his pride. Yet Grimand cannot resist reading the notes. Soon he finds an intriguing idea and is eager to test it himself.

quest:1701.text: Fire Hardened Mail. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard offers an Alliance warrior a new design for Fire Hardened Mail. He will forge it if you bring rare materials from both continents. Furen Longbeard has forged an exceptional buckler for you. Now the dwarf armorer proposes a greater work: mail made to withstand fierce blows. His craft calls for more than iron or steel. He needs rare materials touched by elemental heat and natural resilience. Furen cannot leave his Stormwind forge, so you must gather these dangerous ingredients. Furen sends you to distant wilds and dangerous depths for the materials. The recipe calls for fangs from venomous spiders in the Wetlands' damp crevices. It also needs scorched and galvanized horns from fierce chimaeras in the Stonetalon Mountains. To bind and temper these beast parts into mail, Furen needs volatile phlogiston from Roogug, a geomancer deep within Razorfen Kraul's thorny maze in the Barrens.

quest:1702.text: The Shieldsmith. In Stormwind, Yorus Barleybrew sends warriors to claim the shield he promised. A hard trial in the Redridge Mountains is behind them, and a cask of Barleybrew Scalder is bound for Furen Longbeard, the smith who will shape their shield. You have faced the gnolls and dangers of the Rethban Gauntlet, and Yorus Barleybrew keeps his bargain. Lakeshire cannot provide the promised shield, so he sends proven fighters back to Stormwind City. There, a dwarven armorer is ready to repay a personal debt. Yorus gives you a heavy cask of Barleybrew Scalder in place of a letter of credit. Carry it to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District. The seasoned smith knows whose name stands behind the cask and lends his skill to a warrior who seeks a stout shield.

quest:1703.text: Mathiel. Across the sea, Furen Longbeard sends his crafting notes to Mathiel in Darnassus. On the Warrior's Terrace, the night elf smith may carry dwarven mail forging to another pair of hands. Furen Longbeard has mastered the forging of fire-hardened armor. Now he shares what he knows with other Alliance craftsmen. He copies his diagrams and sends you across the continents to Mathiel, a smith on Teldrassil. At Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace, Mathiel tends a forge for the Sentinels and others who defend the night elf capital. Furen's notes bring dwarven methods from the underground forges of Khaz Modan to kaldorei armorers. Their craft is shaped by their bond with nature.

quest:1704.text: Klockmort Spannerspan. In Tinkertown, Furen Longbeard's fire-hardened mail findings reach Klockmort Spannerspan. The dwarf smith trusts his gnomish colleague to discover what the new techniques can do. You carry Furen's notes from Stormwind to Ironforge, then on to Tinkertown. There, Klockmort Spannerspan works as a blacksmith and can test the discoveries in his own craft. Gnomish blacksmiths are rare among their dwarven hosts. Klockmort is eager to move beyond traditional metalwork, and the notes excite him with the promise of a breakthrough. He is ready to try the fiery techniques in his own unusual projects.

quest:1705.text:
Burning Blood. In Stormwind, Grimand Elmore puts Furen Longbeard’s smithing methods to the test. To try them at his own forge, he needs burning blood and a burning rock from Duskwood. Grimand Elmore is one of the Alliance’s finest armorers. He seldom believes another smith can surpass his methods. Yet Furen Longbeard’s unusual discoveries have stirred his professional curiosity, and Grimand agrees to make a piece of armor using them.

For the work, he needs strange, volatile materials from the dark reaches of the south. They will quench and temper the metal to his exact requirements. Ordinary water and common coals will not do. Grimand sends you to Roland’s Doom, an abandoned mine in Duskwood. Savage Nightbane worgen have overrun its tunnels, and burning ichor pulses in their cursed veins.

He needs vials of their burning blood and a rare flaming core called a burning rock. Gutspill, leader of the pack, carries it. Bring both scorching materials back so Grimand can test Furen’s methods at the forge.

quest:1706.text: Grimand's Armor. Grimand Elmore now offers you a coif made from rare materials. It tests Furen Longbeard's smithing methods and is built to endure crushing blows, a hard-won step in your training as an Alliance warrior. The coif shows that Furen Longbeard's daring methods can strengthen armor against crushing impacts. Grimand Elmore forged it from rare elemental and beast components you gathered in hostile territory, putting the dwarven master armorer's theories to the test. Grimand Elmore treats the metal to bear pressure and blows that would warp ordinary steel. Then he gives you the finished coif. Its strength honors Furen Longbeard's craft and your resolve, and may help you hold the frontline against Azeroth's greatest threats.

quest:1708.text: Iron Coral. In Tinker Town, Klockmort Spannerspan seeks searing coral for a new suit of armor. The gnome blacksmith hopes to test new smithing methods with this rare sea material on the Wetlands coast. Klockmort Spannerspan has shared discoveries with Furen Longbeard, a master dwarven smith. Now he hopes to unite Furen's skill in metallurgy with his own tinkering. Mountain ore alone will not give him the resilient armor he seeks. So he needs searing coral, a material hardened by the sea. Searing coral grows underwater off the Wetlands coast, south of Menethil Harbor. You need to bring back twenty clusters while aquatic predators prowl below. Then carry the harvest to Ironforge. Klockmort plans to smelt and hammer the coral into experimental armor plating.

quest:1709.text: Klockmort's Creation. In Tinker Town, Klockmort Spannerspan puts Furen Longbeard's forging method to work on rare materials. The result is armor made to endure. Using Furen Longbeard's methods, Klockmort finishes a pair of armored gauntlets in Tinker Town. Dwarven metalworking and gnomish mechanical skill come together in gauntlets built to endure punishment that would crush ordinary steel. Klockmort says a siege engine could run over the armor without leaving lasting distortion. Peculiarly treated rare components give it resilience. Dwarven forging and gnomish ingenuity join in armor built to withstand the fiercest frontline battles.

quest:1710.text: Sunscorched Shells. In Darnassus, Mathiel seeks wyvern eggshells to strengthen a new way of crafting mail. He works with Furen Longbeard, a dwarven smith, and sends warriors to gather shells from Highperch in Thousand Needles. From the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Mathiel looks beyond night elven methods. He corresponds with Furen Longbeard, a skilled dwarven armorer in Stormwind, and studies his discoveries in metalwork and armor-smithing. Mathiel hopes to reinforce mail with natural materials that can withstand great strain. To test his idea, he needs materials found nowhere near Teldrassil. Mathiel's experiment calls for shells from Highperch, far south across the sea in Thousand Needles' canyon gorges. Wyverns nest high above the salt flats and red stone mesas beneath Kalimdor's blazing sun. Heat and altitude harden their eggshells. Mathiel plans to grind the sun-baked fragments into a resilient lacquer and coat chainmail links, so the armor bends while enduring exceptional strain.

quest:1711.text: Mathiel's Armor. At the Darnassus forge, Mathiel's Armor joins night elf and dwarven craft. In the Warrior's Terrace, Mathiel uses methods devised by Furen Longbeard to shape exotic materials into armor for Alliance warriors. For millennia, night elf armorers have shaped their work around nature, supple leathers, and carefully worked metals. Trade with the Eastern Kingdoms has led smiths such as Mathiel to try new ways. He joins elven craft with the dwarven techniques devised by Furen Longbeard. Mathiel needs sunscorched eggshells from the Highperch wyvern nests in Thousand Needles. He renders the sun-hardened shells into lacquer, then uses Furen's heat-treatment formulas to forge resilient leggings for the front lines.

quest:1712.text: Cyclonian. At the summoning site, Cyclonian waits for a champion bold enough to face him. A special parchment names the rare materials needed to call forth the wind lord, whose whirlwind heart can strengthen a formidable weapon. A watcher has kept vigil at the summoning site for ages. The raging elemental wind lord awaits a combatant with the raw martial prowess to challenge and destroy him. A special parchment names the rare materials needed to summon Cyclonian. Once the wind lord is called forth, you face him in direct combat. You may defeat him, or fall to his howling gale.

quest:1713.text: The Summoning. At Bath'rah Windwatcher's camp, a warrior faces a trial against Cyclonian, the wind lord. Slay the elemental and claim the Whirlwind Heart, whose storm force can be bound into a weapon. Bath'rah Windwatcher has prepared an ancient ritual to summon Cyclonian into the mortal realm. The fearsome elemental is known as the wind lord. There will be no bargain with the tempest. An able champion must strike it down as soon as it takes form. Cyclonian's Whirlwind Heart sustains his physical form. When the wind lord falls, Bath'rah wrenches the heart free and harnesses the gale within. Its volatile power can imbue a weapon with the force of the storm.

quest:1714.text: Essence of the Exile. At the cauldron, Essence of the Exile draws travelers with its beckoning vapors. Charms set off a violent reaction that reveals molten rock. A bubbling cauldron sends out vapors that draw travelers to its churning depths. Specific enchanted charms stir an intense reaction within the vessel. The charms sink slowly through the liquid. Then a large bubble rises and bursts, revealing a churning lump of molten rock forged from the combined materials.

quest:1716.text: Devourer of Souls. In Stormwind, Gakin sends warlocks across the sea for counsel on summoning a succubus. Takar the Seer holds the wisdom they need. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder guides promising warlocks toward summoning a succubus. The demon devours souls, destroys hearts, and dominates minds, so no warlock should call one blindly into Azeroth. A potent lure is needed: an object tied to pure love. That token draws the succubus from the Twisting Nether, where the warlock can defeat and bind it. Stormwind’s covens cannot teach where to find such an object. Gakin sends his pupils across the Great Sea to Kalimdor for the needed catalyst. Takar the Seer waits in the arid Barrens, near the Horde settlement of Camp Taurajo. An Alliance warlock must cross wilderness patrolled by hostile centaur, quilboar, and Horde warriors to reach him. The journey tests whether a summoner can survive before the ritual begins.

quest:1717.text: Gakin's Summons. From Ironforge, Gakin's Summons sends promising Alliance warlocks south to Stormwind. Beneath the Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder awaits to oversee their progress in commanding greater fiends. Demonology stays hidden across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly watches wandering practitioners for the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock masters their first minions, word travels quickly. Lago sends word to leave the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder coordinates the city's warlocks. He sees every capable student as a valuable but hazardous investment. His summons marks the threshold of true demonic binding. Now begin the trials to subjugate a succubus from the Twisting Nether.

quest:1718.text: The Islander. On Fray Island, warriors from across Azeroth face a trial among their peers. Their trainers send proven fighters there for the next step in their training. The island lies off the Merchant Coast, where chief warrior Klannoc Macleod awaits them. Warrior trainers in Alliance and Horde capitals send students who have outgrown basic drills to test themselves against their peers. Combat shows a fighter's progress, not rank or loyalty. So the journey leads beyond civilized sparring yards to a rugged isle in the Great Sea. Fray Island lies east of the Merchant Coast, just south of Ratchet in the Barrens. You can swim there across waters that pass over submerged sandbar shallows. Political ties matter little on the island. Fighters gather before Klannoc Macleod, its chief warrior, and await the trial he chooses.

quest:1719.text: The Affray. On Fray Island, warriors face challengers before Klannoc Macleod will train them. The Affray tests their strength against the island’s fighters and its champion. Fray Island lies apart from the mainland and draws brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not train every wanderer who arrives by boat. Warriors seeking his lessons must enter the Affray first. There, their stamina and awareness in battle show whether they can fight beyond mere boasting. A warrior begins the Affray by stepping onto the central iron grate among the spectators. Then Ringmaster Twiggy Flathead sends challengers into the ring one after another. Those who survive face the island’s heavyweight champion, Big Will. Only by defeating him can a warrior earn Klannoc’s respect.

quest:173.text:
Worgen in the Woods. In Darkshire, Calor sends hunters against Nightbane Shadow Weavers in Duskwood. The disillusioned former guardsman is stationed in town, and the hunt runs through Brightwood Grove and the Rotting Orchard. Those who face the worgen prove their mettle to Master Jonathan Carevin's monster hunters. The Night Watch struggles against undead, spiders, and outlaws along Darkshire's borders. Calor grew weary of guards too slow and complacent to cleanse the land. He left the Watch and joined Master Jonathan Carevin, turning his blade against heresy and corruption.

Carevin admits no one lightly to his circle. Those who want to aid him must first show they can survive the woods' fiercest horrors. Feral worgen rule Brightwood Grove and the blighted Rotting Orchard. Among them, Nightbane Shadow Weavers use dark magic to blind and ensnare their victims before tearing them apart. Calor sends aspiring hunters to slay these spell-weaving beasts. Their courage is tested as the threat is thinned, though its origins deeply unsettle Darkshire's defenders.

quest:1738.text: Heartswood. In the years since the Third War, warlocks seek Heartswood for an old night elf tragedy. Takar the Seer sends them into Ashenvale for Gakin the Darkbinder, who needs the wood to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. Takar the Seer says Heartswood grew where the night elf lovers Anathera and Latherion fell during the War of the Ancients, ten thousand years ago. Their last breaths and devotion nourished the tree. To mortals, it marks a tragic love. To practitioners of the dark arts, its concentrated emotion is potent magical fuel. Succubi feed on mortal passion, desire, and torment. Takar knows ordinary temptations cannot match an artifact filled with thousands of years of devotion. A piece of Heartswood gives Gakin the Darkbinder the catalyst he needs to draw a cunning demon through the Nether and into a summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

quest:1739.text: The Binding. In Stormwind, warlocks seek to bind a succubus to their will. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb, an initiate uses an enchanted Heartswood core to summon the demon and defeat it in combat. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, a crypt shelters the city's warlocks. They practice forbidden arts there, away from the city watch and the Cathedral of Light. Stone summoning circles channel the Nether's power and let initiates reach across the veil between worlds. A warlock needs a prepared Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. The ritual opens a breach at the summoning circle, but the demon can corrupt and overwhelm even a fortified mind. To master it, the warlock must defeat it in single combat. Its physical form returns to the Twisting Nether, while its true tether is secured.

quest:174.text: Look To The Stars. In Duskwood, Viktori Prism'Antras looks to the skies for answers to the forest's curse. He trusts observation over arcane superstition and asks you to gather parts for a telescope designed by his gnomish associate. Many in fearful Darkshire blame Duskwood's troubles on black magic, curses, and restless dead. Viktori Prism'Antras doubts these alone explain the land's corruption. He believes answers may lie above the canopy. With blueprints from his gnomish partner, Cog, he plans to build an instrument for studying the heavens. Viktori needs a sturdy frame to begin building his instrument for stargazing. Cog's plans call for a machined bronze tube, and Viktori asks you to find one. He trusts practical engineering and careful observation to shed light where mysticism has failed.

quest:1740.text:
The Orb of Soran'ruk. In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan gathers warlocks around the broken Orb of Soran'ruk. They seek to restore the scattered pieces and the essence bound within. When lesser demons lose favor with the Burning Legion, their sentence is eternal. Their spirits are bound in crystal orbs and given to mortal conjurers and warlocks as vessels of power under demonic control. Shattering an orb does not free its captive. Even the shards keep potent magic. Pieces of Soran'ruk lie across two continents. Twilight's Hammer cultists hold smaller fragments in the damp caverns of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale. A sorcerer in the haunted ruins of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest claimed the larger, mostly intact half.

Doan Karhan has spent his life studying Legion orbs and assembled the Orb of Zargain before. With the recovered pieces, he can restore Soran'ruk as a working implement.

quest:175.text: Look To The Stars. Viktori Prism'Antras needs a mirror for the telescope he is building in Darkshire from Cog's blueprints. He sends you south to find Mary, known for carrying a looking glass. Viktori Prism'Antras has the bronze tube for his telescope. Cog's blueprints call for a mirror to guide and reflect light through it. Fine silvered glass is hard to make while Darkshire faces shortages. So Viktori recalls Mary, a local woman known across the region for carrying a looking glass. Mary's old home lies deep in southern Duskwood, just north of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. To reach it, you pass beyond the Night Watch's safe patrols. Blighted groves lie ahead, where ravenous wolves, feral spiders, and wandering undead roam.

quest:1758.text: Tome of the Cabal. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan sends an Alliance warlock to Ironforge. There, the Tome of the Cabal may hold what an unprepared summoner needs to bind a felhunter. An imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus may be subdued by ritual. A felhunter is another matter. It serves the Burning Legion and hunts arcane energy to devour. A common summoning circle crumbles before it can hold the demon. The felhunter drains its summoner’s magic before any binding takes hold. From his redoubt in the Barrens, Strahad Farsan watches over Ratchet. He knows no amateur should attempt the binding unprepared. An acolyte needs the Tome of the Cabal’s arcane formulas to summon and bind a felhunter safely. The manuscript was written by the first mortal cabal of warlocks to break one without outside aid. Its pages explain the geomancy, materials, and binding runes needed to withstand the creature’s hunger. The copy was lost long ago. Strahad and his circle no longer have the masterwork. Strahad cannot provide the text, so he sends Alliance warlocks across the Great Sea to the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Krom Stoutarm, an itinerant dwarven warlock, resides there. In his twilight years, he combs through ancient manuscripts and library records. If any trace of the lost grimoire remains recorded in the Eastern Kingdoms, it lies in Krom’s meticulous catalogs.

quest:177.text: Look To The Stars. In Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras needs Blind Mary's looking glass for his telescope. An Insane Ghoul carried it to Tranquil Gardens Cemetery in southern Duskwood. Blind Mary once treasured an ornate looking glass. An incident took her sight and sanity and left her a weeping spirit. In despair, she threw the glass into the dirt behind her family barn. Now Viktori Prism'Antras, an astronomer in Darkshire, needs the mirror for his telescope. The looking glass was taken long before he began studying the heavens. An Insane Ghoul scavenged the looking glass from behind the ruined farmsteads. Restless hunger drove it south, carrying the mirror to Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. It haunts an abandoned chapel among overgrown tombstones. You face the flesh-eating horrors of the southern woods to reclaim Mary's lost treasure from its rotting claws.

quest:1778.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge teaches initiates what service to the Holy Light demands. They aid someone in need, then return to tell her how they served. Paladins begin their trials by learning humility, duty, and charity. Tiza Battleforge does not ask for feats of arms. A servant of the Holy Light must understand the troubles ordinary people face and offer help without seeking praise or gain. After helping someone in Ironforge, an aspiring paladin returns to Tiza Battleforge. The initiate tells her how they spent their time away and whose burdens they helped bear. When she is satisfied that they acted with charity and duty, Tiza commends them. Such selfless service is what it means to follow the Light.

quest:1779.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, The Tome of Divinity tests paladin initiates in holy power and martial devotion. Entrusted with the Symbol of Life, an initiate is sent to aid Muiredon Battleforge, wounded after a deadly encounter with Dark Iron dwarves. In Ironforge, paladin initiates face a trial of martial skill and holy power. They have already shown humility, patience, and charity. Now they are entrusted with the Symbol of Life and sent into the city to help those suffering from conflicts beyond its gates. Muiredon Battleforge lies badly wounded after a clash with Dark Iron dwarves. A priest tends his immediate injuries as he prepares to tell what became of his expedition and his companion Narm. The initiate must answer that need with the Light’s gift of renewal.

quest:178.text: Theocritus' Retrieval. In Redridge, a strange voice reaches across the mountains through a Shadowhide Pendant. The speaker is Theocritus, High Mage of Tower of Azora, who has intercepted the gnolls' mystical network and urgently asks for the pendant to study. Travelers who fight the savage Shadowhide gnolls in the Redridge Mountains sometimes find a Shadowhide Pendant. Touch the enchanted trinket, and a calm, distant voice answers instead of barking or curses. The speaker is Theocritus, a human mage at Tower of Azora, across the border in Elwynn Forest. His message comes from long study of ways to break the dark sorceries that direct the gnoll packs.

quest:1780.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall guides paladins through a trial of devotion to the Holy Light. They prove their worth through charity, selflessness, and a duty to protect those in need. Paladins in the service of the Holy Light face a defining trial in Stormwind City. At the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall sends initiates to prove their devotion through moral conduct and selfless deeds for the kingdom's citizens. Martial glory alone will not suffice. After aiding the vulnerable, initiates return to Duthorian Rall. They have brought needed relief to children and earned their heartfelt gratitude. Their mentor sees the value in putting others first. He teaches that charity, compassion, and duty to the people of Azeroth mark the path of the Light.

quest:1781.text: The Tome of Divinity. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, a trial awaits paladin initiates: they must focus the holy Symbol of Life. Those who prove their virtue are sent to aid Gazin Tenorm, who barely escaped a Defias ambush near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, patient and charitable paladin initiates receive the Symbol of Life. Duthorian Rall entrusts them with this holy vessel to test their devotion to the Light. Only a worthy champion can focus one of the Light's greatest gifts, the power to restore life to the fallen. Gazin Tenorm shows why the Symbol is needed. He crawled back to Stormwind after Defias bandits attacked him near Heroes' Vigil in Elwynn Forest. Priests tend his severe wounds at the cathedral altar. His companion Henze remains in danger where the outlaws struck.

quest:1782.text: Furen's Armor. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard puts new armor to the test. An aspiring warrior gathers spider fangs, chimaera horns, and phlogiston for his trials. Furen then gives the fire-hardened mail to the warrior and promises to share what he learned with Alliance smiths. Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorer in Stormwind, seeks stronger armor for the Alliance. He tests how well it withstands heat and crushing blows. For these trials, he asks an aspiring warrior to gather rare materials. The resulting mail succeeds, strengthening Furen's standing among Alliance armorers. Furen gives the finished fire-hardened mail to the warrior who gathered the materials. He is grateful for the help, and the experiments have deepened his knowledge of protective smithing. Now he plans to send his notes and findings to other Alliance smiths, so they can use the new methods.

quest:1783.text: The Tome of Divinity. A paladin initiate carries the Symbol of Life to the frigid shores south of Helm's Bed Lake in Dun Morogh. There, the initiate must find Narm Faulk, a brave scout who fell holding off Dark Iron dwarves, and call him back with the Light. South of Helm's Bed Lake, dwarven scouts Muiredon and Narm Faulk watched Dark Iron dwarves entrench themselves. When they saw an enemy commander issuing orders, they struck at several foes and tried to secure a script. The Dark Irons overwhelmed them with unexpected ferocity. Muiredon fled for reinforcements while Narm held the line.

quest:1784.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Dun Morogh, injured scouts need help exposing Dark Iron spies near Helm's Bed Lake. Their orders may persuade Ironforge's skeptical council to heed the danger. Young dwarven paladins answer the call to defend Dun Morogh when an expedition near Helm's Bed Lake goes wrong. Narm Faulk and Muiredon Battleforge set out to ambush Dark Iron scouts. Narm fell wounded, while Muiredon returned to Ironforge to recover. Rumors of Dark Iron infiltrators have reached Ironforge, yet some council members refuse to believe they have entered Dun Morogh. Near Helm's Bed, the paladin can track down the spies and recover a Dark Iron Script from their captain. The orders offer proof of enemy movements and plots near the capital's gates.

quest:1785.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Ironforge, holy champions face a final trial before Tiza Battleforge. The Tome of Divinity shows whether they are ready to wield the Symbol of Life and call fallen allies back to life. You have crossed the kingdom's trials, and now you come to Tiza Battleforge in Ironforge. She is a revered teacher of the holy arts. Her husband watches with pride as you approach, eager to see the dwarven people acknowledge your readiness before the Holy Light. Tiza Battleforge's final blessing tests whether your heart is ready to wield the Symbol of Life. The relic answers only to one prepared to channel the Light's greatest gifts. Prove your worth, and Tiza grants you a sacred scroll that lets you call fallen comrades back from death. Ironforge needs this power against the Scourge and the Dark Iron clan.

quest:1786.text:
The Tome of Divinity. In Elwynn, faith and sacrifice are tested when a Defias ambush leaves Henze Faulk dead at Heroes' Vigil. With the Symbol of Life, you are sent to restore him and hinder the brotherhood's schemes. Henze Faulk and Gazin traveled to Heroes' Vigil after hearing that Defias Brotherhood agents had crossed into northeastern Elwynn Forest. The island lies in the middle of Stone Cairn Lake. The scouts sought proof to present to the king's royal advisors, so they tried to ambush two conspirators reviewing plans.

Defias spellcasters soon joined the fight, and the scouts were overwhelmed. Henze stood his ground against the mages, sacrificing himself to give Gazin time to escape with his life.

quest:1787.text: The Tome of Divinity. You are proving your devotion to the Light through a trial for Alliance paladins. After helping an injured scout in Elwynn Forest, you face Defias Rogue Wizards and seek papers that threaten the realm. As a paladin in training, you are being tested in Elwynn Forest. Henze was injured while watching illicit activity on an island. Help him learn how far the Defias have spread there.

quest:1788.text: The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, paladins face a trial of faith in The Tome of Divinity. An initiate proves mastery of the Symbol of Life by restoring a fallen ally, then earns Duthorian Rall's blessing to wield resurrection. After restoring the fallen Henze with the Symbol of Life in the field, an aspiring paladin returns to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind. The Defias papers recovered from the island are to go to the King's advisors through Gazin Tenorm. First, Duthorian Rall awaits word of the initiate's success. Calling on the Light to restore the dead is no small gift. Duthorian Rall sees mastery of the Symbol of Life as proof that an initiate has the faith and spiritual strength for one of the paladin order's highest callings: resurrection. With this rite mastered, the paladin can safeguard allies on battlefields across the kingdom.

quest:1791.text: The Windwatcher. Northward, warriors who master the berserker stance seek The Windwatcher. After the affray on Fray Island, klannoc macleod sends them to find a weapon worthy of their fury. You survived the affray on Fray Island and learned the berserker stance from klannoc macleod. Now he sends you across continents, far from the Barrens coast, to find a solitary craftsman who can forge an exceptional weapon. Bath'rah the Windwatcher lives beside the river that runs north past Tarren Mill. His camp lies among stone ruins in contested land between the Alterac Mountains and the blighted Western Plaguelands. The troll hermit crafts weapons and commands potent elemental shamanism. He waits for warriors set on forging a weapon of great power.

quest:1792.text: Whirlwind Weapon. A warrior's chosen weapon awaits the storm Cyclonian left behind. The whirlwind heart can bind the elemental's fury into a forged vessel. After Cyclonian falls and the warrior claims its heart, a craftsperson prepares a weapon to hold the storm's power. The heart is fused into the chosen arm, turning forged metal into a channel for elemental fury. Cyclonian's heart holds the violence of howling winds and tempestuous gales. Bound into a forged weapon, it lends the wielder the living might of the storm alongside their own martial skill. Each strike carries the force of the defeated elemental, whose storm now rages in the hands of its vanquisher.

quest:1793.text: The Tome of Valor. In Stormwind and Ironforge, young Alliance paladins face a trial of courage and duty. Their mentors ask them to prove they can fight with skill and protect the innocent. Young paladins in Stormwind and Ironforge must face terrible danger without faltering. Their instructors test their resolve in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries. Dragons and demons may threaten those who cannot defend themselves. The paladins must stay beside them. A holy warrior needs bravery as much as a weapon and shield. The trial teaches paladins that strength means little without a firm vow to shelter the helpless. When danger threatens the Alliance, its defenders must hold their ground and protect those in their care.

quest:1795.text: The Binding. Above Ratchet, warlocks face the rite that binds a felhunter to their will. Strahad Farsan uses the restored Tome of the Cabal to draw an aggressive demon from the Nether, then watches the warlock subdue it in combat. On Kalimdor’s bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port, Strahad Farsan leads dangerous trials in demon summoning. A warlock first gathers the fragments and reagents needed to restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal. Then Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays an inner glyph of containment while his acolytes channel power through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle. Together, the circles isolate whatever emerges from the settlement below. The Tome of the Cabal holds the words that open a bridge into the Twisting Nether. Felhunters are ravenous demonic hounds that hunger for arcane power and feast on magical energy. No gentle enthrallment or persuasion can bind one. The warlock must violently subdue the summoned beast in combat and break its will before it recognizes its rightful master. Surviving the clash proves the summoner can wield the hound against enemy spellcasters.
