quest:1796.text: Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender seeks Robes of Arcana for a garment meant to bear powerful enchantments. Menara Voidrender asks warlocks who seek greater power to bring her a set of Robes of Arcana. She needs a garment strong enough to hold dark magic. A relic's strength depends on the skill, rarity, and effort invested in its materials. Ordinary rags would fail beneath deep enchantments, so the robe must be finely made and ready to receive them. Menara admires warlocks who weave the robe themselves, though ambition matters more to her than pride. You can sew the silk, commission a skilled artisan, or buy the robe at market. However you obtain it, the finished garment is ready to become a specialized tool of fel mastery.

quest:1798.text: Seeking Strahad. Warlocks seek Strahad Farsan in Ratchet, where he can teach them to summon felhunters. Beneath the goblin port, his knowledge opens a path to more dangerous demons. Gakin the Darkbinder sends you from Stormwind to learn how to summon a felhunter. He guides warlocks in the Slaughtered Lamb below the Mage Quarter, but the rites call for knowledge beyond his reach. So you cross the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where another warlock may know the way. Strahad Farsan lives in the arid hills above Ratchet, the goblin harbor. A human warlock and Gakin's peer in their secret cabal, he works from neutral territory. There, Alliance magistrates, church inquisitors, and Horde sentries are less likely to notice him. Warlocks come hoping to master demons that drain mana.

quest:180.text:
Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore. In Lakeshire, a bounty calls for Lieutenant Fangore's death. Magistrate Solomon seeks hunters to stop the Shadowhide gnolls pressing into the Redridge Mountains. Fangore serves the renegade sorcerer Morganth, and his death would strike at Morganth's forces. Lakeshire faces growing danger. Stormwind's army is stretched thin, and King Varian Wrynn is mysteriously absent. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon has left frontier settlements like Redridge to defend themselves.

The Shadowhide clan raids trade routes, burns farmsteads, and presses against the town's perimeter. Magistrate Solomon posts bounties to draw mercenary blades where royal soldiers will not march. Lieutenant Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnolls as Morganth's enforcer. Morganth is a rogue dark wizard hiding in the Redridge hills. Under Fangore, the gnolls strike together instead of scattering like scavengers.

Their attacks threaten to sever Lakeshire from Elwynn Forest. Fangore's severed paw would give Magistrate Solomon proof that Morganth's brute vanguard has been broken.

quest:1801.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan sends Horde warlocks east to seek a lost grimoire. Its rites teach how to summon and bind a felhunter, and the search leads first to cartographer Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Strahad Farsan warns that summoning a felhunter takes more than ordinary fel magic. These predators feed on magical energies and resist common summoning circles. An initiate needs special circles and an ancient grimoire called the Tome of the Cabal. The first warlocks to bind a felhunter without outside aid wrote it. Its rites and seals show how to enslave the dangerous demon. No copies of the Tome of the Cabal remain among warlocks in Kalimdor. So Strahad sends his student across the sea to Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Annison is a royal cartographer who maps Lordaeron, yet he knows much about ancient and obscure texts. He admits that mapmaking wears on him. His true hunger is for rare histories, occult narratives, and treatises on dark magic.

quest:1802.text: Tome of the Cabal. From Ironforge, your search for the Tome of the Cabal leads to a lost manuscript and a sunken ship. Its scattered pages hold rites for binding a felhunter. Only one copy of the Tome of the Cabal was ever written. Violence tore it apart and defaced its pages, sending the remnants to distant corners of the world. A tattered manuscript crossed the sea to Kalimdor, where centaur clans took it. The other half sailed from Lordaeron toward Khaz Modan, but the vessel sank before reaching port. Two dangers guard the missing pages. Those lost at sea washed ashore on the Hillsbrad coast, west of Southshore. Shoreline murlocs near Azurelode Mine took the waterlogged relics and wreckage. The dry half rests in an ancient chest deep in the centaur caverns of Splithoof Hold in Thousand Needles. Once the pieces are together, Krom Stoutarm can inspect the lost text before it returns to Strahad Farsan.

quest:1803.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Undercity, Horde warlocks seek the Tome of the Cabal's scattered halves for Jorah Annison. Once kept in Lordaeron, the grimoire was torn apart, and its remnants lie along the hostile waters of the Eastern Kingdoms and deep in Kalimdor's centaur lands. The Tome of the Cabal once rested in Lordaeron's library. Someone defaced the sinister grimoire, tore away nearly half its pages, and split it in two. The surviving bound text was sent to the dwarven halls of Ironforge. But its transport wrecked along the rocky coast west of Southshore, and the pages now rot in the shallows beneath scavenging murlocs.

quest:1804.text: Tome of the Cabal. In the Barrens, Strahad Farsan awaits the tome and rods needed to bind a felhunter. The warlock brings them so his circle can prepare the rite. Krom Stoutarm binds the Tome of the Cabal's tattered remnants in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. The dwarf scholar parts with the rare work reluctantly, after securing a promise of a copy. He also gives the warlock a fresh missive from Strahad Farsan. The tome holds rites for breaching the Nether, but parchment alone cannot conduct them. Strahad's acolytes need implements to focus the energies used to bind a felhunter. Krom sends the warlock to the Wetlands, where Dragonmaw spellcasters carry rods of channeling. The hostile orcs guard the rods. Taken from them, the rods give Strahad's circle a conduit to control the rift and steady the summoned energies.

quest:1805.text: Tome of the Cabal. Strahad Farsan's work with the Tome of the Cabal now reaches into hostile territory. After helping Jorah Annison restore the tome, you must claim three Rods of Channeling and bring them to Strahad in Ratchet. In the Undercity, Jorah Annison studies the recovered fragments of the Tome of the Cabal. The Forsaken scholar pieces together its eldritch passages and welcomes the rare knowledge they hold. Then Jorah brings an urgent word from Strahad Farsan. Knowledge alone cannot bind a felhunter; a warlock needs precise instruments to focus demonic power into a binding circle. Strahad needs three Rods of Channeling carried by renegade orcs of the Dragonmaw clan. They dwell among the ruins of Angerfang Encampment in the Wetlands, far from Horde lands. You must enter contested territory and face clan remnants who hate the modern Horde as much as they butcher Alliance explorers.

quest:1806.text: The Test of Righteousness. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, you bring the materials for a paladin’s warhammer. Gathered across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, they help turn an apprentice into a recognized champion of the Light. Jordan Stilwell works at his forge outside Ironforge’s gates. He envies paladins who wander the land, yet takes pride in serving their cause. You bring him rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines. With them, the master smith keeps his promise and forges a weapon worthy of a true defender. Jordan Stilwell names the finished warhammer Verigan's Fist, for Bosch Verigan, an honored dwarven paladin and his dear friend. On behalf of himself and his wife, he places the sacred weapon in a young champion's hands. Through it, his fallen friend's memory and valor endure against the darkness threatening Azeroth.

quest:181.text: Look To The Stars. In Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras seeks the last piece for his telescope. Its frame is ready, but no local glass is large enough for the lens his plans require. Viktori Prism'Antras is building a telescope in Darkshire from plans by Cog Glitzspinner, a gnome engineer. He has gathered brass tubes and sturdy mountings from local supplies. But the design calls for an unusually large focusing lens. Magnifying glasses and optical parts from Stormwind traders are too small, so Viktori searches beyond ordinary materials for the piece he needs.

quest:1824.text: Trial at the Field of Giants. At Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem sends warrior aspirants south to face an unfamiliar foe. They have half an hour to slay silithid in the Field of Giants and return with several twitching antennae. Ruga Ragetotem tests growing warriors at Camp Taurajo against an unfamiliar foe. Horde warrior trainers demand more than skill in battle: aspirants must slay the creatures and bring fresh antennae back within half an hour. The run across the southern Barrens tests their speed and resolve. The antennae must still twitch when they reach Taurajo. Silithid hives rise in the Field of Giants beneath massive fossilized ribcages. These strange, crawling insects arrived in the Barrens recently, disturbing tauren hunters and shamans who watch the savannas. Ruga says their presence bodes ill for Kalimdor. The trial tests a young warrior's instincts in battle and gathers intelligence on a growing threat to the land.

quest:1825.text: Speak with Thun'grim. After the Trial at the Field of Giants, Thun'grim Firegaze calls warriors to his camp in the Barrens. The orc smith offers custom armor to those who have proved their valor, and sends them to gather materials for Brutal Armor. Word of the warriors’ trial reaches Thun'grim Firegaze after they prove their endurance and fighting skill to Ruga Ragetotem. His camp stands on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Thun'grim wants to forge them an exceptional suit of battle mail. Thun'grim Firegaze reserves his forge for warriors who meet his high standard. He expects steel to match the spirit of the one who bears it. Reaching his camp means a warrior has moved beyond basic militia drills and can take on the hard work of gathering rare materials across Kalimdor.

quest:1838.text: Brutal Armor. In the northern Barrens, a warrior faces Thun'grim Firegaze's test. The near-blind smith sends seasoned Horde warriors across distant lands for rare ingredients and smelting agents. Bring him what his scroll calls for, and he can begin forging a full set of brutal battle gear. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze listens for news of war. The veteran orc smith's eyesight is failing, yet no hand at the forge is more skilled. Rumors tell him of a warrior whose strength and valor surpass those of ordinary soldiers. So Thun'grim sets out to forge mail fit for the fiercest battles across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Thun'grim's armor requires more than common ore. By firelight, his failing eyes guide him as he writes a precise scroll for the core chestpiece. It calls for refined iron, smoky iron ingots carried by burrowing kobolds, powdered azurite worked by miners across the sea, and a volatile vial of phlogiston. Only a warrior ready for trials across distant lands can gather all the required materials.

quest:1839.text: Ula'elek and the Brutal Gauntlets. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek waits to forge the Brutal Gauntlets for you. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you from the Barrens to Durotar's southern coast. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east after you prove your valor in the Barrens and begin assembling the Brutal Armor set. The veteran orc smith trusts skilled artisans across Horde lands to forge its pieces. For the heavy mail gauntlets, he sends you to Durotar's rocky southern shore. In Sen'jin Village, troll armorsmith Ula'elek works among his Darkspear kin. Thun'grim has told him of your deeds, and Ula'elek says the spirits have watched your triumphs in battle. For a warrior seeking a place among the Horde's elite, fine craft goes hand in hand with spiritual recognition.

quest:1840.text: Orm Stonehoof and the Brutal Helm. In Thunder Bluff, Orm Stonehoof can forge the Brutal Helm. Thun'grim Firegaze sends warriors to him for the work. Warriors who prove their mettle and gather pieces of the Brutal Armor in the Barrens are sent to Thunder Bluff. Thun'grim Firegaze is a skilled armorsmith, but the work has grown beyond his craft. So he directs the warriors to Orm Stonehoof, whose skill is known across Kalimdor. Orm can shape sturdy helms from rare trophies taken from savage beasts. Orm Stonehoof lives and works on Mulgore's high bluffs, near the pool below Thunder Bluff's great central totem. When a warrior comes with Thun'grim Firegaze's word, Orm sets aside his usual work. He speaks with them about the demanding parts needed to forge a helm fit for the Horde's front lines.

quest:1841.text: Velora Nitely and the Brutal Legguards. Across the Great Sea, Thun'grim Firegaze sends Horde warriors to seek Velora Nitely and the Brutal Legguards. In the Undercity, the Forsaken smith uses the craft she kept from her mortal life to forge the armor. Her work helps complete a durable suit for the Horde's warriors. Thun'grim Firegaze sends you east across the Great Sea to find a smith for the Brutal Legguards. You've proved your mettle to the veteran smith during his vigil in the Barrens, and now he points you toward the fabled Brutal Armor. Thun'grim cannot make the whole suit alone, so he depends on skilled allies across the Horde. The greaves call for an artisan whose work was revered before northern humanity fell, in the Forsaken's underground kingdom. Velora Nitely works in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, where her old craft still serves the Horde. Before the Scourging of the north ended her mortal life, she was one of the Kingdom of Lordaeron's foremost armorsmiths. Her homeland was corrupted, and she became one of the Forsaken. Death did not take her mastery of metal. Now she turns her human skill toward the Horde's warriors, with a dry, macabre wit about being undead.

quest:1842.text: Satyr Hooves. In Sen'jin Village, Ula'elek sends warriors north to Ashenvale for Satyr Hooves. He needs their strange power to forge brutal gauntlets. Ula'elek sends you into Ashenvale's ancient woods to gather what his craft requires. Demonic corruption still clings to the satyr covens there. For armor meant to rival Kalimdor's fiercest forces, he needs more than iron and leather. In northeastern Ashenvale, satyrs feed on the forest's lingering purity and twist it into foul power. Those that take in the most grow swollen hooves without the usual cloven split. Ula'elek plans to draw out that concentrated magic and weave it into his gauntlets.

quest:1843.text: Brutal Gauntlets. In Durotar, Ula'elek has finished Brutal Gauntlets for a seasoned Horde warrior. Rare materials from distant lands went into the work, meant to honor both maker and bearer. In Durotar, Ula'elek brings his lineage and skill to armor for a seasoned frontline warrior. He shapes brutal gauntlets from hardened trophies taken from dangerous foes. The finished armor can withstand fierce blows and strengthen the wearer's attacks. Among orcs and trolls, fine arms and armor carry the forge's prestige and the maker's spirit into battle. When Ula'elek presents the finished gauntlets, he entrusts a warrior with his ancestors' legacy. He expects a champion who wears them to answer that craft with courage, martial discipline, and strength.

quest:1844.text: Chimaeric Horn. In the Charred Vale, a suffering chimaera matriarch tests a Horde warrior’s strength and mercy. Orm Stonehoof needs her horn for the Brutal Helm, and the hunt will prove the warrior’s resolve. Orm Stonehoof will forge the Brutal Helm for Horde warriors, but custom asks for proof before he begins. Metal and coin are not enough. A warrior must show martial skill and face the scars left by devastating conflict. The Charred Vale lies in the southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, buried in ash. Once lush and green, the valley was burned into a smoking wasteland. Beasts still roam its soot-covered craters, twisted by pain and fury. Mighty chimaeras nest among dead trees and searing steam vents. To the tauren smith, the chimaera matriarch’s horn is needed for the helm and proves a warrior’s strength. Yet the hunt also ends her torment. By felling the matriarch, the warrior brings mercy to a wild spirit driven mad by the destruction of her home.

quest:1845.text: Brutal Helm. In Thunder Bluff, Orm Stonehoof brings the warrior’s trial to its end with Brutal Helm. After gathering rare beast trophies across Kalimdor, an aspiring warrior earns recognition with a horned helm that honors their strength. Orm Stonehoof is a stern smith in Thunder Bluff who guides Horde warriors through hard rites of passage. The trials test their skill in battle. Initiates hunt dangerous creatures in treacherous lands and claim rare trophies. Only those who meet Orm’s high standards may come before him to complete their armor. The warrior proves their resolve in the wild by bringing Orm Stonehoof a rare chimaeric horn. In return, Orm presents Brutal Helm, heavy mail crafted to honor the beast and strengthen its wearer in the front line. As he gives the helm, Orm calls on the Earthmother’s blessing. He looks to the greater deeds the warrior is bound to undertake across Azeroth.

quest:1846.text: Dragonmaw Shinbones. Velora Nitely sends Horde warriors from the Undercity into the southern Wetlands for Dragonmaw Shinbones. The thick bones will brace Brutal Legguards against the blows a seasoned warrior faces. Velora Nitely, a Forsaken armorer in the Undercity, needs a sturdy brace for Brutal Legguards. She sends Horde warriors to the Wetlands to gather thick bone from the Dragonmaw orcs. Their dense frames can bear the heavy blows that seasoned warriors face. Velora needs bones that can hold firm. Each must pass a hand test; any that snap are too brittle for the forge. So warriors scour renegade camps along the Wetlands' crags, breaking weak specimens until eight sturdy shinbones remain.

quest:1848.text: Brutal Hauberk. Across the Barrens, Horde warriors face a trial before Thun'grim Firegaze will forge their mail. They gather rare materials and face dangerous foes across the lands, then bring their bounty to the reclusive smith. He hammers it into armor built for battle. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze, an orc, forges armor only for warriors who meet his demands. The reclusive smith sends them far and wide to gather tough beast parts, rare metal, and alchemical reagents before he lights his bellows. The finished hauberk protects its wearer and marks the endurance and grit they have shown. Veteran fighters throughout the Horde recognize that hard-won proof. Thun'grim makes his demands punishing by design. Horde arms and armor are expected to carry the sweat and blood of their wearer from the moment they are made. When you hand over the finished Brutal Hauberk, the smith offers no praise. He expects you to prove the armor in brutal combat and return with stories of blood and honor.

quest:185.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack trains hunters to track big cats. She begins with young tigers near the northern camp, testing a newcomer's hunting and tracking skills. Ajeck Rouack learned to hunt tigers from her father when she was a girl. Now she shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition after Welcome to the Jungle. Young tigers are the first quarry. Tracking and hunting them prepare you to pursue greater prey. Young Stranglethorn tigers prowl the jungle near the expedition camp. Ajeck Rouack asks you to hunt ten. She wants proof of your skill before she offers further training.

quest:186.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack sends you to hunt mature tigers. After you defeat young stalkers, she sets you against ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Ajeck Rouack sends you to hunt ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Your success against younger predators has brought you to a harder test in the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. Greater challenges lie beyond this hunt.

quest:187.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack sends you after ten elder Stranglethorn tigers. Their deaths will prove your skill before the final test. Ajeck Rouack sends you into the wilds to hunt ten elder Stranglethorn tigers. He says they are the hardest cats to track and the fiercest to overcome. Their deaths prepare you for a final trial. After it, he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

quest:188.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack sends you after a tiger his hunters have tracked for weeks. Sin'Dall waits in northern Stranglethorn Vale, and her paw will prove the hunt is done. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack sends you on one last hunt after your earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers. His hunters have tracked Sin'Dall through the jungle for weeks. Find the elusive tiger, kill her, and bring back her paw as proof.

quest:1884.text: Ju-Ju Heaps. On the Echo Isles, Un'thuwa asks you to destroy Zalazane's ju-ju heaps. Their corruption threatens Durotar's flow of magic. From Sen'jin Village, Un'thuwa asks you to destroy the heaps Zalazane placed among his huts on the main Echo Isle. The tainted fetishes corrupt wildlife and strengthen warlocks and infernal creatures. Left alone, they may change Durotar's flow of magic forever.

quest:189.text: Bloodscalp Ears. In Booty Bay, Bloodscalp Ears bring Kebok a way to answer for mounting losses. He pays for proof of a kill after clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe have cost him guards and agents. In Stranglethorn Vale, Bloodscalp trolls are killing Kebok's agents and guards. Many of his best guards have fallen in jungle skirmishes. The mounting costs leave him anxious about explaining them to Baron Revilgaz. Kebok offers coin to travelers who hunt Bloodscalp trolls in the jungle. He asks you to bring back fifteen severed ears as proof of the kills.

quest:19.text: Tharil'zun. Near Stonewatch Keep, Marshal Marris targets Tharil'zun, whose outrunners harass the roads. His death is a critical step in breaking the Blackrock clan's hold over northern Redridge, and his severed head brought to Lakeshire marks a hard-fought victory for its watch. The road between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep has become perilous with sudden ambushes. Blackrock outrunners and renegades prowl the rocky ridges, cutting off scouts and threatening reinforcements bound for the fortress. Marshal Marris names Tharil'zun as the commander directing these strikes. He says Tharil'zun must be eliminated, or Lakeshire may be hemmed in entirely. Tharil'zun is a dangerous battlefield leader, vicious and crafty, who unites scattered orc raiders into an effective force. Reaching him in Stonewatch's shadow means cutting through entrenched Blackrock outposts. His death breaks the outrunner patrols' cohesion and clears a path for the Alliance to face the garrison inside the keep.

quest:190.text: Panther Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Sir S. J. Erlgadin tests those who seek a place in Hemet's hunt. They must bring down ten young panthers to prove their skill at tracking. Hemet Nesingwary has gathered seasoned big-game hunters in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks newcomers to prove they can hunt panthers before they join the party. Before trusting newcomers with larger game, Erlgadin sets them a test. They must find and slay ten young panthers. Finding the prowlers is only half the challenge.

quest:191.text: Panther Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition, Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks you to prove your worth among the seasoned hunters. After your hunt for young panthers, he sends you into Stranglethorn Vale for ten fully grown beasts. Your hunt for young panthers is done, and Sir S. J. Erlgadin sets a higher standard. He asks you to prove you can keep company with the expedition's seasoned big game hunters. So you set out to track and slay ten mature panthers, stronger and more dangerous than their young kin.

quest:192.text: Panther Mastery. In Stranglethorn Vale, Panther Mastery sends you after the deadliest panthers. After your earlier trials, ten Shadowmaw Panthers are your quarry. Sir S. J. Erlgadin calls Shadowmaw Panthers the most dangerous cats in Stranglethorn's jungles. To prove yourself as a stalker, you crawl through dense underbrush and track ten elusive beasts. Their ferocity makes them harder to kill than to find.

quest:1938.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. High Sorcerer Andromath seeks Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic in Stormwind. Morganth stole the forbidden tome and carried it to the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Three promising mages studied together in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum. Morganth turned to dark arts and shadow magic despite their desperate warnings. The city's magical order banished him. Before he left, he stole a dangerous work by Ur, an infamous archmage whose studies reached beyond orthodox arcana. Morganth seized the Tower of Ilgalar in the heights of the Redridge Mountains, beyond Stormwind's scrutiny. High Sorcerer Andromath fears the tome's knowledge in the hands of an outcast practicing forbidden sorcery. So he sends Alliance adventurers into the tower to recover it before its wards fall.

quest:1939.text: High Sorcerer Andromath. At Stormwind’s Wizard’s Sanctum, promising Alliance mages are summoned to the tower’s summit. Andromath works among the kingdom’s foremost archmages beyond ruined Dalaran. Jennea Cannon, the apprentice coordinator in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, sends promising casters to the summit of the Wizard’s Sanctum. High Sorcerer Andromath, one of the southern kingdoms’ most senior active practitioners of the arcane, has asked to meet magi ready for greater responsibilities. Dalaran’s magocracy was ruined in the Third War, and its surviving wizards are busy rebuilding. Without easy access to the Violet Citadel’s libraries, the Alliance relies on senior archmages in Stormwind to study ancient threats and guide research into shadowy, forbidden arts.

quest:194.text: Raptor Mastery. At his northern Stranglethorn camp, Hemet Nesingwary tests your hunting skill. He asks you to find and slay ten Stranglethorn Raptors. After Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary tests your skill at tracking and hunting in the jungle. He gives you no map or directions. Finding the Stranglethorn Raptors is part of the trial, and you need to bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

quest:1940.text: Pristine Spider Silk. In Stormwind, High Sorcerer Andromath sends rising Alliance mages to Duskwood for pristine spider silk. They carry eight samples to Wynne Larson in the Mage Quarter, where she weaves an adept’s robe. High Sorcerer Andromath marks a mage’s passage beyond apprenticeship with vestments fit for an adept. In the Wizard’s Sanctum, a mage’s skill is seen in the robes they wear. So each mage must gather pristine silk from dangerous spiders and show both field skill and discernment. Carrion recluse spiders haunt Duskwood’s gloomy woods, and ordinary stalls do not sell their silk. You gather eight fine samples and carry them across Stormwind to Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. There, Wynne Larson weaves the delicate threads into a robe with arcane significance.

quest:1942.text: Astral Knot Garment. In Stormwind City, Wynne Larson weaves pristine spider silk into a garment for dangerous journeys and high-society gatherings. An adventurer brings her rare silk from the wilds, and she shapes it into a magical weave. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, tailors serve arcane elites and visiting nobles. Wynne Larson weaves pristine spider silk into garments both durable and enchanted. Her playful humor shows when she jokes about saving a few precious scraps for her own wardrobe before handing over her finished work. Spellcasters who wear cloth prize the Astral Knot Garment for its resilience and refinement. Its silk comes from dangerous spiders, and its weave is made to endure combat. It keeps the polished look expected at formal banquets in Stormwind Keep.

quest:1943.text: Speak with Deino. In Orgrimmar, Deino calls promising Horde mages to aid their craft. The troll mage works from the Valley of Spirits and seeks an adept for important work. Her summons opens a path to deeper study and duties across Kalimdor. Horde mages sharpen their arcane skill under their instructors’ care. When a student is ready for harder work, a mentor such as Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity points the way to Orgrimmar. There, in the troll quarter, specialized knowledge and dangerous work await. Deino lives in Darkbriar Lodge, in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits. Few Darkspear study arcane magic beside the many witch doctors and priests, making Deino an authority in the capital. Her work reaches Horde mages beyond local concerns. She seeks ambitious spellcasters willing to face dangers far from home.

quest:1944.text: Waters of Xavian. In Ashenvale, Deino seeks water from Xavian to study the city's lingering arcane power. She sends her apprentice to draw a sample from the pool beneath its highest waterfall. Deino, a troll mage in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, searches Kalimdor for primal arcane traces. Now she has turned her attention to Xavian, an ancient night elf city beneath Ashenvale's eastern canopy. Scholars say the city held great magical knowledge before the Sundering. They believe its waters still hold arcane power that modern mages hope to understand. Xavian lies in ruins, overrun by feral, corrupt satyrs who defend their ground from outsiders. To reach the water, you pass Satyrnaar and cross dangerous waterways, steering clear of prowling beasts and demonic sentinels. Deino needs a sample from the pool at the base of the city's highest waterfall.

quest:1945.text: Laughing Sisters. In Ashenvale, dryad hair is sought for an empowered robe. At the Crossroads, the experienced troll tailor Kil'hala needs the enchanted locks to weave a mage robe as Horde mages press against the woodland's native defenders. After you secure water from Xavian, Deino in Orgrimmar sends rising mages to craft their own enchanted vestments. These arcane garments need materials touched by raw magic. Dryad locks carry the forest's ancient vitality, giving mages what they need to weave intricate robes that shield and strengthen a caster. Near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale, mages seek the laughing sisters. These nimble dryads ally with the night elves and fiercely guard their groves from woodsmen and outsiders. They will not willingly give their hair to Horde spellcasters. So the locks are taken by force beneath the ancient trees. The locks travel south across the border to the dusty settlement of the Crossroads in the Barrens. There, troll tailor Kil'hala receives them without remorse. Kil'hala acknowledges the woodland creatures' loss with a touch of irony, then puts the enchanted strands to use. Horde power demands resolve.

quest:1946.text: Nether-lace Garment. At the Crossroads, Kil'hala weaves dryad hair into enchanted cloth for spellcasters. This garment completes his specialized work in the Barrens. At the Crossroads in the Barrens, Kil'hala weaves nether-lace from the locks of laughing sisters. The dryads live in Ashenvale, where their hair is gathered for his craft. He binds the woodland enchantment carried in those rare, resonant locks into cloth that is comfortable and durable. Kil'hala seeks more than fine work from his trade. He hopes to win favor with Deino, a respected troll mage in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. By making exceptional garb for aspiring practitioners, he hopes to earn and keep Deino's good graces.

quest:1947.text: Journey to the Marsh. Your class sends you to Dustwallow Marsh, where Tabetha’s knowledge can help you earn your wand. West of Theramore and just north of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a cottage. Your class asks you to speak with the hermit and learn from her vast knowledge.

quest:195.text: Raptor Mastery. In Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary sends hunters after deadlier quarry. After their first raptor hunt, he asks them to track and kill ten Lashtail Raptors. North of Grom'gol Base Camp, Hemet Nesingwary sends hunters into dense jungle brush. After their first raptor hunt, he expects them to prove their focus and skill with deadlier quarry. Ten fierce Lashtail Raptors must be tracked and killed.

quest:1950.text: Get the Scoop. Near the Mirage Raceway, Magus Tirth has forgotten the words to open his sealed strongbox. His apprentice, Johnson, is missing somewhere around the track, and Tirth needs the spellbook inside. Magus Tirth lives on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. He is an eccentric spellcaster whose arcane knowledge and books draw mages seeking to advance. Patience helps when dealing with him. Tirth relies on an assistant for everyday details, even the spoken passwords guarding his arcane stores. Now a book of power is locked away, and the magic words have slipped from his mind entirely.

quest:198.text: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek needs a courier in Booty Bay to carry supplies north to Private Thorsen. Troll attacks have stopped the regular shipments to Lieutenant Doren's camp near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren's men guard the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood. Krazek arranges regular shipments for them, but local trolls keep attacking. The usual deliveries have become dangerous, so the goblin merchant hires you to carry a package north along the jungle road. Private Thorsen can receive it at the camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

quest:1999.text: Tools of the Trade. In the Undercity, Horde rogues are sent to steal a report from Ambermill. Lord Varimathras orders them to obtain lockpicking tools and learn Dalaran’s condition from Kirin Tor intelligence. A prisoner’s interrogation leads the Deathstalkers to intelligence hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and human mages guard the village’s communications fiercely. Lord Varimathras orders Mennet Carkad, a Deathstalker handler, to guide promising operatives past the Kirin Tor sentries and recover the Dalaran Status Report. Infiltration and lockpicking test skills beyond assassination. Before entering Kirin Tor territory, operatives collect specialized thieves’ tools from Estelle Gendry. Opening the secured chest in Ambermill shows an operative can move beyond street brutality and serve the Forsaken as an espionage asset.

quest:2.text: Sharptalon's Claw. In Ashenvale, Sharptalon's attacks put Horde supply lines at risk. Bring its claw to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post as proof that the predator has fallen. Sharptalon hunts the paths to Splintertree Post while the Horde seeks resources in Ashenvale. The aggressive hippogryph strikes peons and couriers traveling between forward logging camps and the outpost. Its attacks hinder Horde work in the region. Night elven sentinels and dangerous wildlife threaten the newcomers as well. Senani Thunderheart, a tauren huntress, directs Horde hunters against Ashenvale's deadliest predators. Sharptalon's talon proves the hippogryph has fallen. Bring the trophy to Splintertree Post. The outpost's defenders honor the hunt, and frightened laborers can walk the woods with less fear.

quest:20.text: Blackrock Menace. Redridge's Blackrock orcs press from the north and southeast, and Lakeshire is under siege. Marshal Marris asks you to thin their ranks and bring back their battleworn axes. Lakeshire faces threats from several sides, but the Blackrock orcs are the gravest danger. They came south from the fiery Burning Steppes and now roam Redridge's craggy passes. After taking strongholds, they have penned townspeople inside Lakeshire. Trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads have all been cut off. Marshal Marris commands Lakeshire's beleaguered guard, but cannot spare soldiers to attack the orcs' positions. So he calls on you to strike their forward scouts and foot soldiers. Their crude, battleworn axes will prove they are dead. Marris hopes to thin the invaders near Stonewatch in the north and in the rugged pockets of southeastern Redridge.

quest:200.text: Bookie Herod. A leak has Lieutenant Doren searching his ranks for a traitor. Kurzen has learned Thorsen's secret, and Doren wants the records of Bookie Herod, Kurzen's logistics officer, from Kurzen's Compound. Lieutenant Doren suspects a traitor among his men. Kurzen learned Thorsen's secret, and the leak threatens their operations. So Doren needs to find its source. Thorsen kept a line into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer. Herod's written records may show how the operation was exposed. Bookie Herod's papers are inside Kurzen's Compound. When Doren served under Kurzen, Herod's office was on the top floor of the compound's only two-story house. Supply requisitions and messages from Colonel Kurzen may reveal how Thorsen's secret was betrayed.

quest:201.text: Investigate the Camp. Krazek has heard Hemet Nesingwary may be in Stranglethorn Vale. He asks you to find the hunters' camp near Lake Nazferiti and confirm the report. Booty Bay reports place a hunters' camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Krazek has heard it lies along the river, just beyond the Venture Company's mining claim near Lake Nazferiti. The jungle is lawless, with dangers and competing interests. An armed camp draws notice. Hemet Nesingwary may be among the hunters at the camp. The renowned dwarven marksman is known across the lands as an elite explorer with influential ties. Krazek sends you upriver to learn whether the legendary hunter has arrived.

quest:203.text:
The Second Rebellion. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa calls for aid against Colonel Kurzen's overwhelming force. Outnumbered ten to one, the rebels cannot fight a long, open war. They strike swiftly and in secret, hoping to thin Kurzen's ranks and ease the pressure on their refuge. At the Rebel Camp, the rebels face Colonel Kurzen's force with at least ten foes for every one of their own. Sergeant Yohwa knows the Colonel is a brilliant military tactician. An open war of attrition would leave the rebels with no chance.

So they turn Kurzen's covert methods against him. They strike quickly at his encampment, then flee before heavy reinforcements can answer. Sergeant Yohwa asks you to head east into Kurzen's stronghold and eliminate a sizable contingent of his jungle fighters. Their numbers press hard on the Rebel Camp. Thin their ranks, and the refuge can breathe easier.

quest:204.text: Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks a way to weaken Colonel Kurzen's force. His medicine men heal his soldiers and poison Yohwa's fighters, and the resistance needs their remedies and toxins. Colonel Kurzen's medicine men heal his soldiers and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extract. Sergeant Yohwa asks you to gather their supplies from the Kurzen Compound. The remedies can treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp. A sample of venom fern extract will let the resistance study the toxin and make cures of its own.

quest:2040.text: Underground Assault. Shoni the Shilent sends Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines to seize a power core. The exiled gnomes need it to drive drills through the rock around Gnomeregan and reclaim their home. Gnomish tinkerers fled across Khaz Modan and Stormwind after primitive troggs brought Gnomeregan down. Shoni the Shilent is already planning how to break through the rock around their lost home. Her gyrodrillmatic excavationators need great power to bore through the underground stone. Human lands have no local power grids, so the gnomes have turned to heavy goblin machinery in the criminal underworld. In the Deadmines shafts in Westfall, Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood employs goblin engineers to build war machines. One machine is a working goblin shredder, a lumbering automaton. Shoni sends Alliance operatives to destroy or dismantle it and recover its specialized heart, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. The exiled gnomes need that goblin power supply to drive their drills through the underground rock and begin their counteroffensive to reclaim Gnomeregan.

quest:207.text: Kurzen's Mystery. At the Rebel Camp, Brother Nimetz seeks the reason for Colonel Kurzen’s fall. He suspects troll magic and sends you to copy legends from four tablets in Stranglethorn’s troll ruins. Brother Nimetz at the Rebel Camp seeks the cause of Colonel Kurzen’s fall from greatness into depravity. He suspects troll magic has taken hold of the colonel. Legends carved on four old tablets may test that suspicion. You are asked to copy each tablet’s markings and carry them back to camp. One tablet stands in the Bal'lal Ruins. Another lies deep underwater in the Vile Reef, off the coast near a sunken city held by Saltscale murlocs. The last two tablets are in the Ruins of Zul'Kunda.

quest:2078.text: Gyromast's Revenge. Along Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast seeks revenge on the murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship. He sends you to wind up his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Gelkak Gyromast is stranded on Darkshore, but he will not yield to the murlocs along the shore. He has gathered the parts for his plan and seeks revenge on their tribe and its chief. Rather than wade into the surf with his cutlass, the eccentric captain turns to engineering. He gives you a winding key and asks you to tend to his mechanical subordinate.

quest:2098.text: Gyromast's Retrieval. Gelkak Gyromast needs your help on Darkshore's coast. His mechanical first mate cannot work without a winding key, shattered on the rocks. Wildlife and murlocs carried off its three pieces. On Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome pirate stranded far from the South Seas. He says aggressive threshadons attacked and sank his vessel just off the coast. The wreck cast him ashore among the flotsam, marooned and parted from his crew. Gelkak's first concern is his first mate, not provisions or gold. His companion needs a special key to operate, but the key broke into three pieces when Gelkak crashed on the rocky shoals. Reef crawlers on the beach, foreststriders near the woods, and Greymist murloc scavengers carried the shiny pieces away.

quest:210.text: Krazek's Cookery. In Booty Bay, Corporal Kaleb has a broken pot to get mended. He asks you to carry the mechanical cooker he bought from a goblin trader to Krazek. Corporal Kaleb handles most of the camp's cooking. Before he bought a mechanical pot from a goblin trader in Booty Bay, cooking took hours. The pot spared him that work until it broke. Now he asks you to carry Krazek's Crock Pot to Krazek, the goblin who can repair it.

quest:213.text: Hostile Takeover. In Booty Bay, Gelriz's latest move draws Baron Revilgaz's wrath in Hostile Takeover. Gelriz has pushed aside moguls appointed by the trade princes and now moves against the most notorious pirate of all. Kebok sends you to steal strange blue crystals Venture Company geologists have found near Lake Nazferiti. Baron Revilgaz gives Kebok leave to answer the insult as he sees fit. Kebok chooses theft, targeting the strange blue stones Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing. Venture Company geologists working around Lake Nazferiti have taken a keen interest in the unusual crystals. Kebok wants you to bring eight samples back to Booty Bay. How you get them matters little to him, so long as they end up in his hands.

quest:215.text: Jungle Secrets. In northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he rejoined Kurzen's men after you rescued him from an ambush. He sends you to the Rebel Camp to have his commander confirm the reason. Private Thorsen says the scene looks grim and asks you to hear him out. Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men and gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. Thorsen hoped this would let him enter Kurzen's Compound, but the effort soon went badly. He sends you to Doren at the Rebel Camp for confirmation and begs you to keep the matter secret.

quest:2158.text: Rest and Relaxation. From Northshire, new Alliance adventurers follow the road south to Goldshire for rest and welcome. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Innkeeper Farley offers food, drink, and a place by the hearth. Weary travelers leave Northshire and follow the road south to Goldshire. It leads straight to the Lion's Pride Inn, where Innkeeper Farley welcomes those setting out into Elwynn Forest. For new adventurers, the inn is the first major outpost beyond the Abbey, with shelter and hot meals. Innkeeper Farley welcomes those who are tired and cold. Mention your referral, and you can settle by the open fire for a warm meal, sturdy ale, and a rest before continuing through Elwynn.

quest:219.text: Missing In Action. Corporal Keeshan is missing in the Redridge Mountains after Blackrock orcs overran his regiment. They knocked him unconscious and carried him into a cave fortress. Now he needs an escort to Lakeshire, where the garrison awaits his return. Blackrock orcs come down from the northern peaks, making the Redridge Mountains more dangerous. Town guard patrols often meet ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's regiment suffered the worst. Outnumbered and overwhelmed, most of its soldiers fell. Keeshan survived when a crushing blow knocked him unconscious before the orcs could execute him. They dragged him to their cave as a prisoner. Battered and concussed, Keeshan is held deep in enemy territory. He cannot make the trek down the mountain alone, so you escort him toward Lakeshire past the orc warbands on the ridgelines. Marshal Marris has been trying to learn what happened to the missing regiment. He is also preparing Lakeshire for further attacks, and Keeshan's safe return brings him sorely needed relief.

quest:220.text: Call of Water. The water Brine prepared now reaches Islen Waterseer on the eastern Barrens coast. There it begins the next part of the shamanic trial, and will form the base of a sapta that lets an initiate see water spirits in Silverpine Forest. After the trials in the southern Barrens, Brine gives you a Vial of Purest Water. It comes from pure springs and has been consecrated by Brine's rites. You carry it back to the eastern coast, where Islen Waterseer keeps watch. The water joins Brine's teachings to the rites of the totem. Islen explains that mortal eyes cannot easily see water spirits. To meet them, you drink a brew called a sapta. Brine's water forms the base of that draught and opens your senses to what ordinary sight cannot find. Seeing the spirits is only part of the journey. They will test you.

quest:221.text: Worgen in the Woods. Nightbane Dark Runners press toward Darkshire from the Rotting Orchard in Duskwood. Calor sends you to thin their ranks before the pack can surround the town. Calor's scouting has revealed a greater danger than the lone worgen first seen weaving shadowy magic at the forest's edge. Larger and swifter Nightbane Dark Runners have gathered in the Rotting Orchard, just southwest of Darkshire. They make up most of the pack and have made the orchard a staging ground within striking distance of the village gates.

quest:222.text: Worgen in the Woods. Calor sends you into southern Duskwood against the Nightbane pack. Their dens and mines bring the worgen threat close to Darkshire. South of Darkshire, Nightbane worgen fortify caves and abandoned mine shafts as camps. Calor watches their bonfires and fears what their growing hold means for the town. Among the pack, the Vile Fangs and Tainted Ones are its fiercest breeds. Their savagery and stubbornness threaten Darkshire’s perimeter.

quest:223.text: Worgen in the Woods. In Worgen in the Woods, Calor sends you to Darkshire with a letter for Jonathan Carevin. Your hunts against the worgen in Duskwood have earned his trust, and he believes your skill can aid Carevin. You drove the Nightbane pack from Roland's Doom and the shadowed glades, earning Calor's respect. He serves on the dark frontier of the woods and rarely offers praise or formal introductions. Now he gives you a faded scrap of parchment for Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire. Calor believes more fighters like you could help his small company outshine the town's beleaguered Night Watch. Jonathan Carevin works in Darkshire under heavy strain. Worgen, restless undead, demonic forces, and cultists who aid the corruption from within all threaten the town. Wary of outsiders and short on time, Carevin trusts Calor's recommendation. He sees you as a dependable fighter who can help preserve the Light against Duskwood's terrors.

quest:2258.text: Badlands Reagent Run. In Kargath, Jarkal Mossmeld needs Badlands reagents to refill his stocks. He offers coin when you bring them to him. Jarkal Mossmeld needs gizzards from five buzzards, fangs from ten crag coyotes, and shards from five rock elementals. Take each from the creatures themselves. If you do not fight, find friends who do. Jarkal pays in coin when you bring him the reagents.

quest:226.text: Wolves at Our Heels. In western Duskwood, Lars faces hungry, rabid dire wolves. Hunting them gives him room to gather food while he and Sven Yorgen pursue their vendetta against the necromancer Morbent Fel. Sven Yorgen and Lars keep an isolated camp in Duskwood’s western hills, near the Westfall border. Far from Darkshire, they rely on hunting and foraging to survive. As Lars carries fresh game through the dark woods, ravenous predators prowl the riverbanks and underbrush. Starving, rabid dire wolves prowl north and east of the camp, toward the river. Killing the frenzied beasts makes Lars’s hunt safer. With less danger as they gather their daily food, Sven and Lars can focus on Morbent Fel, the necromancer farther east.

quest:2282.text: Alther's Mill. Lucius sends Alliance rogues to test their skill at Alther's Mill. It lies northeast along the road from Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs now draw near. Lucius sends you northeast from Lakeshire along the road to Alther's Mill, carrying your first set of thieves' tools. There, a locked chest puts your skill to the test. Open Lucius's personal lockbox and bring back the token inside to earn your Certificate of Thievery. Alther's Mill once served as a lumber outpost. Now Blackrock orcs press into Redridge and have drawn near, so Lucius makes their presence part of the trial. SI:7 expects its agents to pick locks unseen while moving through enemy-held ground.

quest:23.text: Ursangous's Paw. The Ashenvale Hunt has brought you Ursangous's Paw. Take it to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post, and earn honor among the Horde's trackers. Trackers from Splintertree Post hunt the ancient beasts that rule Ashenvale's canopy. Ursangous is among the fiercest. He kills travelers and warriors who cross his path, so his paw proves the mighty beast has fallen to your hunt.

quest:230.text: Sven's Camp. In Duskwood's western hills, Sven Yorgen still grieves for his slain family and seeks answers. A journal buried at his ruined farm may tell who saw the massacre. You find a small, dirt-stained book beneath freshly turned earth at the ruined Yorgen farm. Dark riders struck while Sven Yorgen was away, leaving his family dead and the farm in ruins. Grief and vengeance sent his allies to search the wreckage. Someone had hastily hidden the book there.

quest:235.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. Warcaller Gorlach sends the Horde north to Ashenvale, where its frontier presses into an ancient forest. You are to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post and join the hunt. Orgrimmar needs timber, meat, and safe trade routes to keep growing. Warcaller Gorlach bears orders from the Horde's high command, sending seasoned wanderers and new adventurers to active campaigns. For those coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, Ashenvale is the next test of skill and survival. North of the Barrens, the Horde holds two strongholds in Ashenvale. Splintertree Post lies in the eastern woods, while Zoram'gar Outpost stands on the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations from Splintertree Post. She organizes trackers and hunters against the beasts beneath the canopy and the night elven sentinels who contest the Horde's claims.

quest:2359.text: Klaven's Tower. From a camp in Westfall, Agent Kearnen watches Klaven's Tower. Strange shipments and altered guards point to danger within the Defias Brotherhood. At Westfall's southeastern edge, the river runs below Klaven's Tower, north of the Dagger Hills. The Defias Brotherhood holds the stone spire, though its human thieves and brigands are common across the plains. Agent Kearnen has watched the tower alone for weeks. Lately, she has seen strange things: a bizarre shipment came straight from Duskwood's shadowed woods, escorted by monstrous, deformed sentries unlike ordinary highwaymen.

quest:2360.text: Mathias and the Defias. In Westfall, SI:7 has found the Defias unusually active. You are sent to Agent Kearnen near an abandoned Alliance watch tower for a debriefing. The Defias have seized an abandoned Alliance watch tower southeast of Sentinel Hill. SI:7 reports they use it as a base to smuggle goods from the Redridge supply route. You are sent to Westfall to find Agent Kearnen, hidden near the tower, and hear her debriefing.

quest:2383.text: Simple Parchment. A message waits for you in the Valley of Trials, sent while you were away. Frang, your class trainer, is outside the Den. The parchment asks you to read its words and speak with Frang. Your class trainer waits outside the Den in the Valley of Trials.

quest:24.text: Shadumbra's Head. At Splintertree Post, Shadumbra's Head proves a feared predator has fallen. Bringing it to Senani Thunderheart completes a trial of the Ashenvale Hunt and helps secure the western roads toward the Zoram Strand. Shadumbra hunted the woods west of Splintertree Post. Horde scouts and couriers used those paths to reach the Zoram Strand. Her speed and stealth made each journey perilous, and every westward patrol kept the post's defenders wary. Senani Thunderheart, a tauren huntress, challenges Horde champions to track and fell Ashenvale's great beasts. Shadumbra's head proves the hunter has slain one of Kalimdor's deadliest native stalkers. Now travelers can use the roads with less danger.

quest:240.text: Return to Jitters. At Raven Hill, you bring Jitters a meal from Chef Grual. The cakes ease his hunger, though fear still holds him there. Chef Grual cooks at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. With little livestock or sea life in Duskwood, he makes use of what the blighted forest provides. His Dusky Crab Cakes contain no crab meat. Instead, gooey legs from venom web spiders make up his specialty. Grual calls it resourceful cooking, though delicate stomachs may disagree. At Raven Hill, Jitters cowers in fear, unable to face the horrors that drove him from the woods. Terror keeps him from hunting or foraging, and hunger only deepens his distress. The warm cakes bring him a rare moment of relief. Desperate for food, he eats without asking what kind of crab Grual used.

quest:245.text: Eight-Legged Menaces. In Duskwood, venom web spiders crowd the western border, and Watcher Dodds fears for the Night Watch. He asks travelers to thin their numbers before more guards fall into their webs. Pygmy venom web spiders swarm the brush beside the western road from Westfall into Duskwood. Beneath the dense canopy, their webs choke the thickets. Travelers and the Night Watch's already fragile defenses are in danger. Watcher Dodds keeps a small camp far from Darkshire, with too few troops to hold the border. Commander Althea Ebonlocke cannot send help while undead and worgen press against the township. Dodds has lost comrades to the spiders. He found them hanging upside down in the canopy, paralyzed by venom as it liquefied their flesh.

quest:2458.text: Deep Cover. Shenthul sends a promising Horde rogue to Sludge Fen to meet an agent among the Venture Company. The Shattered Hand has spent a year placing Taskmaster Fizzule inside its drilling grounds, where he watches their plans. The Shattered Hand guards Orgrimmar’s interests with secret intelligence and assassination. For a year, its members worked to place an agent among the Venture Company. Taskmaster Fizzule won a place at their drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen, among the company’s mercenaries. Fizzule must keep his harsh reputation to satisfy the Venture Company’s overseers. An unexpected visitor could bring an attack. If you reach his tower, fire two flares from the signaling gun within sight, approach quietly, and give the Shattered Hand’s secret salute. Then Fizzule can share what he has learned about the company’s growing schemes.

quest:2460.text: The Shattered Salute. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul teaches newly inducted rogues a silent sign. The Shattered Hand uses it to recognize its agents safely in the field. The Shattered Hand works in secrecy as Thrall's Horde intelligence and assassination arm from Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. On dangerous, secret assignments, its agents cannot use military signs. So Shenthul teaches newly inducted rogues the Shattered Salute, a silent gesture that lets allies recognize one another. For Shenthul's rogues, learning the salute is vital tradecraft, not ceremony. Agents sent into danger or to infiltrate rival factions need to verify contacts without alerting bystanders or targets. Before entrusting an agent with covert fieldwork, Shenthul expects them to recognize and mirror the gesture without hesitation.

quest:247.text: The Hunt Completed. In Ashenvale, a Horde champion faces three legendary predators. Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon test strength, tenacity, and a hunter's skill in the wild. Senani Thunderheart tests travelers among the Horde forces in Ashenvale. Her hunt tests loyalty to the warchief and asks whether a hunter understands survival in the wild. Three legendary predators are its quarry: Ursangous the bear, Shadumbra the cat, and Sharptalon the fierce hippogryph. A hunter must fell all three and secure their trophies to prove their blood runs true. For the tauren, hunting is sacred. It honors balance and respect, even in an active warfront. By overcoming Ashenvale's greatest terrors, a hunter honors the spirits of the land and earns Thunderheart's ancestral blessings. A formal commendation and token of favor mark the hunt's end, and the champion's reputation spreads through the forest.

quest:2478.text: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. In the northern Barrens, Horde rogues infiltrate a Venture Company outpost to steal a potent brew for the Shattered Hand. Their work tests stealth, theft, and combat. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company keeps an isolated drilling tower. Taskmaster Fizzule, a Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, sends rogues to use underworld craft instead of attacking openly. He asks them to pick the key from Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him. Then they climb past workers and sentries changed by the tower’s experiments.

quest:2479.text: Hinott's Assistance. In Orgrimmar, poisoned rogues seek help before Zanzil's mixture claims their lives. The toxin came from an infiltration in the Barrens. Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill can offer a cure and teach rogues to brew poisons. Your infiltration of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen has left you poisoned by Zanzil's altered mixture. It dulls your reflexes and threatens your life. Shenthul, the rogue trainer in Orgrimmar, knows local remedies cannot help. So he sends you across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms for care. Your search for a cure leads south through Lordaeron to Tarren Mill, a village in Hillsbrad Foothills. Serge Hinott lives there as an apothecary and is fascinated by virulent brews. Ordinary healers recoil from Zanzil's venom, but Hinott meets the deadly compound with professional glee. He can dissect the foul concoction and teach worthy rogues to brew their own venoms.

quest:248.text: Looking Further. Theocritus watches eastern Redridge from Elwynn through an enchanted conduit. He seeks the cause of the conflict between Morganth and the Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep, and sends you to place the Glyph of Azora in the nearby watch tower. From his sanctum in Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches eastern Redridge with scrying magic. As he studies the Tower of Ilgalar, he detects a clash between Morganth, a renegade human warlock, and the Blackrock orcs entrenched in Stonewatch Keep. Both hostile factions should be united against the Kingdom of Stormwind, yet they fight over an unknown prize. Theocritus intervenes before their conflict shifts the balance.

quest:2480.text: Hinott's Assistance. In Tarren Mill, Serge Hinott studies the poison clouding a Horde rogue’s mind and prepares a cure. Your trouble began with an assignment in the Barrens. Now you are sent north to Tarren Mill with a toxin clouding your mind. Serge Hinott, a Forsaken chemist, studies the poison made by Zanzil, a jungle troll exile. The troll’s identity and kin matter little to Hinott. He admires the brew’s vicious effect and wants to learn how it works before making an antidote.

quest:249.text: Morganth. Across Redridge, Morganth hunts the Scythe of Elune while Theocritus watches from afar. From the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, Theocritus uses scrying spells to watch the crags of Redridge. There he sees Morganth, a warlock in the Tower of Ilgalar, searching for the Scythe of Elune. Fearing Morganth is close to claiming it, Theocritus asks Alliance champions to stop him before Stormwind is threatened. The Tower of Ilgalar rises above the Redridge basin, where gnolls roam and arcane energies twist its halls. Morganth waits at the summit, wielding shadow magic and guarding his research. You climb through hostile ground to face him directly. Bring back his Pendant of Shadow as proof that the tower has fallen and the threat is broken.

quest:25.text: Stonetalon Standstill. At Mystral Lake, befouled water spirits have halted Horde supply transports bound for Stonetalon. Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post sends you to clear the hostile elementals and scout a night elf gazebo overlooking Silverwind Refuge. The Horde needs lumber, supplies, and messengers to travel between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The Talondeep Path passes Mystral Lake’s western shore, where hostile water elementals have halted travel and battered supply caravans. Mastok Wrilehiss calls for action before the Horde’s supply lines collapse. The water elementals in Mystral Lake have grown befouled, aggressive, and unpredictable. They attack travelers on nearby trails, so you are sent to cull them and defeat the greater spirit Tideress. What tainted the lake’s spirits remains unknown amid the turmoil in Ashenvale’s sacred groves. A night elf gazebo stands on Mystral Lake’s central island, with a clear view across the water to Silverwind Refuge. Horde scouts are sent to judge whether it could serve as a forward observation post. From there, Splintertree’s commanders could watch nearby Alliance movements unseen.

quest:251.text: Translate Abercrombie's Note. In Darkshire, a strange letter comes before the town's leaders for translation. Mayor Ello Ebonlocke turns to Sirra Von'Indi, the scholar who knows obscure scripts. Abercrombie sends Mayor Ello Ebonlocke a sealed letter from his home. Ebonlocke expects an eccentric plea or bitter ramblings from the cemetery hermit, but the parchment bears strange writing that ordinary Common cannot explain. The mayor cannot read ancient or obscure languages, so he will not dismiss it. Even a mad hermit may pose a danger in Duskwood. Ebonlocke sends you across the square to Sirra Von'Indi, Darkshire's scholar of esoteric lore. Sirra knows ancient arts and forgotten tongues. He scoffs at Abercrombie's sanity, saying anyone who lives beside a haunted graveyard must have a rotted brain. Still, he takes the parchment seriously and begins the slow work of transcription.

quest:252.text: Translation to Ello. In Duskwood, you carry Sirra Von'Indi's translation to Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire. It belongs to the Abercrombie story, and the letter bears news of the hermit's writings.

quest:253.text: Bride of the Embalmer. In Darkshire, Lord Ello Ebonlocke sends you to find Eliza's grave. The town now knows the Embalmer is real, and you are to take his living heart from her cursed remains and strip him of his power. Duskwood's children grew up hearing tales of the Embalmer. They said he was a kindly alchemist driven mad by the death of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to cheat death, he turned to sorcery, cut out his own beating heart, and placed it in her chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke once dismissed the tale as village folklore. Recent discoveries prove the Embalmer walks among the living, and his work festers beneath the graveyard dirt.

quest:254.text: Digging Through the Dirt. At Raven Hill Cemetery, you search for the Embalmer’s missing heart. A mound marked Eliza may hold the answer, buried beneath the dirt. At Raven Hill Cemetery, one patch of loose soil bears the name Eliza. Other graves in Duskwood lie open to scavengers or feral ghouls, yet this earth was laid with care. Dig beneath the topsoil and you find splintered coffin boards. They cover the remnant the Embalmer meant to hide from daylight.

quest:256.text: WANTED: Chok'sul. In northeastern Loch Modan, Chok'sul's ogres threaten the settlements and the works that sustain the valley. Magistrate Bluntnose wants the warlord dead before more lives are lost. Ogres now threaten northeastern Loch Modan, where troggs and wild beasts have long tested the valley's borders. They have made camps in the rugged hills and moved beyond simple scavenging. Local scouts and town authorities report raids that are focused, persistent, and dangerous. Magistrate Bluntnose believes Chok'sul directs attacks on Thelsamar, a nearby dwarven excavation site, and the Stonewrought Dam. Fearing for civilian lives and the valley's great engineering work, he offers a bounty for the ogre chieftain's death by any means. Chok'sul's severed head is required as proof.

quest:261.text: Down the Scarlet Path. At Nijel's Point, Brother Anton calls on you to prove your allegiance to the Scarlet Crusade. Brother Anton says the Scourge must be stopped before it swallows the land and casts the world into darkness. The Scarlet Crusade has pledged itself to that fight. To prove your courage and allegiance, destroy thirty undead ravagers in the Valley of Bones, south of Anton. Succeed, and the Crusade will welcome you.

quest:262.text: The Shadowy Figure. Near his ruined farm, Sven Yorgen seeks the stranger who watched his family die. He gives you a strange book found in the wreckage and asks you to learn who left it behind. In Duskwood’s western hills, Sven Yorgen still grieves for his slaughtered family. He once blamed the black riders who terrorize the woods. Yet he remembers a shadowy figure nearby on the night of the massacre. Sven gives you the strange book found at his ransacked farm, the only physical clue in the wreckage. With no clear trail through the perilous wilderness, you head east to Darkshire. Sven hopes one of the superstitious townsfolk will recognize the curious book. Madame Eva is among them, and her occult senses reach beyond ordinary sight. Her divinations may reveal impressions left on mysterious relics.

quest:265.text: The Shadowy Search Continues. In Duskwood, you trace the journal from Madame Eva to Clerk Daltry in Darkshire. It came from the ruins of Sven Yorgen’s ransacked farmstead. Madame Eva found that the journal’s author was an outsider, though its binding came from Darkshire. Clerk Daltry sells blank ledgers and tomes to traveling scholars, spellcasters, and record-keepers. So you follow those local sales for a clue to the sinister trespasser in Duskwood’s groves.

quest:266.text: Inquire at the Inn. Clerk Daltry sends you from Darkshire to the Scarlet Raven Tavern with a journal from Sven Yorgen's ruined farm. He hopes someone there knows who owned it. Clerk Daltry has finished examining the tattered book from Sven Yorgen's farm. He believes any stranger who came to Darkshire would have passed through its tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern stands across town as Darkshire's only gathering hall and lodging house. There, you may learn who came through and where they went.

quest:268.text: Return to Sven. You bring Jitters' finished journal to Sven Yorgen's camp near Westfall. Its pages may answer the questions that have haunted him since his family's murder. When Sven Yorgen's farm came under attack, Jitters fled into the woods and left an incomplete diary behind. Afraid of Sven's anger and haunted by what he had seen, he hid deep in Duskwood. When you find him, he willingly gives you his finished journal. He hopes the full account will spare him from facing Sven in person.

quest:269.text: Seeking Wisdom. In Stormwind, Sven Yorgen asks Bishop Farthing for holy counsel on Duskwood. He sends Jitters' Completed Journal, hoping the bishop can reveal how to break Morbent Fel's shield. Duskwood suffers beneath old curses and ravenous undead. Stormwind's royal court has grown indifferent, and Sven Yorgen knows ordinary strength cannot pierce Morbent Fel's wards. Broken-hearted, he shelters at a camp near the borders and asks you to carry Jitters' assembled journal to the church. The road north leads to the Cathedral of Light.

quest:270.text: The Doomed Fleet. Bishop Farthing sends you north from Stormwind to find a way through Morbent Fel's wards. Your trail crosses Khaz Modan and ends at the wreck of Kul Tiras's Third Fleet off the Wetlands. Morbent Fel's wards turn ordinary steel aside at his retreat on the Forlorn Rowe. Bishop Farthing sends you to seek a weapon bound to the Holy Light. Its key is Lightforge Iron, a rare consecrated metal whose strikes carry holy truth and pierce sorcerous protections. Duskwood has no Lightforge Iron to hand. Bishop Farthing recalls that Kul Tiras's Third Fleet sank years ago along the dangerous Wetlands coast, north of Ironforge. One galleon carried a shipment of the precious ore. You travel to Menethil Harbor to meet Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven contact who knows the marshes and their wrecks.

quest:272.text: Trial of the Sea Lion. Druids in Moonglade seek the sea lion’s spirit through a sacred rite. They recover two scattered pendant halves for agility and endurance, then unite them at the Shrine of Remulos to prepare for Aquatic Form. Druid initiates in Moonglade undergo trials of attunement as they prepare to navigate Azeroth’s deep waters. The Trial of the Sea Lion follows earlier preparations in their spiritual training. Dendrite Starblaze oversees it in Nighthaven, where initiates learn to balance the sea lion’s graceful speed with its resilient stamina. Both are needed to take its form and withstand the ocean depths. The trial centers on reuniting the two halves of the Pendant of the Sea Lion. One represents the sea lion’s agility as it glides through turbulent currents. The other represents its endurance, the fortitude to dive long into freezing water without faltering. Initiates seek guidance from Moonglade’s inhabitants as they search across the world for the scattered relics. Once both halves are found, the initiate brings them near the Shrine of Remulos, where they can be joined into one talisman. The shrine’s energies bind agility and endurance in harmony. The initiate then presents the restored pendant to Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. With the pendant, the druid shows readiness to embrace the sea lion aspect and awaken Aquatic Form.

quest:2745.text: Infiltrating the Castle. At Stormwind Keep, Elling Trias sends you to meet his fellow operative Tyrion. Tyrion has watched Lord Gregor Lescovar from the royal gardens for weeks. At his cheese shop in the Trade District, Elling Trias sees the Defias threat reaching into the kingdom's rule. Ordinary law cannot expose or punish a nobleman as protected and entrenched as Lord Gregor Lescovar. So Trias offers a dangerous path: deliver justice within Stormwind Keep, outside the law, and sever the conspiracy for good. Elling Trias has an operative in the high halls: Tyrion, a clever gnome skilled at concealment. For weeks, Tyrion has watched the keep's courtyards and royal gardens. He has tracked Lescovar's movements, who enters his chambers, and when the traitor meets covert Defias contacts. You need to reach Tyrion without drawing the Royal Guard's suspicion.

quest:2746.text: Items of Some Consequence. Tyrion needs silk and apples to prepare Spybot for a covert approach to Lord Lescovar in Stormwind Keep. The mechanical spy must pass the royal guards and listen to the noble. Elling Trias, the cheese merchant, has moved the operation against Lord Gregor Lescovar forward. He suspects Lescovar's schemes in Stormwind Keep threaten the realm. Tyrion agrees to the tighter schedule in the keep's gardens, but Spybot's disguise needs careful preparation. Tyrion plans to send Spybot, a small mechanical contraption, past the castle guards to reach Lescovar inside the keep. Its strange disguise as a woman should turn suspicion aside. You gather suitably sized apples from Clara's orchard just outside the city walls, along with bolts of silk for the puppet's clothes.

quest:275.text: Blisters on The Land. Across the eastern Wetlands, Rethiel senses sickness spreading through the marsh. The bog beast warden asks travelers to destroy Fen Creepers, hoping to ease the land’s rising fever. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the Wetlands from a grove among the marshes. The mire has always been harsh, but now an unnatural sickness spreads through it. Rethiel feels fever in the earth. It twists wild nature into mindless, shambling horrors. Fen Creepers are decaying masses of swamp plants that wander the waterways. Rethiel calls them diseased blisters swelling on the land. Their tormented presence agitates the marsh, so Rethiel asks passing allies to destroy them. Their tangled remains can then settle into the mud.

quest:276.text: Tramping Paws. At Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands, Rethiel sees the Mosshide numbers rise near the Gate of Algaz. Their fires and trampling threaten the bog, so Rethiel asks travelers to thin their ranks. Mosshide gnolls lived in the Wetlands for many years without overwhelming the natural order. Now their numbers have surged south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and paws crush rare fen plants, and their logging strips groves for campsite fires. If the packs keep growing, the fragile marsh will suffer. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches the marsh for signs of imbalance. The gnolls' existence is not the trouble; their numbers have grown beyond what the Wetlands can support. Thinning the Mosshide gnolls and mongrels helps preserve the fen and may earn the approval of its ancient guardian.

quest:277.text:
Fire Taboo. In the Wetlands, Rethiel turns concern for the forest into action. The bog beast asks travelers to take the crude flints Mosshide gnolls use to burn living trees, hoping to spare the ancient boughs. Rethiel the Greenwarden feels the Wetlands' trees as kin. Rot and renewal belong to the swamp, yet the Mosshide gnolls cut living timber and feed it to their hearthfires. The groans of those boughs weigh on Rethiel. The Greenwarden can no longer watch the trees suffer in silence. Mosshide gnolls cut green trees for warmth and territory instead of gathering deadwood. Rethiel hopes to curb their spread without a long war, so the bog beast asks you to take the crude flints carried by stronger gnolls. Without those tools, the pack cannot burn the timber it fells.

Rethiel smashes each stone and casts its dust into the sea. There, it can never spark the forest again.

quest:283.text: A Dark Threat Looms. Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh needs you at Stonewrought Dam, where Dark Iron saboteurs have planted a charge. Disarm it before the valley below is in danger. The Stonewrought Dam holds back the waters of the Loch above the lowlands of the Wetlands. An explosive charge now sits inside it, a volatile keg left there by Dark Iron hands. If it goes off, the valley below and the lives downstream will pay for it. It falls to you to apply the Disarming Mixture before that happens, then bring word to Chief Engineer Hinderweir the Seventh.

quest:284.text: The Search Continues. The search for the Menethil Statuette continues among nearby Murloc hovels. These shelters hold no sign of it, so you turn to two more. You search this cluster of Murloc hovels, but find no trace of the Menethil Statuette. Two nearby shelters to the north and northeast may hold clues.

quest:285.text: Search More Hovels. Among the Murloc hovels, you have found no sign of the Menethil Statuette. So you press farther north, seeking the next clue. You believe the Menethil Statuette lies in one of the hovels to the north. So you continue your search among the Murloc dwellings.

quest:286.text: Return the Statuette. Karl Boran in Menethil Harbor needs the Menethil Statuette brought back. It was found inside a barrel pulled from the muck, and its return will ease the Blind Princess's captain. The statuette lay packed in fine straw inside the barrel. It shows a young, long-haired Paladin raising a hammer. Karl Boran in Menethil Harbor is waiting for it. The Blind Princess's captain will be relieved to know the cargo is safe.

quest:288.text: The Third Fleet. Outside the Deepwater Tavern, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks through memories of the Third Fleet. He alone survived its burning off the Wetlands during the Second War. First Mate Fitzsimmons spends his days outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. He nurses a hangover and memories that will not leave him. He once served aboard the Wave Mistress, a ship-of-the-line under Kul Tiras's maritime banner. Now he turns to dwarven mead, and another drink may bring his account of a terrible naval slaughter. During the Second War, the Third Fleet sailed along the shores of Khaz Modan when fire fell from the sky. The Dragonmaw clan had subdued the red dragonflight at Grim Batol and unleashed dragonfire upon the unsuspecting warships. Fitzsimmons remembers wooden hulls burning beneath towering flames as their crews were dragged into the deep. He alone survived and washed ashore. His fallen brothers lie in the watery graveyard known as the Doomed Fleet.

quest:289.text: The Cursed Crew. Off the Wetlands coast, The Cursed Crew haunts the ships where the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras sank. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the fleet's sole survivor, asks travelers to free his lost brethren. A dark relic aboard one wreck binds the drowned sailors and marines to their ships as restless undead. The Third Fleet of Kul Tiras wrecked along the jagged shores north of Menethil Harbor. First Mate Fitzsimmons alone reached land alive. His fellow sailors found no peace beneath the waves. As they died, sorcery from a mysterious treasure hidden deep in one hull bound their souls to the battered timbers and denied them rest.
