quest:29.text: Trial of the Lake. In Moonglade, an initiate faces the Trial of the Lake, a timed test of speed and dexterity. You dive into Lake Elune'ara for an unstable Shrine Bauble, then hurry to the Shrine of Remulos before it decays. Success earns Tajarri's recognition and honors the Cenarion Circle's devotion to balance. Moonglade's guardians oversee this rite for initiates. You dive into Lake Elune'ara to find a delicate Shrine Bauble resting along the sunken lakebed. It begins to decay as soon as you disturb it, so you need a sure touch, keen senses, and swift movement to carry it overland before its magic fades. Once you have the bauble, you must hurry to the Shrine of Remulos in northwestern Moonglade. The monument honors Keeper Remulos, who guides the Cenarion Circle in preserving nature and world balance. Activating the bauble there marks its importance to the Circle. Warden Tajarri greets initiates who beat the time limit and the competition.

quest:290.text: Lifting the Curse. First Mate Fitzsimmons asks you to free his fallen crewmates from a restless curse. He believes an artifact aboard the wrecked Intrepid binds them, and Captain Halyndor’s ghost guards the strongbox key. First Mate Fitzsimmons survived the Third Fleet’s fate, yet memories of his comrades haunt him day and night. He believes an evil object locked in the Intrepid’s strongbox is tied to the undeath gripping his shipmates. Captain Halyndor’s ghost watches the wreck and guards the strongbox key.

quest:2904.text: A Fine Mess. In Gnomeregan, you find Kernobee battered among the troggs after a Dark Iron ambush. His rescue brings word of a drilling rig beneath Dun Morogh, bound for Booty Bay. You find Kernobee in Gnomeregan’s dormitory, beaten and groggy. Dark Iron dwarves ambushed the goblin and left him among the feral troggs. You guide him through the contaminated corridors toward safety.

quest:292.text: The Eye of Paleth. Fitzsimmons asks you to recover The Eye of Paleth from the sunken Intrepid. Then carry the cursed gem to Glorin Steelbrow in Menethil Harbor, where the dwarven priest seeks a way to purge its blight. Beneath Baradin Bay, the Intrepid's locked strongbox holds a blackened orb. The Eye of Paleth pulses under the water, warped from sacred light into a source of suffering. Its corruption binds it to the restless spirits and doom that claimed the sailors of the Third Fleet.

quest:2922.text: Save Techbot's Brain!. Tinkmaster Overspark sends you into Gnomeregan to save Techbot's Brain! and recover its memory core. The machine once aided researchers, but radiation filled the city and an electrical surge during its fall polarized its brain and made its behavior violent. Overspark hopes the core will help him reverse the damage and restore his creation. Before Gnomeregan fell, Techbot aided researchers with its devices and deep technical knowledge. Tinkmaster Overspark designed the mechanical assistant, and its built-in gizmos made it a marvel of gnomish ingenuity. Then the trogg invasion brought chaos, and toxic radiation filled the city. A stray electrical surge jolted Techbot's delicate workings and polarized its positronic brain into a volatile negatronic state. Tinkmaster Overspark needs you to recover Techbot's core, for the machine now wanders Gnomeregan's contaminated halls in a frenzy and attacks anyone in sight. Overspark refuses to abandon his prized assistant as scrap. He asks you to find the machine, remove its memory core from the metal chassis, and bring it to Ironforge. With the core, he hopes to understand the polarization and repair Techbot's mind.

quest:2923.text: Tinkmaster Overspark. In Stormwind, Brother Sarno hears that Techbot has failed and that Tinkmaster Overspark grieves in Ironforge. He sends Alliance adventurers to Tinker Town, where Overspark asks for help recovering Techbot's memory core from Gnomeregan. Brother Sarno tends to travelers in Stormwind City and speaks of trouble among the gnomish refugees. Tinkmaster Overspark, one of the minds behind Gnomeregan's wonders, grieves over Techbot's corruption. The mechanical servant once aided the tinkerers faithfully. Then the city fell into ruin. You take the Deeprun Tram from Stormwind to Ironforge's Tinker Town. There, Overspark seeks adventurers willing to help in Gnomeregan's irradiated halls. He asks them to salvage what remains of Techbot's faculties before the construct causes irreparable harm.

quest:2924.text: Essential Artificials. In Ironforge, Klockmort Spannerspan lacks the components his experiments need. Exiled gnomes fled Gnomeregan during the trogg invasion and radiation disaster, leaving essential artificials in the city's lower halls. When troggs overran Gnomeregan and radiation filled its corridors, the gnomes fled with only what they could reach. Essential artificials remained behind. These specialized mechanical parts work in nearly any device, and tinkers and crafters prize them. Now in Ironforge's Tinker Town, master tinker Klockmort Spannerspan cannot continue his new experiments without a supply. Deep inside Gnomeregan, the components rest in heavy, steam-powered containers called artificial extrapolators. To reach them, you cross irradiated halls where mutated leper gnomes, malfunctioning defense automatons, and feral troggs roam. Klockmort needs twelve components to continue his work, keeping gnomish invention moving through exile.

quest:2925.text: Klockmort's Essentials. In Darnassus, Mathiel carries Klockmort Spannerspan's urgent plea across the sea. Bound to his post, he asks Alliance travelers to find his gnome friend in Ironforge. From the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Mathiel sends word to Dun Morogh. Klockmort Spannerspan needs bold allies for a venture into Gnomeregan, but Mathiel cannot leave his post to travel there. So he asks capable Alliance travelers passing through Darnassus to make the journey in his place. Klockmort Spannerspan works in Tinkertown, Ironforge's district for gnomes driven from their underground city. He plans to recover vital machinery from Gnomeregan's contaminated corridors. Mathiel's referral brings you to Klockmort's workshop, where he needs help reclaiming what was left behind.

quest:2926.text: Gnogaine. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt sends adventurers toward Gnomeregan to gather radioactive fallout. He hopes to make a cure for the leper gnomes, though the brew may become potent drink. Since Gnomeregan fell, refugees such as Gnoarn have sought to kill the trogg invaders and reverse the sickness that changed their kin. Ozzie Togglevolt and his partner Razzle Sprysprocket have taken another path from their workshop in Kharanos. Ozzie says they are trying to make a cure for the leper gnomes. Their formula might instead become very strong rum. Ozzie and Razzle need toxic residue from the heart of the disaster. Ozzie gives adventurers a leaden collection phial and sends them toward Gnomeregan's breached tunnels. Irradiated Invaders and Irradiated Pillagers roam there, troggs saturated with leaking waste. The phial needs their green glow.

quest:2927.text: The Day After. In Ironforge and Kharanos, Gnomeregan's survivors search for an answer to their city's ruin. Gnoarn sends travelers to Ozzie Togglevolt, who studies the contamination and hopes to find a solution. In Ironforge's Tinker Town, Gnoarn mourns Gnomeregan and the loss of his gnomefro. Trogg invaders took the mechanical city, and toxic fallout stripped away his prized mane. Fury toward the troggs and hope of reclaiming the city move him to send sympathetic travelers to colleagues who can salvage what remains. In Kharanos, inventive gnomes have begun to face the fallout. Gnoarn sends travelers to Ozzie Togglevolt, who works with his partner Razzle Sprysprocket. Ozzie remembers the catastrophe, when Gnoarn's locks fell out in clumps and madness and thirst for vengeance took hold. Now Ozzie studies the contamination in the snowbound town, using his engineering skill to seek an antidote.

quest:2928.text: Gyrodrillmatic Excavationators. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent readies tunneling machines for Dun Morogh. Short on parts, she sends you into Gnomeregan to salvage them from rogue automatons. Hundreds of gyrodrillmatic excavationators wait to be made ready in the Dwarven District. Gnomish engineers there aid their displaced kin. The machines will carry people and supplies underground, but these massive rigs cannot work without the mechanical parts Shoni lacks. Gnomeregan once supplied gnomish high technology. Its ruined halls and nearby tunnels still hold machines worth salvaging, though malfunctioning defense bots, mechanical sentries, and clockwork laborers roam unchecked. Shoni sends you into the fallen city for two dozen bundles of robo-mechanical guts, to bring back to human lands. Two dozen bundles of mechanical guts provide enough scrap to repair one excavationator. Shoni still has nearly four hundred machines to prepare, so mass transport underground remains a slow undertaking. Each working machine is a small step toward regaining ground lost in Gnomeregan's fall.

quest:293.text: Cleansing the Eye. In the Wetlands, Cleansing the Eye sends adventurers south to Stormwind with a cursed orb in need of aid. After recovering the Eye of Paleth, they seek Archbishop Benedictus to purge its lingering taint. The Eye of Paleth recovered from the marshlands bears no holy light. Shadow clings to it, along with the sorrow and trauma of the tragedy where it was lost. Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarf, recognizes the orb's power. Yet he lacks the divine craft to lift so heavy a curse. Human priests of the Holy Light first fashioned the Eyes of Paleth, so their highest order alone knows how to undo the defilement. Glorin sends adventurers south to Stormwind with the darkened orb, to Archbishop Benedictus, leader of the Church of the Holy Light. Benedictus knows the danger of leaving such a relic unpurified. He takes on the work of restoring its sacred light.

quest:2930.text: Data Rescue. Master Mechanic Castpipe sends you into Gnomeregan to recover its records. Troggs and radiation drove the gnomes from the city, but the punchograph terminals still guard its archives behind layers of clearance. Troggs and radiation drove Gnomeregan's people from the city, leaving centuries of research, schematics, and civic records behind. Matrix Punchograph terminals still line its technological corridors. They manage security clearance and store files. Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge's Tinker Town wants you to recover those punch-encoded archives from the city's depths. Gnomish mainframes demand clearance in stages. First, find a White Punch Card among the wreckage outside the inner gates. Insert it into the Matrix Punchograph 3005-A in the Train Depot to make a Yellow card. Then take that to the 3005-B terminal in the Dormitory for a Blue card. Model 3005-C advances it to Red. The final terminal, 3005-D, waits in the Engineering Labs, where the Red card becomes a Prismatic Punch Card.

quest:2931.text: Castpipe's Task. In Ironforge, Master Mechanic Castpipe calls travelers to recover Gnomeregan's records. The ruined halls still hold vital mechanical and technical knowledge. After Gnomeregan fell and was sealed under radioactive quarantine, its surviving gnomes found refuge in Ironforge's Tinkertown. Troggs and irradiated constructs still overrun their old home. Deep within the city, computing arrays hold operational records and mechanical schematics. Castpipe seeks outsiders willing to brave the toxic halls and recover files that may explain what went wrong or help the gnomes return. Gaxim Rustfizzle of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences spreads word of Castpipe's effort. Castpipe belongs to no academic body, yet his fellow gnomes respect his skill and support his work. Rustfizzle puts the operation's strategic value at an eighty-four percent chance. Travelers can report to Tinkertown for orders.

quest:294.text: Ormer's Revenge. At Whelgar Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid and his two companions cling to a bluff above the raptor-swarmed dig. Beneath the Wetlands, the dwarves uncovered massive prehistoric bones. Mottled raptors came in packs and killed most of the crew. The dwarves came to Whelgar Excavation Site to uncover massive prehistoric remains beneath the Wetlands muck. Their discovery drew the marsh’s native raptors to the dig. Packs of mottled predators swarmed the site, caught the excavators off guard, and tore through their ranks. Only a handful of dwarves survived. Ormer Ironbraid, Merrin Rockweaver, and Prospector Whelgar scrambled up a bluff above the pit, but aggressive packs still pin them there. Ormer grieves for his fallen comrades and burns with anger, yet stays to guard Merrin and the Prospector. He asks travelers to thin the Mottled Raptors and Mottled Screechers below. This is the first strike in his vengeance.

quest:2945.text: Grime-Encrusted Ring. A Dark Iron dwarf in Gnomeregan carries a ring caked in toxic filth and hardened muck. The Sparklematic 5200 in the Clean Zone dormitory can scour it clean and reveal its markings. Fighting leaves Gnomeregan's corridors coated in toxic sludge, oil, and radioactive fallout. Dark Iron dwarves who infiltrate the city carry trinkets fouled by that filth. One ring bears a crust that ordinary washing cannot remove. Beneath it, the metal may be copper, gold, or junk.

quest:2947.text: Return of the Ring. In Gnomeregan, a golden ring bears a maker’s mark that leads you to Ironforge. You place a grime-caked bauble in Gnomeregan’s Sparklematic 5200. The machine strips away years of irradiated grime, revealing a polished Brilliant Gold Ring that still hums with arcane power. Inside the band, three initials, “TdK,” sit beside Ironforge’s hallmark seal.

quest:2949.text: Return of the Ring. A ring from Gnomeregan bears Orgrimmar's seal and the letters NOG. Its trail leads to Nogg, a goblin engineer with a theory about the ruins. You clean a ring from Gnomeregan in the Sparklematic 5200. The machine strips away the filth and reveals Orgrimmar's official seal, a surge of magical power, and the partly legible letters NOG. Gnomeregan lies deep in Khaz Modan, an Alliance city far from the Horde capital. The ring may have been made in Kalimdor or carried there on a doomed expedition, but its seal points back to Orgrimmar.

quest:295.text: Ormer's Revenge. At the ruined Whelgar Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid sends you after the raptors that drove out his expedition. Their smaller young are already thinned, and now he wants the Mottled Scytheclaws and Razormaws killed. Ormer Ironbraid sends you after the adult raptors in the lower dig. You have already thinned the juveniles that overran the upper camp, but Mottled Scytheclaws and Razormaws still threaten any hope of reclaiming the excavation. They tear through dwarven prospectors and leave the trenches strewn with shattered crates and abandoned picks. Raptors have made nests in the excavation pits. From the ridge above the dig, Ormer directs you into the mud to strike at the mature beasts. Prospector Whelgar and his crew hope to salvage ancient relics, but Ormer is consumed by vengeance. He demands a heavy toll of dead Scytheclaws and Razormaws before he turns to the site's apex terror.

quest:2951.text: The Sparklematic 5200!. In Gnomeregan, the Sparklematic 5200! keeps cleaning salvaged valuables for three silver coins. Gnomish ingenuity keeps it working amid the ruined city's chaos. A pocket of surviving gnomes holds a secure perimeter near the Sparklematic 5200! in Gnomeregan. The machine scrubs harsh subterranean filth from salvaged valuables. Troggs and other subterranean creatures pound on the bulkheads, yet it remains ready for what you bring. Place a grime-caked relic and three silver coins in the Sparklematic, and the cleaning begins. The iron machine groans and vibrates, lurching as it strips away toxic sludge, irradiated grease, and rock dust. Moments later, it expels what lay beneath the muck, from precious minerals to mechanical components.

quest:2952.text: The Sparklematic 5200!. In Gnomeregan, the Sparklematic 5200! takes in soiled salvaged objects and cleans them. Its cycles scour away toxic grime, then wrap whatever remains in a gift box. Feed toxic and contaminated refuse into the Sparklematic 5200!, and its cycles scour away grime and caustic residue. Once loaded and paid, the machine rattles through its routine. A cheerful ding follows, then a bow-tied present holds whatever remains. When Gnomeregan fell to the troggs, radiation and industrial mire buried personal effects and scraps of technology. Feed grime-encrusted objects into the machine, and it may recover gemstones, raw ores and other valuables swallowed when the city was vented.

quest:2953.text: More Sparklematic Action. In Gnomeregan, the Sparklematic 5200 still cleans what can be saved. Left behind when the city was evacuated, it scrubs muck and radioactive sludge from curiosities for a small fee in silver. Before the trogg invasion and the fallout that followed, Gnomeregan's engineers installed automated devices throughout the city. Toxic waste and hostile automatons now fill its corridors. Yet the Sparklematic 5200 follows its exact programming: it needs three silver coins and an artifact caked in grime to begin. The Sparklematic lurches as it sprays an inserted relic with potent gnomish solvents and scrubs it clean. A cheerful chime marks the end of the cycle, and the machine dispenses a neatly packaged box. Inside is whatever salvage remained beneath corrosive trogg slime and toxic filth.

quest:296.text: Ormer's Revenge. Ormer Ironbraid seeks vengeance at Whelgar Excavation Site. He believes Sarltooth led the raptor attack that slaughtered dwarven excavators, and asks you to bring back one of its talons as proof. After the Explorer's League diggers were slaughtered at Whelgar Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid watched the raptors from his ridge. One beast stood larger than the rest. Sarltooth perched above the dig works, where Ormer saw it lead the pack that drove the dwarves out. To Ormer, Sarltooth was more than a wild beast. He believed it had led the attack on King Magni Bronzebeard's subjects. Ormer demands death for the massacre. He sends you up the high paths along the excavation walls to kill Sarltooth. Bring back one of the raptor's formidable talons, and the fallen workers will be avenged. Ormer wants the marshes to know that attacks on dwarven expeditions will not go unanswered.

quest:2962.text: The Only Cure is More Green Glow. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt seeks a cure for the leper gnomes. He needs a pure sample of fallout from deep inside Gnomeregan. Ozzie Togglevolt's first tests outside Gnomeregan gave him no answers. The troggs in Dun Morogh carried too little residue, and what they bore was impure. Now, from his lab in Kharanos, Ozzie seeks a fresh, concentrated sample from deep inside the city. He hopes it will help him find a remedy for the leper gnomes. You need to gather potent fallout from inside Gnomeregan. Irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes fill the lower depths around the Hall of Gears and Clean Zone. Their unstable ooze must be carried in a heavy leaden phial, and the work is dangerous. The fallout quickly loses its potency, so you need to get it to Ozzie's lab in Kharanos in time.

quest:297.text: Gathering Idols. At an excavation site, troggs clutch the carved idols Magmar Fellhew seeks. The relics have driven them into a violent frenzy. Researchers uncovered a large cache of strange, carved stone idols shortly before savage troggs surfaced and overran the excavation site. The attack drove the expedition from the ruins before any formal study could begin. Now the troggs clutch the relics and prowl the site, barring a peaceful return. The troggs seem deeply affected by the idols, beyond merely taking them. Their strange carvings exert an unsettling power that drives the creatures into an uncontrollable rage. Magmar Fellhew wants to study the idols safely and quell the frenzy gripping the area, so he seeks to take them from trogg hands.

quest:2985.text: Call of Water. Swart sends an initiate from Razor Hill toward Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. Earth and fire have tested the shaman; water asks for another kind of understanding. Swart, the shaman trainer in Razor Hill, guides initiates through the elements. Earth teaches endurance, and fire tests their command. Once an initiate can wield flame without being consumed, Swart judges them ready to seek the teachings of water. Islen Waterseer lives on the Barrens coast beyond Ratchet. Travel south along the Southfury River into the Barrens, then east to the shore near a massive shark's carcass. Islen dwells where the waves meet the land, apart from the trainers in Durotar's towns. She guides the Horde in communion with water.

quest:299.text: Uncovering the Past. Prospector Whelgar needs the Goaz Stone's four missing pieces from his overrun dig in the Wetlands. Its inscriptions await translation. Before raptors overran the dig in the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar unearthed the Goaz Stone. His first attempts to read its ancient script found broken references to a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. Four pieces had broken away, leaving passages scattered across the dig. To restore the stone, you search the raptor guarded excavation for four fragments: Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. The pieces lie among loose soil and half excavated relics, watched by aggressive Razormaws and Scytheclaws. Reaching them means facing the marsh's fiercest predators.

quest:2996.text: Seeking Strahad. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye sends warlocks south to Ratchet for harder lessons. A human summoner there teaches arts beyond basic summoning. Gan'rul Bloodeye teaches young warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow. There, they learn to command the Nether. When an apprentice outgrows those lessons, Gan'rul points beyond the city walls. More volatile beings demand a tutor with deeper mastery of dark arcana. Gan'rul sends apprentices to Strahad Farsan, a human sorcerer in a tower above Ratchet's goblin port. Horde and humans may be enemies, yet warlocks look past ordinary faction loyalties. Power, discipline, and ritual knowledge matter more than ancestry. Strahad judges an apprentice by inner hatred and the ability to subjugate, not by skin color.

quest:3001.text: Seeking Strahad. Carendin Halgar sends Horde warlocks across the Great Sea to seek Strahad Farsan. Above Ratchet, a human sorcerer offers them a path beyond basic instruction and toward the difficult art of summoning a felhunter. Carendin Halgar trains warlocks in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. When an initiate outgrows basic instruction, he sends them beyond Lordaeron's ruins to find Strahad Farsan. Halgar warns that Strahad is a living human, but no weakling, and says not to treat him as an enemy. The pursuit of demonic mastery can cross racial and factional lines. Strahad works from the bluffs above Ratchet, the goblin port in the Barrens. Near a stone watchtower, he looks down on the sailors, mercenaries, and merchants below, amused by their blissful ignorance of the Twisting Nether. Horde warlocks may reach him with distrust and simmering hatred in their eyes. Strahad accepts that raw malice as fuel to shape into dark authority.

quest:303.text: The Dark Iron War. At Dun Modr, Motley Garmason leads a desperate defense on the Wetlands' northern edge. The Dark Iron clan holds the town after saboteurs shattered the Thandol Span. The Ironforge Mountaineers keep a tenuous line as they wait for reinforcements that may never come. Dun Modr guarded the southern end of the colossal Thandol Span, the bridge linking Khaz Modan to Lordaeron. Dark Iron saboteurs and demolitionists shattered its archway, cutting off Alliance travel before they overran the stronghold. Motley Garmason and a handful of surviving defenders withdrew to an observation camp just outside town. Without a counterattack, the northern gateway may remain under Dark Iron rule. Dwarven regiments are fighting on distant Alliance battlefields, leaving Motley's small detachment largely to fend for itself. His scouts try to signal Ironforge for relief, but communications falter and promised reserves remain out of sight. To buy time and disrupt the enemy's defenses, Motley orders surgical strikes into Dun Modr's ruins. His aim is to thin the ranks of Dark Iron engineers, tunnelers, and front-line soldiers before they push farther south into the Wetlands.

quest:304.text: A Grim Task. In the Wetlands, Longbraid the Grim seeks vengeance for Dun Modr. The Dark Iron assault shattered the Thandol Span and killed his brother and many soldiers. Now he wants Balgaras the Foul slain, with the warlock's ear as proof. Fighting between Ironforge Mountaineers and Dark Iron infiltrators has scarred the northern Wetlands. Dun Modr fell during the siege, and the western bridge of the Thandol Span was shattered. Longbraid the Grim lost his brother and many loyal soldiers in the assault. He wants the Dark Iron clan to pay for those deaths. Scouts such as Roggo have found that Balgaras the Foul commands the Dark Iron force occupying Dun Modr. The warlock hides while his soldiers carry out his dark designs. Longbraid hopes Balgaras's death will break their resolve. Then Ironforge's survivors may secure the passage north.

quest:305.text: In Search of The Excavation Team. Tarrel Rockweaver waits in the Wetlands for news of Merrin at the Whelgar Excavation Site. Two weeks have passed without a letter, and he fears for the eastern dig. For two weeks, Tarrel Rockweaver has heard nothing from his wife, Merrin. From the Whelgar Excavation Site, she once sent weekly letters about the work. Now Tarrel fears disaster has struck the camp. With dwarf authorities stretched thin, he turns to passing scouts to learn whether the diggers are alive. East in the Wetlands, dwarves at the Whelgar Excavation Site seek ancient Titan relics and history. The crews work in the wild, where beasts and threats from below may find them. The site lies far from the main roads. Whatever stopped the letters has left the diggers beyond easy reach.

quest:306.text: In Search of The Excavation Team. At Whelgar's Excavation site, Merrin Rockweaver sends word after mottled raptors overrun the dig. Her letter tells Tarrel Rockweaver she survived, though most of the expedition did not. Merrin Rockweaver has news for you from the ridge above Whelgar's Excavation site. Her team was uncovering rare artifacts and massive prehistoric fossils when packs of mottled raptors swept through the dig. Most of the crew died in the attack. Merrin and the other survivors remain cut off from Menethil Harbor. At Menethil Harbor, Tarrel Rockweaver learns his wife survived with at least two companions. Ormer's courage helped them escape, and Tarrel's fear eases. Yet the deaths of so many colleagues still weigh on the town and its frontier spirit.

quest:3090.text: Tainted Parchment. A tainted parchment waits for you after your absence, and your teacher Nartok asks to speak with you. Its words challenge Thrall’s rule and warn of the dangers warlocks face. The tainted parchment is believed to come from Nartok, your new teacher. Read it, then speak with him in the Den in the Valley of Trials. He calls the orcs a proud people and says Thrall turns away from power that could make the land theirs.

quest:3091.text: Simple Note. At Camp Narache, Harutt Thunderhorn calls young tauren warriors to defend their people. His summons reminds them that warriors stand beside druids and shamans in guarding the tribal borders from centaur. At Camp Narache, a messenger brings young warriors a summons from Harutt Thunderhorn. The veteran trainer calls each fighter to report and begin training to defend the tribe. The Shu'halo revere their spiritual leaders, yet Harutt teaches that warriors bear an equal burden. They patrol tribal borders and hunt predatory centaur packs to protect their peaceful kin from attack. Battle may bring glory, but warriors remain humble and complete the same traditional rites as shamans and druids.

quest:3095.text: Simple Scroll. A sealed scroll bearing Dannal Stern’s mark finds you while you deal with the Scourge. It calls you to Deathknell, where Dannal speaks of your freedom and offers to teach you. While you were away dealing with the mindless Scourge, a scroll arrived for you. Its seal bears Dannal Stern’s mark. He is the warrior trainer in Deathknell, and the message asks you to read it and speak with him before setting out again. Dannal says others escaped death and fled to town. He sees promise in their resilience. He credits Sylvanas with freeing you in body and spirit, though the plague still afflicts you. He offers to teach you as you gain experience. Sylvanas will need people of your class to help save the Forsaken.

quest:3099.text: Tainted Scroll. In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken warlocks receive a summons bearing Maximillion's name. It calls them back to the ruined settlement to weigh freedom, power, and servitude. Newly risen Forsaken are clearing mindless Scourge remnants around Deathknell when a sealed scroll arrives. It bears the mark of Maximillion, the local warlock trainer. The message asks its recipient to consider servitude and freedom, then return to the ruined settlement and speak with him.

quest:3100.text: Simple Letter. At Northshire Abbey, new warriors are sent to Llane Beshere for training. Their letter calls them to aid the valley's troubled residents. New warriors arriving in Northshire Valley are directed by letter to Llane Beshere, the trainer at Northshire Abbey. They are to meet their instructor and learn the lay of the surrounding land. Then they can prepare for the demands of martial life. The Knights of the Silver Hand guard Northshire Abbey, yet trouble reaches people beyond its protection. Llane Beshere tells new warriors that valley residents need able protectors. He urges them to master their weapons and defend those who live there.

quest:3101.text: Consecrated Letter. At Northshire Abbey, the Consecrated Letter calls new initiates of the Holy Light to training. It sends each bearer to a class trainer and reminds them that their conduct reflects their faith. In Northshire Valley, the Consecrated Letter begins an initiate’s journey in the Holy Light. It calls those newly arrived to find their trainer at Northshire Abbey. There, they can formalize their instruction and take up their duties in the Kingdom of Stormwind. The letter reminds each initiate of the weight of their calling. Those who channel the Holy Light shine before all, symbols of hope to allies and clear targets to adversaries. Their trainer teaches that such power demands discipline. Others will judge the faith by their conduct. The letter begins a lasting bond between student and mentor. As the initiate tests their mettle against threats around Northshire, they are expected to return often to the abbey grounds. There, their trainer guides them toward deeper understanding of combat and divine grace.

quest:3102.text: Encrypted Letter. At Northshire Abbey, Jorik Kerridan summons promising rogues to meet him in secret. His letter points them toward a quiet stable and counsel for the dangers ahead. Northshire Abbey looks peaceful, yet covert talents are recruited within its walls. After dealing with the kobolds, promising novices receive a letter bearing Jorik Kerridan's seal. It is addressed discreetly, away from the priests and paladins. The bearer is sent to a secluded meeting in the stables behind the Abbey. Jorik Kerridan keeps to the stables because they are quiet and draw little notice. When newcomers arrive unseen, he speaks plainly about the wider world. Stormwind's SI:7 and the Defias Brotherhood both seek stealthy operatives. Jorik urges each novice to keep their freedom and resist powerful groups that would push them around. A clever rogue holds the cards.

quest:320.text: Return to Bellowfiz. You bring Evershine to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. After the local hunting, the thirsty driver awaits a fresh drink. After helping with local hunting, you receive a fresh cask of Evershine for Pilot Bellowfiz. Carry it through snowy Dun Morogh to Steelgrill's Depot. Such favors help people on the cold frontier look after one another. Steelgrill's Depot lies just outside Kharanos. Gnomes test machinery, tend vehicles, and practice their craft there. The pilots face freezing winds and welcome a strong local drink. When you arrive with the cask, Pilot Bellowfiz is eager to uncork a bottle and taste the brew made by locals.

quest:321.text: Lightforge Iron. In Menethil Harbor, Glorin Steelbrow seeks cargo lost with an elven destroyer. The Flying Osprey carried rare Lightforge iron when it sank with the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras during the Second War. The Flying Osprey sailed from Lordaeron beside the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras. The elven destroyer carried a precious cargo of Lightforge iron and traveled with the fleet for safety. Then the Dragonmaw clan's enslaved red dragons swept down from the sky. They set the ships ablaze, sending sailors and sanctified metal beneath the waves.

quest:322.text: Blessed Arm. In Stormwind, Glorin Steelbrow sends lightforge iron toward a weapon against Morbent Fel. You bring the rare metal from the wreck of the Flying Osprey in the Wetlands to master weaponsmith Grimand Elmore, who can forge it for the fight. Glorin Steelbrow packs the recovered lightforge iron for Stormwind. Rare and powerful against foul and unholy beings, the metal needs a smith who knows how to work it. The shipment came from the wreck of the Flying Osprey off the Wetlands coast. Glorin knows only one artisan in the southern kingdoms suited to the task: master weaponsmith Grimand Elmore. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Grimand Elmore keeps one of the city's finest anvils. Years have passed since he last hammered lightforge iron, he says, when you bring him the recovered shipment. The veteran artisan welcomes the chance to strike at the necromancer Morbent Fel. He agrees to put his hammer to work.

quest:323.text: Proving Your Worth. In Duskwood, Sven Yorgen tests your strength before you face Morbent Fel. The hermit wants revenge for his family and needs proof you can defeat the undead at Raven Hill Cemetery. Sven Yorgen grieves at a secluded camp north of the howling woods. Fury burns in him over the slaughter of his family. He has learned that the Dark Riders who destroyed his homestead were allied with the necromancer Morbent Fel. Sven wants revenge, but he will not send an untried ally into Fel's grasp. First, he asks you to prove your fighting skill against the skeletons at Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery lies south of Forlorn Rowe, and corpses bound by Fel's magic fill its grounds and mausoleum. Skeletal Raiders patrol among the tombstones with swords. Below, Skeletal Warders and Healers tend the chambers. To earn Sven's trust, you must press deep into the necropolis and clear this vanguard. Mor'Ladim, a vengeful phantom, prowls the cemetery paths.

quest:324.text: The Lost Ingots. Glorin Steelbrow seeks Lightforge iron from a shipwreck off the Wetlands. The chest holds only one ingot, and Bluegill murlocs have taken the rest. The Flying Osprey lies broken off the Wetlands shore. Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven priest, sent you to recover its Lightforge iron. Yet the waterlogged chest in the cargo hold holds only one ingot. Bluegill murlocs near the wreck scavenged the rest of the shipment. Lightforge iron is rare metal, fit for sacred smithing. Glorin Steelbrow needs it for a weapon, so the bars cannot remain in Bluegill camps. The Bluegill raiders hunt the shallows near the broken hull. Reclaim the scattered ingots for Glorin.

quest:325.text: Armed and Ready. You carry Morbent's Bane back to Sven Yorgen, a weapon made to break Morbent Fel's unholy defenses. Ordinary steel cannot break Morbent Fel's hold over Raven Hill cemetery. Blades shatter or glance from the dark wards around him. Grimand Elmore shaped the metal in Stormwind's Dwarven District, and sacred power consecrated it. Now Morbent's Bane can sever Fel's tie to unlife.

quest:328.text: The Hidden Key. Bookie Herod's papers lead you to a strongbox in the Stockpile. Its contents may reveal how Private Thorsen's cover was blown. Bookie Herod's ledgers never name Private Thorsen. But one book hides a small brass key in its binding. Scraps among the papers point to a strongbox in the Stockpile, the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound. Inside may lie the reason Thorsen's cover was blown. Deep in the cave system behind Kurzen's Compound, the strongbox waits among stacked crates. The sturdy chest is heavy and bound in bronze.

quest:329.text: The Spy Revealed!. You have found a muddy note in Bookie Herod's strongbox. Its account of Private Thorsen's daily routines points to an informant among the rebels in northern Stranglethorn Vale, and it is meant for Lieutenant Doren. At the Rebel Camp, the note traces Private Thorsen's patrols, companions, and daily activities. Someone has watched him closely. The signature is only -M, and the detail points to a traitor living beside him in the camp.

quest:330.text: Patrol Schedules. At the Rebel Camp, Lieutenant Doren searches for the writer behind a note signed only with an initial. The writer says they shared patrol routes with Private Thorsen the previous week, and the duty records may reveal their name. A note found at the Rebel Camp bears the initial M. Its writer says they walked regular routes with Private Thorsen during the previous week. That may point to the one aiding the Kurzen forces. Lieutenant Doren sends you to Corporal Sethman, who keeps the duty logs. His records may show who patrolled beside Thorsen.

quest:331.text: Report to Doren. Corporal Sethman sends you to report the patrol findings to Lieutenant Doren. The rebels' commander receives them at Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Corporal Sethman wants you to give Lieutenant Doren a direct account of the patrol information. Bring back what you learned.

quest:335.text: A Noble Brew. Beneath Stormwind, Zardeth of the Black Claw schemes against the city's nobles. Lord Wishock's call for an investigation threatens the hidden warlock coven. Warlocks gather beneath the Mage Quarter in the Slaughtered Lamb, keeping their coven hidden. Lord Wishock, a member of the House of Nobles, has heard of the dark magic below the city. Now he urges his peers to begin a full investigation. The city guard and royal scrutiny could soon fall upon the coven.

quest:336.text: A Noble Brew. Zardeth of the Black Claw sends you to the Royal Keep with Black Claw Stout for Lord Baurles K. Wishock. The brew must reach him in the Hall of Petitioners. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock speaks of his importance and the kingdom’s future. Yet patrons of the Slaughtered Lamb know he drinks in the tavern’s upper rooms at night and leaves large bills unpaid. By day, he petitions to have the tavern shut down.

quest:3369.text: In Nightmares. A shard from the Wailing Caverns brings a troubling vision to Thunder Bluff. You carry the glowing Nightmare Shard to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem on Elder Rise, where it reveals corruption within the Emerald Dream. Falla Sagewind sees the Emerald Dream's pure essence in a strange crystal from the Wailing Caverns. Within it lies a dark, chaotic vision, more waking nightmare than peaceful slumber. Unwilling to speak openly of the omen, she entrusts the shard to you. Then she sends you to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, Thunder Bluff's most venerated elder druid.

quest:337.text: An Old History Book. Milton Sheaf awaits a lost Stormwind chronicle at the Royal Library. The book, The History of Stormwind, bears the library’s seal and vanished before the kingdom rose again after the First War. Its return may help preserve the history of the southern human lands. You find the mud-caked book among the ruins of Duskwood, where undead and ogres roam. Its first page bears Stormwind’s formal library seal, marking it as a rare relic from before the city’s destruction. It was checked out decades ago, before the Horde razed the capital, and was thought lost when the south fell. Milton Sheaf recognizes the book when you bring it to the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep. He plans to place it in the rare books archive, though years in the haunted wilds have badly damaged its pages. The discovery sends Sheaf seeking more lost knowledge in Southshore, the nearest town to Alterac’s ruined kingdom and abandoned libraries.

quest:3370.text: In Nightmares. Falla Sagewind sends a glowing shard to the elder druids in Darnassus. It holds the essence of the Emerald Dream, clouded by dark visions. Falla Sagewind sees more than a crystal in the glowing shard recovered from the depths of Wailing Caverns. Within it lies the pure essence of the Emerald Dream. Yet the shard shows fearful visions where nature should be in harmony. Shaken, Falla will study it no further. She sends you to carry the shard to the senior druids of the Cenarion Circle.

quest:34.text: An Unwelcome Guest. In Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose asks you to stop Bellygrub for good. The wild boar wrecked her garden and trampled her daffodils, and she offers a bounty for his tusk. Martie Jainrose lives in Lakeshire, a town by the lake beneath the gathering shadows over the Redridge Mountains. A wild boar keeps breaking into her garden and ruining the peace of her home. Bellygrub has trampled her daffodils beyond recovery for the season. Now Martie asks travelers to end the animal's rampage. Marshal Marris, who leads Lakeshire's town guard, gave the boar his name: Bellygrub. He spends most of his time rooting through the fields southwest of town. His hunger and boldness bring him close to homes, where he ruined Martie's flower beds. The damage has left her wanting him gone.

quest:343.text: Speaking of Fortitude. Brother Kristoff has sent Head Librarian Milton Sheaf searching the Royal Library for an exact volume. Brother Kristoff is preparing a sermon on the Fortitude of the Spirit. To give his congregation a clear picture of spiritual strength, he turns to metalworking alongside scripture. He hopes a treatise on iron enduring pressure will serve as his example. Head Librarian Milton Sheaf knows the Royal Library's archive by heart. Still, he must check whether it holds the exact title Kristoff seeks. Its centuries of histories, civic writings, and craft works give him plenty to search.

quest:344.text: Brother Paxton. At Stormwind's royal archives, Milton Sheaf sends you to Northshire Abbey for a missing dwarven treatise. The book went there months ago for copying, but it has not returned to the city's shelves. Stormwind's head librarian, Milton Sheaf, is searching for a book missing from the capital's shelves. 'The Stresses of Iron,' a treatise on metallurgical techniques by dwarven prospector Margulf Blaggon, was loaned months ago to the clerics of Northshire Abbey for copying. It was not misplaced in Stormwind. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton tends the library and its books. The Holy Order of Northshire Clerics values knowledge, but copying a long technical manuscript by hand takes time. Paxton admits he has not finished duplicating Blaggon's work. So the original has not yet returned to Stormwind.

quest:345.text: Ink Supplies. Brother Paxton at Northshire Abbey has run short of the ink his writings need. He sends you east to Lakeshire for Rethban ore. Brother Paxton uses his special ink for important writings, including The Stresses of Iron. The ink dries quickly and resists smearing. Yet its recipe has a flaw: left too long, it hardens in the pot. To make a fresh batch, Paxton needs raw Rethban iron ore from the rocky Redridge Mountains. Foreman Oslow has no workers to spare for mining. His laborers are strengthening Lakeshire’s barricades, rebuilding ruined structures, and defending the town from Blackrock orc raids. So you must brave the perilous Rethban Caverns yourself to find the ore Paxton needs.

quest:346.text: Return to Kristoff. In Cathedral Square, Brother Kristoff waits for the return of The Stresses of Iron. After a long search in Northshire, you bring the borrowed book back to the Cathedral of Light. Brother Kristoff waits in Cathedral Square for The Stresses of Iron, a book on metallurgy. Its path led from Stormwind Keep's Royal Library to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton copied it by hand. The work stalled when Paxton ran short of Rethban ore for his ink. Now the ore has been found and the copy is complete. You bring the original book back to Stormwind. Brother Paxton asks you to apologize to Librarian Milton Sheaf for the delay. Northshire's copyists preserve civic and spiritual lore, though their supplies are scarce. Valuable books must be copied stroke by stroke with mineral-rich ink. Only then can they leave the abbey and return to Stormwind's care.

quest:347.text: Rethban Ore. In Redridge, Rethban Ore is needed at Northshire Abbey for its dark color. Foreman Oslow sends you into Rethban Caverns to gather the soft mineral, which cannot make strong weapons or armor. Scribes at Northshire Abbey prize Rethban Ore for its dark, flat color. Bart Rethban discovered it, but the mineral has little use at an armorer’s anvil. Smelted metal from the ore is too weak for sturdy weapons or plate. Its raw color instead makes a valued base for manuscript dyes. The main ore deposits lie in Redridge’s northern mountains, inside Rethban Caverns. Lakeshire’s stoneworkers have left, driven out by a fierce band of Redridge gnolls. The gnolls force drudgers to chip ore from the rocky veins for their own crude purposes. Brother Paxton, a monk at Northshire Abbey, needs the pigment to copy historic texts. His work on The Stresses of Iron has stopped without the proper dye. Messengers and adventurers now travel into gnoll-held territory to bring him the raw stone.

quest:349.text: Stranglethorn Fever. In Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa prepares a chant to draw Mokk the Savage from the jungle. He needs ten Gorilla Fangs to begin. As he communes with the spirits, nearby gorillas come to threaten him. Witch Doctor Unbagwa knows a ritual that can draw Mokk the Savage from the jungle. He asks for ten Gorilla Fangs before beginning the chant. As he communes with the spirits, the chant draws nearby gorillas. They threaten the witch doctor while he tries to finish the ritual.

quest:350.text: Look to an Old Friend. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to find an unusual ally in Stormwind's Trade District. Noble corruption shields traitors from ordinary justice, so Shaw turns to the city's finest cheesemonger and his intelligence network.

quest:3513.text: The Runed Scroll. Found in Kalimdor's wilds, The Runed Scroll bears a formal message from across the border. Its discovery sends Horde scouts to warn the guards at Mor'shan Rampart of activity to the north. A silvery ribbon binds the scroll, unlike the rough leathers and parchment common in the Barrens. Its craft and script point north, to the night elves beneath Ashenvale's canopies. The ridges and roads are contested, so a message taken from the enemy could matter greatly to the Horde's front lines. The scroll belongs with local command, not in the Warchief's hall in Orgrimmar. Kadrak, an orc warrior, watches the border from Mor'shan Rampart, where the Barrens' red earth meets Ashenvale's forests. Bring the scroll to this outpost, and its guards will learn of night elf troop movements.

quest:3514.text: Horde Presence. At the Barrens border, Kadrak sends a Horde champion into Stonetalon Peak after a missive is intercepted. The champion is to kill the dryad Rynthariel and plant a Horde banner inside the Talon Den. Kadrak watches the Barrens’ northern boundary for Alliance and night elf incursions. A messenger carrying a runed scroll is cut down, and Kadrak decodes the missive. It leads him to Rynthariel the Keymaster, an influential dryad in Stonetalon Peak. Rather than merely guard the mountain passes, Kadrak strikes first, hoping to deter future scouts from probing Horde territory. Horde warriors enter the Talon Den, a cavern overlooking Stonetalon Peak. Killing Rynthariel strikes at the night elves’ local coordination. Kadrak’s banner is planted inside the cave. Its red standard marks the heart of dryad territory with a warning: incursions into the Barrens will meet decisive violence.

quest:3567.text: To the Top. Marli Wishrunner offers you a view from one of Feralas's twin colossals, with one warning: the way up is one way. Marli Wishrunner can send you to the top of one of Feralas's twin colossals for a view. She warns you to think about how you will get down. The journey goes only one way.

quest:359.text: Forsaken Duties. Magistrate Sevren needs word from Tirisfal Glades' eastern border. He fears Scourge may slip past The Bulwark and threaten nearby settlements. Magistrate Sevren watches over Brill and the countryside, keeping wary eyes on Tirisfal Glades' eastern border. The Scourge swarm across the Western Plaguelands, so sentries must report what they see. Sevren sends you south along the main road, then east, to bring back Deathguard Linnea's assessment. Deathguard Linnea watches the frontier from an outpost beside the eastern road. Her report confirms Sevren's fears. The Bulwark holds the main Scourge host, but small groups sometimes slip past its defenses. Those strays gather around nearby Balnir Farmstead, threatening Tirisfal Glades.

quest:3633.text: Goblin Engineering. Among master inventors, Goblin Engineering offers a path to command explosive power and volatile concussive ordnance. Its craft relies on high-yield blasting powders and relentless firepower, making it a destructive choice beside intricate tinkering. Azeroth's engineers follow two distinct philosophies. Goblin tinkerers favor violent combustion, while other inventors make delicate clockwork and subtle devices. Goblins harness blasting powder to build tools of great devastation, turning fire, shrapnel, and concussive force toward practical problems. Goblin engineers make no secret of the hazards. Recruits work with volatile compounds, heavy incendiaries, and prototypes that may singe their creator's eyebrows or level an opposing barricade. They prize maximum yield and destructive power, and welcome engineers who choose decisive firepower over fragile safety rules.

quest:373.text: The Unsent Letter. A sealed letter from Edwin VanCleef awaits Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect. Its delivery brings their shared past to light. A sealed letter rests in Edwin VanCleef's clothing aboard his juggernaut beneath Moonbrook. Newly penned, it bears Baros Alexston's name. VanCleef chose the City Architect, not a criminal lieutenant or financier.

quest:3765.text: The Corruption Abroad. In Stormwind, Argos Nightwhisper seeks adventurers to aid his brother in northern Kalimdor. Gershala studies a spreading decay in Darkshore, where he needs fresh hands. Stormwind faces internal turmoil and unrest in its surrounding regions. Even so, envoys from distant kaldorei lands walk its stone streets. Argos Nightwhisper seeks seasoned champions willing to look beyond human borders. The kaldorei are relatively new allies to the Eastern Kingdoms, and formal military aid is scarce. So families and researchers recruit independent champions who will answer the call. Argos points you toward auberdine, a misty port on Darkshore’s fog-shrouded coast. His brother Gershala studies an ominous malaise afflicting the local wildlife and flora. Reaching him means a long voyage from stormwind harbor across the Great Sea. It is a traveler’s first true passage into Kalimdor’s ancient wilderness.

quest:377.text:
Crime and Punishment. In Darkshire, Crime and Punishment begins with a sentence the capital has overturned. Councilman Millstipe seeks Dextren Ward, held in the Stormwind Stockade, after the House of Nobles spared him from Darkshire's death sentence. Ward had been caught robbing graves for the necromancer Morbent Fel. Duskwood already suffers beneath creeping horrors and indifference from the capital. Dextren Ward was caught digging fresh corpses from Darkshire's cemetery. He sold them to Morbent Fel, a necromancer.

Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced Ward to beheading. Before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles claimed him as an imperial prisoner. They transferred him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade. To Councilman Millstipe and Darkshire's grieving citizens, sparing Ward was an intolerable insult. The nobles in their secure city showed complete disregard for frontier families whose dead relatives had been fed into Fel's dark craft.

Frustrated by Stormwind's meddling, Millstipe recruits daring mercenaries to infiltrate the riotous Stockade. They are to assassinate Ward in his cell and sever his hand as proof of execution.

quest:378.text: The Fury Runs Deep. Motley Garmason seeks vengeance against Kam Deepfury, held in Stormwind's Stockade. Deepfury planned the assault on the Thandol Span, where Bronzebeard defenders died, including Longbraid the Grim's brother. Stormwind keeps Deepfury as a political prisoner, so Motley asks an adventurer to carry out dwarven justice. The Wetlands' northern reaches remain troubled by clashes between Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and Dark Iron insurgents. When the Thandol Span came under attack, sabotage killed several dwarves, among them Longbraid the Grim's brother. Roggo uncovered intelligence showing Kam Deepfury planned the strike. Rather than face execution on the front lines, Deepfury was taken to Stormwind's Stockade as a political prisoner, not executed for murder. Motley Garmason is stationed at Dun Modr, and he will not let Stormwind's political calculations shield a war criminal. To him, human law puts decorum before blood debts. Bound to remain beside Longbraid in the Wetlands, Motley sends trusted champions into the rioting Stockade beneath the human capital. They are to take Deepfury's head and settle the clan's score.

quest:386.text: What Comes Around.... In Lakeshire, Guard Berton presses for Targorr the Dread's execution. The Blackrock orc remains in Stormwind Stockade despite his sentence, while political delays keep justice out of reach. Targorr the Dread earned his name in the Redridge Mountains. He served as supreme executioner under General Gath'Ilzogg, chieftain of the Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep. Even among the invaders, his cruelty was notorious. He oversaw the torture and execution of many Redridge defenders. After his capture, Stormwind sent him to its high-security prison, the Stormwind Stockade, and condemned him to die for his crimes against the realm.

quest:387.text: Quell The Uprising. Beneath Stormwind, Warden Thelwater calls for help as the Stockade erupts in riot. Defias prisoners have seized the cell blocks, and he wants the uprising crushed before the city's leaders learn how badly the prison has failed. The Stockade holds criminals, conspirators, and outlaws who threaten the Kingdom of Stormwind. Now Defias operatives have risen in sudden violence and seized the cell blocks from the guards. Armed prisoners crowd the corridors, and order has broken down. The guards depend on visiting champions to fight through the riot and retake the prison. Warden Thelwater orders Defias prisoners killed on sight. Desperate and afraid for his position, he suspects foul play behind the coordinated mutiny. He fears losing his post if the House of Nobles or the wider nobility learns the Stockade is out of control. He hopes a death sentence for insurgency will break the inmates' resolve and crush the rebellion before word passes the canal gates.

quest:388.text: The Color of Blood. Nikova Raskol grieves for Mac, her young grandson, killed inside Stormwind City's prison. Anger consumes her, and she sends adventurers into The Stockade to take the Defias gang's red bandanas in retribution. Mac Raskol was fourteen when he took up arms as a guard in The Stockade. Stormwind's regular soldiers had gone to distant fronts, so volunteers and the city's youth took on local defense. Mac watched hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood. The prison was far more dangerous than his experience could prepare him for. The Defias inmates tore apart their wool prison blankets and fashioned red bandanas from the scraps. The color marked their loyalty to the Brotherhood, even behind prison walls. Mac rebuked them and tried to enforce discipline. The prisoners stabbed him in the back, and he died on the stone floor. After Mac's pointless death, Nikova Raskol turns from official channels to cold revenge. She sends you into The Stockade to quell the rioting prisoners and bring back ten of their cherished red bandanas. Dyed the color of her grandson's spilled blood, the tokens offer a broken family a grim sense of closure.

quest:389.text: Bazil Thredd. Beneath Stormwind, a Defias prisoner may know what the Brotherhood still intends. After an unsent letter is found in the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston sends you to the Stockade for answers. Baros Alexston and Edwin VanCleef once led the Stonemasons Guild. The masons rebuilt Stormwind after the First and Second Wars. Yet when the white walls and towers were complete, the nobility refused to pay the wages they had promised. Some senior masons received government posts to quiet them. VanCleef would not leave the rank-and-file laborers behind. He led a violent riot out of the city and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:391.text: The Stockade Riots. At Stormwind's prison gates, Warden Thelwater sends you into the Stockade Riots to prove your loyalty to the city guards. The uprising has seized the prison, and he orders you to find and execute its ringleader, Bazil Thredd. Beneath the Mage Quarter's cobblestones, the Stockade has fallen into lawlessness. Criminals, Defias insurgents, and violent cutthroats have broken containment and seized the cell blocks. The prison is now an impenetrable war zone. Warden Thelwater and his guards hold desperately to the entrance, unable to push inside and restore order by ordinary means.

quest:392.text: The Curious Visitor. After the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater has found a troubling link to Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, a man called Maelik visited Thredd with papers that passed inspection. After the riot, Warden Thelwater learned that Bazil Thredd’s former comrades had not abandoned him. For months, a quiet visitor met with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized papers, and gave his name as Maelik. Thelwater suspects those visits helped coordinate the bloody uprising. He sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston with a description, hoping to learn who the visitor was.

quest:393.text: Shadow of the Past. The trail from a Stockade prisoner leads into Stormwind’s hidden dealings in Shadow of the Past. Baros Alexston sends you to Mathias Shaw after a mysterious visitor spoke with Bazil Thredd. Baros Alexston cannot name the visitor who spoke with Bazil Thredd, the Stockade’s chief prisoner. Warden Thelwater’s account brought investigators to Stormwind’s city architect, but he has no name to give. So Baros points you to Master Mathias Shaw. Shaw leads SI:7 and makes it his business to know Stormwind’s secrets.

quest:394.text: The Head of the Beast. In Stormwind, The Head of the Beast takes you from Elling Trias to Master Mathias Shaw in Old Town. Your report of Lord Gregor Lescovar’s death confirms your place in Stormwind’s covert intelligence network. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind’s covert apparatus through SI:7 from hidden chambers in Old Town. When you report Lescovar’s death, Shaw recognizes your skill and ruthlessness. He praises your efficiency and thanks you for serving the people of Stormwind.

quest:395.text: Brotherhood's End. In Stormwind Keep, questions remain after Lord Gregor Lescovar is killed. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston and warns you to keep the killer's identity quiet. Baros Alexston, the City Architect who helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, is relieved that Lescovar is dead. Edwin VanCleef had marked Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort for vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat to the kingdom's architects and nobility has passed.

quest:396.text: An Audience with the King. At Stormwind Keep, the Defias report comes before the Crown. After a long inquiry through Westfall and the Deadmines, you bring City Architect Baros Alexston's findings to the capital. Edwin VanCleef has fallen, and the conspiracy beneath Moonbrook is broken. City Architect Baros Alexston prepares an official report for the Crown. He believes you should be honored for ending the guild's criminal enterprise. So you carry the findings across Stormwind's grand canals to Stormwind Keep, expecting to meet the realm's ruler.

quest:397.text: You Have Served Us Well. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb, Stormwind's warlocks have secured a refuge. They report to Zardeth of the Black Claw, whose cabal has kept the city guard and curious nobles at bay. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb, Stormwind's warlocks practice their dark arts, tolerated so far by the authorities. Lord Wishock threatens to expose their hidden studies or bring them to an end. So the coven gives him a tainted draught, and his death preserves their refuge beneath the inn.

quest:401.text: Wait for Sirra to Finish. In Darkshire's Town Hall, Sirra Von'Indi writes as he deciphers Abercrombie's cryptic note. Dread settles over the room, and the hermit's words hint at danger. Sirra Von'Indi has the note Abercrombie sent from his seclusion. He aids the Night Watch and Darkshire's leaders, and needs only a short time to decipher the message. He does not yet know what horrors the words conceal.

quest:4021.text: Counterattack!. At Regthar Deathgate’s outpost west of the Crossroads, Kolkar warriors strike back for their fallen leaders. Reinforcements have crossed from Desolace under Warlord Krom'zar. The Kolkar have been humiliated in the Barrens. Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark are dead, leaving the remaining centaur shattered and without direction. News of their defeat crosses the mountains to Desolace, their ancestral homeland. There, hardened Kolkar warriors rally instead of scattering into the scrubland. Burning for blood and retribution, they enter the Barrens and march against the young Horde encampments.

quest:416.text: Rat Catching. In the western foothills, tunnel rat kobolds trouble the roads into Thelsamar. Mountaineer Kadrell calls on travelers to drive them back and bring proof of the cull for a bounty. West of Thelsamar, tunnel rat kobolds have made dens in the foothills of Loch Modan. They foul the surrounding ground and trouble the roads leading into town. Their warrens threaten the safety and cleanliness of those roads. Mountaineer Kadrell has set a bounty on the tunnel rat kobolds. He asks passing travelers to bring their severed ears as proof of the cull. Then he pays coin and compensation, though the trophies are foul to inspect.

quest:434.text: The Attack!. Tyrion and Elling Trias draw a traitor into a garden meeting inside Stormwind Keep. Their plan puts his Defias contact within reach. Inside Stormwind Keep, an automaton disguised as Priestess Tyriona brings word to the library: Lescovar’s guest has arrived. Lord Gregor Lescovar sends his guards away and leaves for the quiet garden. The guest is Marzon the Silent Blade, an assassin tied to the Defias Brotherhood. But Tyrion, a spy working with the cheese merchant Elling Trias, has fed Marzon false information, and it has drawn him within their reach.

quest:442.text: Assault on Fenris Isle. High Executor Hadrec sends Forsaken agents to Fenris Isle. They are to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of Thule Ravenclaw, the necromancer commanding the island stronghold in Lake Lordamere. The Forsaken hold the western roads and have made their presence known at the Sepulcher. Yet the Scourge remain entrenched in Fenris Keep, on an island in Lake Lordamere east of Silverpine Forest. Their forces threaten the forest and the southern waterways that lead toward the Undercity. High Executor Hadrec sees Thule Ravenclaw’s experiments as a danger to Forsaken control of Silverpine. From the keep, Thule commands the Scourge close to the Forsaken shore.

quest:453.text: Finding the Shadowy Figure. Sven Yorgen's farm has been devastated, and Finding the Shadowy Figure turns toward the stranger who fled it. Tavernkeep Smitts points the search west from Darkshire into Duskwood's haunted woods. Sven Yorgen pleads for help identifying the figure who fled his devastated homestead. The trail leads to the Scarlet Raven Tavern, where Tavernkeep Smitts offers several clues. The fugitive was a complete stranger to Darkshire, nervous and jittery, and left the faint lamps at the town's edge in haste. He vanished into the wilderness to the west.

quest:4542.text: Message to Freewind Post. At Thousand Needles' western approaches, Brave Moonhorn sends an urgent warning to Freewind Post. Centaur raids are rising, and he reports strange behavior among the Grimtotem. Brave Moonhorn watches Thousand Needles' western approaches. Centaur attacks have risen sharply, and the border sentries need to alert their leaders. So Moonhorn asks you to carry a dispatch southeast to Cliffwatcher Longhorn, commander of the mesa settlement at Freewind Post. Cliffwatcher Longhorn confirms that centaur recently intercepted and slaughtered a supply caravan. Freewind Post must defend itself and answer the attack. Moonhorn also warns you to avoid the nearby Grimtotem tauren. Their strange, hostile behavior points to growing divisions across the arid flats.

quest:455.text:
The Algaz Gauntlet. At Dun Algaz, orcs have seized the pass between Loch Modan and the Wetlands. The Dragonmaw threaten Ironforge's route to Menethil Harbor, so Mountaineer Rockgar sends Alliance travelers to strike them and carry word to Valstag Ironjaw. Crags divide Loch Modan from the Wetlands, and Dun Algaz is the way across. It is the only overland mountain pass between them, and Ironforge depends on it for trade, troop movements, and supplies bound for Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's main coastal port in the region.

If the pass falls, Ironforge loses its route to the western seas. Isolated outposts would also lose access to dwarven reinforcements. Dragonmaw remnants have haunted the hills and ruins of the Wetlands since the Second War. Now they have pushed into Dun Algaz in an organized assault, seizing the tunnels and fortifying the pass with their scouts and grunts.

Mountaineer Rockgar asks Alliance travelers to slay the orcs and carry word of the attack to Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor.

quest:4581.text: Kayneth Stillwind. In Ashenvale, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire sends a scouting report east from Astranaar. Druid Kayneth Stillwind needs help watching corruption spread through the ancient woods. In Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire watches over western Ashenvale. Kayneth Stillwind, a druid at Forest Song in the eastern forest, has asked her to judge the region's security. Shifting wildlife and dark omens along the coasts and through the woods trouble him. So Swiftfire seals her observations in a note and entrusts it to a traveler crossing the dangerous central forest. The road to Forest Song crosses Nightsong Woods, where satyrs encroach, wildlife turns hostile, and the Horde ventures from the south. At the shrine, Kayneth Stillwind studies the balance of Ashenvale's natural spirits. Swiftfire's report confirms his fear: corruption spreads through the forest, neither confined to one place nor passing quickly. The druids need more help to confront the wickedness taking root.

quest:463.text: The Greenwarden. From Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons sends Alliance travelers northeast into the Wetlands marshes. They seek a mysterious being rumored to dwell among the beasts. At Menethil Harbor, sailors and wanderers trade stories of a beast lurking in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons calls the Greenwarden an appetite with legs and those who seek it gullible. Leave the dry road, he warns, and ol’ Greenie will bite you in two. To the folk on the docks, anything huge in the murky waters is another man-eating danger in the marsh.

quest:464.text: War Banners. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist sends Alliance champions against Dragonmaw orcs gathering strength in the Wetlands. He wants their banners taken from a camp northeast of town. During the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan held the red dragonflight captive at Grim Batol. When their control broke, the freed dragons hunted their captors nearly to extinction. The few orcs who survived fled Grim Batol into the high mountains east of Whelgar's Excavation, hiding from the red flight's wrath. Dragonmaw survivors have gathered again northeast of Menethil Harbor. They have raised a war camp and planted crimson standards in the marsh. Captain Stoutfist sees danger in an armed orc force so near the harbor town. He wants their ranks thinned and their banners torn down as proof of defeat.

quest:465.text: Nek'rosh's Gambit. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist braces for Nek'rosh's assault. The Dragonmaw chieftain has built catapults to batter the port, while fighting at Dun Algaz blocks reinforcements. You are sent into the marshes to destroy the engines before they reach the town. Dwarven scouts uncovered the plan while Alliance fighters clashed with Dragonmaw raiders. Chieftain Nek'rosh has overseen the building of full-scale siege catapults in the Wetlands encampments. He means to bring them to Menethil Harbor and batter its fortress walls. The attack threatens the Alliance's main shipping hub on the western coast. Fighting and greenskin activity clog the mountain passes at Dun Algaz. The lowlands are cut off from Ironforge's main garrisons, so Captain Stoutfist cannot spare troops to guard the harbor's perimeter. Without aid from Khaz Modan, Menethil's survival depends on sabotaging the catapults before they can be brought against the town. Scouts carry Dwarven Tinder into the heart of the Dragonmaw encampment. There, they must set the timber catapults ablaze and destroy them. This will strip Nek'rosh of his artillery and deny his warriors the firepower to break Menethil's defenses. The engines must be ruined before the warlord can be confronted.

quest:466.text: Search for Incendicite. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear seeks samples of volatile incendicite ore from the Wetlands. He believes its explosive force could change dwarven artillery, and needs you to reach a secluded cave and bring back the dangerous mineral. Siege engine pilots and mechanics at Steelgrill's Depot have heard of rare, unstable ore. Rich veins are rumored in a cavern northwest of Algaz Gate, in the Wetlands. Careless miners there risk having the reactive mineral detonate in their faces. Pilot Stonegear sees military promise in the ore. Refined correctly, it could power dwarven artillery or serve as its payload. Cannon shells might gain enough force to break fortified defenses. He wants raw samples so researchers can test smelting methods without blowing up the depot.

quest:467.text: Stonegear's Search. At Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Stonegear seeks rare ore to strengthen his tank's weapons. He asks you to find fresh fuel for its firepower. Pilot Longbeard or Mountaineer Kadrell may send you to hear Stonegear's proposal. The ambitious pilot wants his siege engine to hit harder, and word of his plans has spread through Ironforge and Loch Modan. At the proving ground and staging yard just east of Kharanos, Stonegear seeks prospectors to search for rare, volatile ore. He believes it can greatly increase his tank's firepower.

quest:468.text: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. At Dun Algaz, Mountaineer Rockgar is preparing an expedition into the Wetlands. Mountaineer Kadrell sends you north from Loch Modan to join him in the sodden lowlands along the pass between the dwarven homeland and the northern territories. Dun Algaz cuts through the northern ridge between Loch Modan and the marshy Wetlands. Trade, messengers, and military detachments pass through this fortified route between Ironforge and Alliance settlements farther north. As tensions rise along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell watches the road and seeks hardy volunteers for the northern outposts.

quest:469.text: Daily Delivery. In the Wetlands, Daily Delivery takes cured crocolisk hides toward Menethil Harbor. Einar Stonegrip asks travelers bound for town to carry them to a local tanner. Einar Stonegrip hunts the Wetlands, especially the aggressive crocolisks along its waterways. Their skins are valuable, but bringing them to Menethil Harbor means going home. His marriage to Sida is going through a rough patch, so Einar would rather stay in the field than face her. He gives his parcels to travelers heading toward town. James Halloran tans hides in Menethil Harbor. Local hunters bring him leather for boots and goods suited to merchants and sailors passing through the port. Einar has been away for a week, and Halloran guesses that a quarrel with Sida explains the delivery by proxy. He wonders whether his own wife should step in and make peace with her.

quest:470.text: Digging Through the Ooze. In Menethil Harbor, Sida needs her bag back from the ooze that swallowed it. She fled Ironbeard's Tomb when foul oozes filled the barrows. Sida lives in Menethil Harbor and often travels northeast into the Wetlands to pay homage at Ironbeard's Tomb. On her latest visit, foul, dripping oozes filled the ancient barrow. In panic, she hurled her satchel at one of them. The ooze swallowed the bag whole, giving Sida just enough time to flee back to the port town. Now she asks travelers to search for it. Near Dun Modr, the contested stronghold, Ironbeard's Tomb holds the remains of a storied dwarven hero. Corruption in the surrounding marshland draws amorphous, acidic slimes that consume anything in their path. Sida cannot remember which creature swallowed her belongings. Search the tomb grounds and cut through the creeping blight to find her drenched satchel.

quest:471.text: Apprentice's Duties. In Menethil Harbor, James Halloran needs giant crocolisk hides for his trade. His apprentice has been mauled in the marshes, so Halloran asks travelers to take up the dangerous hunt. James Halloran sent his young apprentice into the Wetlands marshes to skin giant crocolisks. When the boy failed to return, Halloran went looking and found him badly mauled. Menethil Harbor's tradesmen rely on materials from the surrounding country, though the bogs make such work dangerous. The town midwife believes Halloran's apprentice will live, though the attack cost him a leg. Halloran needs hides for his trade, and he wants vengeance on the beasts that tore into the boy he loves like a son. He asks you to go north along the coast, past the murloc hovels, and hunt the giant crocolisks.

quest:472.text: Fall of Dun Modr. At Dun Modr, Dark Iron forces have broken the northern fortress and its garrison. In Menethil Harbor, a badly wounded survivor asks an Alliance adventurer to go north and learn whether Longbraid the Grim or any defenders lived. For generations, Dun Modr guards northern Khaz Modan and the vital road and bridge across the Thandol Span. They link the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. After an ambush at the bridge, the garrison falls back to regroup inside the fortress. Before the defenders can restore their defenses, overwhelming Dark Iron forces strike and drive them into a desperate flight. Harlo Barnaby, a young defender, is gravely wounded when a stray axe strikes his back during the retreat. Believing him doomed, Longbraid the Grim and the remaining troops strap Barnaby to their last surviving horse and send him south to Menethil Harbor. He survives and wakes in the harbor tavern, burdened by survivor's guilt. He has no idea whether any of his comrades escaped alive.

quest:473.text: Report to Captain Stoutfist. In Menethil Harbor, Valstag Ironjaw sends proven fighters to Captain Stoutfist as the Dragonmaw threat spreads across the Wetlands. The harbor is an Alliance military post, and the captain directs its defense from the keep. For years, dwarven mountaineers have watched Dun Algaz's narrow passes. Now the Dragonmaw clan has returned beyond Loch Modan. The orcs push outward, raise encampments, and threaten the marshlands. Valstag Ironjaw knows the pass is only the first part of keeping the road to Ironforge safe. Captain Stoutfist directs Menethil Harbor's defenses from the war room inside Menethil Keep. Dark Iron saboteurs, local beasts, and marsh murlocs threaten the port. So the captain relies on capable volunteers to meet dangers beyond the walls. Valstag sends you to carry out direct orders against the Dragonmaw war machine.

quest:4736.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Alliance warlocks cross the sea to find Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. From Strahad Farsan's tower above Ratchet, she teaches seasoned practitioners to craft tools and garments that strengthen their hold over demons. Briarthorn can tell when a warlock has moved beyond basic demonology and resisted corruption. He sends those pupils beyond Ironforge, across the sea to Kalimdor, rather than keeping them beneath the mountain. There, an artisan of greater skill can teach them practical felcraft. Strahad Farsan keeps a solitary tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. Warlocks often set aside racial and political borders to survive in a world wary of dark magic. Menara Voidrender stays at Strahad's sanctuary and works with warlocks of every allegiance. She helps them sharpen their craft and keep their summoned fiends bound.

quest:4737.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Zevrost sends warlocks from Orgrimmar to find Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. He fears fel magic will enslave them, yet directs them to a mentor who can help shape powerful arcane vestments. Beneath Orgrimmar, warlocks gather in the Cleft of Shadow, where others tolerate them uneasily. Zevrost, one of their bitter tutors, scorns acolytes who seek mastery of the dark arts. He believes each step deeper into fel magic brings them closer to enslavement. To Zevrost, demonic addiction will claim every practitioner in time. Even the most disciplined scholar will become a thrall of the Twisting Nether. Zevrost knows that other warlocks see a different path. Word has reached Orgrimmar of Menara Voidrender, a skilled warlock on the bluffs above Ratchet, the neutral goblin port. Menara seeks promising disciples to help craft special implements for their arcane might. For warlocks eager to advance their craft, her summons begins the making of the legendary Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. Menara waits high above Ratchet, where warlocks face the hard truths of their order. They must set aside racial and cultural rivalries and support one another. The demons they bargain with show neither prejudice nor mercy to anyone who falters. Sharing knowledge and crafting protective vestments is practical, not charitable.
