Warlocks need both to survive the hostile beings they bind to their service.

quest:4738.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. An Alliance warlock is sent across the Great Sea to seek Menara Voidrender. From a tower above Ratchet, she trains warlocks of every faction in binding and artifact making. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Demisette Cloyce trains warlocks with strict standards. When a student is ready to make powerful items, Demisette seldom believes they are prepared. Yet the cabal's higher authorities order the student onward, far from the capital, to prove their mettle. Menara Voidrender keeps her laboratory in a stone tower above Ratchet, the goblin port in the arid hills of the Barrens. There she takes apprentices of every race and allegiance, beyond Stormwind's laws and Orgrimmar's watch. The fiends and demons warlocks face bear the same malice toward every mortal soul.

quest:4739.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Menara Voidrender awaits Horde warlocks seeking deeper study in Ratchet. From the Undercity, they cross the Great Sea to her refuge above the port. Kaal Soulreaper watches warlocks grow more skilled in the Undercity. When one outgrows simple hexes and impish thralls, he sends them across the Great Sea for specialized instruction. Demonic control leaves little room for error. A skilled mentor can help a warlock survive the Nether’s volatile powers. Strahad Farsan’s tower rises from a high bluff above Ratchet. There, away from the scrutiny of city guards, practitioners such as Menara Voidrender teach younger initiates. Warlocks from different backgrounds set tribal and political rivalries aside. The demons they bargain with will consume human, orc, or Forsaken alike if their summoner’s will falters.

quest:474.text:
Defeat Nek'rosh. In the Wetlands, the Alliance closes in on Nek'rosh and his Dragonmaw warband. Their catapults are burning, but Menethil Harbor remains under threat until the chieftain falls. The Dragonmaw have long plagued the marshlands of Khaz Modan. They hold fortified camps and threaten Menethil Harbor's sea lanes. After the clan's catapults are found and burned, the marsh's defenders strike at the warband's leader. Chieftain Nek'rosh commands the local orcs and remains the last obstacle to breaking the siege. Without him, the remaining raiders lose their leader's direction. Bring Nek'rosh's severed head to Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor, and Ironforge's garrison will claim a major victory. The Dragonmaw have lost their heavy siege weapons and their chieftain, a blow they are unlikely to recover from quickly.

Menethil Harbor is the Alliance's main lifeline between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan. With Nek'rosh fallen, its docks and trade vessels are safer from sudden attack.

quest:4767.text: Wind Rider. At Freewind Post, Elu hopes to join the Horde’s wind riders. He asks you to gather wild wyvern eggs at Highperch, where the Horde needs more mounts. Across Kalimdor, wind riders carry Horde couriers, scouts, and warriors over long distances. At Freewind Post, young tauren Elu hopes to join their ranks. The Horde needs more mounts, so Elu has been asked to help find new wyverns for its master wind riders. He asks travelers for help. Highperch rises above the Thousand Needles mesas and is a prime nesting ground for wild wyverns. To gather viable eggs, you climb the cliffs and face adults guarding their roosts. Elu hopes the eggs will prove his dedication. Then he can begin raising and training wyverns for the Horde’s flight masters.

quest:4770.text: Homeward Bound. Pao'ka Swiftmountain is stranded among the wyverns of Highperch. You are helping the young tauren naturalist reach the canyon floor and return toward Whitereach Post after he wandered into their nesting grounds. Pao'ka Swiftmountain came to Thousand Needles with the elder Motega Firemane. They meant to study the canyon floor's wildlife and towering stone pillars. Curious and too sure of himself, Pao'ka went alone into Highperch to watch its wyverns up close. The territorial beasts drove him off. Now the young scholar has spent days frightened and stranded among the crags. Aggressive wyverns guard their clutches and high roosts throughout Highperch. You clear a way through the nesting predators so Pao'ka can reach level ground. The panicked youth cannot defend himself in the open, and relies on passing Horde travelers to fend off the wyverns. He needs to reach the safer canyon path leading east.

quest:480.text: The Weaver. In Silverpine Forest, Ataeric works to wake a dormant ley node for Dalaran. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends you to stop the archmage and take his staff, lest Dalaran’s magic threaten Forsaken control of southern Lordaeron. After your earlier inquiries into Ambermill and Dalaran’s movements, the Forsaken learned that its wizards seek to wake a dormant ley energy node in Silverpine Forest. Dalaran could draw on that concentrated arcane power to strengthen its position and threaten the Undercity’s hold over southern Lordaeron.

quest:4821.text: Alien Egg. At Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof sends you after an egg guarded by serpents beneath the stone needles. He wants it brought back before anything inside can break free. Hagar Lightninghoof hears of an unusual egg in the serpent dens below the stone needles. The canyon serpents guard it as though it were their own brood, striking at travelers who draw near. Concerned for the hunting grounds, Hagar asks you to find the nest, pass its sentries, and bring the strange egg back for study.

quest:484.text: Young Crocolisk Skins. In Menethil Harbor, James Halloran needs fresh skins from young marsh crocolisks. Their cured hides are wanted across the sea, keeping his trade supplied. Bring him the softer skins, and you earn his trust for more leatherworking work. Menethil Harbor links the Eastern Kingdoms with distant continents. Its trade draws on the surrounding marsh, where James Halloran tans and cures hides from the region's reptilian predators. Merchants and ships carry his leather goods to far ports, so his workshop needs a steady supply. Einar brings Halloran regular hauls of mature hides, but those are too firm for some luxury goods. Halloran turns to travelers to find softer leather in the shallow bogs just outside Menethil's palisades. The young crocolisks' skins must stay intact for his careful curing.

quest:4841.text: Pacify The Centaur. At Freewind Post, you face the Galak camp below. Cliffwatcher Longhorn wants the threat at Splithoof Crag cut down before it reaches the tauren post. Freewind Post stands on a desert mesa above Thousand Needles. From there, the tauren watch the canyon floor, where enemies gather beneath the ropes and lifts. The Galak centaur have built a war camp at Splithoof Crag, directly north along the canyon wall. Their camp threatens the supply lines and tauren movement through the needles. Cliffwatcher Longhorn sends Horde travelers to weaken the Galak ranks. The tauren believe Freewind Post will be safe only when the centaur vanguard is broken in its own camp. Galak Scouts, Galak Wranglers, and Galak Windchasers all face the fight. Their deaths may blunt an attack before it reaches the post.

quest:4865.text: Serpent Wild. At Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof sends you northwest after signs of Arikara emerge in Thousand Needles. Strange eggs point to a vengeance spirit from tauren legend, and Hagar seeks Motega Firemane's counsel at Whitereach Post. Strange eggs have appeared across Thousand Needles, and local tauren fear an ecological disaster. Their signs point beyond ordinary predators to Arikara, a vengeance spirit from old tauren tales. The evidence shakes Hagar Lightninghoof. A threat he knew only from fireside lore now faces the canyon. Hagar Lightninghoof seeks Motega Firemane's counsel because this danger reaches beyond physical defense. Motega watches over the canyon floor from Whitereach Post, northwest of Freewind Post. As a spiritual guide versed in the Needles' traditional omens, he may help the Horde understand the rising spirit and decide whether to appease or destroy it.

quest:4881.text: Assassination Plot. In Thousand Needles, centaur move against Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. Intercepted orders reveal their plan to attack the tauren hunter. Kanati Greycloud is a tauren hunter camped at Whitereach Post in contested Thousand Needles. The small post lies southwest of the Great Lift, amid warring centaur clans and dangerous wildlife. The local centaur see his camp as a bold intrusion into their territory. They mean to kill Greycloud and discourage further Horde expansion through the canyon.

quest:490.text: Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Outside Darnassus, the Alliance bounty on Gnarlpine furbolg remains in force. Corruption spreads through Teldrassil, and Shayla Nightbreeze asks hunters to bring back the beasts’ fangs. Outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze carries the Sentinels’ orders to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. They once lived peacefully in the ancient forests. Now corruption has stripped away their reason and made them vicious threats to travelers and Teldrassil’s natural sanctity. Hunters cull the Gnarlpine across the boughs of the World Tree and collect their fangs as proof. Ban'ethil Hollow lies south of the road west of Dolanaar, and it is one of their two major strongholds. The other is the ruined Starbreeze Village to the east.

quest:4904.text: Free At Last. Lakota Windsong is making her way back to Thalia Amberhide at Freewind Post. After refusing Arnak Grimtotem, she was taken to his stronghold above Thousand Needles and now needs protection on the journey home. Arnak Grimtotem wanted Lakota Windsong for his bride. When she refused, he returned by night and attacked her home. Lakota's brother tried to defend her, but Arnak struck him down. Then he dragged Lakota to Darkcloud Pinnacle. Darkcloud Pinnacle rises above Thousand Needles, with high wooden bridges linking its spires. Grimtotem warriors guard the heights. As Lakota makes her way down, you fight off bandits who mean to seize her before she reaches the canyon floor. Lakota reaches the canyon floor and makes her way to safety at Freewind Post. There, Thalia Amberhide welcomes her with relief, though she grieves for Lakota's brother. Thalia gives his remaining belongings to those who brought Lakota home alive.

quest:4921.text: Lost in Battle. At the Crossroads, Mankrik searches for his wife, lost in a Bristleback ambush at a tauren camp. Wounded and unable to look for her himself, he asks travelers to search the Barrens for any sign of her. Mankrik, an orc warrior at the Crossroads, fought beside his wife at a small tauren camp. Bristleback quilboar suddenly swarmed them. His wife held off three attackers alone, but fresh reinforcements cut her off from Mankrik in the fight. Mankrik faced the advancing quilboar in a blind rage, but their numbers soon brought him down. A passing tauren druid found him near death on the Gold Road and tended his wounds. Still too injured to search for his wife, Mankrik asks travelers passing through the Crossroads to look across the Barrens and bring back any sign of her.

quest:493.text: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Renferrel sends his research south to Tarren Mill, where Forsaken apothecaries press on with their plague studies. You carry his notes from Silverpine Forest to Apothecary Lydon in Hillsbrad Foothills. Since breaking free of the Lich King's control, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has pursued a New Plague that could destroy both the living and the Scourge. The Royal Apothecary Society works under the Banshee Queen's relentless pressure to create it. Its researchers are spread across Lordaeron, so they share chemical data and test findings to hasten their work. Apothecary Renferrel works from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. He sends you south with his recent findings for Apothecary Lydon. Your road leaves the pine woods and crosses open pastures in Hillsbrad Foothills. Tarren Mill lies beneath the Alterac Mountains, an outpost where the Forsaken stage their research.

quest:494.text: Time to Strike. At Hillsbrad's border, Lesh sends a warning east to Tarren Mill. Her coded words carry word from a quiet watch to Forsaken plans against the human settlers. Deathstalker Lesh watches the valley from high ground near the border of Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills. Below her, human settlers and militia move through the valley. The Deathstalkers watch enemy settlements for the Undercity before its troops deploy. Lesh holds her post and asks passing Horde travelers to carry her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

quest:496.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon prepares a brew meant to kill the living. He needs animal reagents from the surrounding foothills. Tarren Mill is a Forsaken stronghold in the Hillsbrad Foothills and a research station for the Royal Apothecary Society. Apothecary Lydon works there, surrounded by green countryside he despises. He longs to see human settlements poisoned and conquered. For his experimental Elixir of Suffering, he needs potent, virulent ingredients from nearby creatures. Apothecary Lydon sends hunters into the wilds around Tarren Mill for Gray Bear tongues and the rare ichor of Moss Creepers. Unholy alchemy refines these animal substances into the base of a lethal mixture. He means it to kill living trespassers across Hillsbrad.

quest:4966.text: Protect Kanati Greycloud. At Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles, you join Kanati Greycloud as Galak assassins close in. Their orders name the tauren for death. At Whitereach Post, Kanati Greycloud finds centaur orders naming him as a target. The Galak centaur have long fought the nomadic tauren and their Horde allies. Raiding supply paths is not enough for them. They also seek to kill those who settle in their canyons. Kanati suspects the Galak will strike soon, and their numbers may be greater than he first thought. So he asks travelers at the post to stand with him. When the assassins attack, Kanati holds his ground beside his allies. Their blades and spells can break the ambush before the centaur kill him.

quest:498.text: The Rescue. In Tarren Mill, Krusk needs your help after Syndicate bandits seize the orc scouts sent to Durnholde Keep. Thrall sent them to investigate the growing threat and retrieve an object from the keep. Warchief Thrall sent orc warriors to Hillsbrad Foothills to investigate the growing Syndicate threat and retrieve an object from Durnholde Keep. Gol'dir led them toward the fortress ruins, but the Syndicate overwhelmed the scouts in an ambush. Krusk broke free and limped back across the river to Tarren Mill. The human bandits captured Drull, Tog'thar, and Gol'dir.

quest:499.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon tests a poison for the Royal Apothecary Society. He wants to learn how quickly it kills before it is used more widely. Apothecary Lydon works in Tarren Mill, making chemical weapons for the Dark Lady's ambitions. His blight is meant to destroy the Alliance's living humans and the Scourge's undead horrors. Once he has the needed reagents, Lydon mixes them into a foul brew called the Elixir of Suffering. He wants to see its power before the Society uses it more widely.

quest:5.text: Jitters' Growling Gut. In Raven Hill, Jitters is starving and afraid, with only weeds and insects to eat. He asks you to travel east to Darkshire for Chef Grual’s famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill shelters ravenous undead and lurking beasts among its ruined streets. Jitters has hidden there for weeks, moving through crumbling shanties beneath a sky that never seems to brighten. He has found only grubs in the dirt and wild weeds to eat. Hunger and fear wear him down, far from ordinary comforts. Jitters longs for a taste of safety: the seasoned patties made at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He asks you to cross the haunted road and speak with Chef Grual. If the chef agrees to make Dusky Crab Cakes, a hot meal may quiet Jitters’ growling gut.

quest:500.text: Crushridge Bounty. From Southshore, Marshal Redpath warns that Crushridge ogres have settled near Alterac's ruins. He offers a bounty to anyone who hunts them in the Alterac Mountains. Marshal Redpath sends you north after reports that Crushridge ogres have dug a mound in the Alterac Mountains near Alterac's ruined city. They have taken the ruins too. Redpath fears they may grow comfortable there, then move down into the foothills and reach Southshore's door. He offers a bounty for hunting them and bringing back the Dirty Knucklebones they carry.

quest:501.text: Elixir of Pain. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon seeks mountain lion blood for a lethal brew. His work serves the Royal Apothecary Society’s drive to perfect the New Plague. Apothecary Lydon takes little comfort in Tarren Mill. Hillsbrad’s blooming meadows and brisk mountain air offend him. Like many in the Royal Apothecary Society, he gives himself to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the New Plague. The Society works to perfect this engineered scourge, made to kill the living and bring retribution to its enemies. Apothecary Lydon seeks ingredients for a poisonous mixture among animals that prowl the foothills and slopes toward the Alterac Mountains. He believes mountain lion blood holds what he needs for an Elixir of Pain. So he sends agents into the wilds for ten vials. The blood will support the Society’s continuing chemical trials along the contested southern front.

quest:502.text: Elixir of Pain. In Tarren Mill, the Elixir of Pain is ready for a trial on Farmer Ray’s dog, Stanley. Apothecary Lydon prepares the draught for the Royal Apothecary Society. Apothecary Lydon serves the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner from Tarren Mill. He gathers fresh blood from local wildlife and brews it into the volatile Elixir of Pain. The Society seeks proof in the field of how its experimental poisons and mutagens affect living bodies. Lydon sends his agents to the northern farm in Hillsbrad Fields, beyond the human defenders. Farmer Ray keeps his dog Stanley there. An agent pours the draught into an open hand and offers it as an ordinary treat. Stanley does not know what he is being given.

quest:503.text: Gol'dir. In Tarren Mill, Krusk has found where Gol'dir is held. The documents point north to a large Syndicate base, perhaps in the Alterac Mountains, and Gol'dir has been captive too long. In Tarren Mill, Krusk studies the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to a large Syndicate base up north, perhaps in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has been held too long, and Krusk wants him freed. Syndicate fill the inn at Strahnbrad, where Gol'dir is held in the top room. A Rusted Iron Key opens the lock. Jailor Borhuin carries it and may be in any building in town.

quest:5042.text: Agamaggan's Strength. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers strength drawn from Blood Shards. The captive Razormane shaman honors the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan and hates the rival Bristleback tribe. Quilboar honor Agamaggan, an ancient boar demigod. They say his spilled blood formed the red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. The crystals are sacred to them, and their power strengthens the fighters who stand at the front. Mangletooth, an elder Razormane shaman held captive in Camp Taurajo, offers that strength to Horde champions. He says your foes will cower before you as they do before the mightiest Razormane champions. Mangletooth offers his strength out of spite. Orcs and tauren captured and caged the old quilboar, whose Razormane tribe is at war with the rival Bristleback. He cannot break his chains and slaughter them himself, so he trades Agamaggan's gifts for help against them. Those who destroy Bristleback tribes and take the sacred Blood Shards from their lands earn his blessing.

quest:5043.text: Agamaggan's Agility. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a blood shard ritual. The captive quilboar channels his ancient boar god's power, blessing those who bring him shards from the Barrens with swift movement and sure aim. Crimson blood shards jut from the Barrens soil, especially near quilboar camps and great brambles. Quilboar tradition says the crystals formed from Agamaggan's spilled blood. The Great Boar Ancient fell fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Though caged in Camp Taurajo, elder quilboar Mangletooth can channel the stones' divine power for anyone who brings him shards. Quilboar hunters and scouts prize ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. For four blood shards, Mangletooth calls on the fallen demi-god's power. He lends the petitioner the instincts and supple grace of his people's finest stalkers. Mangletooth grunts at outsiders, yet honors his pact and weaves Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

quest:5044.text: Wisdom of Agamaggan. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde spellcasters a way to draw on Agamaggan’s power. The captive quilboar asks for blood shards in return. At Camp Taurajo, the Horde holds Mangletooth prisoner. The quilboar trades his people’s magical secrets for blood shards, crimson crystals said to have formed from Agamaggan’s spilled blood. The towering boar Demigod fell in the War of the Ancients. Mangletooth says his tribes’ geomancers and shaman use the shards to channel divine power in their rituals. Some shard offerings bring physical resilience or swiftness. Mangletooth’s Wisdom ritual instead sharpens the mind and arcane ability. For four blood shards, he calls on Agamaggan’s spirit to grant you cunning in your confrontations. Then he reminds you that you are mortal.

quest:5045.text: Rising Spirit. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers you an old blessing drawn from Agamaggan's power. Bring blood shards taken from his Bristleback rivals, and he will strengthen your will and spirit. In a cage at Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth knows the geomancy and ancestral magic of the quilboar. He takes pride in his people's devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. To Mangletooth, an unbroken spirit carries a warrior onward when strength fails and defeat draws near. Mangletooth asks you for blood shards to raise your spirit. These crystals hold Agamaggan's ancient blood, which seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. Bring shards gathered across the Barrens, especially from his Bristleback enemies. Then Mangletooth can channel their power into a blessing that strengthens your will.

quest:5046.text: Razorhide. In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers a rite to those who bring him blood shards. The captive quilboar trades Agamaggan’s life essence for a blessing that hardens the skin before battle. The quilboar trace their power to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who died fighting the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood sank into the Barrens and hardened into crystalline shards, still alive with ancient power. The Horde and quilboar remain sworn enemies. Yet Mangletooth, held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, may share sacred knowledge in exchange for these fragments. Quilboar are born with thick hides and protective quills. Their warriors call on Agamaggan to harden their skin against blades and claws. Mangletooth can perform the rite for outsiders, channeling four blood shards to strengthen their defenses and help keep their bones unbroken in the wilds.

quest:505.text:
Syndicate Assassins. Southshore’s new magistrate suspects the Syndicate Assassins killed his predecessor. His clues point north of Tarren Mill, where he wants the gang slain. Magistrate Henry Maleb now holds office in Southshore. The previous magistrate was assassinated, and the killers were never found. Maleb is almost certain the Syndicate hired them.

Thieves make up the gang, led by villainous nobles from the fallen kingdom of Alterac. Maleb’s last clues point north of Tarren Mill, which the Horde occupies. He asks you to slay the Syndicate members at the camp there.

quest:5052.text:
Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Across the Barrens, the Blood Shards of Agamaggan still hold the power of a fallen boar god. Quilboar say his blood sank into the earth and hardened into red stones. At Camp Taurajo, captive Mangletooth trades that power to the Horde for his own reasons. Quilboar lore tells how Agamaggan fell ten thousand years ago in the War of the Ancients. His blood raised giant thorn mazes across the plains, then sank into the soil and seeped into minerals. In time, it hardened into blood-red stones.

The quilboar honor the shards as sacred remnants of their creator. They gather them from mineral seams and holy grounds, then use them as totems in battle and sorcery. The tauren hold Mangletooth in a cage at Camp Taurajo. He bears a bitter grudge against his own kind, saying his tribe betrayed him and cast him out.

Without freedom or his people's magic, he bargains with you for blood shards. Their power lets him reach Agamaggan's magic despite his captivity, then channel it to Horde champions. He takes pleasure in turning that power against the quilboar who rejected him. Mangletooth speaks with reverence of Razorfen, the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south. The tribes say the vast briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs grew from Agamaggan's colossal skeleton and tusks.

They believe Razorfen Downs lies within the demigod's gaping maw. It is a holy threshold that devours and crushes any who enter without the Boar God's favor.

quest:506.text:
Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir is already free and carries word to Krusk in Tarren Mill. Aliden Perenolde, leader of the Syndicate, visited him and spoke of enslaving orcs who resist. Perenolde brought Elysa, who wears the pendant the Warchief desires. Gol'dir has word for Krusk after a visit from Aliden Perenolde, leader of the Syndicate. Perenolde called himself lord of the land and spoke of enslaving orcs who resist him. His father and mentor, the despised Blackmoore, had planned the same.

Gol'dir sends you to carry this news to Krusk in Tarren Mill. He will follow once he has settled his own business where he is. Perenolde also brought his mistress, a slight girl named Elysa. Around her neck hung the pendant the Warchief desires.

quest:5062.text: Sacred Fire. At the Boiling Pool, hunters seek Incendia Agave for a sacred flame meant to call Arikara from the canyons of Thousand Needles. Motega Firemane asks you to prepare the sacred fire of life, an ancient flame that calls Arikara. The monstrous wind serpent cannot be tracked across the canyon floor. You must draw her to the fire instead. Ordinary kindling will not feed the flame. It needs rare Incendia Agave, which grows around the scalding waters of Thousand Needles. Incendia Agave grows near the Boiling Pool, below Darkcloud Pinnacle. You brave blistering waters and steam elementals drifting through the mists to gather its spiky leaves. Many bushels lie beneath the surface. The hot lake water tests every hunter sent to collect them.

quest:5064.text: Grimtotem Spying. At Freewind Post, Cliffwatcher Longhorn sends you to learn what the Grimtotem are planning. Three unknown couriers visited Darkcloud Pinnacle, and guarded notes lie scattered through their village. Their words may threaten the tauren settlements of Thousand Needles. Freewind Post clings to high spires, where its defenders watch their hostile cousins. The Grimtotem have long resented the Horde and kept to strongholds atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Then Cliffwatcher Longhorn noticed a change. Three unknown agents arrived over several weeks and met secretly with clan leaders. He suspects they brought orders or proposed alliances against Thunder Bluff's presence in the canyon. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified village of sheer mesas joined by wooden rope bridges. Dense patrols of hostile Grimtotem warriors and shamans guard the way in. Longhorn's scouts found the agents' messages locked in separate chests among the central dwellings and outer bluffs. You cross the settlement to recover all three notes and take the clan's private words under its watchful eyes.

quest:5088.text: Arikara. From Thunder Bluff, Magatha Grimtotem warns that Arikara may be hunting High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. She sends Horde adventurers to summon and slay the ancient wind serpent at the burial spires of Thousand Needles. Magatha Grimtotem enchants refined Incendia powder to call Arikara. She warns that ancient tauren traditions have changed too quickly under the new Horde alliance. Those changes, she says, stirred the vengeance of the ferocious wind serpent spirit. So she sends you south to the canyon of Thousand Needles. There, among the elevated burial sites of Darkcloud Pinnacle, you are to cast the powder onto a ritual pyre.

quest:509.text: Elixir of Agony. In Hillsbrad, the Elixir of Agony is part of Lydon's work against the living and the Scourge. In Tarren Mill, you gather Mudsnout Blossoms for the Royal Apothecary Society's experiments under Lady Sylvanas. The Scourge ravages the north, while the Alliance clings to towns such as Southshore. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon works under the Dark Lady's command to develop a plague against both. He finds alchemy tedious, yet gathers potent organic toxins from the countryside. With them, he brews elixirs meant to hasten the destruction of Sylvanas's enemies. Nethander Stead lies south of Tarren Mill and east of the river. The abandoned human farmstead is overrun by vicious Mudsnout gnolls, and Mudsnout Blossoms grow among its filth and neglected soil. These foul-smelling mushrooms hold concentrated organic poisons prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. You can cut through the gnoll packs or weave quietly past their ramshackle camps to gather them.

quest:510.text: Foreboding Plans. The Syndicate's papers call for supplies to reach Southshore soon, where Magistrate Henry Maleb awaits them. The Syndicate papers list food, weapons and clothing. They also call for masks, oil and poison. The supplies are needed soon for an important undertaking against Southshore. Magistrate Henry Maleb is to receive them there.

quest:511.text: Encrypted Letter. Among the Syndicate papers, one letter cannot be read. You take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore. Among the Syndicate documents, one letter is written in a cipher no one can read. You bring it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore.

quest:512.text:
Noble Deaths. In Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb fears the Syndicate means ruin for the town. He sends you north to Strahnbrad's ruins in the Alterac Mountains, where he believes its leaders have their headquarters. After Foreboding Plans, Magistrate Henry Maleb wants the Syndicate's leaders struck down before their plans come to pass. Its cutthroats answer to former Alterac nobles, who may hide among ordinary agents. Their signet rings mark them out. Maleb asks you to bring him seven Alterac signet rings in Southshore.

He believes the Syndicate has made its headquarters among Strahnbrad's ruins, north in the Alterac Mountains.

quest:513.text: Elixir of Agony. In the Undercity, the Elixir of Agony awaits its final treatment. Apothecary Lydon sends his freshly mashed Mudsnout Composite from Tarren Mill to Master Apothecary Faranell, who must add a colloid of decay. The Royal Apothecary Society is developing a new plague for the Forsaken. The Royal Apothecary Society sends discoveries from regional researchers to the Undercity for refinement. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon has mashed local Mudsnout Blossoms into a composite. Only the capital's laboratory has the advanced reagents needed to make his work lethal. Master Apothecary Faranell works under pressure in the Apothecarium. The Scourge threatens from the north, while aggressive human populations press from the south. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has demanded a potent new plague to defend the Forsaken. Lydon's composite may give Faranell the toxic breakthrough the Dark Lady expects.

quest:514.text: Letter to Stormpike. In Southshore, Loremaster Dibbs entrusts you with an encrypted letter for Ironforge. He hopes Prospector Stormpike can read it. Dibbs sends you to Ironforge to find Prospector Stormpike. He is in the Library, inside the Hall of Explorers. Tell him Dibbs sent you and show him the letter. Dibbs believes no one north of Blackrock Spire can read it better than Stormpike.

quest:5147.text: Wanted - Arnak Grimtotem. At Freewind Post, a Horde bounty calls for Arnak Grimtotem’s death. The authorities seek the violent Grimtotem exile for murder and kidnapping on the mesas above the canyon. Tauren of the Horde and the reclusive Grimtotem have long been at odds. Arnak worsened that strife by murdering a tauren and abducting the victim’s sister, Lakota Windsong. Branded an outcast, he drew the notice of Cliffwatcher Longhorn at Freewind Post. Longhorn sanctioned an open bounty calling for Arnak’s death. Arnak has taken refuge on the high northern cliff mesas of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Grimtotem encampments spread across the high crags near the entrance to Razorfen Downs, linked by rope bridges. Lakota Windsong is held captive there and waits for rescue. Anyone who reaches her must cross the Grimtotem bridges.

quest:515.text: Elixir of Agony. In the Undercity, Faranell prepares Lydon's mixture for a deadly purpose. The Royal Apothecary Society needs reagents from the coast and alchemical draughts to make its new plague ready. Apothecary Lydon sent his Mudsnout Blossom mixture from gnoll-held Nethander Stead to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell leads the Royal Apothecary Society, and he saw the mixture's grim potential at once. Its toxic properties pleased him, so he added his own colloid of decay. Then he named the catalysts that could turn it into a weapon. To activate the mixture's contaminating agents, Lydon needs exact reagents in Tarren Mill. Faranell calls for a restorative draught of Strong Troll's Blood to feed and steady the chemical reaction. He also needs organic parts from Hillsbrad's southern shore: scales from the serpentine Daggerspine naga and eyes from the coastal Torn Fin murlocs.

quest:5151.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. In Thousand Needles, Wizlo Bearingshiner waits at Whitereach Post after a centaur ambush. He needs his invention back from the wreckage, where a caged panther wears it around its neck. Beneath Thousand Needles' sandstone spires, centaur guard the canyon floor. Just north of Whitereach Post, they overran a trade caravan, killed its travelers and plundered the wagons. Only Wizlo Bearingshiner, a goblin tinkerer, escaped. He limped back to safety. The centaur left one ruined wagon untouched, though they looted nearly every other valuable scrap. Inside its transport cage, a ferocious, enraged panther remains bound with Wizlo's prized hypercapacitor gizmo fastened around its neck. The centaur feared the beast and left the cage closed. Now Wizlo entrusts its key to mercenaries willing to face the predator and reclaim his invention.

quest:516.text: Beren's Peril. In southern Silverpine Forest, Shadow Priest Allister moves against Scourge gathering in a hidden cave. The Forsaken hope to strike before the undead begin their offensive. Shadow Priest Allister has heard that servants of the Lich King gather deep in southern Silverpine Forest. Their growing numbers threaten Forsaken operations across the region. So Allister sends scouts to strike first and destroy the Scourge in their secluded lair before they can mobilize. South of Ambermill, the Dalaran-aligned settlement, a hidden cave cuts into the hills. Its rough slopes make the cavern easy to miss, and the approach runs around the hills’ southern face. Ravenclaw drudgers and guardians dwell within. Destroying these Scourge remnants helps the Forsaken hold their ground in the forest.

quest:517.text: Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon puts his Elixir of Agony to a deadly test. He sends Horde champions to Dun Garok for a keg of Shindigger Stout. Apothecary Lydon serves the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas from Tarren Mill. He has gathered lethal ingredients across Hillsbrad and finished a new concoction. Frogs and stray dogs cannot test its strength. Lydon wants to see what it does to living adversaries. Lydon needs a quiet way to carry his experiment. South of Hillsbrad, Ironforge dwarves hold the fortified stronghold of Dun Garok. He sends Horde agents into its underground barracks and mess halls. There, they must slip past dwarven rifles and axes to steal a keg of Shindigger Stout.

quest:518.text: The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara seeks to weaken Mug'Thol's ogres before striking their hold in the Ruins of Alterac. She sends you to hunt the Crushridge maulers. Mug'Thol and the Crushridge ogres hold the Ruins of Alterac. Melisara sees little chance of punishing Mug'Thol while so many ogres remain around him. Their numbers must fall before she can make her next move. You are sent after the Crushridge maulers.

quest:522.text: Assassin's Contract. In Hillsbrad Foothills, a Shadowy Assassin bears a contract naming Magistrate Henry Maleb for death. You are to carry it to Maleb in Southshore, where red wax bears a distinctive signet ring's mark. A Shadowy Assassin carries a contract in Hillsbrad Foothills. It names Magistrate Henry Maleb for death, and a distinctive signet ring has marked the red wax. Bring the paper to Maleb in Southshore.

quest:524.text: Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon prepares a deadly poison for a cruel test. He plans to disguise it as stolen dwarven ale and use it on human prisoners. Apothecary Lydon gathers foul ingredients across the Hillsbrad Foothills and steals dwarven ale from Dun Garok. The Royal Apothecary Society has charged him with making a deadly brew called Elixir of Agony. Once mixed, the poison waits inside a keg that appears to hold ordinary mountain stout.

quest:525.text: Further Mysteries. In the Alterac foothills, a decrypted letter leaves Prospector Stormpike searching for meaning. He sends you to Southshore's magistrate with the message. Prospector Stormpike has decrypted the letter you found among thieves in the Alterac foothills. Yet its meaning escapes him, and he wonders why thieves had it at all. Southshore lies nearest to Alterac. If a threat is brewing, its magistrate should hear of it, so you carry the message to Magistrate Henry Maleb.

quest:527.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. Across Hillsbrad, the Forsaken strike at the farms that feed the human town. High Executor Darthalia directs the attack from Tarren Mill under Varimathras's command. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign from Tarren Mill. Varimathras in the Undercity has ordered her to break the human resistance in Hillsbrad Foothills. So Darthalia targets the northern fields before attacking the defended town. Those farms feed the town. Disrupting them cuts provisions to the human militia and brings disorder to the homesteads. The Forsaken press the human defenders while the Royal Apothecary Society prepares a plague meant to destroy the living and the Scourge. Darthalia uses the fighting to hold the humans down until the plague is ready. Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz are among the landowners killed in these early attacks.

quest:528.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, Forsaken forces press south after strikes on the northern farms. Horde operatives now hunt the peasants who fled to the orchards. Hillsbrad's human farms have come under attack, driving laborers south into the fields. After strikes on the northern farms, many flee to the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad Fields. They hope to escape the advancing undead. High Executor Darthalia sees their flight as a chance to break the township's remaining labor force and morale. From Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia orders Horde forces to hunt the displaced laborers in the fields. The peasants have no protection. Their deaths choke Hillsbrad's food supply and weaken civilian resolve. For Darthalia and the Forsaken, each human killed tightens their hold over the surviving township and helps keep Lordaeron in Forsaken hands.

quest:529.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Hillsbrad, the Forsaken press their advance against the humans who resist them. High Executor Darthalia orders the smithy in Hillsbrad Fields destroyed, hoping to cut off the weapons arming the local people. In the Hillsbrad Foothills, the Forsaken face fiercer resistance than High Executor Darthalia expected. Rural humans refuse to scatter or yield to the Deathstalkers and soldiers sent from Tarren Mill. The Forsaken learn that the peasantry fight with more than pitchforks and scythes. In the fields, they are being armed for war. At the southwestern edge of Hillsbrad Fields, Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices forge blades and armor for the militia from raw ore. Darthalia sends an operative to kill Verringtan, butcher his apprentices, and seize their stockpiled iron. She aims to weaken the settlement's defenses and use the metal in the eventual assault on Southshore.

quest:530.text: A Husband's Revenge. In the Undercity, Raleigh Andrean sends you to hunt the man who murdered his wife. An engraved ring from Silverpine Forest stirs Raleigh Andrean's mortal memories. He recalls his close friend Valdred Moray, who murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. The Scourge's chill and undeath have dulled his grief and love. Yet his thirst for revenge remains, and you are sent to find Valdred.

quest:532.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad town, Forsaken forces strike to break human rule. High Executor Darthalia directs the assault from Tarren Mill. Hillsbrad’s human defenders hold to their authority despite heavy losses in the fields and among the patrols. High Executor Darthalia knows the peasants and militia rally behind the town’s leaders. So she sends Forsaken operatives into the Town Hall to kill Magistrate Burnside and five councilmen. Without them, the town loses its command. Darthalia seeks to break Hillsbrad’s civic life as well as its leadership. She orders operatives to burn the Hillsbrad Proclamation, a political document bound to the settlement’s charter and pride. They also seize the town registry from surviving Alliance loyalists. Its official records and citizen rolls give Undercity’s intelligence a detailed view of the local people.

quest:5321.text:
The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade struggles to stay awake on the road from Darkshore to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Newly roused from a long sleep, he carries the Horn of Awakening and needs help past furbolgs and cultists. Kerlonian Evershade is a Druid of the Claw, newly awakened from sleep in the barrows. For millennia, druids communed with wild spirits through the Emerald Dream. The Third War called them to wake, but centuries of hibernation left Kerlonian struggling to stay conscious.

He set out south from Darkshore to meet Liladris Moonriver in Ashenvale, yet exhaustion soon overtook him. Sudden naps leave him helpless in the wilds, so he relies on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep moving. The road from Darkshore into Ashenvale is dangerous for Kerlonian. In Twilight Vale, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs stalk the road. Farther south in Ashenvale, members of the Dark Strand cult lie in ambush. Sleep may lay Kerlonian down wherever he stands, so you need to keep watch and rouse him with the horn.

quest:533.text: Infiltration. In Tarren Mill, Krusk seeks word of Gol'dir, the orc prisoner the Syndicate keeps moving. He sends you to its large camp just north of town for any information you can bring back. Krusk has heard word and rumor of Gol'dir, an orc prisoner held by the Syndicate. Its human captors keep moving him, but the search has narrowed to their large camp just north of Tarren Mill. Krusk sends you there to find what you can and carry it back. Each day, he fears Gol'dir's prospects grow darker.

quest:535.text: Valik. In a Syndicate camp, Valik lies dying with an enemy before them. Valik expects you to kill them, but offers answers for a mug of Southshore Stout. Henchman Valik lies wounded in the Syndicate camp, with you standing before them as an enemy. They expect you to kill them all the same. Yet Valik offers answers to your questions if you bring a mug of Southshore Stout to the camp. They even wonder aloud whether your kind drinks at all.

quest:536.text: Down the Coast. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle leaves Southshore's defense to passing adventurers. Sent from Stormwind, he would rather drink ale than patrol while Torn Fin murlocs gather along the Western Strand. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle left Stormwind's city guard for a post in Southshore. The port feels dreary to him, and the harbor's fishy odor is more than he can bear. So he spends his days drinking at the inn instead of patrolling the frontlines. Marshal Redpath has ordered him to protect Southshore from nearby dangers, but Orinelle hires passing sellswords to do the work. The Western Strand runs along the coast west of Southshore. Orinelle scoffs at the murlocs as overgrown fish, yet the Torn Fin tribe threatens coastal travel and local shipping. Its tidehunters and oracles gather in camps along the breakers. There, they ambush anyone who strays too far from town walls, so clearing the shoreline means facing them.

quest:5361.text: Family Tree. Cliffwatcher Longhorn sends you to Ghost Walker Post with news of unusual centaur activity. His brother is there in Desolace. Cliffwatcher Longhorn asks you to carry a report to his brother, Nataka, at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. A year has passed since his last letter. Now the centaurs are acting unusually, and Nataka needs to hear what is happening. From Thousand Needles, travel to Stonetalon Mountain, north of the Crossroads. Go west into the Charred Vale, then south into Desolace. Follow the road south to Ghost Walker Post.

quest:5381.text: Hand of Iruxos. At Shadowprey Village, Taiga Wisemane sends you to Thunder Axe Fortress for a Demon Box. The Burning Blade uses the Hand of Iruxos inside it to open portals for demons at Mannoroc Coven. Taiga Wisemane wants the demons' passage into our world stopped. She gives you a demon pick for the red crystal inside Thunder Axe Fortress. Use it to reach the Demon Box, then bring the box and pick back to Taiga in Shadowprey Village.

quest:5386.text: Catch of the Day. At Ghost Walker Post, Nataka Longhorn is longing for cooked fish. She praises the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers, but centaur activity keeps her from making the journey. She asks you to bring her two Bloodbelly fish. At Ghost Walker Post, Nataka Longhorn has gone a long while without cooked fish. She trusts the trolls of Shadowprey Village to catch the finest fish, but centaur activity leaves her little time to travel. So she asks you to speak with Jinar'Zillen, the village's local fisherman, and bring back two Bloodbelly fish. They are Nataka's favorite. The road south of the post bends west toward the troll village.

quest:539.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Azurelode Mine, Horde forces strike to cut iron shipments to Alliance armories. High Executor Darthalia has ordered Foreman Bonds and his crew killed. High Executor Darthalia marked Azurelode Mine as vital to human strength after the Horde seized the Hillsbrad Town Registry in earlier raids. The mine lies just south of Hillsbrad Fields. There, workers keep drawing rich iron ore for Alliance weaponsmiths and armories. If the mine stays open, Southshore can rearm and strengthen its garrisons, undoing Tarren Mill’s earlier victories. Darthalia orders Horde forces to kill Foreman Bonds, the human overseer, and a large part of his workforce. The attack reaches into the mine’s dark shafts to halt production. Southshore receives a clear warning: the Forsaken can strike its supply lines and isolated labor camps.

quest:54.text: Report to Goldshire. Marshal McBride sends you south to Goldshire with dispatches for Marshal Dughan. Beyond Northshire's sheltered valley, Stormwind's nobles give Elwynn Forest less and less thought. You've proved yourself against Northshire's troubles, and McBride releases you from the valley's guard. His transfer papers send you past the border gates and down the road to Goldshire. From there, your duty reaches across the wider forest. Marshal Dughan waits in Goldshire to receive McBride's dispatches and make you an Acting Deputy of the Stormwind Marshals. His welcome carries a grim warning: beside the dangers roaming Elwynn, Northshire is a peaceful garden. Stormwind's royal army is bound up in distant nobles' politics, instead of guarding home ground.

quest:540.text: Preserving Knowledge. In Southshore, Loremaster Dibbs sends you into the Ruins of Alterac to save books from the ogres who have settled there. One worn leather volume matters most: it holds The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Loremaster Dibbs fears for the books left in the Ruins of Alterac, now home to ogres. You search for the tomes they have looted and recover what you can. Dibbs would climb into the mountains to search too, but fears old bones would not survive the journey. Among the tomes, Loremaster Dibbs most wants a worn leather book containing The Arm of Gri'lek. Dibbs is bent on learning its ancient troll lore. The Ruins of Alterac were the last known home of an intact copy.

quest:541.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken's campaign now turns on Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia sends Horde champions to break the dwarven garrison aiding local humans and kill its commander, Captain Ironhill. High Executor Darthalia has already pressed the human farmers and town militia across the foothills. Now she directs Tarren Mill's fury at Ironforge's troops. Dwarven soldiers have taken up arms for Southshore, strengthening the human presence in Lordaeron. Darthalia sees that bond as an obstacle. She means to show the Alliance that aid for the human survivors will bring devastation. Dun Garok clings to Thoradin's Wall in southeastern Hillsbrad. Disciplined mountaineers hold the fortified stronghold, joined by skilled riflemen and battle-hardened priests. Horde forces must break through those defenders and kill Captain Ironhill. His death breaks Ironforge's forward command in the region, leaving the remaining human enclaves isolated.

quest:5421.text: Fish in a Bucket. In Shadowprey Village, Jinar'Zillen leaves the shellfish gathering to others. The traps lie below the docks, and he offers a Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village. He would rather someone else gather from them, and offers a fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

quest:544.text: Prison Break In. Magus Wordeen Voidglare faces a crisis in Tarren Mill while pursuing his research. Four Forsaken fled the Undercity months ago with artifacts stolen from a secure vault, and Sylvanas wants them returned. Magus Wordeen Voidglare came to Tarren Mill to research. Now a crisis calls for his attention. Four Forsaken turned from their brethren and stole from the Dark Lady. They broke into a secure vault and took four artifacts the apothecaries need for certain studies. Sylvanas wants them returned. The thieves fled the Undercity for Dalaran. Its wizards placed them in quarantine at the Lordamere Internment Camp. You are sent to find the traitors, recover the artifacts and report to Voidglare in Tarren Mill. There are four: a Bloodstone Wedge, Marble, Shard and Oval. Dermot holds the wedge, Ricter the marble, Alina the shard and Kegan Darkmar the oval.

quest:545.text:
Dalaran Patrols. In Tarren Mill, Magus Wordeen Voidglare turns his gaze toward Dalaran’s outskirts. Beyond the great dome, ruined streets may hold treasures of magical worth, but wizards and their elemental slaves patrol them. Voidglare wants those patrols thinned. After Prison Break In, Voidglare turns his attention to Dalaran’s wizards. They raised a great dome of magic over the heart of their city. Some say it shields them from the violence of the age. Others say they sought solitude to study and plot. Voidglare cares nothing for their reason.

Beyond the dome, the ruined outskirts may hold treasures of real magical worth. Yet wizards and their elemental slaves patrol those streets. You are sent to hunt six Dalaran Summoners and twelve Elemental Slaves, then return to Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

quest:546.text: Souvenirs of Death. At Tarren Mill, Deathguard Samsa watches others march against Hillsbrad's human settlements and longs to join them. He asks for thirty human skulls taken in battle for his collection. High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken campaign against Hillsbrad's human settlements. Deathguard Samsa keeps watch in Tarren Mill while others are sent to raid, burn, and pillage. He envies their chance to slaughter the living, denied to a guard held at his post. Samsa hates the humans of Hillsbrad and collects the skulls of those slain in the campaign. He asks for thirty as trophies from a war he longs to fight himself. No arcane rite or military plan lies behind his request.

quest:547.text: Humbert's Sword. Near Dun Garok, Humbert's Sword is missing from the camp where its owner left it. Deathguard Humbert had gone for firewood while watching the dwarven stronghold on High Executor Darthalia's orders. Ironforge scouts took his weapon, and now he fears Darthalia will learn he failed. Deathguard Humbert watches Dun Garok for High Executor Darthalia. His hidden post lies near the dwarven fortress. One morning, he leaves camp to gather firewood for boiling water. Ironforge scouts find the post unguarded and loot it. When Humbert returns, his sword is gone, carried into the heavily defended bunker. Humbert knows losing his weapon to the enemy he was sent to watch could cost him his life under Forsaken command. If High Executor Darthalia learns what happened, he fears she will hang him from the rafters in Tarren Mill. He cannot storm Dun Garok alone. So he turns to passing Horde adventurers to recover his blade before his commander notices anything amiss.

quest:549.text: WANTED: Syndicate Personnel. At Tarren Mill, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's bounty calls for every Syndicate member's death. The Forsaken want the brigands driven from Durnholde Keep before they threaten Horde operations in the foothills. The Syndicate's sudden arrival southeast of Tarren Mill has drawn the Forsaken's attention. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her commanders see the Syndicate as a plague, not displaced nobles to bargain with. Her bounty orders their immediate death. Any prisoners brought in will be executed without trial. Durnholde Keep was once an infamous internment fortress. Now it lies shattered and lawless. Syndicate Rogues and Watchmen have taken its crumbling ramparts and towers as an operations hub. High Executor Darthalia needs the armed bandits driven out to secure the road and protect Tarren Mill's southeastern approach.

quest:55.text: Morbent Fel. Above Raven Hill Cemetery, Morbent Fel's wards keep ordinary steel from reaching him. Sven Yorgen sends you with Morbent's Bane to break them and end the necromancer's terror in western Duskwood. Morbent Fel haunts an abandoned house atop a rocky ridge just east of Sven's camp. The house looks over the sprawl of Raven Hill Cemetery. From there, the necromancer sends undead through the surrounding forest and defiles Duskwood's graves. Dark magic and loyal undead thralls keep ordinary steel from reaching him. Morbent Fel's wards turn a direct assault into suicide and deflect conventional attacks. Sven entrusts you with Morbent's Bane, an enchanted artifact made to unravel that magical shielding. Invoke the relic and the barrier collapses. Then Fel is open to a mortal strike.

quest:550.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. At Hillsbrad, the Forsaken have broken the township's defenses. High Executor Darthalia sends you to carry her commendation to Varimathras in the Undercity. Fierce fighting in Hillsbrad Foothills has decided the struggle for southern Lordaeron. From Tarren Mill, Horde champions struck the township's farmers, militia, blacksmiths, and civic leaders. Alliance forces are crippled, and the territory is secured for the Forsaken. Now High Executor Darthalia prepares an official commendation so the champion's deeds reach the highest ranks of command. Darthalia's sealed commendation takes you to Varimathras in the Undercity's Royal Quarter. The dreadlord oversees military operations across Lordaeron beside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. The Scourge from the northern Plaguelands remains the Dark Lady's greatest threat. Yet surviving human enclaves still endanger the Forsaken's southern borders.

quest:5501.text: Bone Collector. At Kormek's Hut in Desolace, Bibbly F'utzbuckle is waiting on ten more kodo bones. A caravan is due any moment, and the goblin expects the bones to change the world. Bibbly F'utzbuckle sees a fortune in the kodo bones around the hut. Customers turn them into furniture, musical instruments, and even blasting powder. So Bibbly sends you south to the Kodo Graveyard for ten bones, promising something in return. A caravan comes by Kormek's Hut to collect Bibbly's kodo bones. It sells them at Shadowprey Village, and it is due any moment. Bibbly is ten bones short of a career high.

quest:552.text: Helcular's Revenge. In Tarren Mill, Helcular's Revenge turns on Thaivand's vow of vengeance. Master Helcular, a great wizard near becoming a lich, was killed by a human lynching crowd after it found his ritual lair in the hills. Before vengeance falls on Southshore, Thaivand needs Helcular's Rod, which he believes one of the yeti holds. Master Helcular was near becoming a lich when a human lynching crowd found his ritual lair in the hills and killed him. They buried his body in the Southshore cemetery. Thaivand, his apprentice, finds this treatment of a great wizard unacceptable. He vows that Southshore will face vengeance. Thaivand says Helcular's Rod must be found first. Yeti have taken over the ritual lair, and Thaivand is sure one of them has the rod. So many yeti roam the region that the search will be difficult. You can find them at Growless Cave and Darrow Hill.

quest:553.text: Helcular's Revenge. In Hillsbrad, Helcular's Revenge begins with a rod and three flames. Novice Thaivand gives you the Rod of Helcular. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell, and each flame must charge the rod before it is driven into Helcular's grave in Southshore. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell, and each flame must charge the rod. The Flames of Azel and Veraz burn in the yeti cave at Darrow Hill, within the Foothill Caverns. The Flame of Uzel lies in a small cave above the caverns, farther north in the mountains near Growless Cave. After all three flames charge the rod, it is to be driven into Helcular's grave at Southshore, a heavily guarded human town. The graveyard lies in the town's northeast corner by the river. Helcular's grave is at the graveyard's southeastern corner.

quest:555.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. Chef Jessen wants Soothing Turtle Bisque back on Southshore's tavern menu. Unrest has cut off his snapjaw turtle meat, so he asks cooks to brave the northern waters near Dalaran and Lake Lordamere. Southshore is one of Lordaeron's last intact coastal towns held by the Alliance. Civilian life continues there amid growing strife. Chef Jessen says his cooking rivals any tavern north of Stormwind. Patrons supposedly come from Darkshire in Duskwood to taste his bisque. The rich soup calls for fresh meat from snapjaw turtles native to the rivers and lakes of the northern mountains. In calmer years, Jessen gathered turtle meat himself. He traveled past Dalaran to the eastern shore of Lordamere Lake. Now rising tensions, hostile wildlife, the Syndicate, and Forsaken incursions make the lands beyond town deadly for ordinary townsfolk. To keep the bisque on his menu, Jessen relies on armed travelers to gather meat from snapjaws along the riverbanks and northern shores.

quest:556.text:
Stone Tokens. At Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil sends you to recover Stone Tokens from Dalaran agents in Alterac. The Forsaken seek to learn how Dalaran's mages bind and command elementals. Magus Voidglare studies those arcane methods for them. Dalaran's magi have long commanded elemental beings with specialized conduits and enchanted foci. They bind creatures from other dimensions and force them into servitude.

Though the city is still rebuilding, its agents and remnant forces patrol the surrounding territory. They use elementals as laborers and defensive shock troops. Magus Voidglare, an arcane researcher in Tarren Mill, works for the Forsaken and seeks to uncover the sorcery that compels these beings to obey.

quest:5561.text: Kodo Roundup. At Scrabblescrew's Camp, five tamed kodos are needed for a caravan due soon. You take Smeed Scrabblescrew's kodo kombobulator among Desolace's ancient, aged and dying kodos, then lead each tamed beast back to camp. A caravan is due at Scrabblescrew's Camp shortly, and Smeed Scrabblescrew says it depends on him. Bibbly thinks no other goblin in Desolace knows how to make a profit. Smeed disagrees. He has formed a partnership with Cork and Rigger, and the caravan is willing to brave this land. Smeed built the kodo kombobulator to revive aged and dying kodos and bring them under control. Aim it at an ancient, aged or dying kodo, and the device jolts the beast into a tamed kodo that follows you. Bring five kodos and the device back to Scrabblescrew's Camp.

quest:557.text: Bracers of Binding. In Tarren Mill, Keeper Bel'varil watches for what the Magus may need next. As the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Bel'varil sends you to the ruins of Dalaran for four Bracers of Earth Binding. The Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, and Keeper Bel'varil expects another need to follow. Bracers of binding are worn on an elemental's wrists, binding the creature to a mage's service. The elementals wear them among the ruins of Dalaran. Bel'varil asks you to bring four Bracers of Earth Binding back to Tarren Mill.

quest:5581.text: Portals of the Legion. At Mannoroc Coven, six demon portals threaten to widen the flow of demons into this world. Taiga Wisemane asks you to close them from Shadowprey Village. From Shadowprey Village, Taiga Wisemane gives you the Hand of Iruxos. She says you need to carry it to Mannoroc Coven and banish the portals there. The demon threat is growing, and each portal you close limits how many demons cross into this world. She wants all six banished. Beware their guardians.

quest:559.text: Farren's Proof. Along Southshore’s coast, Farren Orinelle sends Alliance recruits to prove his patrol’s work. Marshal Redpath wants evidence that the murlocs are gone from the Western Strand. After the first coastal sweeps in Down the Coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle faces questions from Marshal Redpath and Southshore’s leaders. Farren says the local murlocs are gone, but his superiors want proof. So he sends wandering Alliance adventurers back to the shore to bring evidence of the kills, leaving the grim work to them. West of Southshore, coastal murlocs live along the shallows of the Western Strand. Farren asks you for ten severed murloc heads to satisfy the garrison’s officers. He detests the creatures, whose repulsive sight and smell have spoiled his appetite for Southshore’s chief export and staple food.

quest:56.text: The Night Watch. In Darkshire, The Night Watch holds the line against the dead rising nearby. Stormwind has withdrawn its garrison, leaving the town’s local militia to rely on travelers at Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Stormwind once guarded Duskwood, but its royal resources dwindled as political discord took hold in the capital. Then the crown withdrew its commissioned soldiers, leaving Darkshire with little defense against the forest’s encroaching shadows. The people formed a local militia called the Night Watch, led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke. It stands between the cursed forest and the town’s remaining residents. South of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery was once a peaceful resting place. Now restless skeletons and reanimated spellcasters roam its graves. The Night Watch is stretched thin along Duskwood’s borders, so Commander Ebonlocke sends arriving travelers to strike down Skeletal Warriors and Skeletal Mages before the dead reach the roads.

quest:560.text: Farren's Proof. At Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle sends you to carry his report to Marshal Redpath. The murloc heads are proof of your work, but Farren will not carry them himself. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle patrols and secures the southern coast of Hillsbrad Foothills. Yet the harsh work of frontier warfare turns his stomach. After you cull the murlocs along the beaches, he cannot bring himself to touch the severed heads you bring back as proof. So he sends you across Southshore to deliver them to the town's command. Marshal Redpath oversees Southshore's defenses and military readiness as threats rise from Tarren Mill and wild beasts. He receives the sack of murloc heads from you, rather than directly from Farren. Redpath knows you have become Farren's errand runner, but accepts your help. Southshore needs every willing hand to keep its borders safe.

quest:561.text: Farren's Proof. In Southshore, Marshal Redpath sends Lieutenant Farren Orinelle orders to turn toward the naga on the Eastern Strand. He wants Orinelle to drive them back and report in person. Marshal Redpath sends word across Southshore to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Reports tell of naga incursions on the Eastern Strand, and Redpath wants Orinelle focused on that threat. The lieutenant must set aside other concerns, drive back the naga, and report his progress to the Marshal in person.

quest:562.text:
Stormwind Ho!. Alliance High Command fears the naga threat, and Stormwind Ho! gives Farren Orinelle a way south. He hopes to claim their defeat and win a return to Stormwind City. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle finds his post in Southshore miserable. The town lies on Lordaeron’s edge, hemmed in by Forsaken forces, syndicate brigands, and sea fiends. Farren once served as a city guardsman in Stormwind, where his days meant drunks and petty brawls. Now he longs to return south.

His former mentor tells him Alliance High Command grows anxious about naga encroaching on the coasts. Farren sees a chance to leave the north behind. Farren admits he lacks the courage and skill to face Daggerspine sirens and shorehunters in open combat. So he sends you to scour the beaches southeast of Southshore and thin the naga ranks.

He needs your deeds for an impressive dispatch to Major Samuelson in Stormwind. With that credit, Farren hopes to secure a reassignment.

quest:563.text: Reassignment. In Southshore, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle seeks a way back to Stormwind. He sends an adventurer to Stormwind Keep with an exaggerated account of his deeds against the coastal naga, meant for his former mentor, Major Samuelson. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle resents his posting in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Southshore lies far from the capital, and Marshal Redpath keeps a stern watch over the town. So Farren spends his days plotting a transfer south. He claims credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga, hoping to look like an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ready for promotion. Farren wants a transfer without arousing Marshal Redpath's suspicion, so he goes around the local chain of command. He turns to Major Samuelson, a senior officer in Stormwind Keep who mentored him in the past. A report sent straight to Samuelson puts Farren's claimed deeds before an officer with authority over garrison assignments.

quest:564.text: Costly Menace. In Southshore, Darren Malvew fears the mountain lions descending from Alterac. Undead, the Syndicate gang, and other scoundrels have cost the town horses, but the lions trouble him most. Darren Malvew lives in Southshore and hates seeing the town lose its beautiful horses. Undead, the Syndicate gang, and other scoundrels in the region have already taken quite a few. Yet Darren fears the mountain lions of Alterac most. They keep coming down from the hills. Darren wants eight Mountain Lions and ten Hulking Mountain Lions dealt with. The Mountain Lions roam the lower hills of the Alterac Mountains.

quest:5643.text: Shadowguard. In the Undercity, Aelthalyste sends a Darkspear priest across the Great Sea to Orgrimmar. She has seen the young troll grow ready for the tribe’s sacred rites, and Ur'kyo awaits in the Valley of Spirits. In the Undercity, Aelthalyste watches the troll priests who come to learn. When an initiate grows strong enough for the tribe’s trials, she sends them across the Great Sea to their own elders. She does not press Forsaken teachings upon them. Their faith follows the traditions of their people. In Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits, Ur'kyo tends to the Darkspear tribe’s spiritual needs and ancient rites. He welcomes the returning initiate and prepares them for a rite of passage. The rite deepens the priest’s bond with the loa and uses spells to ward off harm.

quest:5644.text: Devouring Plague. Across the sea from Lordaeron, Devouring Plague awaits Forsaken priests ready to learn its dark art. Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff sends the adept to Aelthalyste in the Ruins of Lordaeron for this signature Shadow magic. In Thunder Bluff, Miles Welsh trains Forsaken priests among the tauren. He watches their divine and shadowy studies, and knows when an acolyte is ready for higher mysteries. Rather than teach those secrets himself in Kalimdor, Miles sends the worthy back to the Ruins of Lordaeron. Aelthalyste waits beneath the city ruins in the Undercity's War Quarter. She is one of the foremost mentors of the Forsaken priesthood, guiding acolytes who weave shadow. Devouring Plague drains its victim and carries a corruptive force. Aelthalyste teaches it only to those able to wield that force without succumbing.

quest:5645.text: A Lack of Fear. In Ironforge, High Priest Rohan tests promising dwarven disciples. In the Mystic Ward, he teaches them as their strength of spirit grows. Local mentors send priests serving the Alliance abroad to senior clergy of their order. For dwarven disciples, that summons brings you to High Priest Rohan in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. There, basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper uses of holy magic, tested through trials. Dwarven tradition teaches that the Light is a shield in physical conflict. When you report to High Priest Rohan, you show that you have endured trials in the wider world. Now you must prove your mettle and master fear on the front lines.

quest:5646.text:
Devouring Plague. In Orgrimmar, Ur'kyo sends Forsaken priests home to learn Devouring Plague. They came to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear, but Aelthalyste waits in Undercity to teach them their people's shadow arts. Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power in Orgrimmar. Darkspear trolls and Forsaken share a curious bond in matters of faith, while orcs and tauren show little desire for priestly worship. Ur'kyo knows Forsaken initiates must master the shadow arts tied to their own condition. Out of respect between their peoples, he sends wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to finish their training. Beneath Lordaeron's ruins, Priestess Aelthalyste tends her flock in Undercity's War Quarter. Forsaken priests follow a solitary, grueling path shaped by their turn to shadow. They endure the painful touch of the Holy Light and learn to wield the devastating affliction of Shadow magic.

When an initiate gains enough skill, Aelthalyste gathers them close. There, she teaches the affliction her kind calls Devouring Plague.

quest:565.text: Bartolo's Yeti Fur Cloak. In Southshore, Bartolo Ginsetti gathers materials for Bartolo's Yeti Fur Cloak. The eccentric artisan claims his mantle is renowned throughout the Alliance and calls for tailoring supplies, a leatherworker's cloak, and raw yeti fur. Travelers in coastal Southshore can commission a Yeti Fur Cloak from Bartolo Ginsetti. The artisan boasts that no finer garment exists anywhere on the planet. His work draws on materials gathered from the local wilderness and the skill of allied trades. Bartolo needs more than a pelt and needle to make his cloak. Bring him a Bolt of Wool, Fine Thread, a Hillman's Cloak, and ten clumps of Yeti Fur from beasts roaming the foothills. With those goods in hand, he works the raw materials into his cold-weather mantle.

quest:567.text: Dangerous!. At Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia names four Hillsbrad humans for execution. She says they killed Forsaken and struck at supplies. Across Hillsbrad Foothills, the fighting is brutal and personal. High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill see ordinary Hillsbrad citizens as deadly foes. A wanted notice names four people whose resistance has killed Forsaken and cost them valuable shipments from the Undercity. The bounty names Clerk Horrace Whitesteed, who killed Deathguard Toma; Citizen Wilkes, who murdered Apothecary Eli; Miner Hackett, who killed Deathstalker Fry; and Farmer Kalaba, who sabotaged supply convoys from the Undercity. Each works from a different pocket of Hillsbrad resistance and remains elusive amid the wider conflict.

quest:5672.text: Elune's Grace. In Darnassus, young night elf priests answer the Sisterhood of Elune's call. Their first journeys prepare them for deeper teaching from Priestess Alathea. In the Temple of the Moon, the Sisterhood guides young acolytes from their first prayers toward mastery of lunar magic. Night elves trust the Mother Moon, Elune. Humans and dwarves instead follow the Holy Light. When a novice reaches a milestone in devotion, senior mentors take notice and judge the disciple ready to bear greater divine power. Priestess Alathea brings the Sisterhood's summons to the acolyte. She honors their devotion and welcomes them into traditions kept through millennia. By accepting the rite, the novice seals a bond with Elune. From then on, protective wards and lunar invocations of the kaldorei faith are within reach.

quest:5674.text: Elune's Grace. Night elf priests leave Dolanaar for Darnassus to receive Elune's Grace. The rite marks their readiness for a divine talent reserved for the kaldorei. A priest of the Sisterhood of Elune needs more than skill in prayers of mending and smiting. With experience, an acolyte reaches the point where blessings reserved for the kaldorei may be bestowed. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar cannot teach these deeper arts, so they send promising disciples to the spiritual heart of their order. Initiates cross Teldrassil to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. There, beneath the gaze of the high priesthood, Priestess Alathea judges whether each petitioner is ready to bear the goddess's defensive mantle. She teaches Elune's Grace there, a divine talent reserved for the kaldorei.

quest:5676.text: Arcane Feedback. In Stormwind, High Priestess Laurena teaches Arcane Feedback to priests bound for dangerous roads. At the Cathedral of Light, faith becomes a defense against hostile spellcasters. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena warns the acolytes that arcane magic remains dangerous. The Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order. Raw magic can turn volatile and lead to corruption or catastrophe. Warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts threaten the faithful, so priests learn to make their faith an active ward against spells. Arcane Feedback turns a hostile spellcaster's power back against them. The ward does more than deflect spells; it burns through the caster's mana and brings agony. Laurena teaches the rite to human priests preparing to travel beyond Stormwind. Thus the Cathedral's emissaries can face sorcery with a defense of their own.

quest:5677.text: Arcane Feedback. In Ironforge, human acolytes seeking deeper teaching are sent back to Stormwind. There, the Cathedral of Light holds the traditions of their people. High Priest Rohan welcomes a human priest who seeks deeper spiritual teaching in Ironforge’s Mystic Ward. Dwarven and human priests both serve the Holy Light, yet each people keeps its own rites, disciplines, and prayers of defense. Rohan reserves Ironforge’s teachings for his own clergy. So he sends human priests back to Elwynn to learn the traditions of humankind. After reaching Stormwind City, the acolyte finds High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Laurena is relieved that Rohan’s guidance has brought the traveler to her, and welcomes them as their powers begin to grow. In the Cathedral, human priests can keep learning Stormwind’s spiritual practices. There they prepare to wield the Holy Light against the threats around the kingdom.

quest:5678.text: Arcane Feedback. Human priests are being called from Darnassus to Stormwind. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess Alathea reluctantly honors the Alliance summons. High Priestess Laurena waits at the Cathedral of Light to prepare the acolyte for deeper instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests at Darnassus's Temple of the Moon. She honors the formal alliance between the kaldorei and Stormwind, yet distrusts human ways of magic and faith. For ten millennia, grief from the War of the Ancients has shaped the night elves' fear of arcane power. Even human divine rites trouble the clergy when radiant faith blurs with arcane workings. Alathea honors the bond between the Alliance races and sends you to answer a recall from the Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena has sent couriers across the seas to gather human priests for advanced training. In Stormwind, you leave Elune's moonlit groves for grand stone sanctuaries and the golden radiance of the Holy Light.

quest:5679.text: Devouring Plague. In the Undercity, Devouring Plague marks the shadow path of Forsaken priests. Priestess Aelthalyste teaches the rite to those who have proven their dedication to shadow magic. In the Undercity’s War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste teaches Forsaken priests the grim arts of the Shadow. Priests of other races draw on the Holy Light or ancestral spirits, while the Forsaken have shaped their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague gives that path a fearsome form. It torments foes and drains their stolen vitality to sustain the caster’s decaying body. Priestess Aelthalyste shares the plague’s power with care. This potent weapon is meant to turn the tide against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. She warns her disciples to practice until their command is sure. Greater trials await those who seek mastery of the dark arts.

quest:568.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. At Grom'gol, Commander Aggro'gosh guards the Horde's foothold in Stranglethorn Vale. He works to keep supplies moving safely to Stonard by thinning the Lashtail Raptors outside the base camp. Commander Aggro'gosh guards the Horde at Grom'gol Base Camp. The camp is vital to a safe supply line to Stonard, but local inhabitants stand in the way. Lashtail Raptors outside Grom'gol threaten the supply line. Aggro'gosh calls on loyal fighters to thin their numbers, then report back for new orders.

quest:569.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. At Grom'gol, Commander Aggro'gosh moves to guard the supply road to Stonard.
