Skuerto says you need to activate its defenses to have a chance against them. Only then can you reach the items alive. The Boulderfist shaman took certain gems from the tower and have grown fond of them. Skuerto says they will not keep the gems for long. Bring an azure agate to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe. Kryten knows the spell that will enchant it to work as a key.

quest:695.text: An Apprentice's Enchantment. At the camp, Apprentice Kryten enchants the agate you brought from the Boulderfist shaman. It can wake the tower's defenses, and Kryten sends you to Skuerto before you leave. Apprentice Kryten gives you the enchanted gem and explains its power. Touch it to a pedestal at the tower's foot, and its defenses will wake. When you are ready to enter and search for the rest of Trelane's items, use the gem. Kryten will wait for you at the camp. Before you go, speak with Skuerto, who can answer any other questions.

quest:696.text: Attack on the Tower. At Refuge Pointe, Skuerto sends you to search the ogre-held tower for three items tied to Trelane. The phylactery, orb and ember agate should be in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be pleased when you return with them. After Kryten enchants the gem, Skuerto sends you to find Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three items should be in chests inside the tower, ready for you to open. But the ogres are dangerous. The tower's defenses will not deal with them, and the ogres will hurt you if they catch you stealing.

quest:697.text: Malin's Request. In Stormwind, Skuerto's letter carries news from Arathi to Archmage Malin. You are sent to the Mage Quarter with word that Kryten and Skuerto will soon be home. After your work in Arathi, Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It says Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto trusts Malin will repay you well for helping them and wishes you a safe journey.

quest:6981.text: The Glowing Shard. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, you find a green shard whose smoky depths stir unease. Its mystery draws you to Ratchet and onward. You carry a green crystal from deep within the Wailing Caverns. Beneath its bright, solid face, shadowy wisps seem to churn. Those who touch it feel uneasy, and its strange presence hints at the corruption around the sleeping druids and their nightmare-haunted sanctuary.

quest:70.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Goldshire, an old letter renews the search for Stalvan Mistmantle. Its trail runs from Elwynn Forest to Stormwind's Canal District. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Innkeeper Farley recalls a stormy night years ago. A traveling courier came in from the rain to find shelter. Around midnight, he rushed downstairs in a panic, wearing only his sleepwear. He vanished into the storm, and no one saw him again. The courier left his satchel and personal chest in the upstairs room. Among the forgotten cargo was an unsent letter bearing the name Stalvan, addressed to someone in Stormwind City's Canal District. The chest remained untouched at the foot of the bed until Farley allowed it to be opened.

quest:700.text: A King's Tribute. Magni Bronzebeard gives Sully Balloo a memorial in Ironforge. Granite from Lordaeron keeps the fallen dwarf in his people's memory. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned a monument for Sully Balloo, a dwarf who died serving his people. Grand Mason Marblesten carved it from fine granite brought from Lordaeron's war-torn lands. The monument stands in Ironforge, honoring soldiers whose sacrifices help preserve the dwarven kingdom. When told the monument is complete, Magni considers stone and mortality. Carved rock can never equal a brave dwarf's life, he knows, yet he hopes the memorial endures. Then generations walking Azeroth may remember the heroes who bled to secure their tomorrow.

quest:701.text: Guile of the Raptor. Tor'gan seeks to awaken Gor'mul's dormant warrior spirit through the guile of the raptor. He gathers Highland Fleshstalker hearts to make an enchanted charm and restore Gor'mul's fighting resolve. Tor'gan wants to draw Gor'mul out of his listlessness and restore the warrior spirit that lies dormant. He turns to primal magic instead of persuasion, hoping a charm filled with wild predators' essence will stir Gor'mul to action. Through the charm, he seeks to renew Gor'mul's martial resolve and show him the strength of this power. Tor'gan needs Highland Fleshstalker hearts to call on the instincts of a cunning hunter. In shamanic and primal traditions, a predator's heart carries its ferocity and guile. Tor'gan uses these trophies to make a physical token and weave a spell. He hopes they will give Gor'mul a predator's cunning and help him rediscover his calling.

quest:702.text:
Guile of the Raptor. At Hammerfall, Tor'gan sends you to Gor'mul with an orb to rouse the warrior's spirit. Its energy bears the raptor's essence and may give Gor'mul fresh purpose. Tor'gan gives you an orb meant to fill Gor'mul with the raptor's essence. He hopes it will rouse the warrior's spirit and set him on a fresh course in life.

Once Gor'mul is himself again, Tor'gan plans to explain the Horde's present state. He hopes to win the help of a great warrior in its unceasing battles. Gor'mul greets your return with bitterness. He says all he wants is more of Tor'gan's pity, then mocks you with talk of brightly colored string.

quest:705.text: Pearl Diving. In the Badlands, Rigglefuzz is running low on powder for his flash bombs. He sends you to the Vile Reef in Stranglethorn to gather more. Rigglefuzz admits the Badlands frighten him. A short little goblin, he faces predators and scavengers all around. He knows how to make flash bombs, and uses them to drive the wildlife away. Now he is running low on crushed blue pearl powder. Clams at the Vile Reef in Stranglethorn hold blue pearls. Rigglefuzz jokes that you had better wear good boots, then waits in the Badlands for nine pearls. He promises to make your effort worthwhile.

quest:710.text: Study of the Elements: Rock. In the Badlands, Lotwil Veriatus needs stone shards to test his work on elemental shackles. Lesser rock elementals roam the hills just west of him. In the Badlands, Lotwil Veriatus is making shackles of elemental binding. When finished, they will let mages summon stronger elementals for greater uses. To test his offensive spells and a few pieced-together gizmos, he needs ten small stone shards. Lesser rock elementals roam the hills immediately west.

quest:711.text:
Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus is ready to test larger pieces after the small shards behaved as he expected. He needs three large stone slabs from rock elementals. Lotwil Veriatus needs sturdier pieces for his next tests. Rock elementals have larger bodies, so their remains may yield slabs big enough.

He points you farther west or southeast along the mountain edges to gather three large stone slabs. For now, Lotwil needs time to test the smaller pieces you brought. Lotwil's spells acted on the smaller pieces as he predicted. If the next experiment goes as he expects, the elementals he controls will outshine anything he has summoned before.

quest:713.text: Coolant Heads Prevail. Lotwil Veriatus needs Frost Oil for the shackles holding his summoned friend. Bro'kin, Lotwil's goblin friend in Alterac, can teach you to make it. Lotwil Veriatus says Frost Oil keeps engines and gears from overheating. He calls it an unmatched lubricant. It also helps magical items hold their enchantments. The oil could strengthen Lotwil's shackles enough to stop his summoned friend from killing everyone. Bro'kin, Lotwil's goblin friend, can teach you to make Frost Oil. He sells from a spot on the old city's wall in the Ruins of Alterac.

quest:714.text:
Gyro... What?. In the Badlands, Lotwil Veriatus is still at work on his contraption. You have brought him the Frost Oil from Coolant Heads Prevail, but one small part is missing: a gyrochronatom. Lotwil Veriatus is so caught up in his work that he praises you for doing the job beyond all standards. Then he says you may apply for work if you meet him in Kharanos.

A hurried scramble follows as Lotwil tries to catch hold of something. Then he asks for a gyrochronatom. The part is small but crucial, and with it the project should be ready to complete.

quest:7162.text: Proving Grounds. In Alterac, recruits face a trial before they may join the Stormpike Guard. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends them into Icewing Caverns for a planted battle standard. Success earns an official Stormpike Insignia and opens the way through the expedition’s ranks. The Stormpike Guard fights the Frostwolf Clan in Alterac Valley. Lieutenant Haggerdin directs Alliance forces from their encampment in the Alterac Mountains. Before recruits reach the battlefield, he tests their skill and nerve in Icewing Caverns southwest of Dun Baldar. Deep in Icewing Caverns, a Stormpike banner waits among the frozen tunnels. Frost harpies nest in the icy recesses and attack unwary trespassers. A recruit who brings the banner back intact has crossed dangerous ground, faced its predators, and kept discipline under pressure. Return from the caverns with the standard, and you earn a Stormpike initiate’s insignia and a place in the expeditionary force. Haggerdin says the insignia can improve as you earn greater honor on the battlefield. The Eye of Command is one distant aim.

quest:718.text: Mirages. In the Badlands, Sigrun Ironhew's party has fled the Uldaman excavation and gone hungry. Sigrun's party fled the Uldaman dig in such haste that they took little with them. They left wagons and supply crates behind, and ogres from Camp Kosh have been picking through them. The ogres took the cart with all the party's weapons. Since then, the party has had no food. Sigrun admits the trouble is embarrassing and asks you to retrieve the supply crate.

quest:719.text: A Dwarf and His Tools. Prospector Ryedol escaped an attack on his dig site and now seeks his lucky pick. Dark Iron dwarves resembling the Shadowforge clan are all around. Dark Iron dwarves resembling the Shadowforge clan attacked the excavation site where Ryedol worked. Nearly everyone died, including his boss, Hammertoe. Ryedol barely escaped with his life. The site lies north of where he waits. Prospector Ryedol is trying to recover supplies lost in the attack, especially his lucky pick. One of the Dark Iron dwarves has it, though Ryedol does not know which one. He hopes you will help and waits south of Hammertoe's Dig Site.

quest:72.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Stormwind, you search for Stalvan Mistmantle among the Flintridge belongings. By the canals, sealed crates hold what remains of the household, watched over by restless spirits tied to the massacre. You follow Stalvan’s path from Duskwood to Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom guards what remains of the Flintridge household. His father served the estate before him and had to mop up blood after a massacre claimed the household. Somehow, Stalvan’s name is tied to that slaughter. The Flintridge trust funds are gone, and royal tax collectors press the estate. Surviving heirlooms and packed belongings wait inside sealed shipping crates along the canal embankment, awaiting auction. You search them for Stalvan’s trail before the family’s remaining goods scatter to collectors across the kingdom.

quest:720.text: A Sign of Hope. Hammertoe Grez lives, and a chalk plea on a crumpled map calls Prospector Ryedol to help. The note says they are taking Hammertoe to Uldaman. Hammertoe leaves a brief plea for Ryedol in chalk on a crumpled map. The note says they are taking Hammertoe to Uldaman and asks for help. Tell Prospector Ryedol that Hammertoe Grez lives.

quest:729.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. In southern Darkshore, hostile stone golems overrun a dig site, and Archaeologist Hollee seeks help in Auberdine. She fears for Prospector Remtravel, her senior colleague, whose research often blinds him to mortal danger. Archaeologist Hollee came across the sea with the Explorers' League. Master Greywhisker sent her to apprentice under Prospector Remtravel, whose discoveries had made him renowned in Ironforge's academic circles. The League sent them to study ancient ruins along Darkshore's untamed coast. As they dug through what seemed to be the remains of a great civilization, violent stone golems burst from the earth and overran the site. In panic, Hollee fled through the night to Auberdine, the night elf port, to seek help. Remtravel barely noticed the danger. Absorbed in his relics, the elderly prospector stayed among the rubble as lumbering constructs surrounded his camp. South of Auberdine, anyone who reaches him finds him grumbling about missing stone brushes and misplaced fossils.

quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. At Darkshore's southern ruins, Prospector Remtravel presses on with his dig, hoping to find a prize for the Explorers' League. Hostile troggs and his forgetfulness make the search perilous, and word of his safety must reach his assistant in Auberdine. Far south in Darkshore, Remtravel's Dig lies among ancient ruins. Dwarven excavators searching there uncovered troggs, who drove out the workers and besieged their camp. Remtravel will not return to Auberdine empty-handed. He wanders into danger to recover a fossil, hoping to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:7321.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. In Tarren Mill, Christoph Jeffcoat hopes Soothing Turtle Bisque will prove the Forsaken can cook with care. He needs snapjaw meat from Hillsbrad's waterways and the shores of Lordamere Lake. Many think the Forsaken have given up the comforts of life, fine cooking among them. Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill holds otherwise. He boasts that his rich turtle bisque could tempt souls back from beyond the grave. With care in the cooking, he means to show that undead hands can still make a warming dish in a land marked by plague and war. Jeffcoat once gathered ingredients from Hillsbrad's waterways and Lordamere Lake's eastern shores in neighboring Alterac. Now his duties in Tarren Mill and nearby Alliance forces keep him from hunting. So he relies on passing Horde cooks to hunt snapjaws and bring back their meat. Their help keeps his recipe alive.

quest:736.text: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. In the Undercity, Keeper Bel'dugur tests those who seek to lead their own circle. To found a new chapter, they need Yagyin's Digest, but he asks for three unnamed items of power. Practitioners who hope to lead their own circle come to Keeper Bel'dugur in the Undercity. To found a chapter and gather followers, they need Yagyin's Digest, a work of ritual lore in his keeping. Bel'dugur will aid a brother, but first he asks for proof of worthiness before entrusting him with such knowledge. Keeper Bel'dugur asks for three items of power in exchange for Yagyin's Digest. Their names carry peril or sacred weight, so he will not speak them aloud. Instead, he writes them on a private note. Finding all three proves a practitioner worthy of founding a chapter of their own.

quest:738.text: Find Agmond. Weeks have passed without word from Prospector Agmond at the Badlands digs. Prospector Ironband now needs you to find Agmond and bring back his report. Prospector Agmond oversaw the Badlands excavations southwest of Ironband. Ironband calls him a prospector no longer, for weeks have passed without word. He needs you to find Agmond and recover the report. Agmond was last heard from at the southernmost dig, a small outfit beyond Angor Fortress. Begin there.

quest:74.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Beside Stormwind City's canals, you find a clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past in the Flintridge crate. Its torn journal page points toward Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. Beneath a ceramic vase in the sealed crate lies a torn page from Stalvan Mistmantle's journal. Musty Flintridge heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits fill the crate. Stalvan's own hand offers a glimpse of the reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. From Darkshore, Hollee sends Remtravel’s fossil to Darnassus while she stays to watch the wandering prospector. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker takes a keen interest in the find. Prospector Remtravel has found a curious fossil on Darkshore’s coast. He would rather keep digging than follow protocol. So Archaeologist Hollee stays with him among the shore’s dangerous beasts and hostile cultists. She asks you to carry the specimen to Darnassus, where a dwarven scholarly delegation is kept. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea under the Explorers’ League banner. They seek ancient relics and lost history in Kalimdor’s soil. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker marvels at Remtravel’s knack for finding ancient treasures. Night elves see their forests as living sanctuaries, while the League sees ancient lands as ground to study and decipher.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. In Thunder Bluff, The Ashenvale Hunt sends young Horde champions north to serve at the forest outposts. Heralds direct them to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post for a proving hunt. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation through Thunder Bluff for proven adventurers. North of the Barrens, the Horde has footholds in an ancient forest, and its outposts need young warriors. Those who answer will face harsher country and test their survival skills beyond Mulgore. Ashenvale offers the Horde rich resources and severe peril. Splintertree Post lies along the main road, while a remote outpost stands on the western coast at Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart is a veteran outdoorswoman who organizes a great hunt. There, recruits tame the wilderness and win glory for the Horde.

quest:744.text: Preparation for Ceremony. Eyahn Eagletalon is making a headdress for his brother, who soon stands before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof. He asks you to gather the vibrant feathers from harpies beyond Thunder Bluff while he tans the leather bands. Among the tauren, standing before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof brings pride and reverence. Families honor the occasion by preparing proper attire. The traditional headdress is made from treated leather and symbolic plumage, with each part chosen to show dignity and respect before the leader of the united tribes. A ceremonial headdress needs a leather band and feathers for its crown. While the leather straps are tanned, long, pristine feathers must be gathered. Harpies roost in the craggy hills north and northwest of Thunder Bluff, so you must venture into their hostile nests to find feathers of the needed size and color.

quest:75.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Elwynn, your search for The Legend of Stalvan leads you to Marshal Haggard's home. The veteran's failing eyesight left an upstairs chest of papers unread. Marshal Haggard lives near Elwynn Forest's southeastern edge, close to Duskwood and Redridge. Upstairs, an old chest holds parchments he found when he moved into his secluded home. His failing eyesight kept him from reading them, and they have remained untouched until you ask about Stalvan.

quest:750.text: The Hunt Continues. Grull Hawkwind sends young hunters into the southern hills of Red Cloud Mesa for mountain cougar pelts. The hides will clothe the tribe's children and help mend its tents. At Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind sends young hunters south into the hills of Red Cloud Mesa to hunt mountain cougars. This is no search for trophies. The hunt teaches young hunters to provide for their community. Camp Narache needs the pelts to make clothing for the tribe's children and mend worn hide tents. When you bring them back, the elders will be grateful for your contribution. Grull promises to tell his father, Chief Hawkwind, what you have done.

quest:755.text: Rites of the Earthmother. On Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren begin their spiritual journey under Chief Hawkwind's care. He sends them south of Camp Narache to Seer Graytongue, who guides their first steps toward the trials. On Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind sends young tauren to Seer Graytongue in the hills south of Camp Narache. The seer guides the youth as their spiritual path begins. This journey carries them beyond everyday camp life and toward the duties their tribal customs demand. The Earthmother shapes tauren beliefs about creation and daily life. Her rites test maturity, resilience, and spiritual depth. Seer Graytongue warns those who reach his sanctuary that the trials call for full devotion to the traditions of the mesa.

quest:7792.text: A Donation of Wool. In Darnassus, wool cloth is gathered to support the city's stores. Your sixty pieces earn recognition for your generosity. Darnassus needs sixty pieces of wool cloth from you. Others across the realm are expected to provide the rest of its stores. Your donation earns full recognition for your generosity.

quest:78.text: The Legend of Stalvan. Marshal Haggard sends you to find Tavernkeep Smitts, who may know the hand behind a page from Stalvan's journal. Marshal Haggard cannot read the faded writing on the torn journal page you recovered from his chest in Elwynn Forest. His failing eyesight leaves the words beyond him. He recalls serving with the Stormwind Guard and spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. So he sends you across the river to Tavernkeep Smitts, whose years behind the bar have made him a keeper of local history and rumors.

quest:7802.text: A Donation of Wool. At Ironforge, wool donations help support its stores. Sixty pieces bring full recognition for your generosity. Ironforge asks you for sixty pieces of wool cloth. Its stores need only that much from you. Others are expected to give enough to support the drive.

quest:7807.text:
A Donation of Wool. Across the realm, A Donation of Wool calls for aid to the Gnomeregan Exiles. Driven from Gnomeregan, they need wool cloth to sustain their displaced people. Sixty pieces earn formal recognition among the gnomes. Gnomeregan's fall to trogg invaders and radioactive contamination drove its surviving gnomes from their high-tech city. They now live as refugees, hosted chiefly by their dwarven cousins in Ironforge.

Outside their ancestral halls, the Gnomeregan Exiles face severe strain in supplying their people. Regular drives for cloth and other basics help keep them clothed, supplied, and organized. The drive asks each volunteer for exactly sixty pieces of wool cloth. By gathering modest contributions from across the realm, the exiles can collect the textiles they need for bedding, bandages, and clothing without overburdening any one supplier. Those who aid their recovery receive formal recognition among their people.

quest:78124.text: Nar'thalas Almanac. Scholars seek the Nar'thalas Almanac to preserve ancient magical study. Its recovery brings forgotten lore into a library where researchers can study it. A rare work of arcane study, the Nar'thalas Almanac comes from the ancient traditions of pre-Sundering night elven scholarship. For caretakers of great archives, securing the volume rescues centuries-old lore from obscurity and adds an important piece of history to their shelves. Those who uncover neglected works help bridge forgotten antiquity and modern scholarship. Across Azeroth, archivists and researchers seek lost treatises, field notes, and chronicles. Bringing the Nar'thalas Almanac to a dedicated library lets its keepers safeguard, catalog, and study it, rather than leave it to rot in ruins or fall into careless hands. Each recovered volume offers fresh insight into the arcane arts of past eras.

quest:78127.text: The Dalaran Digest. The librarian asks you to bring magical works for the collection. Each book adds knowledge to the library. The librarian welcomes magical works that may benefit the library. You bring a book to join the collection, helping its knowledge grow.

quest:78142.text: Bewitchments and Glamours. In Ironforge, the library is seeking magical works for its shelves. You can help its keepers widen their knowledge by bringing in books that may benefit the collection. Bring magical works to the library in Ironforge, where each addition can broaden what its keepers know.

quest:78143.text: Secrets of the Dreamers. A library's scholars seek writings tied to the Dreamers and other magical lore. Travelers bring forgotten works from across the realm, where they can be studied and kept in the archives. Scholars across the realm depend on travelers to recover rare magical texts and historical treatises. These works lie in ancient ruins or private hoards, far from the archives. So adventurers carry them safely to those who study Azeroth's arcane mysteries and preserve its lore. When travelers bring in treatises, archivists add them to the library's permanent collection. Researchers seek obscure writings on the Emerald Dream and arcane theory. Their work continues, and they welcome further magical texts found in the field.

quest:78146.text: Goaz Scrolls. The librarian asks you to bring Goaz Scrolls for the collection. Your contribution adds to the library’s knowledge. The librarian thanks you for contributing Goaz Scrolls. More magical works could help the library too, and the librarian welcomes them.

quest:7820.text: A Donation of Wool. Thunder Bluff seeks wool cloth, and you can earn its full recognition by giving sixty pieces. Other donors are expected to bring enough supplies to support the drive. Thunder Bluff is gathering wool cloth. Give sixty pieces to earn full recognition for your generosity. Other donors in the realm are expected to bring enough to support the drive.

quest:7826.text: A Donation of Wool. In Orgrimmar, A Donation of Wool asks for help gathering cloth. The city has wool in its stores and expects more donors to bring in enough for the drive. Orgrimmar asks you to give sixty pieces of wool cloth. In return, the city promises recognition. Its stores already hold some wool, and other donors are expected to help support the drive.

quest:7833.text: A Donation of Wool. A Darkspear troll gathers wool donations, and your sixty pieces of Wool Cloth join a larger collection. The Darkspear trolls are gathering Wool Cloth to replenish their stores. The collector can take your sixty pieces now, while help from others is expected to complete the collection.

quest:789.text: Sting of the Scorpid. At the Den in the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new Horde recruits after scorpids northwest of camp. Ten tails will prove they can face danger in battle. Gornek tests novice Horde recruits against the Valley of Trials' wildlife. Scorpid workers roam the rocks northwest of the Den. Their venom has humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. Recruits must face them and bring back ten tails as proof of their skill. Scorpids are dangerous, yet their venom also helps save injured initiates. The Den keeps antivenom brewed from extracted scorpid venom to treat fallen novices. Gornek teaches recruits to stay watchful in battle. Even a small foe can wield enough venom to fell a mighty warrior.

quest:79.text:
The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, The Legend of Stalvan rests on muddy pages and new proof. Tavernkeep Smitts gives you the pages and sends you to Commander Althea Ebonlocke. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard once investigated the slaughter of a visiting noble family in Duskwood. Haggard then led the Stormwind Guard. At the scene, they found torn, muddy journal pages, but had no handwriting samples or other papers to confirm who wrote them. So the notes could not formally implicate the recluse rumored to live in the wilderness.

Now evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood links the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle. The old rumors have become proof of murder.

quest:79007.text: ... and that note you found. At a recent campsite, cooling embers and scattered supplies are all that remain. A scorched parchment bears a riddle about finding a twin land, the only clue left behind. A recent campfire is dying beside scattered provisions and a blistered piece of paper. Whoever stayed here left recently, and the parchment narrowly escaped the flames. The supplies remain exposed, as though the traveler departed in haste or was interrupted. The surviving scrap bears one instruction: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” No signature, coordinates, or further context survived the fire. The riddle is the only trail left for whoever finds it.

quest:79008.text: ... and that note you found. A scorched note lies beside a dying campfire in Westfall. Its brief message points to a place called the twin land. Travelers crossing Westfall’s abandoned fields and wind-scoured plains find camps left by vagrants, outlaws, or desperate wanderers. This small camp was left in haste or secrecy. Its provisions lie abandoned, embers still glow, and a scorched slip of parchment rests among the scattered debris. The blistered note bears two short sentences: “Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.” Its words point away from Westfall but give no clear direction. What place shares a name, geography, or fate with this land?

quest:79091.text: Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography. In Ironforge, you seek Archmage Antonidas: The Unabridged Autobiography. The rare volume holds the late Kirin Tor leader's own account and offers insight into Dalaran's history and high arcane scholarship. Archmage Antonidas led the Kirin Tor for decades and ruled Dalaran. One of Azeroth's most brilliant minds, he rose through the ranks of the Violet Citadel and mastered the arcane. His unabridged autobiography records his leadership during the Second and Third Wars. For scholars and practitioners of magic, it offers a firsthand view of Dalaran's inner workings and the arcane arts. Before reaching its new home, the rare manuscript rested in Ironforge's grand library. In the Hall of Explorers, dwarven archivists kept it beside ancient titan relics and dwarven histories. Their vast collections hold texts gathered from ruins and foreign kingdoms across Azeroth. Yet arcane scholars elsewhere seek such works for their own collections, sure the busy archivists will never notice one missing volume.

quest:79092.text:
Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus keeps a journal of his investigations. Now you carry its magical insights to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, where they can join the dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is an esteemed spellcaster known throughout the Alliance. He is stationed at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, where he has studied alone for years. His investigations range from curious artifacts and ley line anomalies to nearby magical threats.

He records his findings in detailed journals. This volume offers a rare chance to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage. The Explorers' League and the caretakers of the Ironforge Library maintain one of the continent's greatest archives. You bring Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal to them, helping preserve and catalog its arcane insights beside the historic volumes of Khaz Modan. The librarians welcome further magical discoveries that can broaden their shared wisdom.

quest:79093.text: Rumi of Gnomeregan: The Collected Works. A compiled work by Rumi of Gnomeregan is sought for a library’s collection. Its pages preserve gnomish writings and knowledge that might otherwise be lost. Gnomish writings were scattered, buried, or left in danger when troggs overran Gnomeregan. Now scholars and archivists seek surviving manuscripts, treatises, and compiled works. They hope to keep the wisdom and ingenuity of gnomish thinkers alive. When travelers find collected works in the field and bring them to the archives, curators add them to their growing collections. Each recovered manuscript widens what scholars can study. Archivists welcome more magical and historical texts, keeping them within reach of scholars, mages, and historians who guard Azeroth’s learning.

quest:79095.text: The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer. Curators seek The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer to enrich their archives. Its delivery helps preserve rare alchemical and arcane theory for researchers and spellcasters. Curators welcome The Apothecary's Metaphysical Primer for its study of esoteric and magical principles. Owen Thadd adds the text directly to his working collection of magical references. Owen Thadd's collection in Undercity preserves specialized treatises. By bringing him rare primers on arcane and alchemical theory, you help keep metaphysical insights safe in the archives and accessible to researchers instead of leaving them lost in the wilderness.

quest:79096.text: Ataeric: On Arcane Curiosities. Ataeric seeks rare magical writings to enlarge a library's collection. Scholars hope these works will deepen their study of the arcane and keep its lore safe. Across Azeroth, scholars rely on travelers to recover rare tomes and treatises from dangerous ground. Ataeric seeks magical writings to broaden an institution's study of the arcane. Each volume can help scholars piece together practices that might otherwise be scattered or lost. The curator adds each curiosity to the archive. The library remains eager for further magical writings found across the world, so its collection can grow with ongoing scholarship.

quest:79097.text: Baxtan: On Destructive Magics. At the library, Baxtan: On Destructive Magics joins the works scholars gather to understand dangerous arcane power. Scholars seek to preserve what is known of arcane lore. When you find a text on destructive magic, its place is in careful academic keeping. There, its power and peril can be understood instead of lost. The library holds works on history, science, and the arcane. Its scholar welcomes travelers who recover forgotten treatises from dangerous corners of the world. Each volume adds to the library's knowledge.

quest:79192.text: Stepping Stones. At a backcountry camp in the Barrens, a weathered note points toward Stepping Stones, a mountain refuge near Desolace. It says two couriers made deliveries for the New Plague, and calls their sudden ends simple apothecary accidents. A torn message hangs from a wooden plank at a backcountry camp in the Barrens. Mercenaries, cutthroats, and drifters stop at such camps for brief shelter, far from the eyes of the Crossroads or Ratchet. Among the ordinary signs of the wilds, the note gives you reason to look beyond the camp toward the mountains.

quest:79236.text: Cherry for Your Thoughts?. In Booty Bay, Tokal offers a drink for the truth about attacks on human and dwarven outposts. Rumors blame the Horde, but her band served a private mercenary contract. Tokal keeps out of sight in Booty Bay and watches for law enforcement. Recent raids devastated human and dwarven camps, and rumors blame the Horde. When travelers come who clearly do not work for the marshal asking questions, Tokal gives another account. She offers to tell it in exchange for a drink.

quest:79974.text: Wet Job. On a mountainside, Wet Job sends you to recover an emergency reserve stash. Someone prepared it for a hasty escape and hid it near a high cliffside perch. In dangerous country, a reserve can make a quick escape possible. You search the rugged heights for a stash someone left there in case plans went wrong. Its supplies are waiting to be recovered. The directions lead to a high mountain perch, described as carved from the waterfalls of time. There, at the eagle's nest, a weathered messenger bag lies partly buried in the earth. Inside, provisions and parchment have endured beneath the soil, protected by dwarven craft.

quest:79975.text: Eagle's Fist. At a misty overlook, Eagle's Fist keeps a lonely watch over a weathered barricade. A letter speaks of loyalty to the Old Kingdoms and the Eagle and Fist, though its writer has left in haste. A folded letter lies inside a toolbox at a high overlook. From here, its writer says, one can call the shots or launch a parachute glider across the land. Misty spray dampens this lonely post, but the view reaches across historic lands. The letter's writer pledges lasting loyalty to the Eagle and Fist. To serve that cause well, the writer says, one must keep a measured distance. The nearby barricade has fallen into disrepair, like the Old Kingdoms it once shielded from danger. Still, the watcher vows never to abandon the post.

quest:79976.text: This Must Be The Place. At This Must Be The Place, a camper has vanished moments before anyone could catch up. A torn note says the writer has taken their work underground to keep it from the wrong hands. Someone broke camp at this secluded spot only moments ago. An inadequately secured sleeping bag unrolls underfoot, while heavy canvas lies bundled over assorted gear. A small scrap of paper holds a hurried parting message, but whoever camped here has vanished before anyone could catch up.

quest:79980.text: Scramble. A scavenger's note sends travelers down a steep cliff in search of Scramble's hidden supplies. One hundred paces north, they find provisions and a dirty parchment. A note points the way to a hidden supply cache. Its writer offers a few informal words of encouragement, then gives precise directions: go one hundred paces due north down the treacherous cliffside. Provisions wait there to keep a traveler going.

quest:80.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, the search for Stalvan Mistmantle brings a bloodstained journal page to the Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke sends you to Clerk Daltry to compare its writing with the town records. The Night Watch has gathered journal pages from across Duskwood and the surrounding human territories. Together, they seem to condemn Stalvan Mistmantle, the elusive tutor. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has suspected him for some time, but she needs proof before passing judgment. The bloodstained page alone cannot show who wrote it. Its hand must be matched to Stalvan’s.

quest:815.text: Break a Few Eggs. Cook Torka is waiting on fresh eggs from the Echo Isles before the next meal. You carry them back unbroken so the kitchen can keep to its schedule. At Razor Hill in Durotar, Cook Torka prepares meals from morning through evening. Breakfast gives way to lunch, then dinner, with little time to leave the stove for provisions. So Torka sends you to the Echo Isles for Taillasher eggs before the next meal service falls behind. Bring them back whole, and the cook can keep the kitchen working on time. Cook Torka has little time for praise while meals wait to be made. Eggs need a gentle touch, since a cracked shell spoils an ingredient the kitchen needs. When you bring the eggs back unbroken, Torka sends you on your way and returns to work over the fire.

quest:822.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn turns to another recipe Chen Stormstout shared with him. Trogg ale calls for rare organs and glands from the Barrens' beasts. You helped Brewmaster Drohn recreate Chen Stormstout's first draught. Now you learn the wandering pandaren shared more brewing secrets. Drohn has the formula for trogg ale, a strange brew made from potent parts of the wild beasts of central Kalimdor, not grain. Trogg ale calls for lightning glands from stormhides, a saliva gland from greater thunderhawks, and a hearty liver from the roaming kodos of the plains. Distilled together, these ingredients make a fiercely stimulating drink for life in the wilderness.

quest:824.text:
Je'neu of the Earthen Ring. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu of the Earthen Ring studies a corruption spreading through the region. Horde travelers bring him a corrupted water globe taken from Ashenvale's elementals. He seeks to understand the blight along the Zoram Strand and in Blackfathom Deeps, hoping to halt the poison in the waters. Mastok Wrilehiss sends you to Je'neu Sancrea with a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals. Strange elementals have appeared across the region, driven by power the scouts cannot explain. Among their remains, one intact globe pulses with corrupted magic.

Mastok knows soldiers and scouts lack the spiritual insight to understand it. So he directs Horde travelers to someone versed in ancient legends and elemental lore. Je'neu Sancrea serves the Earthen Ring, an order of shamans devoted to balance among Azeroth's primal forces. Horde forces guard the Zoram Strand frontier while he studies the spiritual wound in the nearby temple ruins of Blackfathom Deeps.

To Je'neu, an elemental drawing strength from a tainted vessel is no isolated threat. It is an alarming omen: unseen ancient powers are perverting the natural order.

quest:8249.text: Junkboxes Needed. Fahrad keeps Ravenholdt supplied with locked boxes for rogue training. He trades specialized throwing knives for authentic heavy junkboxes, and his demand never ends. Ravenholdt Manor hides in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, where training never ceases. Master thief Fahrad oversees the guild's operatives and prizes skill at picking locks. Zan supplies practice contraptions for new recruits. Fahrad finds them too crude for experienced thieves who must open stubborn mechanisms in the field. Fahrad pays for heavy junkboxes stolen from dangerous targets across Azeroth, and accepts them in batches. Only skilled thieves can lift the boxes from their marks in the wild, but anyone may bring them to the manor. Even boxes stripped of major valuables earn his favor and finely balanced throwing knives from the manor. A token coin must remain inside, to motivate the initiates.

quest:8312.text: Hallow's End Treats for Spoops!. For Hallow's End Treats for Spoops!, an ailing child asks travelers to gather holiday sweets. Innkeepers in the cities and Kali Remik in Sen'jin Village share treats, and Spoops offers magical candy in return. Spoops is too ill to join Hallow's End outdoors. While others celebrate, Spoops asks travelers to gather holiday treats. In return, Spoops offers candy that changes whoever eats it into strange shapes. Travelers can find holiday treats in settlements across the realm. Innkeepers in major cities ask visitors to perform tricks before sharing their sweets. Kali Remik also gives out treats in Sen'jin Village on the coast of Durotar.

quest:837.text: Encroachment. At Razor Hill in central Durotar, Gar'Thok sends you west against Razormane camps. Their fortified dens still threaten the young orc homeland. When Thrall brought the orcs to Kalimdor and founded Durotar, the Razormane already ranged across much of the harsh, arid land. These aggressive, boar-like quilboar became a constant danger to the new settlement. The Horde drove most of them back through sustained military efforts. Yet fortified pockets remain in thorned redoubts west of Razor Hill. Gar'Thok, an officer at Razor Hill, leads the effort to remove the remaining Razormane. He sends seasoned defenders into the western bramble camps to kill their scouts, warriors, and dustrunners. Gar'Thok and the Horde leadership fear any quilboar foothold near Razor Hill could bring disaster. They see this strike as the first step toward securing Kalimdor. Once the quilboar defenders are gone, Horde forces can burn the bramble dens and keep the Razormane from reclaiming the western foothills. The fire destroys an enduring menace and secures Durotar's western perimeter. It also protects the vital supply roads between Razor Hill and the wider realm.

quest:8373.text: The Power of Pine. During Hallow’s End, Sergeant Hartman asks you to clear Forsaken stink bombs from Southshore. A pine-scented cleaner helps keep the village clean. During Hallow’s End, the Forsaken foul Southshore with stink bombs. The bombs mar the celebration of liberation. Sergeant Hartman asks you to remove any that have landed in the village with a Stink Bomb Cleaner.

quest:843.text: Gann's Reclamation. In the southern Barrens, Gann's Reclamation turns toward Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire, a tauren exile, asks you to strike at the dig after it drove him from his clan's ancestral home and hunting grounds. Gann Stonespire walks alone along the southern road, seeking justice for his fallen kin. His clan lived among the red bluffs south of the Barrens. Dwarves from Ironforge built Bael Modan there, driving the tauren out or killing them to make room for quarries and trenches. Gann says peaceful protests and diplomacy failed. Now he seeks vengeance for his displaced and slain clan. At Bael Modan, dwarven excavators tear into the hills with steam engines and explosives. Prospector Khazgorm leads the dig deep underground. Gann asks you to thin the ranks of Bael'dun excavators and foremen, kill Khazgorm, and bring back the prospector's personal excavation notes. He wants to learn what the Alliance expedition seeks in the sacred soil.

quest:846.text: Revenge of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire prepares to strike back at the Bael Modan dwarves. After Prospector Khazgorm's death, he sends Horde allies into the fortress to seize volatile munitions for his attack. Gann Stonespire knows Prospector Khazgorm's death has only slowed the Bael Modan dig site. The dwarves will return to work, and another foreman will soon direct the machines cutting through Gann's ancestral land. He will not watch the earth suffer more excavation. So Gann means to turn the invaders' demolitions gear against them and rupture their stronghold from within. Bael Modan's fortress guards an excavation base and a garrison of soldiers, riflemen, and officers who protect dwarven interests in the Barrens. Its defenders carry nitroglycerin, wood pulp, and sodium nitrate for industrial demolition. Gann sends Horde allies past the perimeter to take these volatile supplies. With enough in hand, he can assemble a powerful satchel charge.

quest:847.text: Guile of the Raptor. Tor'gan's orb has filled Gor'mul with a raptor's essence. The power makes him wonder about shaman magic, and he will hear Tor'gan out for now. Power runs through Gor'mul, and he wonders if it is the shamans' power Tor'gan tried to show him. The thought interests him. So he asks you to tell Tor'gan he is convinced for now and will hear what Tor'gan has to say.

quest:849.text: Revenge of Gann. At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for his fallen tribe. Bael Modan’s dwarven excavation covers ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors depend on a gyrocopter for reach and military strength. It waits on a watchtower above the dig, surveying the Barrens and guarding the dwarves’ supply lines. To Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

quest:857.text: The Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan, Feegly the Exiled still begs for the Tear of the Moons, the relic that drove him mad. Dwarves found the Tear of the Moons while cutting into the southern Kalimdor hills for Bael Modan. It was the expedition’s first major discovery. Its strange influence fell at once on Feegly, one of the workers. Feegly claimed the Tear gave him immense power. He turned violently on his comrades to protect it. General Twinbraid saw the relic’s corrupting hold, called it cursed, took it from Feegly, and locked it in the keep. Banished from the excavation camp, Feegly took refuge among the cliffs. Bitter and obsessed, he begs passing travelers to steal the Tear back.

quest:862.text: Dig Rat Stew. Grub waits east of the Crossroads, hungry for dig rat stew. He sends travelers to Bael Modan in the southern Barrens for the rodents his recipe needs. Hunters cross the dry Barrens in search of zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors. Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads, wants something else: dig rats. Hungry all day, he offers his recipe to any traveler willing to catch the burrowing rodents. Deep in the southern Barrens, dwarven prospectors dig into the red earth at Bael Modan. Their work has disturbed nests of dig rats. The dwarves see an infestation; Grub sees a feast near the excavation. Grub says dig rats taste best after rotting for several weeks. For a hungry traveler who wants food now, he accepts fresher meat. His recipe shows how forgiving roadside cooking can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

quest:86576.text: Bloodfury Trinkets. Mor'rogal asks you to bring him sunstones from the Bloodfury harpies in the Charred Vale. He says they are bound to the lights of the skies. The Bloodfury harpies gather shiny things, among them golden-yellow sunstones. Mor'rogal is up on the hills above you and has mentioned using them. He asks you to bring him any Glittering Sunstones you find. Mor'rogal says sunstones reflect the sun's majesty. They can adorn shrines and homes with small motes of light. At night, the moon lends them its silver beauty. To him, they recall a bond with the lights of the skies.

quest:86585.text: Banner of the Fallen. In trogg territory, Mountaineer Ylva’s search for missing comrades ended beneath the trampled standard of Ironforge. Raising it again draws out the trogg that struck her down. Mountaineer Ylva’s trampled Ironforge standard marks where the Alliance scout met her end. She entered trogg territory to find comrades who had vanished on patrol, carrying the city’s banner as a sign of defiance. A powerful trogg struck with enough force to shatter her defenses. The standard was left in the dirt.

quest:86614.text: Silver of the Waves. A lost silver hair clip waits among fishing debris, and its owner is caught up in daily chores. Its return brings relief and restores a keepsake thought lost to the water. Among discarded fishing debris, you find an ornate silver hair clip marked with the initials K.D. Rusted hooks and broken wire spools lie nearby. Moisture has tarnished the clip, but its fine work still shows beneath the corrosion. The clip belongs to a hardworking local, busy with daily chores. You return the keepsake, which its owner had thought lost to the water for good. A little polishing will restore its shine, and the grateful owner welcomes its return.

quest:86667.text: Snowbound. In Loch Modan, Grenhild studies the local elementals while Norric Lochthane asks for snow from South Gate Pass. His request carries a deeper hope: the aging shaman longs to see his former student again. Grenhild is studying Loch Modan's local elementals when a minor elemental arrives with a message from Norric Lochthane, her former mentor. He urgently needs fresh, unmelted snow for his shamanic workings. Grenhild asks a traveler to fetch it so she can stay with her studies. The snow comes from South Gate Pass, where cold drafts preserve the drifts year-round, and must be sealed in a specially crafted ceramic jar to keep the valley heat at bay. Norric Lochthane lives in a quiet cottage on the Loch's northwest coast, away from the settlements. When the jar arrives, he is pleased to have the cold reagent for his mystical research. Yet he laments that Grenhild did not come herself. His request was for more than a magical ingredient: the aging shaman hoped to reconnect with his former student, now following her own path.

quest:86776.text: Ingredients for the Forge. In Thelsamar, Morhan Coppertongue needs bronze bars to fill his dwindling workshop stores. Far from Ironforge's steady trade, the settlement depends on travelers to bring the metals its forge needs. Thelsamar keeps a quieter pace than Ironforge's Great Forge. Far from the capital, supplies can be hard to come by. Morhan Coppertongue, the local blacksmith, makes the hardware, pots, and tools the township needs. Yet bronze and other raw metals often run short. Without regular shipments from the city, passing travelers and prospectors help keep the local anvils at work. Bronze bars let Morhan resume making goods for daily use. But the forge still faces shortages, and Loch Modan has no reliable merchant route bringing coal to town.

quest:868.text: Egg Hunt. Across the Barrens, Korran seeks silithid eggs for study. The Horde scholar at the Crossroads has heard of clever insect creatures in the south and wants their intact eggs brought to Orgrimmar. From the Crossroads, Korran watches the Barrens and sends reports to Orgrimmar. The Horde faces tribal conflicts and Alliance incursions, yet the land itself is changing. In the southern Barrens, intelligent insects have begun to burrow. They move as one mind. Korran needs samples to learn where the silithid come from and what drives them. With an excavation claw, you travel to the Field of Giants and lift intact eggs from the dirt mounds. Disturb one mound and the nearby brood comes to defend it. Their coordination is uncanny.

quest:8682.text: Skyseer the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skyseer the Elder waits atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Travelers come to honor the ancestors and receive his blessing. Wooden bluffs tower over Freewind Post. Elder Skyseer rests among them in a shaft of celestial light, near the bridges leading to the great mechanical lifts. Winds sweep across the mesas of Thousand Needles around his ghostly form. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Skyseer welcomes travelers who come to honor the past. He can guide them to his kin across Kalimdor, including Elder Morningdew and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8724.text: Morningdew the Elder. In Thousand Needles, pilgrims seek Morningdew the Elder beneath a beam of starlight during the Lunar Festival. She offers wisdom and directions to elders across Kalimdor. During the Lunar Festival, ancient ancestor spirits appear across Azeroth to bless travelers. In Thousand Needles, Morningdew the Elder stands beneath a shaft of lunar light, amid red stone and industrial noise. She urges mortal travelers to turn from earthly concerns and look to the stars. Morningdew points seekers toward the countless stars for answers to earthly mysteries. She also guides festival pilgrims to other honored spirits across the lands: Elder High Mountain, Elder Grimtotem, Elder Mistwalker, Elder Moonwarden, and Elder Windtotem.

quest:87288.text: Soft Saber Pelts. Across Azeroth, Soft Saber Pelts come from cats that threaten travelers on the roads. Their thick coats make warm blankets and shawls. Saber cats prowl the roads used by couriers, merchants, and lone travelers across Azeroth. People may admire their grace, yet growing numbers near trade routes bring sudden attacks. Hunters keep those roads safe for everyone who depends on them. The hunt yields more than pelts. Frontier camps value saber cats’ dense coats for their warmth and strength. Skilled hands make the pelts into shawls and heavy blankets, giving shelter from harsh weather.

quest:873.text: Isha Awak. Along the Merchant Coast, Mahren Skyseer sends you hunting in the Great Sea. Slay Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, and bring back its heart for a rite of spirit and respect. South of Ratchet, Isha Awak prowls beneath the waves. The immense sea creature is known as the Deep Doom and holds the coastal waters by force. Human forces camped along the shore fear those waters. They have lost many scouts and soldiers to the predator. Mahren Skyseer reveres the leviathan, while the humans fear it. To the tauren mystic, Isha Awak is no curse or mere pest. It is a worthy foe whose might tests a hunter's resolve. Slaying the beast brings spiritual communion. Its heart holds the beast's essence, and claiming it lets the hunter carry that untamed spirit forward.

quest:874.text: Mahren Skyseer. At Camp Taurajo, proven hunters are sent east to Mahren Skyseer. Jorn Skyseer sends them to his sister to learn how to track along the Barrens shore. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer tests hunters against the dangerous beasts of the southern Barrens. Once they prove themselves on the red plains, he sends them beyond dry earth and open savanna. A tracker must learn to follow prey through swamps, over sheer crags, and beside the crashing waves of the Great Sea. Mahren Skyseer keeps a camp far east along the coast. Jorn studies thunderhawks and plains stalkers, while his sister follows creatures that live in the salt spray. Reaching her means crossing dangerous ground. Kul Tiras marines and Theramore expedition forces hold fortified outposts and watchtowers across the coastal lowlands.

quest:87491.text: Spark of Freedom. The fire elemental has spent its strength in a blazing display. The Dark Irons held its attention, and the rest of the group is relieved it never turned on them. The fire elemental's display leaves the onlooker amazed, then relieved when the creature runs out of strength. The Dark Irons had drawn its attention. Had it turned on the rest of the group, they too could have been in danger.

quest:876.text: Serena Bloodfeather. Across the northern Barrens, harpy attacks threaten the Crossroads supply lines. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing flock against the Horde, driven by vengeance for her sister, whom Rexxar slew during Durotar’s founding. Breaking the flock’s coordination could open the trails again. Witchwing harpies strike the trails northwest of the Crossroads under Serena Bloodfeather’s command. Hunger is not their only cause. Serena seeks vengeance against the Horde for her sister, the notorious matriarch Bloodfeather, whom the beastmaster Rexxar slew during Durotar’s founding. Now Serena rallies her flock against supply trains, scouts, and merchants on the arid trails.

quest:878.text: Tribes at War. From his cage in Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth bargains for help against the Bristleback. The Razormane captive offers intelligence about quilboar attacks in exchange for the deaths of rival spiritual leaders. The tauren hold Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar, in Camp Taurajo. For years, the Razormane and Bristleback have contested the Barrens. Their sudden ambushes make it hard for the Horde to secure its settlements and supply lines. Mangletooth offers to explain who is tormenting Thork's outpost, but first he asks a Horde champion to kill the Bristleback's most revered casters. Mangletooth sends you north to strike at the Bristleback's spiritual heart: its Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. Killing these casters weakens Bristleback rituals and leaves the tribe open to Razormane rivals. It also eases pressure on nearby trails.

quest:879.text: Betrayal from Within. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers Horde travelers a path to vengeance. His Razormane kin left him for dead, and he names three warlords from Razorfen Kraul who direct attacks across the Barrens. Mangletooth sits in a cage at Camp Taurajo, abandoned by his Razormane kin after their defeat. He has lost all loyalty to them and now faces execution. He offers Horde travelers knowledge of the leaders behind the ruthless raids across the plains, hoping to see those leaders fall before his own end. Razormane attacks trouble the Horde, while Thork at the Crossroads struggles to curb them. Mangletooth names three commanders from deep within Razorfen Kraul: Lok Orcbane, a formidable warrior, and his companions Nak, a tracker, and Kuz, a spellcaster. They direct raiders from encampments far to the south. Mangletooth demands their severed skulls as proof that his betrayers have fallen before his own end arrives.

quest:883.text: Lakota'mani. At Camp Taurajo, hunters bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer after the hunt. The offering honors the kodo's spirit and marks the hunter as an equal to its strength. Across the Barrens, Lakota'mani moves among the kodo herds, famed for great size and endurance. In Taur-ahe, the tauren tongue, his name means “Earthshaker.” Each step rumbles across the plains. Tauren hunters track and defeat such a beast not for slaughter, but to meet the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife in a sacred hunt. When you bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the hunt reaches its close. Jorn sees new power and a stronger stride in hunters who return from the encounter. The trophy earns his blessing. It honors Lakota'mani's courage and primal spirit as companions on your path.

quest:884.text: Owatanka. In the southern Barrens, Owatanka roams as a swift thunder lizard the tauren call Bluebolt. Bring his crackling tailspike to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. The gift honors the elders’ tradition of learning from Kalimdor’s primordial beasts. Tauren hunters speak of Owatanka with reverence. Unlike his massive, plodding kin, he moves with blinding speed. They call him Bluebolt, for the storm changed him. Tauren lore says lightning struck Owatanka long ago. The thunder lizard survived, filled with unending energy and fury. Even after his death, his tailspike crackles with stray sparks when handled, a remnant of the storm’s power. Take Owatanka's Tailspike to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. It marks a hunter’s prowess and spirit. Jorn recognizes the encounter in the eyes of any hunter who has outmatched the beast’s speed. Presenting the trophy honors Bluebolt’s enduring swiftness.

quest:885.text: Washte Pawne. Across the southern Barrens, Washte Pawne's feather leaves hunters with a pain they carry to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. For the tauren, the hunt becomes a trial of regret. Thunderhawks are hard to find in the Barrens, and the nomadic tribes honor them. In Taurahe, Washte Pawne means “Spirit Biter.” Its death is no ordinary hunt. Shamans whisper that striking down a thunderhawk may bring triumph or misfortune. After Washte Pawne falls, its feather burns against the skin with a pain that lingers. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer explains that the ache is regret, not poison. Taking a magnificent life carries a burden. The hunter must face that sorrow and turn it into lasting wisdom.

quest:8852.text: Ten Signets for War Supplies. Warlord Gorchuk trades Horde Commendation Signets for war supplies in Orgrimmar. Champions exchange formal recognition for equipment to help keep soldiers supplied at the front. Warlord Gorchuk oversees the Horde's supplies in the Valley of Spirits. As the Horde gathers its legions, weapons, rations, and armor must reach the front. Champions who have proved their dedication can trade commendation signets for useful equipment from the army's reserves. Horde Commendation Signets prove a soldier's service and bring prestige with the leadership. Trading them for gear gives up that recognition for a better chance to survive the fighting. Gorchuk knows a satchel of supplies or a sturdy weapon can mean the difference between life and death when armies clash.

quest:88756.text: Bring Back a Bang. A construction site has lost blasting powder to Dark Iron dwarves camped east on Direforge Hill. Their marked barrels could bring danger to the surrounding lands. Dark Iron dwarves camp east on Direforge Hill. They raided a nearby construction site and carried its vital blasting powder back to their tents. Blasting powder in malicious Dark Iron hands threatens the surrounding lands. The stolen barrels bear red markings that set them apart from common supplies. Recover them before the dwarves put the powder to destructive use.

quest:889.text: Spirit of the Wind. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a swift crossing of the Barrens through Agamaggan’s blood shards. His ritual lends them the speed to pass through the plains. The Barrens are easier to cross quickly, before its beasts and centaur warbands find you. At Camp Taurajo, the captive quilboar Mangletooth draws on red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. Bring him ten, and he channels their lingering power into a burst of swiftness called the Spirit of the Wind. Quilboar honor Agamaggan, the Great Boar whose blood spilled across central Kalimdor during the ancient War of the Ancients. Though held captive, Mangletooth knows the rites that channel that blood. His ritual stirs wild vigor, lending a runner speed to match the zhevra herds. The quilboar are bitter enemies of the Horde, yet Mangletooth shares Agamaggan's boons with travelers who bring him fresh shards.

quest:89.text: The Everstill Bridge. In Lakeshire, The Everstill Bridge waits unfinished while its iron goes to war. The town forged its construction iron into weapons during the last orc invasion, and Redridge gnolls ambushed the replacement caravan from Stormwind. Across Lake Everstill, Lakeshire's stone bridge still lacks its final work. It links the western roads toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. Recent orc incursions nearly ruined the town. To survive, Lakeshire melted the bridge's iron into munitions, blades, and plate armor against the Blackrock invaders. The bridge remained unfinished and exposed. Foreman Oslow sought fresh materials from the House of Nobles and Stormwind. A caravan bearing iron set out, but Redridge gnolls ambushed it on the road. They carried iron pikes and rivets to their camps in the northern hills. You can help recover the stolen supplies. Without them, repairs remain stalled as gnolls and orcs tighten their hold on the mountains.

quest:891.text: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet wants Northwatch Hold's guns silenced. Its gunners have been firing on merchant vessels, so he sends you down the Merchant Coast to strike the artillery officers and bring back badges from fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold guards the southern Barrens coast for the humans of Theramore. Its soldiers watch Horde activity in Kalimdor. Yet fear makes them see every unfamiliar sail as a threat. Their guns fire without warning at passing ships, putting Ratchet's merchant traffic and privateering vessels in danger. Captain Brightsun wants an answer for the attacks on his ships. Captain Fairmount commands Northwatch, while Whessan and Smythe direct its guns. Defeat them and take Theramore medals from the garrison. The artillery will fall into disarray, giving Ratchet's ships room to travel along the Merchant Coast.

quest:893.text: Weapons of Choice. At Camp Taurajo, Tatternack Steelforge studies reports of sturdy Razormane weapons. He sends travelers past the Field of Giants to recover them, so the Horde can judge the danger. In the southern Barrens, the Razormane are making unusually durable weapons. The Horde has taken notice, for most quilboar are thought to fight crudely with wood, bone, and stone. Tatternack Steelforge, an orc smith at Camp Taurajo, investigates under orders from Warchief Thrall. He doubts the quilboar know proper metalwork and seeks proof: have they learned new techniques, or found better supplies? Tatternack needs weapons from different parts of the Razormane arsenal to study their craft. South of the Field of Giants, scouts face Razormane war camps and seize weapons from their fighters. Razormane Stalkers carry backstabber daggers, Razormane Seers wield charred wands, and frenzied shock troops bear heavy war shields. Together, these arms reveal something of the martial and mystic arts behind the Razormane push against Horde territory.

quest:897.text: The Harvester. In the southern Barrens, a severed head brings The Harvester’s strange presence to Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer examines the remains, and the creature’s arrival threatens the land’s spiritual and natural balance. You find the severed head of a silithid called the Harvester in the southern Barrens. Lions, raptors, and kodos roam these grasslands, but this chitinous insect is unlike the native wildlife. Its presence suggests an alien ecology has reached Kalimdor’s open plains.

quest:898.text: Free From the Hold. At Northwatch Hold, Gilthares Firebough waits in a dungeon after Alliance forces sink his ship off the Barrens coast. The elf deckhand longs to reach his captain in Ratchet. Gilthares Firebough is held in the dungeons of Northwatch Hold. Theramore keeps this fortress on the Barrens coast as its military foothold, with a garrison watching for threats. Gilthares was aboard a ship carrying moonshine between Ratchet and Booty Bay when Alliance forces bombarded it and sent it beneath the sea. He alone survived. The soldiers brought him to Northwatch and accused him of conspiring against the Alliance as an enemy agent. Gilthares says he is only a deckhand who carried illicit liquor. With help from Horde forces, he fights his way out of Northwatch Hold and flees north along the shore toward Ratchet. There, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun welcomes him back to the crew of the Thalo'dan Privateers.

quest:899.text: Consumed by Hatred. At the Crossroads, Mankrik turns his grief into a campaign against the Bristleback quilboar. Separated from his wife in a violent ambush, the orc calls on Horde travelers to kill the creatures and bring back their tusks. Mankrik still bears the grief of the quilboar ambush that battered him and left his wife missing. At the Crossroads, he looks toward the arid horizon and thirsts for Bristleback blood, though he has killed many himself. Now he calls on fellow Horde travelers to help him carry on the fight. Mankrik demands sixty Bristleback quilboar tusks. Each one marks suffering returned to the creatures that tore his life apart. The trophies cannot heal his grief or end his desire for revenge. Yet seeing the Bristlebacks bleed brings the wounded warrior a fleeting, bitter satisfaction.

quest:90.text: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Chef Grual prepares his signature dish for Darkshire. He asks you to hunt Duskwood wolves for meat while his herbs arrive from Stormwind City. Darkshire stands isolated among the horrors creeping through Duskwood. Trade caravans seldom reach town, farming has failed, and undead lurk nearby, yet people still need food. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, Chef Grual turns dangerous forest wolves into hearty skewers. The local soil and timber cannot support delicate crops, so he relies on spices from the capital to make the gamey meat palatable. Grual has just received a shipment of Stormwind Seasoning Herbs. Now he needs lean meat from the ferocious wolves stalking Duskwood. The delivery shows how Darkshire remains tied to the wider kingdom. Royal military aid has dwindled, while supply lines between city merchants and outer hamlets barely endure.

quest:906.text: Betrayal from Within. In the central Barrens, Betrayal from Within brings the hunt for Lok Orcbane to its end. His fall will weaken the Razormane raids, and you carry his severed head to Thork at the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth is a captured Razormane quilboar held in a cage. He names Lok Orcbane as the chieftain directing attacks on Horde caravans. After you slay Lok deep in the southern thorn mazes, Mangletooth gives you the chieftain's skull. He finds it amusing that the orcs will benefit from betrayal within the tribe without knowing a captive quilboar helped them.

quest:91.text: Solomon's Law. In Lakeshire, Bailiff Conacher seeks proof that the sentence against the Shadowhide gnolls has been carried out. They aided Morganth, an enemy of Stormwind, and the town hall has decreed their deaths. Lakeshire governs Redridge with little military help from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon and the town officials rely on strict frontier authority to keep order. Bailiff Conacher works from the town hall as the magistrate court's arm. When threats reach the township, the court places bounties on offenders. It depends on hired mercenaries and traveling defenders to uphold the kingdom's laws. The Shadowhide clan faces execution for aiding Morganth, a rogue spellcaster in the eastern hills. Lakeshire and Stormwind law calls for death when someone directly helps a declared enemy of the realm. The gnolls carry out Morganth's bidding. So the court treats them as treasonous fighters, not wild scavengers.

quest:91282.text: A Second Home. Newly risen Forsaken are being invited to join an order in Tirisfal Glades. They are directed to Bandarion Keep, a monastery on the bluffs northwest of the Solliden Farmstead near the Whispering Woods. The order offers community, shared faith, and mutual support as they make a place in their new unlife. Newly risen Forsaken in Tirisfal Glades are urged to find fellowship among their peers. Together, they can face unlife through mutual faith and community, and discover their full potential. Travelers are directed to Bandarion Keep, a monastery on the bluffs northwest of the Solliden Farmstead. Beside the Whispering Woods, it offers the new order a refuge to study, practice, and establish roots in Tirisfal.

quest:91285.text: Murlocs at the Gates. Breton Samuels asks you to drive back murlocs troubling the keep. Their attacks make rebuilding harder. Murlocs still trouble the keep after you and the others drove them from their spawning grounds. Their attacks are growing harder to manage, so Breton Samuels asks you to drive back some of them. They lurk in the bluffs along the eastern road and in camps around the lake to the west. Breton Samuels expects the attacks to continue. He hopes pushing back the Vile Fin attackers and seers will slow them down. The keep is already hard to rebuild while murlocs strike at its people.

quest:91294.text: Touring the Grounds. Breton asks you to walk Bandarion Keep after the murloc attacks come under control. Meeting Danitha Morr is your first step toward settling among the residents. Breton asks you to meet Bandarion Keep’s residents and look around the stronghold. Once you have finished, Danitha Morr can help you settle in. The keep is still small, but its people call it home. Danitha Morr introduces herself as the closest thing Bandarion Keep has to a commander. She welcomes those seeking fellowship with people still loyal to the Light. The keep needs help before it can be fully established.

quest:913.text: Cry of the Thunderhawk. In the southern Barrens, Cry of the Thunderhawk brings a hunter to the final trial. Entrusted by Camp Taurajo's elders, you seek a winged serpent in the scrublands and return with its wings to prove mastery of the savanna's fiercest beasts. After hunters prove themselves against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, Jorn Skyseer directs them toward their final challenge. The thunderhawk is one of the fiercest aerial predators around Camp Taurajo. Slaying one takes patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess. Bringing back the thunderhawk's wings ends a novice's tutelage under Camp Taurajo's watch. To the tauren, hunting is no mere slaughter. It is a spiritual walk in harmony with the Earthmother and the wild's natural order. Besting this proud creature shows strength, courage, and honor, virtues needed before entering the harsher wilderness beyond the central plains.

quest:91316.text: Making Repairs. At the fortress, a shortage of building materials has made restoration difficult. You are sent to Shadowvale to search for lumber. Shadowvale is a ruined village in the Whispering Forest, southwest of the fortress. Search an old root cellar in one of its buildings for usable materials. The fortress lies far from settled lands, so bringing in supplies is difficult. Its repairs depend on what can be found there.

quest:91317.text: The Tarnished. At Shadowvale in Tirisfal Glades, the Tarnished threaten a fledgling order's place among the Forsaken. Their attacks deepen mistrust and put the order's future at risk. Some risen still bear prejudices from their former lives, and now attack their fellow Forsaken. The Tarnished have gathered at Shadowvale, southwest of here. Their violence must end, and Commander Rudolph Gelhardt’s head must be brought back. The Tarnished’s attacks give those who distrust the order more reason to turn against it. Stopping them may help the order earn a place among the Forsaken. Acceptance could still take years or decades.

quest:914.text: Leaders of the Fang. In the Wailing Caverns, four leaders of the Druids of the Fang threaten the Barrens. Nara Wildmane sends Horde champions from Thunder Bluff to slay them and take their twisted dream gems. If the druids are not stopped, their serpentine nightmare may claim the land. Naralex, a night elf druid, entered the Wailing Caverns' underground springs. He hoped the Emerald Dream would bring life back to the dry Barrens. But when he fell asleep, his dream became a nightmare. The acolytes who came with him abandoned nature's harmony and fell under its corruption. They became the Druids of the Fang. Four leaders of the Druids of the Fang carry dream gems that channel warped dream energy. They hope to reshape the Barrens into their own viperous Eden. Lord Cobrahn, Lady Anacondra, Lord Pythas, and Lord Serpentis each carry one gem. While the gems remain with them, corruption spreads through Kalimdor's soil and waters.

quest:91723.text: Delicate Instruments. Hamish Bergwort's instruments at the Tower of Azora falter as surges of magic rise from the north. Their source is Jasperlode Mine, where kobold geomancers stir the earth. At the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort's arcane apparatus needs careful calibration. Uncontrolled surges keep unsettling his measurements. He cannot make precise adjustments while the interference continues. The magical pulses lead north to Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have taken its tunnels, where their geomancers work crude earth magic. Their frequent rituals send ripples through the stone. Those tremors unsettle the Tower of Azora's sensitive instruments.

quest:91724.text: Delicate Instruments. At the Tower of Azora, Defias magic troubles Delicate Instruments. Hamish Bergwort's equipment suffers from erratic spellcasting near Stone Cairn Lake. The disturbance must end before his instruments can work properly. Hamish Bergwort studies arcane questions in the Tower of Azora. His work depends on precise readings, and even a slight change in local magic can ruin hours of careful study. He suspects crude spells nearby are causing the interruptions. Defias rogue wizards practice magic near Stone Cairn Lake, and their casting causes the interference. Their unchecked spellcraft brings unstable magic into Elwynn. End their casting, and the disturbance will cease, allowing Bergwort's instruments to give clean readings.

quest:91725.text: Stolen Enchanting Supplies. Near the Tower of Azora, Blixie Fitzwink has lost the supplies she was carrying after a gnoll ambush. The enchanting reagents are scattered among camps around Stone Cairn Lake. Their return could spare her weeks of chore duty and keep Master Theocritus's arcane studies supplied. Blixie Fitzwink was carrying supplies from a trading post to the Tower of Azora when gnolls ambushed her on the road. She fled, leaving the cargo scattered among their camps along Stone Cairn Lake. The valuable reagents were meant for Master Theocritus, whom Blixie assists. Now she asks travelers to recover them, fearing weeks of cleanup duty after her arcane polymorph experiments. Master Theocritus conducts sensitive magical research at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. His work depends on delicate reagents brought from local trading posts. Gnoll packs around Stone Cairn Lake have grown bolder, making the route dangerous. The lost supplies could interrupt his studies, while their return may spare his beleaguered assistant further trouble.

quest:91732.text: Good Steel. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Hagar Lowe seeks good steel for the tools worn by its woodcutters.
