quest:93948.text: Deliver the Signet. A traveler carries the recovered Shadowsong Family Signet to High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. Its return confirms his nephew's death on Zephras Isle, and Talaanis points the traveler toward the local peacekeepers. A traveler carries the Shadowsong Family Signet to Valanaar, recovered from an isolated tower. The grim token is meant for Talaanis Shadowsong, the High Elder of Zephras Isle. His people love him, though hardship weighs on the settlement. The ring confirms his nephew has perished, and Talaanis receives the heirloom with condolences. In Valanaar, High Elder Talaanis thanks the traveler for returning the signet, though grief shadows him. He recognizes the traveler's skill and points them to Captain Valennia Stormfist, who leads the Valanaar peacekeepers. The settlement faces strained circumstances and mounting pressures. Its protectors welcome capable hands.

quest:93949.text: Bugged. In Valanaar, seasonal skyhopper swarms now threaten the settlement. High Order mages found listening enchantments on slain insects, and local cultists are suspected of spying through them. When skyhopper season comes, lowland insects swarm around Valanaar. High Order mages inspected several slain skyhoppers and found listening enchantments on them. Local cultists are suspected of using the seasonal pests to eavesdrop on the city. The enchanted skyhoppers look like ordinary insects, so Valanaar's protectors must cull the whole swarm. Clearing them out denies the hostile cult intelligence and ends its magical surveillance of the city.

quest:93951.text: A Little Beauty. In the Shen'dar Highlands, the Skyborne gather hippogryph down near Zephras. Its bright plumes bring beauty and small joys to the village through hard times. Wild hippogryphs nest on Zephras Isle, southwest of the village in the Shen'dar Highlands. They are territorial and can trouble travelers nearby. Yet they shed vibrant, silky soft down, which the Skyborne gather to weave into hair ornaments. For Zephras's artisan, gathering feathers for hair is more than vanity. Even in hard times, small joys shared with others help keep the community's spirit alive. Beauty gives each day in the village something to celebrate.

quest:93958.text: The Inner Sanctum. At the Shrine of Akir, Valennia Stormfist's assault has gone silent. Her force breached the deepest chamber amid fierce fighting, and now allies outside fear for those within. Valennia Stormfist led her detachment into the inner sanctum of the Shrine of Akir after a hard assault. Fighting sounded from deep within the chambers, fierce and desperate. Then the noise stopped without warning. Allies waiting outside can only fear the worst.

quest:94.text:
A Watchful Eye. At the Tower of Azora, Theocritus watches Morganth from afar. He sends travelers east into Redridge Mountains to place an enchanted glyph at an old lion statue near the Tower of Ilgalar. From his tower in eastern Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches the hills. His rival, Morganth, is a powerful sorcerer who has claimed the Tower of Ilgalar in Redridge Mountains. Fearing Morganth's dark magic may cross the border, Theocritus made the Eye of Azora to watch the rogue wizard from afar. A distant view cannot show Theocritus what Morganth plans. So he gives travelers the Glyph of Azora and sends them to the Old Lion Statue near the Tower of Ilgalar. The statue has kept watch there for decades.

Set the glyph into the worn hollow at its base. An arcane link then reaches back to Azora, letting Theocritus look into his rival's mind.

quest:94003.text: The Skybreaker Bulwark. At the Shrine of Akir, Zaal Stormshield holds the Skybreaker Bulwark. The last of the Skybreakers seeks its return from the cultist who took it. On Zephras Isle, the Al'Aketh have slain the Skybreakers, leaving one survivor. The last of the family bears deep sorrow and bitter shame over the loss of their greatest heirloom. The cultist Zaal Stormshield took the Skybreaker Bulwark and now lurks at the Shrine of Akir. By family tradition, the Skybreaker Bulwark protects anyone truly worthy to wield it. The last Skybreaker believes Zaal unworthy of its divine favor. So the survivor seeks an adventurer to strike down the thief at the Shrine of Akir and reclaim the ancestral shield. In return, the Skybreaker offers training in the Skybreaker Defense technique.

quest:94007.text: Taming the Beast. In Valanaar, Quel'ana Quickgale can teach you to tame a beast. Your time in the highlands has prepared you to seek an animal companion. Your host believes you are ready to seek an animal companion after your time in the highlands. Go to Valanaar and speak with Quel'ana Quickgale. He will teach you the art of beast taming.

quest:94013.text: Taming the Beast. Quel'ana Quickgale gives you one last trial in taming a Vuldren Alpha. Mastering it prepares you for the deeper teachings of your class. Quel'ana gives you a Taming Rod and sends you to the Gustberry Lowlands. There, you are to tame a Vuldren Alpha. Then return the rod to him in Valanaar. This trial proves your mastery and prepares you for deeper class teachings.

quest:94050.text: Training the Beast. In Valanaar, you meet Quel'dora Quickgale to learn how to train your pet. Her teaching helps you care for and guide it. Your fellow hunter sends you to his sister, Quel'dora Quickgale, in Valanaar. You already know how to tame a pet. Now Quel'dora can teach you to train your companion. Quel'dora teaches you to guide your pet, teach it new abilities, feed it, and revive it if it falls in battle. She urges you to respect the balance and remain in awe of the nature around you.

quest:942.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. In Darkshore, a strange fossil draws you across the Great Sea to the Wetlands. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sends you to Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor, hoping he can unlock its secrets. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sees a likeness between the strange fossil from Darkshore and a relic shown at an Explorers' League conference in Ironforge. Archaeologist Flagongut presented that relic and believed such fossils held powers waiting to be unlocked. Greywhisker thinks Flagongut is the only dwarf who can discern what makes this Kalimdor find so extraordinary. You carry the mysterious fossil from Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Flagongut was last seen lodging at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, waiting for an armed escort to the Whelgar Excavation Site. When you bring him the fossil, the Darkshore survey reaches across continents as part of a wider archaeological inquiry.

quest:94222.text: Craftsman's Writ: Iridescent Hammer. A customer awaits one Iridescent Hammer, with delivery and payment details set down in a writ. Its transferable mark lets the holder complete the exchange. The customer asks for one Iridescent Hammer. Bring the writ to complete the exchange at the marked location.

quest:94243.text: Craftsman's Writ: Heavy Quiver. A faded Craftsman's Writ: Heavy Quiver asks you to bring one Heavy Quiver to a marked location and gives payment details. The note asks you to acquire one Heavy Quiver and bring it to the place marked on your map. Keep the writ with you to complete the exchange.

quest:94253.text: Craftsman's Writ: Colorful Kilt. A customer seeks a disguise for slipping into Zul'Gurub, and Craftsman's Writ: Colorful Kilt names the garment they want. The transferable writ asks you to bring one Colorful Kilt to the marked location. The customer plans to pass through Zul'Gurub's gates dressed as one of its ritualists, and says the kilt suits the disguise.

quest:943.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. In Darkshore, Remtravel's dig sends his search across the Great Sea. In Menethil Harbor, Archaeologist Flagongut hopes to join Remtravel's finds with his own fossil and the lost Stone of Relu, revealing the relics' hidden powers. You once helped the distracted Prospector Remtravel during an escort through northern Darkshore. Now the search crosses the Great Sea to the Wetlands marshes. Prospector Whelgar keeps Flagongut's original fossil at his excavation site. After reviewing the finds, Archaeologist Flagongut believes the Stone of Relu can unlock the mysterious powers within the fossils.

quest:94369.text: The Fate of Zephras. In Valanaar, you bring Talaanis Shadowsong word of the danger facing Zephras. The fallen wards leave the isle exposed to Al'Akir, and its people must decide how to protect their home. You tell Talaanis what happened above the Shrine of Akir. You share Elaadrin's plan to leave Zephras Isle. High Elder Shadowsong needs to understand the danger and why you were sent to Azeroth. The people of Zephras must find a way to save their home.

quest:94373.text: Call of Earth. At Anvilmar, Teo Hammerstorm tests initiates who seek the earth's favor. They face Frostmane trolls to the south and claim bear pendants before receiving an earthen sapta. In Coldridge Valley, Teo Hammerstorm guides initiates at Anvilmar along the earth's rugged path. He teaches young wanderers to heed the mountains and see the land as firm ground. Stone can shield those who respect it. The earth shares its wisdom only with those who show grit and patience. To prove they are ready, initiates face Frostmane trolls in a cave south of Anvilmar. The trolls make coarse pendants from Iceclaw bears that roam the frozen heights. Recovering two bear pendants from the den proves the stubborn resolve and strength the elemental spirits expect.

quest:94374.text: Call of Earth. At a mountain Spirit Stone, an initiate drinks Earth Sapta and binds spirit to the world's enduring foundations. The draught opens the way to elemental awareness, teaching humility and patience amid snow and rock. At an isolated mountain shrine, you drink Earth Sapta, an enchanted brew. Ancient elemental magic gives it power to show mortal eyes elemental spirits and subtle currents beyond ordinary sight. Its strength makes the shrine the only safe place to drink it, where spirit and stone can form their bond. High on a snow-swept mountain, the Spirit Stone waits at the end of a secluded path. You travel through bitter cold to stand humbly before the ancient rock. The living earth welcomes those who come without pride. Mountains give lasting physical strength, while the vast, steady plains teach patience. Communion with stone is a foundational rite for spiritual pathfinders. Wind, fire, and crashing water carry restless fury, while earth teaches discipline and quiet resilience. You absorb earth's still essence, preparing mind and body for the conflicting, chaotic dualities of the more volatile elements that roar across the world.

quest:94375.text: Call of Earth. Young shaman in Dun Morogh seek the earth spirits’ favor through Call of Earth. They carry rough quartz to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar, where he shapes it into the heart of an Earth Totem. In Dun Morogh, young shaman begin their spiritual path by seeking the earth spirit and listening to its teachings. The spirit gives them rough quartz, a humble stone meant to become the heart of an Earth Totem. The rite calls for humility, patience, strength, and resolve. An initiate learns from the earth and does not measure worth by size. Teo Hammerstorm waits in Anvilmar for the initiate to bring back the rough quartz. He judges whether the mountain spirits have acknowledged them, and sends away anyone who arrives without the stone. Bring him the quartz, and he shapes it into an Earth Totem. The totem binds the young shaman to the strength of the world's roots.

quest:94411.text: Meddlesome Mages. In the Shen'dar Highlands, High Order apprentices gather at sacred stones and meddle with magic. Their spells threaten the fragile forces that hold the island together. North of the village, High Order apprentices gather around ancient standing stones. Repeated warnings have not turned them from the sacred sites. They press on with their arcane studies, while local leaders hesitate to shed the blood of their shen'dorei kin. So they call for outside help to drive the apprentices away before lasting harm is done. Delicate mystical forces bind the island's land together and keep it safe. The defenders fear the High Order gives little thought to the danger in its spellcraft. One careless spell could break those bindings. Then ruin would come to everyone who lives there.

quest:94413.text:
A Magical Affront. On Zephras, A Magical Affront sets the local order against the Windshapers. The order seeks to harness and study the surfaced leylines, while the Windshapers see them as scars to heal. Their conflict has reached the southwestern forest. Ancient conduits of raw magic have recently broken through the earth on Zephras. For scholars and practitioners of the local order, this is a rare boon. Direct contact with the leylines gives them new insight into the arcane currents across the region and deepens their mastery of magic. The Windshapers see the exposed energies as open wounds and scars across Zephras. They gather at the rupture sites to suppress or mend the leylines and heal the earth.

The order depends on that raw power, so it sees their efforts as a threat. It sends you southwest into the forest to drive the Windshapers back.

quest:94427.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Your order sends you to Tanis Alderwood in Undercity’s Trade Quarter. There, a chance to show grace comes through good deeds. Your order teaches that divinity means doing good for its own sake, not seeking godhood. It says tragedy brought you here. Now it asks you to find Tanis Alderwood in Undercity’s Trade Quarter. Tanis is in need and may benefit from your grace.

quest:94434.text: A Lesson in Divinity. In the Undercity, Tanis Alderwood asks you for fresh cloth. His wife is falling apart, and he hopes to wrap her until an apothecary is free. The apothecaries are occupied with the Dark Lady's business. So Tanis asks you to bring linen for his wife. He hopes the cloth will hold her together while they wait for help.

quest:94435.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Tanis Alderwood thanks you for your help and calls you a friend. Danitha Morr sees this small act of service as a way to strengthen the Forsaken’s connection to the Light. Danitha Morr says your help may strengthen the Forsaken’s connection to the Light. Mistrust and conspiracies linger among the Dark Lady’s followers. The Forsaken must meet that fear with courage and righteousness. Danitha gives you a symbol for what comes next.

quest:94436.text: A Lesson in Divinity. In A Lesson in Divinity, Danitha Morr asks you to show what a priest can do with the Symbol of Life. Deathguard Billmuth at Bandarion Keep has come seeking aid for a friend. Billmuth says the priests turned him away, and his friend may have no one else to turn to. He is not proud to ask you, but he needs aid for the Forsaken. The Symbol of Life is meant to show your ability to channel the Light. Handling it may cause discomfort. Its power can still be your ally and guide, even to the Forsaken, whose creation is tied to a force opposed to the Light.

quest:94438.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Danitha Morr sends you to Venomweb Vale to find Deathguard Falgan. He and his companion were separated after learning the Scarlet Crusade plans an attack on Brill. Deathguard Falgan went with Billmuth to scout Scarlet activity in Venomweb Vale. They learned the Scarlet Crusade plans some kind of attack. Now Falgan asks whether you will help the Forsaken further.

quest:94440.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Deathguard Billmuth needs you to recover Scarlet Crusade attack plans from Venomweb Vale. The Deathguard expects an assault and hopes the plans will help prepare an ambush. Scarlet Crusaders carry deployment orders in their satchels, and the Deathguard expects an attack. Bring a copy of the plans to Deathguard Billmuth at Bandarion Keep. Then the Deathguard can prepare an ambush.

quest:94441.text: A Lesson in Divinity. A fellow Forsaken asks you to thank Danitha Morr for the paladins’ service at Bandarion Keep. Your work has earned the Deathguard’s gratitude and brings a gift of redemption. A fellow Forsaken asks you to carry their thanks to Danitha Morr at Bandarion Keep. The rest of the Deathguard will hear of the service you and the other paladins performed. They are proud to count you among the Forsaken and trust the Dark Lady watches over you.

quest:94449.text: Call of Fire. In Dun Morogh, an elder sends shaman initiates to Bruegs Kindleborn to test their readiness for the fire sapta. They have already learned patience and grounding through earth. After proving patience and grounding through earth, shamans face a more volatile force: the fire elemental spirit. Stone holds steady, but fire promises chaos, ruin, and fierce energy. So an elder sends the initiate across Dun Morogh’s snow-laden peaks to seek guidance before trying to harness its wild heat. Bruegs Kindleborn keeps watch in a secluded cave high in the mountains above South Gate Outpost. When an initiate arrives with an elder’s recommendation, Bruegs prepares them for the sapta of fire. He warns that flame’s hunger to burn and consume is easily stirred. To master it, a shaman must know when to hold back.

quest:94465.text: Call of Fire. You carry the Torch of the Dormant Flame through Loch Modan to seek Braldir Ashmantle. The trial tests whether an initiate is ready to wield elemental flame. To earn the totem of fire, you carry the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame into the crags of Loch Modan. Beyond the stone carvings of the Valley of Kings, a steep path climbs to an isolated mountain summit. There the elements hold sway, far from the roads travelers know. Braldir Ashmantle watches over the Shrine of the Dormant Flame on a high, windswept peak. Unprepared wanderers and fortune hunters find only silence and bare stone. But when you arrive as a true initiate bearing the sacred torch, Braldir reveals the elemental power sleeping within the shrine's brazier, waiting to be rekindled.

quest:94466.text: Call of Fire. In Loch Modan, initiates seek the Eternal Flame and the fire totem it grants. Braldir Ashmantle guides them through a trial that calls for reagents from kobolds and troggs. They prepare a fire sapta and learn that flame can forge and give life as well as destroy. In Loch Modan, Braldir Ashmantle guides initiates who seek the power of flame. Before they can commune with fire spirits, they must attune their mortal spirits with a sacred draught called a fire sapta. Without it, the Eternal Flame would consume them instead of enlightening them. Braldir asks each petitioner to gather two reagents from hostile valley dwellers and prove their resolve. A fire sapta needs substances rich in elemental power. In the north, Tunnel Rat Geomancers gather sticky fire tar in their warrens to fuel their subterranean magic. In the south, Stonesplinter Seers carry reagent pouches filled with primitive elemental charms across the hills. Claiming these items means facing two of Loch Modan’s most entrenched pests, and gaining what is needed to bind an initiate’s soul to flame. Once the reagents are gathered, Braldir Ashmantle teaches patience alongside the power to destroy. To him, fire means more than fury and ash. It is life, the craft of the forge, and the breath of creation. Mastery calls for balance: shadow gives meaning to light, and flame keeps stone from being only a cold memory. To master fire, an initiate must learn when to blend rather than burn.

quest:94467.text: Call of Fire. At the shrine, an initiate drinks fire sapta to face the trial called Call of Fire. The rite asks them to subdue a spirit and offer its embers to the sacred brazier. An initiate receives prepared fire sapta, guided by elemental lore. The draught awakens their senses to the unseen world. After drinking at the shrine, they climb toward the peak, where mortal sight gives way to primal forces. There, a dormant manifestation of fire awaits their challenge. The Minor Manifestation of Fire tests an initiate's resolve and endurance. It does not attack until challenged, then grows fiercer with each passing moment. When subdued, it yields glowing embers. Carry them to the brazier atop the Shrine of Eternal Flame to kindle the torch and win the spirit's lasting favor.

quest:94468.text: Call of Fire. Above Loch Modan, an initiate kindles the flame that must reach Dun Morogh. Bruegs Kindleborn awaits its return and judges the traveler's command of the elements. An initiate lights the Torch of Eternal Flame on a mountain ridge above Loch Modan. The flame marks the beginning of a deeper bond with the elements. From there, the initiate carries it down the trails and into the snowy vales of Dun Morogh. In Dun Morogh, Bruegs Kindleborn awaits the traveler. He is an elemental mentor who judges whether the traveler's inner fire has taken hold. The blazing torch proves the initiate's will and reverence for fire. Bruegs then grants the Fire Totem, welcoming the flameborn into a lineage of elemental guidance for their kin.

quest:94484.text: Unnerving Silence. In northeastern Shadowgale Forest, a druid enclave has gone silent. Since Ban'aethall fell into ruin, unrest has spread through the territory. After Ban'aethall fell into ruin, unrest stirred through the territory. Regular messages from the druid conclave in a cave in northeastern Shadowgale Forest have now stopped. Their allies have heard nothing, and worry grows as the forest grows more unsettled. You are sent into northeastern Shadowgale Forest to find Elegael Thornpaw, a prominent druid of the enclave. Has the conclave withdrawn deeper into communion with nature, or have the dangers that tore through Ban'aethall reached the cave? No one knows the enclave's fate.

quest:94485.text: Tears of the Lady. In Shadowgale, Lady's Tear moss may keep Elegael's wounded companions alive. They are trapped in Nightclaw Den, and Elegael needs medicine from nearby trees. Elegael needs your help in Shadowgale. Wounded companions are trapped inside Nightclaw Den, critically injured and waiting for aid. Ordinary supplies are scarce, so you gather medicine from the surrounding woods. Their wounds cannot wait. Elegael needs Lady's Tear, a spindly moss clinging to tree bases across Shadowgale. Its secretion is viscous and sticky, with natural antiseptic properties. It seals open gashes and shields traumatic wounds from worsening in the damp wild. With enough moss, Elegael can prepare dressings to stabilize the fallen.

quest:94486.text: Feathers for Binding. In Shadowgale Forest, healers need young shrieklings’ feathers to bind a healing poultice. The usually docile birds now attack travelers, making the plumage dangerous to gather. Field healers in Shadowgale Forest treat grave injuries with moss and antiseptic tree sap. Harsh weather can dry the sap or rob it of its strength. So they bind the poultice with young Shadowgale shrieklings’ feathers, which shield the wound and hold the medicine in place. Gathering the soft feathers has grown dangerous. Young Shadowgale shrieklings are usually docile woodland dwellers, but lately they have turned inexplicably aggressive. Their strong talons can inflict lethal wounds. Now the fledglings strike at passersby. Local caretakers mourn the need to cull young beasts. Yet emergencies threaten the region, and the shrieklings grow more dangerous. Thinning their numbers gathers vital curative materials and curbs a rising threat along forest paths. Each feather is treated with respect, so the beasts’ sacrifice is not wasted.

quest:94487.text:
Unwanted and Unworthy. On Zephras, bloodshed in Shadowgale Forest drives Elegael to seek vengeance and recover stolen heirlooms for the High Elder. The Al'Aketh Cultists ambush the local druids in Shadowgale Forest. Elegael had thought these zealots harmless dreamers, with clouds between their ears. Now druid blood stains the forest floor, and Elegael demands swift retribution against the Footsoldiers and Stormchasers responsible. Elegael believes the cultists' betrayal has cost them their heritage. They no longer deserve the name shen'dorei, nor do their remains deserve the winds of their homeland. Many were young, their promising futures cut short by fanaticism.

Their bloodied heirlooms must return to the High Elder. There, the sacred items await a wiser and more worthy generation.

quest:94488.text: The Ties That Bind. Elegael Thornpaw faces a traitor among Shadowgale Forest’s druids. Haalien vanished months ago, then joined the attacking cultists and rose to command them. Now Elegael orders his execution. Druids face a vicious cultist attack in Shadowgale Forest. Elegael Thornpaw finds Haalien’s scent over the slaughter. Haalien was a druid of the circle who vanished months ago, but he did not perish in the wilds. He joined the invading cultists and now commands their violent campaign against his former kin.

quest:94489.text: The Wounds of Betrayal. In Shadowgale Forest, Elegael cares for the shen'dorei druids wounded in a terrible assault. Poultices are ready for Nightfang Den, north across the clearing, while her mate Jorel Windsinger is missing. Elegael tends the shen'dorei druids hurt in the assault on Shadowgale Forest. She has prepared poultices for her brethren sheltering in Nightfang Den, just north across the clearing. Few shen'dorei druids remain, and every survivor matters to their fragile enclave.

quest:94490.text: Ripped Missive. Haalien bears a bloodied letter after an attack on a druid den in Shadowgale Forest. Its words reveal what the cultists sought and point toward danger within Valanaar. Haalien's missive gives a glimpse of the violence in Shadowgale Forest. Found after a fierce skirmish, the torn scrap bears grim news of cultists who attacked a local druid den. Its words offer clues to those seeking justice for the fallen.

quest:94491.text: The Fate of the Den. At the druid den, survivors mourn their fallen after the cultist assault. The Fate of the Den reaches Lotheluum in Valanaar with a recovered missive and word of heavy losses. The dispatch reveals that someone in Valanaar has been feeding vital information to the enemy. Cultists struck the druid den and left its defenders battered and grieving for fallen comrades. Outside aid brought the immediate danger under control, but the physical and emotional devastation remains immense. The dead cannot be brought back, and the wounded survivors are too weak for the long trek. Lingering cultists still roam nearby.

quest:94493.text: A Sacrifice in Vain. Elegael Thornpaw fears the Al'Aketh Cultists will overwhelm the wounded in her den. A message meant for Valanaar has not reached them, leaving her to ask for help. The Al'Aketh Cultists fell upon Elegael Thornpaw's fellows with almost no warning. Many in her den are wounded or dying, and she does not know how long they can survive the attack. She had tried to send word to Valanaar, but the message did not get through. With no reinforcements in sight, Elegael asks you to help.

quest:94494.text: Call of Water. In Loch Modan, Norric Lochthane calls a shaman toward water's purity. Having found harmony with wind, earth, and flame, the initiate is ready to commune with water. A shaman who has found balance with earth, wind, and flame now turns to water. Its lesson reaches beyond a force to wield. Water offers a spiritual image of purity and resilience. Norric Lochthane urges the initiate onward without delay. Communion with the elements demands effort and endurance, and the way climbs through rugged country. The mountain waits for no one. Understanding begins with the ascent.

quest:94495.text: Call of Water. In the Wetlands, seekers learn what pure water can do and search for the water sapta. Beneath the southern falls, Hervdana Saegrund welcomes those who brave the wilderness. Pure water gives life anew, carves stone, and washes away impurities. Tainted water brings the threat of ruin. Those who seek communion with water are sent into the wild to obtain a water sapta from those who dwell beside the element. Hervdana Saegrund and her family make their home in a secluded cave directly beneath the southern waterfalls of the Wetlands. Ironforge guards are far away, and Dark Iron dwarves lurk in the surrounding swamps. Still, Hervdana and her kin keep their isolated home by the falls.

quest:94497.text: Call of Water. In the Wetlands, an initiate gathers water to earn the sapta through Call of Water. The marsh is dangerous, but its waters show how water's energies shape and sustain the land. Hervdana guides initiates through the search for water in its many forms. They learn how it moves, changes lives, and sustains the land. Their path toward the sapta and communion with the spirits begins at an estuary, where ocean tides meet fresh runoff from the highlands. Below Hervdana's cave, waterfalls carry highland springwater into the marsh. There it meets saltwater pushed inland by the coastal tides. The ocean brings sediment, minerals, and energies unlike those in clear mountain snowmelt. An initiate can find wisdom in the land's natural ways where these waters meet. Dangerous marsh creatures make gathering water risky. Dark Iron dwarves have also pushed far north into the Wetlands. Hervdana regrets the hostility between the dwarven clans. She sees how much dwarfkind might achieve if they set aside their feuds.

quest:94499.text: Call of Water. Hervdana Saegrund sends you from the Wetlands to test the waters at Stonewatch Falls in Redridge. What you bring back will serve in your spiritual trials. Hervdana Saegrund sends you south from the Wetlands to examine the waters at Stonewatch Falls in Redridge. Lake Everstill supplies clean water to Lakeshire, but murlocs lurk beneath the cascade. They have grown unusually large and twisted. Hervdana suspects venom, foul sorcery, or seepage from the old fortress above. She asks you to gather a sample in an Empty Red Waterskin.

quest:94500.text: Call of Water. In Ashenvale, you gather pure water from the lake beside Astranaar. It is the last sample you need before returning to Norric. You are sent to fill a waterskin with Ashenvale's uncorrupted water. Astranaar is a haven beside the lake, whose ancient waters lap against sunken ruins. This is the last liquid sample the giver needs before sending you on to Norric. To reach Ashenvale from the Eastern Kingdoms, cross the sea by ship from Menethil Harbor toward Auberdine. The ship puts in at Southshore along the way. From Auberdine's docks, follow the road inland beneath Ashenvale's green boughs. Stay alert among the watchful shadows of the trees.

quest:94501.text: Call of Water. At Loch Modan, seekers prepare to commune with water spirits. Hervdana blesses pure water for Norric Lochthane as aspiring shamans draw nearer to the water totem rites. You seek harmony with water through patience and reverence. Hervdana blesses the water you gather, and you carry it to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan.

quest:94502.text: Call of Water. You travel from Loch Modan to Westfall, where a corrupted spring has silenced the water spirits. At Stendel's Pond, you can cleanse the corruption and awaken an old shrine to seek their favor and the Water Totem. Near Moonbrook, Stendel's Pond lies under a dark taint spreading across Westfall. Its waters were once clear, but now the local water spirits are silent. An old shrine stands neglected along the shore, covered in dust and cobwebs. You can seek to awaken the powers sleeping within it.

quest:94503.text: Call of Water. In Westfall, you drive restless spirits from the waters before a Minor Manifestation of Water can speak with you. Corrupt spirits disturb Westfall's waters and their natural balance. You speak sacred words, and radiant light scatters the restless essences into ash and quiet mist. Once the corrupt spirits are driven back, a Minor Manifestation of Water can emerge. It warns that the land's vital energies still wane, and that preserving life demands constant care.

quest:94505.text: Call of Water. In Westfall, you learn what water can give and what corruption can take. Bring a Shard of Water to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, and he grants you a water totem. You travel to Westfall and return to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan with a Shard of Water. The journey tests your dedication to water and your understanding of its power to give life and purge corruption. Those who prove themselves receive a water totem and take an essential step on their elemental path. Water gives life, and corruption brings it to an end. Norric Lochthane teaches you to use water's restorative strength to protect the vulnerable and preserve living things. Its gifts reach beyond mending the body. They bring endurance, renewal, and spiritual balance.

quest:94568.text: The Cult's True Plans. The cult's informant has died before sharing what he knew. Talaanis Shadowsong must help investigators find another way to oppose the cult. A frightened insider left the cult and hoped to seek help beyond it. Before he could reveal what he knew, he was killed. His warnings remain, but the cult's plans do not.

quest:94616.text: Water Sapta. In Westfall, you take the Water Sapta to seek a troubled pond. The ceremonial draught sharpens your sight to water spirits and hidden corruption, so you can investigate the imbalance. Shamans prepare a sapta to let them see beyond the physical world. The Water Sapta attunes your senses to water, revealing disturbances and spirits hidden from ordinary travelers. Without that changed sight, an elemental presence might seem like no more than ripples. The Water Sapta leads you to Westfall, an arid Alliance realm troubled by unrest and neglect. A pond there holds spiritually polluted water. With the sapta's sight, you seek the corrupted water, uncover the disturbance, and restore harmony to the local water spirits.

quest:94792.text: Taming the Beast. Josephine Carson is teaching aspiring hunters in Taming the Beast how to care for a wild companion. The trial uses a Rockhide Boar and a Taming Rod, with nature’s balance in mind. Traveling alone in the wild can be dangerous. An animal companion offers protection in battle and company on long journeys. For aspiring hunters and trackers, forming that bond is a vital step. Josephine Carson guides novices through a trial with a Rockhide Boar and a Taming Rod. To calm and direct the beast, they must stay composed and focused without giving in to fear or causing needless bloodshed. Josephine Carson warns her pupils not to exploit beasts recklessly. Taming calls for patience and discipline, never cruelty or dominance, and nature’s balance must be kept. The enchanted rod lets novices practice handling a formidable Rockhide Boar without permanently depleting local wildlife. Once they learn to command and soothe the beast, they return the rod. Respect for nature comes before pride.

quest:94793.text: Training the Beast. In Goldshire, Training the Beast shows young hunters how to care for a tamed companion. Isaac Chan teaches them to feed and revive their beasts, then train them for life at their side. You seek Isaac Chan, an experienced woodsman in Goldshire, to learn how to train your beast. A tamed creature needs care and discipline before it can become a steady ally. Without Chan's guidance, your companion may remain unruly in the wilderness. Isaac Chan teaches you to care for your animal companion. You learn to feed it and revive it if it falls in battle. He also teaches commands that help it fight, and reminds you that power over wildlife calls for respect. Honor nature's balance and live in awe of the world around you.

quest:94863.text: Taming the Beast. Josephine Carson guides you through Taming the Beast as you learn to handle a boar before facing a Gray Forest Wolf. With a Taming Rod, you seek the fiercer creature's trust. Josephine Carson watches as you take another step in learning to handle beasts. You have practiced with simple boars; now you enter the forest to tame a Gray Forest Wolf. The enchanted rod she gives you helps calm the predator. Patience and respect matter as much as tracking and marksmanship when you seek a wild creature's trust. Josephine Carson gives you a specialized Taming Rod to calm dangerous wildlife. Approach the wolf with patience and precision, and overcome its aggression without lethal force. After practicing your bond with the beast, return the rod to Josephine as proof of your growing skill.

quest:94864.text: Taming the Beast. In Elwynn Forest, hunters face Taming the Beast, the final trial Josephine Carson oversees. After taming a boar and a wolf, each hunter uses a Taming Rod to earn a Young Forest Bear’s trust. The test deepens the hunter’s bond with beasts and teaches respect for the woodland’s balance. Hunters in Elwynn Forest learn to live among the wild creatures around them. After taming a wolf and a boar, they face one last test of courage and patience. Josephine Carson sends each hunter to a Young Forest Bear, the strongest of the forest’s common predators. The hunter must endure the bear’s strength and earn its trust, rather than force it to submit. Taming wildlife in Elwynn calls for respect, not dominion. Forest bears embody the woodland’s strength and vitality, and help keep its natural order. With a Taming Rod, hunters learn to calm a bear’s aggression and form a bond through understanding. Earning the trust of such a powerful animal deepens a hunter’s bond with the wild and completes the first lessons Josephine Carson oversees.

quest:94896.text: Aid For The Refugees. After Ban'aethal fell, its survivors have little left to call their own. The settlement deep in Shadowgale Forest began to fall into the sky in the middle of the night, and danger keeps the refugees from retrieving what they left behind. Ealaane and the other refugees fled their homes deep in Shadowgale Forest. With almost nothing gathered around them, they ask travelers to brave the dangers they left behind. Ban'aethal began to fall into the sky in the dead of night. Its inhabitants had only moments to escape, leaving their personal possessions behind. The surrounding woods grew hostile and dangerous.

quest:94897.text: The Fate of a Loved One. Resaan has been gone from the Ruins of Ban'aethal for more than a week, and his partner waits for news. Travelers bound there are asked to bring him home or return his cherished heirloom. Resaan's partner pleads with him to stay as he prepares to return to the Ruins of Ban'aethal. Yet he feels compelled to brave the ruins for supplies. His partner is left waiting for word. More than a week has passed since Resaan set out, far longer than a swift return should take. His partner asks travelers bound for Ban'aethal to search the ruins. If Resaan lives, bring him home. If tragedy has taken him, recover his family heirloom.

quest:94911.text: Child of Nature. A fellow Skyborne sees promise in your druidic arts and points you toward Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff. He can teach you how to reach the Cenarion Circle’s stronghold in Moonglade. Your teacher believes the druids of the Cenarion Circle will welcome you and share their knowledge. Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff can show you how to reach their stronghold in Moonglade.

quest:94912.text: Child of Nature. In Stormwind, Sheldras Moontree can show you the way to Moonglade. There, the Cenarion Circle’s druids have wisdom to share with a child of nature. Sheldras Moontree, a night elf in Stormwind, can show you how to reach Moonglade on Kalimdor. The Cenarion Circle keeps its stronghold there. It is an ancient order of naturalists and druids, with much to teach you.

quest:94914.text: Moonglade. Your teacher opens a way to Moonglade, where Dendrite Starblaze awaits. There, you can speak with him about the path you have begun. Your teacher welcomes druids to Moonglade. Keeper Remulos watches over those who rest there. You receive Teleport: Moonglade, a spell that carries you there when you seek knowledge or solace. Your first lesson is to speak with Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven about the path you now follow.

quest:94946.text:
The Magical City of Dalaran. A mage in Valanaar sends you from Zephras Isle to Dalaran City, where several mages await your people's arrival. The city offers a place to begin exploring Azeroth, but the lands beyond can be dangerous without preparation and experience. Recent events with the cult keep the speaker in Valanaar for now. Several mages wait in Dalaran for your people, so you are sent to the dock outside the lodge. There, you board a skycutter bound for Dalaran City.

When you arrive, speak with Danaaris Stargale. Your people are still making their home in the city, and the country beyond its safety can prove dangerous.

quest:94947.text: Welcome to Azeroth. You arrive in Stormwind through the Skyborne Portal and are welcomed by its regent. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon grants you leave to travel across Alliance lands. You step through the Skyborne Portal into Stormwind, the human capital. From there, you make your way along the city's grand thoroughfares to Stormwind Keep, where the regency awaits your arrival. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives the arriving members of the High Order in the throne room. A Kirin Tor courier had warned him they were coming. It has been some time since high elves walked the halls of Stormwind Keep, yet Bolvar welcomes them as guests and grants them free passage across Alliance territories on behalf of the King.

quest:94978.text: Taming the Beast. Quel'ana Quickgale teaches you the bond between beast and master. You begin by taming a Windsong Crawler near the waters of Zephras. You have the Taming Rod and a Windsong Crawler to tame. Find one near a body of water and practice your skills. Then return the rod to Quel'ana Quickgale in Valanaar. This creature is your first step toward mastery.

quest:94979.text: Taming the Beast. In the Gustberry Lowlands, Quel'ana Quickgale asks you to tame a galestrider. Your skill on open ground will prepare you for trials ahead. You've already shown you can tame the river's crawler. Now Quel'ana Quickgale gives you a Taming Rod and sends you to the lowlands of Zephras. There, a proud, winged galestrider runs swiftly across the plains. Earn its trust and practice your skill. Then bring the rod back to Quel'ana in Valanaar.

quest:95.text: Sven's Revenge. In Sven's Revenge, grief drives Sven Yorgen from his ruined farm in southern Duskwood to hunt its killers. Now camped in the western hills, he asks travelers to return to the farmstead, where a stranger buried something near the barn. Hooded Dark Riders came from Deadwind Pass and attacked Sven Yorgen's farm in southeastern Duskwood. Sven was away, and they killed his family. When he returned to the slaughter, he saw an unknown figure skulking near the barn and hurriedly burying something. Sven left the object hidden and set out to hunt the killers. Sven Yorgen is camped in the western hills, consumed by wrath and seeking help at his farmstead. Between the farmhouse and ruined barn, a mound of loose dirt behind an old tree stump marks where something was hastily buried. Recovering it may explain why the shadowy riders targeted a quiet Duskwood farmer.

quest:95036.text: A Moon-Kissed Blade. Trevan warns you that worgen threaten Silverpine Forest. Old Fire-Eye resists death through unknown magic, and Trevan asks you to learn what a special blade will require. Old Fire-Eye is the worgen who attacked Trevan and his companions. Trevan will give you a list of materials for a weapon against him. The materials are gathered, and Trevan believes he knows a smith who can craft the blade.

quest:95042.text: Seeking the Kor Gem. In Ashenvale, Ulric Frostveil sees your search for a Kor Gem as familiar work for Alliance spellcasters. He points you north to Blackfathom Deeps, where naga still use the gems. Ulric asks you to bring him a Kor Gem from the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, north of Ashenvale. The naga below still use the gems. They can empower magical weapons and implements, but Ulric warns you not to go alone.

quest:951.text: Mathystra Relics. Along Darkshore's northeastern coast, Mathystra Relics may reveal how the Twilight's Hammer bends ancient elven magic. Onu, an Ancient of Lore in the Grove of the Ancients, seeks them to learn what the cult intends. Onu sends you to the Ruins of Mathystra on Darkshore's northeastern shore. Before the Sundering, Mathystra was a shining bastion of highborne civilization. The city fell to rubble, weeds and naga, yet its old enchantments endure in shattered urns and relics scattered among the stone foundations.

quest:95111.text: An Underrated Talent. In Silverpine Forest, Trevan Rol gives Ott a chance to make a blade to your design. Ott’s simple weapons have earned praise from smiths in the Undercity. Trevan Rol asks you to carry materials to Ott in Tarren Mill and offer him a commission. Ott sells simple blades to travelers. Trevan bought one and later took it to the Undercity for maintenance. There, local smiths praised its quality and mistook it for the work of a famous master. Now Ott has the chance to forge a blade to your specifications.

quest:95125.text: Ott's Masterwork. Ott is ready to forge a blade for you from fine materials. You may watch him at work. Ott values the fine materials and hopes his work will meet your expectations. He forges a blade for you, then offers it for your travels.

quest:95126.text: The Moonsilver Blade. In Silverpine Forest, Trevan Rol awaits the blade that will complete his work before he faces a beast. Ott thanks you for the chance to help and asks you to carry his gratitude to Trevan. You bring Ott's Masterwork back to Trevan Rol in Silverpine Forest.

quest:95140.text: Old Fire-Eye. Lumina Windsinger sends you after Old Fire-Eye in Silverpine Forest with the Moonsilver Blade. The Windshapers await his death, and Lumina hopes the blade will guide you well. The Windshapers have given you the Moonsilver Blade. Locals say Old Fire-Eye hunts across a wide stretch south of here, usually near the gates to Gilneas. Lumina asks you to find him and use the blade to end him. The Windshapers' gratitude depends on his death.

quest:95161.text: Remember That I Love You. In Stormwind, a blood-stained letter is bound for Jeremy Heartweaver, now living with his adoptive mother, Avette Fellwood, in Duskwood. War, hardship, and the kingdom's turmoil have left many children at the Stormwind Orphanage without families. Jeremy Heartweaver was among them until Avette Fellwood adopted him and brought him to live in Duskwood. There, gloomy woods bring peril and hard labor. The caretakers believed a family could offer him more than life in the city orphanage.

quest:95189.text: Crest of Lordaeron. In the ruins of Capital City, a weathered Crest of Lordaeron survives from the fallen northern kingdom. Relics like it are scarce, and Lady Dena Kennedy in Stormwind City is eager to claim one. The Scourge left Lordaeron's palaces and archives in ruins beneath the shadow of the Undercity. Its proud insignias were destroyed or left to decay, so few relics bearing the royal crest remain. A weathered crest from the northern ruins keeps a piece of human history. After the Third War, thousands of refugees fled south from Lordaeron toward the Kingdom of Stormwind. They carried memories of home. In Stormwind City, Lady Dena Kennedy seeks remnants of their homeland. For those who left the north behind, a crest like this is a cherished link to Lordaeron.

quest:95195.text:
Bloodied Insignia. In Lordaeron's blighted ruins, Bloodied Insignias bear the old Alliance crests of fallen defenders. Many soldiers' families fled south to Stormwind during the Third War. Prince Arthas returned with the Scourge and laid waste to Lordaeron. Its great army was overwhelmed, and countless soldiers died defending the capital and the lands around it. Rusted armor and bloodstained brass are all that remain of many who fought.

The old Alliance insignias belonged to those who stood against the undead. Trampled into soil and rubble, the medals recall Lordaeron's last defense. Many survivors fled south across the sea and settled in Stormwind City. Alliance and kinship bind the two human realms, and families in the south still seek news of loved ones lost in the north.

General Marcus Jonathan commands Stormwind's city guard and takes custody of the bloodied insignias. He preserves the defenders' memory and helps their surviving families learn their fate.

quest:95204.text: Crest of Lordaeron. The Forsaken preserve what little remains of Lordaeron in Undercity. A weathered crest bears the fallen kingdom’s emblem, a rare link to its past. The Third War shattered Lordaeron. Ash, ruins, and Scourge desolation swallowed much of the kingdom, leaving few emblems behind. To the Forsaken beneath the ruins of the Capital City, those that survive are precious links to the civilization they once belonged to. The weathered crest is brought from the wider world to Oran Snakewrithe in Undercity. Oran tests the metal with a bite, then confirms it is genuine and mostly intact. For Oran and the Forsaken archivists, each recovered piece helps restore a history the Scourge sought to erase.

quest:95212.text: Never Saddle on Quality. At Amberstill Ranch, handlers prepare rams for the Alliance expedition in Alterac. They need pristine mountain leopard pelts to make warm saddles for the beasts, so mounts and riders can face the northern mountains' biting frost. The handlers of Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh are readying sturdy mountain rams for Alterac. But the work has stalled: they lack the material needed to make durable, cold-weather saddles for the rams. The expedition's mounts need thick insulation to endure the freeze of the Alterac mountains. Hunters are sent to the eastern crags to track the largest, fiercest mountain leopards in Dun Morogh and bring back pristine pelts. The Alliance forces need gear that can withstand the high passes.

quest:95213.text: Stolen Blasting Powder. Near Gol'Bolar Quarry, an empty keg of hazardous blasting powder has turned up among troggs. Its return to Quarrymaster Thesten reveals a breach in the quarry's security and explosive stores. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, a warning stamped on an empty keg shows that hazardous blasting powder has slipped out of authorized hands. The explosives are reserved for controlled quarrying, with the quarrymaster's direct approval. The keg was found among hostile troggs, and that points to a threat beyond ordinary trouble for the miners.

quest:95214.text: Stolen Blasting Powder. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Stolen Blasting Powder has gone east with the troggs. Quarrymaster Thesten needs help recovering the missing munitions before the brutes set them off by accident. At Gol'Bolar Quarry in Dun Morogh, dwarves use heavy blasting charges to break stone and open deep veins. But primitive troggs from the nearby crags stole a bulk shipment of high-grade powder. Quarrymaster Thesten needs capable hands before the pack causes an accidental detonation. The missing keg holds enough force to reduce King Magni Bronzebeard's grand throne room to an open-air courtyard. The troggs carried the powder east to their rough foothill camps. Left alone, they may soon discover fire or strike stone against spark.

quest:95216.text: The New Plague. In the Undercity, Theodore Griffs studies reports of a lethal creature in the ruins above. Its venom consumes even undead flesh, and he seeks to learn how its toxins work. The Royal Apothecary Society gathers dangerous substances from across Azeroth. Theodore Griffs is one of its researchers. He tracks strange beasts and deadly contaminants to advance Forsaken alchemy. Now rumors tell of a venomous creature in the shattered stone above, so Griffs sends you to bring back a sample before the chance is lost. Witherfang is the venomous arthropod stalking the surface ruins of Lordaeron. Its venom breaks down living tissue and dead, preserved flesh alike. Griffs wants to learn how it overcomes the resistance of dead flesh, knowledge that could help refine biological weapons and protect the Forsaken kingdom.

quest:95217.text:
The Quarry's Smith. At the quarry, The Quarry's Smith, Frast Dokner, needs metal and leather for camp repairs. With a supply shipment late, he asks travelers to bring the materials. In return, Dokner offers practical smithing techniques. An excavation needs steady care. Pickaxes must be sharpened, worn brackets replaced, and camp gear reinforced. When a vital shipment misses its schedule, work begins to grind to a halt. Without fresh stock from the major trade routes, the craftsmen must improvise and look to passing travelers for help.

Frast Dokner works the forge through these delays. He asks anyone willing to gather basic metals and hides to help keep the camp running, rather than wait for transport wagons that may be far behind. Dwarven blacksmithing guilds prize discipline and guard their methods, rarely sharing trade secrets with casual wanderers. Dokner weighs that custom against the camp's immediate needs. He lacks workable copper and durable leather for patching tools and camp gear.

Bring the raw materials to his anvil, and he will teach you his personal smithing techniques. The bargain trades useful craft knowledge for materials the camp needs to endure and keep its gear in repair.

quest:95250.text:
Abominable Creatures. At Lordaeron's fallen capital, Captain Truman waits anxiously for reinforcements and news of his missing commander. He believes the revered Grand Marshal still fights in the nearby ruins, and asks a capable traveler to find him. The search reveals the defenders' grim fate and deep hostility among the loyalists. Captain Truman keeps watch outside Lordaeron, anxious for long-overdue reinforcements. He calls his superior a renowned Grand Marshal, tall and statuesque, and believes him a formidable fighter. Ordered to hold the line while his commander charged into battle, Truman remains bound by duty.

He distrusts outsiders and scorns those he calls lesser breeds, refusing to rely on local irregulars. When a capable traveler arrives, he asks you to enter the ruins, check on his master's well-being, and learn how the battle fares. The search takes you into the Ruins of Lordaeron, the shattered capital that fell to the Scourge during the Third War. Captain Truman expects his glorious leader to stand triumphant over the fallen, but the blighted city tells a grimmer story.

Horrors, undead remnants, and abominations roam its broken stone plazas. The ruined streets show what became of the defenders who entered the city. No immaculate knight holds the line; the commander has met a tragic, twisted end among the monstrosities in the courtyards.

quest:95328.text: Whispering Horror Residue. Beneath the Whispering Forest, Whispering Horror Residue is carried to Undercity for study. Father Lankester awaits it in the War Quarter. Beneath the Whispering Forest, you recover a strange beast’s twitching remains. The unsettling material is carried to Undercity, where researchers may study it. In Undercity’s War Quarter, Father Lankester receives the remains. He says the Whispering Forest has long been touched by the void. Its physical traces may help him study the mysteries of shadow.

quest:95349.text:
The Earthen Ring. From Zephras, the Windshapers of The Earthen Ring reach Azeroth as an advance vanguard. After cult activity delays the rest in Valanaar, they board a skycutter outside the lodge and make landfall in Mulgore to meet Alaana Stormwalker and adjust to a vast, dangerous world. Cult activity in Valanaar has disrupted the Windshapers’ plans to travel to Azeroth. Their senior leaders stay behind at the lodge to finish urgent business and quell the threat, while a small vanguard sets out ahead. At the docks just outside the lodge, the pioneers board a skycutter bound across the skies.

Their commanders promise to join them soon. Until then, the advance group must establish a presence before the rest can follow. In Mulgore, Alaana Stormwalker welcomes the arriving adventurers from Zephras. Establishing a foothold in Azeroth will take time, so newcomers are encouraged to scout the surrounding territory and grow accustomed to it.

The winds favor the expedition, but Azeroth is unfamiliar and perilous. Travelers should learn the local terrain, wildlife, and neighboring inhabitants before those still in Valanaar arrive to join them.

quest:95350.text: Welcome to Azeroth. In Kalimdor, the Windshapers reach beyond their isolated home to seek allies. Guided by their ties to the Earthen Ring, an emissary travels from Thunder Bluff to meet Warchief Thrall in Orgrimmar. The Windshapers look beyond their isolated origins to the peoples of Kalimdor. They know isolation cannot shield them from Azeroth’s threats, so they seek companions to face the wilderness together. Their search reaches the neighboring tauren city of Thunder Bluff and the orcish bastions to the east. The envoys travel first to the soaring towers of Thunder Bluff, then across the barrens to Orgrimmar, the Horde’s capital. Warchief Thrall waits in the tranquil Valley of Wisdom. An audience with him draws the Windshapers into Kalimdor’s political and spiritual life, joining them to the Horde through shared purpose and respect for the elements.

quest:95494.text: Bruised Pride and Lion Hides. An injury leaves a hunter or tradesperson unable to gather lion hides for a local tanner. They turn to you to keep their trade agreement and their professional record intact. A hunter or tradesperson has been hurt and cannot safely track wild beasts. Their agreement with a neighborhood craftsman is still due, so they hire you to hunt wild lions and gather their pelts. The raw hides go to a local tanner, who exchanges them for finished leather goods the giver needs for their livelihood. The giver’s pride is stung by needing help, but honoring the bargain keeps their professional reputation unbroken.

quest:95495.text: The Hermit Tanner. You carry raw hides across the Barrens to The Hermit Tanner, who lives above the Dry Hills. Vrang cannot make the climb, so he sends you to his secluded trading partner. Across the Barrens, Vrang trades with a tanner who lives on a ridge above the Dry Hills. The steep, rocky climb is too hard for Vrang, so he asks passing travelers to carry raw hides to his partner's homestead. Vrang warns you that the solitary tanner's unusual appearance may startle you, but says he is no danger to visitors. When you bring the hides to the ridge, the hermit welcomes you warmly. He regrets that Vrang could not come himself, for there is something he hoped to discuss with the trader.

quest:95507.text: Vrang's Game. Vrang sends you across a valley in the Barrens to check his traps. The small game they catch can help him, though other wildlife makes the area dangerous. Vrang has traps scattered across the valley, and he wants you to bring back any small game they have caught. Keep your attention on the wildlife too, for it can make the area dangerous.

quest:95508.text: Unwelcome Guests. You helped someone survive an encounter with unwelcome guests, and they are grateful. What brought you together remains unclear.

quest:95621.text: Trouble in the Valley. A squad of Kul Tiran soldiers is searching the valley, and their purpose is unknown. They have camped near a wrecked caravan to the south, drawing the attention of local scouts. A rifleman watching the lowlands spotted human soldiers searching the valley floor. Through his scope, he recognized the heraldry and livery of Kul Tiras. Armed foreigners rarely work so openly here, and their presence has raised alarm. The soldiers have camped near a ruined caravan to the south. What they seek among the wreckage remains unknown. Local observers consider their armed presence an immediate concern, so investigators are sent to eliminate them and uncover the purpose of their search.

quest:95646.text: Horrors in the Highland. Rethiel the Greenwarden senses corruption flowing through a mountain gully into the Wetlands' freshwater. He sends you to the highland excavation sites for a Highland Horror's root core, then warns that digging stirs an ancient energy and endangers the whole region. Rethiel the Greenwarden senses the land changing deep in the Wetlands. Through a mountain gully, foul taint reaches the highlands and infects their freshwater creatures. Lowland life has been shaped by brackish water, but these creatures have never known the sea's protective salt. Rethiel fears they cannot withstand the spreading evil. He asks you to climb to the excavation sites, slay a Highland Horror, and bring back its root core.

quest:95647.text: Lost in the Thicket Things. Ardin Grassman is missing near an excavation site after following word of towering grasses. His alchemist wife asks travelers to find him, as dangerous wildlife has attacked the crew. Ardin Grassman's alchemist wife asks you to find her missing husband. He has a keen sense for nature and often braves cliffs and distant wilds to gather herbs and plants for her work. When an excavation crew spoke of towering grasses unlike any they had seen, Ardin's curiosity drew him toward the site.

quest:95697.text: Changing Tastes. At Borstan's Firepit, a new dish may bring travelers to Orgrimmar. Zamja's advice and tales of giant raptor talons lead Borstan to seek thicket raptor meat from the Wetlands across the sea. Borstan's Firepit in Orgrimmar hopes to widen its menu. Zamja suggests homestyle raptor cooking for travelers who miss the familiar meals of their birth villages. Borstan likes the thought of drawing new patrons with raptor, but simple village fare seems too modest for the Horde's great capital. He wants a bolder version of the old staple. A hunter returns to Orgrimmar with a massive talon from a thicket raptor of the Wetlands excavation sites. The beast's size and quality catch Borstan's interest. He arranges for adventurers to cross the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms, brave the excavation grounds, and bring back prime thicket raptor meat for his fires.

quest:95737.text:
Seeking Caitlin. An alchemist waits for word about a rare grass. She asks you to find Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor, whose husband has not reported back from an excavation. The alchemist heard from Caitlin that her husband's excavation team found signs of a primordial grass. Caitlin does not know how much they found or whether it can be reached.

Now the alchemist asks you to speak with Caitlin in Menethil Harbor. Both women are waiting to learn what happened to the promised seeds.

quest:95772.text: Songblade Search. Dorin Songblade waits for word from his brother Daewyn in the Wetlands. Daewyn joined an archaeological crew from Loch Modan to dig in unexplored hills, but his silence is unlike him. Dorin Songblade tends his workshop, buried in orders to refit girdles. His brother Daewyn has gone north with a dwarven excavation crew from Loch Modan. The hills they seek in the Wetlands have never felt a dwarven pickaxe. Daewyn usually writes as soon as he arrives, but no word has reached Dorin, and the silence unsettles him.

quest:95774.text: Her Name Is Olgra. Mankrik mourns Olgra and prepares a monument to keep her name alive. He asks you to seek her missing bone adornments among the nearby Razormane raiders. A healer saved Mankrik, but Olgra died from her wounds on the battlefield. Grieving, Mankrik prepares a lasting tribute so her name and sacrifice will be remembered. Olgra wore cherished ornaments made of polished bone, but they are missing from her resting place. Mankrik asks you to recover them from the nearby Razormane raiders, so they can rest beside the monument he is raising for her.

quest:95795.text: Fallen in the Fen. At the excavation, a fallen dwarf leaves grim news for his brother in Lakeshire. Dorin Songblade learns what became of his kin and faces the gifts he could not finish in time. At the excavation sites, an adventurous dwarf lies dead. You cover his remains with his own cloak, then carry the grim news to Lakeshire and seek out his kin.

quest:95803.text: A Token of Good Faith. Danitha sends you to carry Rudolph Gelhardt’s head to Sylvanas Windrunner in the Undercity. The delivery is meant to show the Forsaken that your people are devoted to their prosperity. Danitha says Sylvanas distrusts your people and openly disparages them. She asks you to bring Rudolph Gelhardt’s head as proof that you tend to your own house and stand with the Forsaken.

quest:95805.text: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha. On Red Cloud Mesa, An'she and Mu'sha receive honor as the Earthmother's eyes. You carry smoldering incense to a shrine in the southeastern hills, where its smoke rises toward the sun and moon that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains. Tauren honor An'she and Mu'sha as the sun and moon, the Earthmother's twin eyes. Elemental spirits dwell in Azeroth's stones, winds, and waters, while the celestial twins watch from the heights of heaven. As they cross the sky, they mark day and night and bring warmth, guidance, and hope to living creatures. For tauren, honoring them is a spiritual duty. Balance calls for reverence toward the land beneath your feet and the light above. Carry smoldering incense into the southeastern hills overlooking Red Cloud Mesa, just south of the prickly quilboar grounds. Make the journey with speed and care. Keep the embers dry and reach the shrine before they burn to cold ash. At the elevated shrine, cast them into the sacred fire. Their fragrant smoke carries your respect skyward, toward the sun and moon.

quest:95809.text: Heartwoven. In the Wetlands, Ardin Grassman has survived the marsh’s dangers and sends word to Menethil Harbor. A traveler carries a reed heart to Caitlin Grassman. Ardin Grassman went to see the strange grasses at the Wetlands excavation sites, but became stranded among the marsh’s dangers. You clear a path through the wilderness, giving him room to rest and gather his harvest. Tired but determined, Ardin prepares to return toward the safety of the port. Before setting out for home, Ardin takes marsh reeds from his pack and braids them into a heart. He gives you the token to carry to Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor. She has been waiting in worry. Word that Ardin survived and will soon return brings relief, along with the reed heart and the promise of a warm meal.

quest:95810.text: Lost Relic Carry. You carry a broken rock-mech relic through the Wetlands toward Prospector Whelgar. Its strange material draws the eye of dwarven researchers. A rock-mech has left behind a fractured piece of its ancient craft. Its unfamiliar composite marks it as part of a sophisticated mechanism tied to the Titans. Prospector Whelgar studies ancient remains at the Wetlands excavation site. Bring the relic safely to him, and dwarven scholars will have physical evidence for their study of their ancient heritage.

quest:95883.text: The Tortured Soul. At Beren's Peril in Silverpine Forest, a dark rite waits unfinished. An abandoned note names the last offerings still needed: blood and a soul marked by suffering. At Beren's Peril in Silverpine Forest, an altar bears the remains of a hastily assembled dark rite. A scrawled note lies among the scattered materials. Most of the ingredients are already gathered, but the rite still calls for blood and a Tortured Soul.

quest:95884.text: The Offering Stone. In Beren's Peril, a ritual offering is being prepared at the Offering Stone. Fragments of a weathered note point travelers to the altar in Silverpine Forest. A weathered scrap found in Silverpine Forest holds fragments about a ritual and an offering stone nearby. Time and moisture have worn away most of its words. Follow the clues into Beren's Peril, and you can find the crude altar in the wilderness. At Beren's Peril, strange implements and bizarre items lie scattered across the rough stone. Someone has been using the site to prepare an offering or dark rite, far from prying eyes.

quest:95885.text: The Offering of Blood. At Beren's Peril, the scrap of note calls for blood at the Offering Stone. You bring a Tortured Soul to answer it. Deep in Beren's Peril, the Offering Stone waits for a final offering. Scraps of note call for a willing sacrifice, and lead you to bring blood to the altar. As you approach with the restless essence, dread closes in.

quest:95981.text: Watching the Roads. Shadow Priest Allister sends the Forsaken against Kirin Tor patrols near Ambermill. With Dalaran's barrier down, their wizards and watchers guard the roads into Silverpine Forest while carrying magical goods into Forsaken lands. Near Ambermill, Kirin Tor wizards and sentries watch the roads into Silverpine Forest. Since the barrier around Dalaran fell, they have tightened their hold on travel across the border. From the Sepulcher, the Forsaken see the human magi using these roads to carry dangerous relics and enchanted pendants into contested lands. Shadow Priest Allister wants to stop the flow of Dalaran's magical goods at its source. He sends agents after the Kirin Tor escorts on the roads near Ambermill. By striking Dalaran Wizards and Dalaran Watchers, the Forsaken aim to break the Kirin Tor's hold on regional travel and guard their eastern frontier from outside arcane meddling.

quest:95998.text: The Great Outdoors. At Sam’s fire, travelers learn to rest and endure the road. Then they can turn to tradeskills and work in the wild. Sam welcomes restless travelers who cross Azeroth in search of fortune, danger, and renown. Ambition alone cannot keep a newcomer warm or ease the miles. By his fire, you learn when to rest, how to build a fire, and how to gather strength for the open road. A campfire offers warmth against the night chill and a chance for boosted rest. Those who know the wild understand that endurance comes from resting between journeys. Once you have learned these basics, you can turn to tradeskills. Craftsmen and gatherers can learn to make camp fixtures suited to their work in the field.

quest:95999.text: WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon offers a bounty for Incinerator Gar'im, whose forces threaten the town. The hostile orc commander holds Render's Valley with shadowcasters and is said to work with the Blackrock clan at Stonewatch Keep. Blackrock orcs press out from their mountain strongholds, making the Redridge Mountains more dangerous. In Render's Valley, Gar'im leads an incursion with loyal shadowcasters and dark sorcery. Lakeshire's guard is stretched thin, and the crown's armies are largely absent. So Magistrate Solomon calls on independent fighters to eliminate Gar'im, who is said to work with the Blackrock at Stonewatch Keep. Gar'im is known for destructive magic and command over shadow-weaving casters. To claim the township's reward, hunters enter enemy-held territory and defeat him. They must return his shattered staff to Lakeshire's town hall as proof that the threat has ended.

quest:96.text:
Call of Water. You bring the Shard of Water to Islen Waterseer on the Barrens coast. This return shows your harmony with restorative energies and earns you a Water Totem. You carry a gift from the Minor Manifestation of Water back across the sea. To earn it, you crossed continents to the tainted shores of Silverpine Forest and faced the corruption there. Water gives life, adapts, and heals, yet its pliant nature leaves it open to blight and dark magic.

Before the Minor Manifestation, you witnessed pure elemental will and received the Shard of Water. Now you return to the sun-scorched Barrens, where the shard reminds you that water joins distant corners of the world. When you give Islen Waterseer the shard, she weighs more than proof of your journey. She tests whether you have learned the balance between preservation and renewal. Lordaeron's spreading rot can hide small victories, yet cleansing even one wellspring matters to the spirits. Islen accepts your offering and gives you a Water Totem. Through it, you can channel cleansing, healing, and mana-restoring streams into the mortal realm, binding you to the tide.

quest:96031.text: Camping 101: Leatherworking. At a camp in the wilderness, leatherworkers put cured hides to use and make shelter of their own. A sound campsite needs a pitched tent and a fire, whose kindling is taught by cooking trainers. For tradespeople who work with hides and leather, making a shelter of their own is an essential milestone. A sturdy leather tent shields travelers from harsh weather, wind and the chill of night on open ground. Townsfolk frown on tents pitched in crowded streets or market squares, so you need to pass beyond the city gates and into the wilderness to make camp. A pitched tent is only half a campsite. A proper fire keeps back darkness and cold winds, and gives you a hearth in dangerous lands. Since cooking in the field begins with building and tending a fire, seek instruction from culinary masters and cooking trainers. They teach you to kindle a campfire before you establish camp.

quest:96044.text: Camping 101: Blacksmithing. Smiths bound for the wilderness are sent to Kharanos to learn from Tognus Flintfire. He teaches them to make a portable sharpening wheel for keeping weapons keen at camp. You are sent to Kharanos to learn how a smith can serve far from a town forge. There, skilled hands turn raw metal into tools for camp. A blade kept keen is ready for the long road. In Kharanos, Tognus Flintfire teaches capable smiths to make a sharpening wheel. Set one beside your campsite and warriors and rogues can grind nicks from their weapons and hone dull edges before the next march.

quest:96045.text: Camping 101: Alchemy. In Ironforge, Vosur Brakthel shows alchemists how to prepare for the road. With a Mana Well, they can give spellcasters and healers a place to recover while traveling. Vosur Brakthel trains alchemists in Ironforge to carry their craft beyond the city. Brewing vials in a quiet laboratory is only part of the work. Out in Azeroth's wild places, alchemists can use what they know to make a Mana Well for a camp, helping companions endure the journey. A Mana Well can refresh healers and spellcasters, but it belongs at a wilderness camp, not on an Ironforge street. City folk frown on tents pitched within their walls. A proper camp also needs a fire, so seek a cooking trainer's guidance before heading into the wild.

quest:96046.text: Camping 101: Mining. Out beyond the guarded roads, miners learn to make a lodestone for a wilderness camp. The work pairs knowledge of stone with the firecraft needed to live outdoors. Beyond guarded roads, a miner must rely on fieldcraft. Mineral knowledge gives you the means to shape a lodestone, the anchor for a campsite in the wild. A campsite belongs beyond town limits, where travelers can pitch their shelters without troubling settled folk. Choose a place in the open wilds. A camp also needs a fire to ward off the night chill. Learning to build one is part of the same fieldcraft as working stone.

quest:96050.text: Camping 101: Fishing. You’re preparing for wilderness fishing with a Fish Bowl and a campfire. Learn where to set up and what makes a resting place comfortable. Travel through Azeroth calls for a little knowledge of the wild. When you need a place to rest, keep your tent and gear beyond town borders. Townsfolk and guards dislike travelers spreading their belongings through settlements. Take your supplies into the open wilderness instead. A proper campsite needs a few comforts. Start with a warm campfire; a cooking trainer can teach you how to make one. Once the fire is ready, set out a handcrafted Fish Bowl. Then your stop is fit for an angler.

quest:96055.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. In Ironforge, herbalists can learn to make Incense Candles for life in camp. Reyna Stonebranch teaches the craft to gatherers ready to put wild herbs to practical use. Gathering wild herbs can serve a camp as well as a traveling party. With skill, herbalists turn what they gather into useful aids for life outdoors. In Ironforge, proficient herbalists can seek instruction from Reyna Stonebranch. Once they prove their skill, she teaches them to make an Incense Candle. Its soothing aroma lifts the spirits at camp and brings calm to spellcasters and healers on long expeditions.

quest:96056.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Ironforge, skilled skinners learn to make a Camp Chair from animal hides. Balthus Stoneflayer teaches the craft after they prove their skill. Skinning fallen beasts gives armorers and crafters leather to work with. Hides from cats, bears, and other beasts have uses in the field, too. You are sent to turn those materials into something useful at camp instead of selling them. Balthus Stoneflayer teaches skinners in Ironforge to make a Camp Chair from prepared pelts. First, you need to show him you know how to skin beasts. Only then will he share his crafting methods. A Camp Chair gives you a place to sit by the fire and unwind while traveling. Rest there, and you can meet the next danger with your senses sharp and your strength restored.

quest:96101.text:
The Great Outdoors. Raan welcomes new wanderers and shows them how to endure the wild. Rest by his basic campfire to gain Boosted Rest, then visit nearby trade trainers to learn practical professions. Raan has traveled the wilds and teaches others how to survive beyond settlement walls. Ambition and steel alone will not carry you through harsh weather; practical campcraft matters. He welcomes those seeking fortune and glory, and offers guidance to anyone willing to learn. Raan asks you to sit beside his basic campfire and rest until you gain Boosted Rest. Across Azeroth's wild places, knowing when to pause, make camp, and recover can mean the difference between life and death.

After the lesson, Raan directs you to nearby village trainers. There you can learn a trade and craft specialized fixtures for your campsite.

quest:96102.text: Camping 101: Tailoring. Tailoring training teaches you to make a Rallying Banner. Its test belongs in the wilderness, where a camp needs a campfire. You can now craft a Rallying Banner, and its completion note calls for a wilderness test. A camp needs a campfire before you set it up. Most cooks can teach you to make one, so ask a cooking trainer for the basics if you have not learned them.

quest:96130.text: Chakuyak. Near the tree stands west of Stonebull Lake, Chakuyak threatens travelers crossing Mulgore. Local tribesfolk have marked the fierce wolf for hunting, and her pelt will be honored. Chakuyak prowls the tree stands west of Stonebull Lake, where prairie wolves roam Mulgore’s grassy plateaus and rolling hills. This fierce alpha female has become a danger to travelers arriving from abroad, so local hunters have marked her for removal before more wanderers are harmed. For the local tribes, killing Chakuyak calls for solemn respect, not boasting. They see it as necessary to protect travelers and villagers. Her thick pelt is cured and put to use, honoring the wolf and ensuring her sacrifice is not wasted.

quest:96243.text: Call of Earth. In Coldridge Valley, the Call of Earth sends an initiate to seek Teo Hammerstorm at Anvilmar. There begins a shaman’s communion with the spirits of stone. An initiate’s first communion with the elements begins when the earth calls. Other elemental energies may already stir, but speaking with stone brings balance.
