The earth teaches the initiate to find strength that will not yield. Firm footing comes beneath their boots and within their spirit. In Dun Morogh’s snowy reaches, initiates find shelter and instruction at Anvilmar. The holdfast lies in Coldridge Valley, forged by hammer, fire, and will. Teo Hammerstorm waits within, teaching fledgling shamans to heed the rumbling earth and begin their elemental duties.

quest:96339.text: Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle. A parcel addressed to you waited in a caretaker’s hands until you came to claim it. Inside was a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle, left by a courier whose name is unknown. The caretaker kept nothing in storage and had no wish to hold the parcel. The courier insisted you would come for it, then hurried away before the caretaker could refuse. You arrived just before the box was cast into the ocean with the evening’s refuse. Inside the parcel is a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle, a tribute to the firearm craft of the dwarven capital. Dwarven mountaineers and marksmen carry deadly weapons through Dun Morogh. Replicas like this recall the intricate barrelwork and pneumatic mechanisms perfected by Ironforge craftsmen.

quest:96394.text: The Restless Dead. Beneath the Hall of Thanes, restless spirits trouble the crypts where generations of dwarven dead lie at rest. The caretakers fear to enter the vaults, and the disturbance has reached the spirit of Anvilmar. Generations of honored dwarves rest in the ancestral crypts beneath the Hall of Thanes. Their spirits usually sleep in peace, but something unseen has stirred them violently. Strange noises rise from the lower vaults and frighten the caretakers. They will not enter those chambers or perform their duties until order returns. Now adventurers are called to quiet the agitated souls.

quest:96403.text: Important Heirlooms. In the Hall of Thanes, Dark Iron dwarves break into the vaults while Thom is caught inside. The nervous gnome asks you to gather the scattered dwarven relics before the invaders reach them. Thom is a gnome caught in the Hall of Thanes when Dark Iron dwarves tunnel up in mole machines. He cannot secure the vaults alone, so he asks passing adventurers to enter the hostile dig site. The dwarven relics lie scattered through the chambers. The invaders may seize or destroy them.

quest:96604.text: The Great Outdoors. Brakk welcomes travelers beside his Basic Campfire and teaches them to rest in the wild. From there, they turn to practical crafts. Brakk greets aspiring adventurers with a hearty “Lok-tar” and welcomes those seeking fortune and glory. The road through Azeroth’s wilds asks for more than skill at arms; travelers must also endure the elements. Learning to make camp and regain strength is a first step toward surviving out there. Rest beside Brakk’s Basic Campfire brings a restorative pause in the open air and teaches travelers how to recover. Once they know these basics, novice adventurers can visit craftsmen in a nearby village. There, they can study tradeskills and learn to build camp fixtures suited to their chosen craft.

quest:96605.text: The Great Outdoors. At Kaga's wilderness camp, newcomers learn how to rest and recover. From the campfire, they go on to nearby artisans to learn tradeskills and craft camp fixtures. Kaga shows newcomers how to endure the wilderness beyond civilization. Courage alone cannot keep you safe there. You also need to know how to make camp and withstand the open elements. Kaga's campfire gives weary travelers a place to rest. Sit beside it to gain the Boosted Rest buff. Once you know how to rest in the wilds, Kaga urges you to visit artisans in a nearby settlement. They can teach you tradeskills and how to craft camp fixtures.

quest:96606.text: The Great Outdoors. At Lyreena's campfire, hunters learn how to rest before traveling through the wilds. They can gain the Boosted Rest buff there. Lyreena is an experienced scout who guides hunters beyond civilization's borders. She welcomes you to rest beside her campfire between hunts. In Azeroth's wilds, knowing how to make camp and regain your strength matters as much as tracking quarry. A campfire offers warmth and a quiet rest from travel. Sit near the flames to gain Boosted Rest and recover energy for the journey ahead. Rest helps you survive in the wilderness.

quest:96608.text: The Great Outdoors. Eric waits by his campfire to teach travelers how to rest in the wild. Beyond settled places, ambition and a weapon or holy symbol are not enough. You need to know how to rest amid the elements. Eric has traveled far, and he welcomes you beside his campfire. There, he teaches why proper rest matters before you face the wilds. A campfire begins a useful campsite for a long journey. Once you have learned how to recover in the wild, visit tradeskill trainers in nearby settlements. They can teach you to make camp fixtures for your trade. Then your craft can support your travels wherever the road leads.

quest:96626.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In Goldshire, Cook Tomas shows new travelers how cooking kindles a campfire. With that fire, they can make a simple camp in the wild. A campfire gives you a place to prepare food and begin a camp in Azeroth's wilds. Learn to cook, and you learn to build that fire. Then an open stretch of wilderness can become a place to camp. In Elwynn Forest, new travelers find Cook Tomas in Goldshire and learn the craft. His instruction gives you the skill to make a basic camp in the wild. At first, your camp holds few furnishings. Greater cooking skill lets you build larger fires, while other crafting trades give you more ways to furnish and shape your campsite.

quest:96629.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In Dun Morogh, travelers learn to cook and make a fire for the wilds. Gremlock Pilsnor teaches novice adventurers in Kharanos. Cooking keeps food ready for the road and helps travelers light campfires at wilderness campsites. Your first camp in Dun Morogh begins with a fire. In Kharanos, Gremlock Pilsnor teaches novice adventurers to cook. The skill keeps food ready for the road. A sturdy campfire gives an outdoor camp its center. Once you can build a campfire, you can pitch a humble camp in the open wilderness. A simple fire holds only a few furnishings, but greater cooking skill lets you build larger blazes. Artisans trained in other crafts can make furnishings, turning a basic rest stop into a fully outfitted encampment.

quest:96634.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In the wild, you begin with cooking and a fire, and trainers such as Zarrin in Dolanaar can teach you the trade. A campfire anchors your camp and opens the way to outdoor survival. When you travel through the wild, a campfire gives you a place to begin. Seek cooking training first. Cooking lets you prepare meals from wild game and teaches you to light a basic campfire. That fire anchors an outdoor camp. Without it to ward off the chill and keep darkness at bay, you cannot make a reliable campsite in the wild. A basic campfire lets you make a modest camp in the wild. It holds only a few simple furnishings, but you can expand your camp as your skills grow. More cooking training teaches you to kindle larger, sturdier fires. Trainers in other trades can teach you to make furnishings and improve your camp.

quest:96646.text: Camping 101: Cooking. At Shen'dar Village, Zerril Softbreeze shows you how to kindle a campfire. Camping 101: Cooking teaches you to make a fire and establish a campsite in the wilderness. A campfire gives you a place to rest in untamed lands. Learning to cook begins with making that fire. It is the first step toward establishing a safe campsite. Speak with Zerril Softbreeze in Shen'dar Village to learn the fundamentals of cooking. Once you know how to kindle a campfire, you can establish a small campsite in the wilderness. A basic camp has only a few furnishings. As your cooking skill improves, you can kindle larger fires. Other tradeskills help furnish the site.

quest:96655.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In Razor Hill, Cook Torka shows travelers how to cook and make a campfire. With those skills, they can establish camps in the wild. Beyond a settlement's gates, surviving in the wild takes more than sharp steel and sturdy armor. In Razor Hill, Cook Torka teaches budding adventurers to cook. Across Durotar and beyond, cooking means more than preparing a hot meal. It also teaches travelers to light a reliable campfire, the heart of any campsite. Once travelers know the basics, they can pitch a modest camp almost anywhere on the frontier. A novice campfire supports only a few essential furnishings. Greater cooking skill lets travelers build larger blazes. Other trades teach them to craft what they need to furnish and improve a camp into a reliable shelter from the wild.

quest:96661.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In Bloodhoof Village, Pyall Silentstride begins your lessons in cooking and campfires. Across Kalimdor, those skills help you make a campsite and prepare meals from hunted game. When night falls, a campfire gives you a place to return to. Across Kalimdor, basic cooking teaches you to build a fire in the wild. It also shows you how to prepare nourishing meals from hunted game, making cooking part of surviving outdoors. In Bloodhoof Village, Mulgore, Pyall Silentstride teaches you the basics of cooking. With that training, you can kindle a campfire and pitch a simple camp in the wilderness. As your cooking skill grows, you learn to build larger fires. Other crafts can furnish your outpost.

quest:96800.text: Past Due. A scholar needs a missing tome from the Scarlet Monastery to study Grim Batol’s ancient Wildhammer runemasters. The old Dalaran library’s ledgers show that Arcanist Doan borrowed the tome before the Third War and never returned it.

quest:96821.text: Legging It. The peons have halted their southward travel because dangers line the road. Their work waits until the way is safe again. Peons have left their assigned work undone and stopped traveling south. Perils along the road have made the journey too dangerous. Once the threats are pushed back, overseers can send their crews to work again. Peons do much of the Horde’s hard labor, from harvesting timber and quarrying to building outposts. They have little skill in battle, so roadside predators or hostile scouts can halt the movement of supplies. Clear routes keep settlements supplied and let the work continue.

quest:96822.text: For Honor. Fallen warriors live on in memory through For Honor. Their sacrifices endure in the minds of those who remember them. Those who outlive fallen warriors carry their memory forward. Remembering those who gave everything is a duty. Your efforts keep the fallen fighters alive in memory. Those who remember them continue to honor their sacrifices.

quest:96825.text: This Fruit Could Bite Back. In Durotar, prickly pears feed Orgrimmar and promise more food ahead. Gathered with care, these hardy fruits can nourish the Horde capital and provide seeds for future crops. Durotar is rugged and sun-baked, where traditional farming is nearly impossible. Its hardy prickly pears thrive in the arid soil, so inhabitants gather them to help feed Orgrimmar. Their protective spines call for care, and their fruit brings needed nourishment. Prickly pears feed people now and can help supply food in the years ahead. Their flesh is prepared for dishes, while their seeds are carefully preserved for planting. The aim is to grow this resilient crop around Orgrimmar, creating a lasting food source close outside the fortress walls.

quest:96874.text: This Is Spinal Axe. Ug’thok in Orgrimmar asks you to gather spines from the huge beasts of Thunder Ridge. He hopes to shape them into an axe head for your smithing lessons. Ug’thok asks you to bring five Weathered Spines and five Rough Grinding Stones. He believes the spines could make a fine axe head, though Saru laughed at the idea.

quest:96875.text: Beasts of Thunder Ridge. Across Durotar, Orgrimmar's builders need hides to keep the growing capital strong. Kamari sends you to Thunder Ridge for lizard hides and cured light hides. Orgrimmar keeps growing as the Horde makes a home in Durotar. New homes, workshops, and defenses need lumber, stone, and animal skins. Timber comes from farther away, but Durotar's beasts provide sturdy hides for the peons and builders. The lizards of Thunder Ridge have tough hides, too thick and stiff for wearable armor. Properly harvested, their pelts line the walls and ceilings of Orgrimmar's timber and stone buildings. There, they shield the interiors from the harsh sun and sudden canyon winds.

quest:96876.text: Ukor's Lost Pack. In southern Durotar, Ukor's Lost Pack lies abandoned in the wilds. Its owner fled a huge spider and left his supplies behind. In southern Durotar, you find a traveling bag with Ukor's name crudely stitched across its flap. In these harsh lands, discarded gear may point to trouble nearby. Ukor receives his pack in southern Durotar and tells how he lost it. A huge spider ambushed him, and he fled in panic, certain his supplies were gone. Finding the bag intact earns you Ukor's heartfelt gratitude and praise.

quest:96877.text: Halikor's Hoof. In the wilds, Halikor's Hoof is carried to Orgrimmar as proof of a hunter's triumph. The enormous severed hoof honors the hunter's victory over the formidable lizard. Halikor's vast size is plain in the hoof taken from its remains. Hunters and warriors in the wilds have long claimed a piece of a formidable beast to prove the kill. The hoof leaves no doubt of the lizard's great size and strength. The heavy hoof is carried to Orgrimmar to announce the beast's defeat to the Horde. Strength and survival against the land's harsh predators matter in this warrior society. Presenting the trophy honors the hunter and assures the capital that a dangerous creature has been slain.

quest:96895.text: The Argent Emissary. In Tirisfal Glades, two Argent Dawn emissaries hunt Scourge cultists near the Undercity. Both are Forsaken, yet local authorities distrust an armed neutral order in their territory. Two Forsaken emissaries of the Argent Dawn have recently reached Tirisfal Glades. Their arrival puts local authorities on edge. The Argent Dawn fights the Scourge, but the Forsaken distrust an armed neutral order acting without oversight in their territory. Even their shared heritage does little to ease that wariness. The emissaries pursue Scourge cultists southeast of the Undercity, near its outskirts. They mean to root out the Lich King's agents before the cultists gain a foothold. One emissary watches their movements from near the city gates.

quest:96896.text: A Righteous Cause. Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr meet again to remember the Undercity's defense against Naxxramas. They speak of Garek Bandarion, a fallen undead hero who found the Holy Light again as a paladin, and of the Forsaken who carry his path onward. Leonid Barthalomew the Revered and Danitha Morr meet again after defending Lordaeron together. They survived Naxxramas's assault on the Undercity, though many comrades fell. Now they remember the dead and the hard road faced by Forsaken who still honor the Holy Light. Leonid and Danitha remember Garek Bandarion, the fallen hero whose name was given to the keep. Leonid believes Garek may have been the first Forsaken to wield the Holy Light again as a true paladin. Most Forsaken have turned from the Light. Danitha and her cohort keep Garek's legacy alive and explore what holy unlife may allow. After speaking with Danitha, Leonid prepares to leave the keep and return to the fight against the Scourge in the ravaged east. He is stationed at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. There, he welcomes able-bodied adventurers ready to take up arms.

quest:96897.text: The Cult of the Damned. In Tirisfal Glades, living servants of the Scourge threaten the people once more. By culling Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers, you help keep the Lich King's agents from repeating the betrayals that shattered Lordaeron. The Scourge has living servants who swear fealty to the Lich King. They serve where the mindless dead cannot. In Tirisfal Glades, people already face roaming undead and the relentless zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Now, newly discovered cells of Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers show the Scourge seeking a foothold again. The marching dead were not the only cause of Lordaeron's fall. Neighbors betrayed neighbors as the Cult of the Damned infiltrated villages and poisoned granaries. From the shadows, they helped bring the kingdom down. Fresh Cult activity in Tirisfal threatens to repeat that history in the scarred lands of the north.

quest:96898.text: Remnants of War. Across Tirisfal Glades, remnants of war lie scattered beneath the soil. Naxxramas was driven from the Undercity at great cost to the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn. Its shattered necrotic focusing crystal remains a danger, and Scourge cultists seek its fragments for the dark magic within. Naxxramas once loomed over Tirisfal Glades, seeking to wipe out the Undercity and the Forsaken. The Forsaken and the Argent Dawn fought off the floating fortress in a desperate defense. Both sides suffered heavy losses. During the battle, the immense necrotic focusing crystal atop Naxxramas was destroyed, scattering fragments across the glades. Naxxramas was driven away, but pieces of its crystal remain in the soil. Scourge cultists search for the fragments, hoping to use the dark magic still within them. Gathering the shards keeps that power from the Scourge. Yet clearing every fragment from Tirisfal will take years.

quest:96899.text: Bandarion Keep. At Bandarion Keep, Commander Leonid Barthalomew waits for travelers in western Tirisfal Glades. The Argent Dawn once held the secluded fortress against the Scourge, and Danitha and her paladins now guard its walls. After you aid the Argent Dawn against Cult of the Damned activity, you are sent northwest across Tirisfal Glades. Commander Leonid Barthalomew waits at the fortress to speak with you about the order's ongoing crusade against darkness. The Argent Dawn once used the stronghold as a staging post against Scourge incursions across Tirisfal Glades. Then the order turned its focus to the Eastern and Western Plaguelands. The fort was left behind and began to decay, until Paladin Danitha and her companions took stewardship of its walls.

quest:96986.text: The Grave Knight. In Tarren Mill, Melisara sends you after Atrexis, who raises the dead beneath Dalaran. She sees his work as an affront to the Forsaken. Melisara calls Atrexis a traitor to the Forsaken. Beneath Dalaran, he raises an undead army. She asks you to defeat him, though she cares little for the mage city's fate. No one is beyond the Dark Lady's reach.

quest:96988.text: Source of Power. In Dalaran, rogue constructs have turned on their makers, and Doctor Martin Felben sees a chance for the Forsaken. He wants their arcane cores for his work in Undercity and hopes to catch the Dark Lady’s eye. Dalaran’s rogue arcane constructs are laying siege to the magi, and the Forsaken are eager to exploit the city’s turmoil. Doctor Martin Felben, an apothecary in Undercity, seeks to scavenge the cores that power the sentries rather than aid the besieged sorcerers. Dalaran has long guarded its magical research, but its vulnerable sentries now offer an opening to opportunistic researchers. Doctor Felben wants the cracked sentry cores to advance his standing within the Royal Apothecary Society. He hopes to infuse Forsaken abominations with volatile Dalaran construct magic and raise a devastating army of arcane-powered flesh beasts. Such a breakthrough, he believes, would win Lady Sylvanas Windrunner’s undivided attention and show his alchemical genius. He hopes to rise in the Society, where ruthless cunning and potent results dictate survival and rank.

quest:97.text: The Legend of Stalvan. In Darkshire, Clerk Daltry matches the recovered handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle. His report makes the Night Watch's suspicion certain. Back in Darkshire's town hall, Clerk Daltry compares the bloodstained journal page with signatures in the Town Registry. The handwriting matches Stalvan Mistmantle exactly. After the trail led through manors, inns, and civic records across the human kingdoms, the Night Watch now has proof that the danger is close at hand.

quest:970.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At Maestra's Post, Delgren the Purifier sends you south to stop the Cult of the Dark Strand. Its threat reaches from the Tower of Althalaxx into Ashenvale, and you are to recover a Glowing Soul Gem from the ruins of Ordil'Aran. Reports from the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore have led you south to Delgren the Purifier at Maestra's Post. He has fought the Cult of the Dark Strand for a long time, but the cult now presses into Ashenvale's ancient elven woods. Its reach crosses both territories, so Delgren seeks to strike at the source of its sorcery. Northeast of Maestra's Post, the ruins of Ordil'Aran are overrun by Dark Strand cultists. Delgren says their operatives carry glowing soul gems, vessels enchanted with magic that sustains the cult's power. Hunt among the ruins and recover a gem. Delgren can break its enchantment and uncover the source of the cult's rite.

quest:97003.text: Chol'aruk the Ravener. In the Barrens, Gur'ak sends travelers after a colossal quilboar called Chol'aruk the Ravener. He believes the tales and asks them to return with its head. Razormane quilboar whisper of Chol'aruk, an enormous terror they call The Ravener. They say it lairs deep in a cavern at Thorn Hill, northeast of the local trails. By their account, it is roughly five times the size of an ordinary quilboar and driven by an unquenchable thirst for blood. Many dismiss the tales as campfire exaggeration. Gur'ak knows better from past battles with similar beasts. Gur'ak knows a beast of such size poses a real danger. He directs capable travelers to track Chol'aruk to its lair in Thorn Hill, end its threat, and bring back its head as proof. The Ravener is said to be ferocious and colossal. Gur'ak warns that only well-prepared groups should enter the cave to face it.

quest:97005.text: Chol'aruk the Ravener. On Thorn Hill in the Barrens, Chol'aruk the Ravener haunts a cave. Bainham seeks its severed head to avenge comrades slain by beasts like it. Northwest of Bainham's camp, Thorn Hill rises above the Barrens Savannah. The Razormane tribes have long fought over its plateau. Now a monstrous abomination is said to lurk in one of its caves. The Razormane call it Chol'aruk or the Ravener. Some travelers doubt the tale that it can swallow an armored orc whole. Those who have seen the carnage know the danger is real. Bainham knows Chol'aruk is no campfire tale. He has fought similar horrors and carries scars from those encounters. His comrades fell to such beasts, and he still mourns them. He fears the abomination threatens everyone crossing the Savannah. Bainham asks seasoned champions to climb Thorn Hill, enter its underground lair, slay Chol'aruk, and bring back its massive head.

quest:971.text:
Knowledge in the Deeps. In Ironforge, Gerrig Bonegrip sends you across the sea to seek an ancient manuscript. He wants the Lorgalis Manuscript from the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale. In Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip gathers ancient texts. His interests reach beyond ordinary histories and civic records. He seeks forgotten lore that can open doorways and awaken 'Those Who Sleep.'

Bonegrip speaks of surviving beyond 'the end days.' Such words make him seem either an eccentric scholar or a devotee of powers that slumber in shadow. Bonegrip sends you to Ashenvale's shadowed shores, where the night elven sanctuary of Blackfathom Deeps lies drowned. Before the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart, night elven scholars gathered great magical knowledge in coastal temples.

Now naga, satyrs, and Twilight's Hammer cultists crawl through the flooded halls. Among them lies the Lorgalis Manuscript, forbidden lore kept in a Pitted Iron Chest.

quest:972.text: Water Sapta. At Islen Waterseer's shore, a young Horde shaman receives Water Sapta for a journey across the Great Sea. The trial leads from the Barrens to Silverpine Forest, where a spring has been corrupted. Among Horde shaman, a sapta is a draught that opens the senses to the world's spirits. A stream may look calm and a pond still to ordinary eyes. Drink a sapta, and the veil of the physical world parts. Then the elementals dwelling in the water come into view. After the shaman proves devotion to the spirits, Islen Waterseer gives them the draught. She lives alone on the barren shore south of Ratchet. Then she sends the initiate across the Great Sea, from Kalimdor's dry valleys to Silverpine Forest. There, an elemental corruption poisons Lordaeron's streams, and the shaman must face it.

quest:97220.text: Philmor's Favor. A delicate shipment is bound for the Gatehouse in Stormwind under Philmor's Favor. With dockhands scarce, travelers carry it to a stockroom entrance above Trias' Cheese in the Trade District. Stormwind's freight handlers are short of dockhands, and ordinary cargo schedules are strained. They rely on trustworthy travelers to carry sensitive crates into the city's commercial quarter and keep deliveries moving. The Gatehouse shipment is bound for an unusual destination. Carry the crate to the second floor of Trias' Cheese in the Trade District, where a concealed entrance opens onto a stockroom. Supplies and ceremonial gifts for the guard's officers pass through there, beyond prying eyes.

quest:97222.text: Gatehouse Goods. In Stormwind, Gatehouse Goods moves from Trias' Cheese to the neighboring gatehouse. The route takes the shipment up the shop's stairs to a landing on the same floor, where guards can collect it outside the stockroom. Shared quarters link the city's shops and defenses. Couriers carry a gatehouse shipment up the stairs inside Trias' Cheese. The cheese shop is a separate business with its own inventory, yet its building shares a floor with the neighboring gatehouse. From the upper landing, couriers can move supplies between the two quarters without using the front avenues. The crate is left outside the stockroom door rather than carried inside. Gatehouse guards watch for deliveries and arrange for someone to collect each package when returning to their posts. The door opens inward, so a crate outside will not block the entry or hinder anyone inside.

quest:97223.text: Bloodtalon Matriarch. Near Sen'jin Village, handlers face a threat from the Bloodtalon Matriarch as they seek her young. Her pack is prized for speed and cunning, but adults resist taming. The Darkspear seek to secure her clutch and raise loyal companions from the egg. Along Durotar's coast, Bloodtalon raptors are prized for speed and cunning. Handlers in Sen'jin Village value those traits in dependable mounts and companions for the Darkspear tribe. Yet full-grown raptors have stubborn, violent instincts. Once grown, wild adults are scarcely tamed. Repeated attempts to capture and train the Matriarch have only made her more aggressive. Now she threatens the surrounding territory. The trolls seek to protect their tribe and preserve her bloodline. They must quell the dangerous mother and save her clutch, so the next generation can be raised from the egg as loyal allies.

quest:97225.text: Forgotten Loa Idols. The Darkspear seek the Forgotten Loa Idols so their sacred rites can continue. The relics preserve the tribe’s bond with its patron spirits. The Darkspear honor the loa through sacred rites. These primal animal spirits and wild gods belong to the trolls’ ancestral heritage. The lost idols are needed for ceremonies in their honor. Without them, spiritual leaders cannot perform the rites that keep the tribe in harmony with its divine guardians. The Darkspear approach the loa with respect and humble reverence. Other hostile troll factions across Azeroth practice blood sacrifice or try to command spirits by force. Losing their patrons’ favor would be a grave catastrophe for the Darkspear. So restoring the idols is vital to preserving the tribe.

quest:97234.text: Reading Room. At Roy's Book Club, members trade older literature for newer works from the Stormwind library. Wrapped books carry the exchange between the club and the librarian. Roy's Book Club gathers readers in Stormwind to discuss classical legends and provocative writings. To keep those talks fresh, members rotate their reading. They trade older or less popular works for newer volumes from the city's library. Roy's Book Club keeps an established lending arrangement with the Stormwind library. Roy wraps the club's returned books in a distinctive way, and you carry them to the librarian. In return, the club receives a new list of modern tomes.

quest:97236.text: Fang of Githyiss. Near Aldrassil, Githyiss’s hunt brings a rare specimen to the sanctuary. Scholars can study the giant spider’s fang and watch for predators in Shadowglen. Githyiss threatens travelers in Shadowglen’s wilds. The giant spider’s fang matters both as a danger and as a specimen worth studying. Scouts carry it through the underbrush to the sanctuary beneath the great tree. In Aldrassil, night elf naturalists and scholars watch the wildlife on the forest floor. A fresh, intact fang from a spider as large as Githyiss can teach them about arachnids beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Researchers welcome the find as they study the glade’s aggressive creatures.

quest:97237.text: Shelf Picked. In Stormwind, Roy Lewells sends a runner to gather books for a reading group in the Park. Roy Lewells has sent a note asking for several books from the Stormwind library. The librarian checks the list and confirms every title is in stock. The books are there for you to find and pull from the shelves. The librarian stays at the desk to keep the inventory records. Roy Lewells's note makes you an official courier, so you are not responsible for returning the borrowed books. That duty belongs to Lewells's establishment. Once you bring the volumes to the Park, Roy prepares them for lively after-hours discussions in a cellar. The books have an exotic smell.

quest:97242.text: Yelmak's Medley. Tensions rise in Yelmak's Alchemy and Potions, in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Master alchemist Yelmak hopes a calming mixture made with local water plants will quiet his apprentice Whuut's clumsy frustration and stubborn pride. At Yelmak's Alchemy and Potions, young apprentice Whuut's pride is making trouble. Rather than ask for help when he is out of his depth, he breaks the shop's equipment in frustration. Master alchemist Yelmak seeks to calm the youth without bruising his fragile ego, so he devises a soothing concoction. The recipe calls for fresh cattails and speargrass from the watercourses winding through the Valley of Honor. Kor'geld cannot leave the shop without alerting the suspicious apprentice, so someone discreet must gather the plants. The botanical mixture is meant to temper Whuut's attitude and restore peace to the alchemy shop.

quest:97243.text: Call of Fire. In Skywall, initiates carry the Torch of Dormant Flame to Olariaan Swiftburn for teaching. The shrine lies in the Gustberry Lowlands. Skywall belongs to the air elementals, though its currents reach the wider Elemental Plane. Spirits of earth, water, and fire still speak to those who can hear them. Some Windshapers are especially open to these other forces. Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei among them, is deeply attuned to fire. Initiates take the Torch of Dormant Flame to the Gustberry Lowlands. Far along the island rim, west of Valanaar, stands the Shrine of Flames, Olariaan Swiftburn's home. Olariaan receives the dormant flame and offers to teach aspiring students to heed fire's demanding call amid the air realm's churning currents.

quest:97244.text: Call of Fire. The Windshapers send you after a traitor who chose power over his order. Skypriest Faladiel has fled to the Gustberry Lowlands, and they need his heart for a ritual. The Windshapers send you after Skypriest Faladiel, once one of their own. He left the order to join the Al'Aketh and traded his calling as a flame-caller for power. He betrayed his former brothers and sisters, and their blood stains his hands. Now the Windshapers send you to carry out their judgment. Faladiel hides at a farm in the Gustberry Lowlands, northeast past Valanaar and just south of the Shrine of Akir. The Windshapers seek more than vengeance. They need his heart for an upcoming ritual. They believe a betrayer's heart will lend their sacred flames unmatched intensity.

quest:97245.text: Call of Fire. In the Shen'dar Highlands, Olariaan Swiftburn sends you to face Kuramaa, an ancient forest sprite. Flame can pierce its defenses, and its wooden mask is needed in the Gustberry Lowlands to kindle an eternal flame and commune with fire spirits. People in the Shen'dar Highlands speak of Kuramaa, an ancient forest sprite that dwells in a twisted tree stump. The stump stands atop a hill near the regional Anchor Pylon. Strike the bark with a bare fist, and Kuramaa comes forth to meet you in combat. Kuramaa's natural wards turn aside most arcane and divine magic. Only searing flame pierces its ancient bark and brings it low. Defeat the sprite, and its wooden mask is yours, an artifact of great power. Yet Kuramaa is eternal. When called again, it reforms.

quest:97246.text: Meal Appeal. In Orgrimmar, Thatog worries his young son Migi is skipping meals to play. He asks you to fetch lunch from Borstan's Firepit and find Migi behind Grommash Hold. Thatog's daily duties keep him at his post in Orgrimmar. He has little time to watch Migi, his energetic young son. From morning until dusk, Migi races through the city with his friends. He often ignores his hunger until he comes home famished. Thatog arranges a hot lunch for Migi at Borstan's Firepit and asks you to carry it. Migi would rather keep playing than stop to eat. So you take the meal to the yard behind Grommash Hold, where Migi and the neighborhood children play.

quest:97249.text: Favorite Food. In Orgrimmar, Migi's parents worry that play keeps him from eating enough. Borstan of Borstan's Meats prepares varied lunches with a taste Migi loves, so he and his friends stop to eat. Behind Grommash Hold, young Migi and his friends spend their afternoons playing along Orgrimmar's dusty paths. His parents worry that he often neglects his meals and does not eat enough. So they ask Borstan's Meats to prepare daily packed lunches. They insist that Borstan vary the meals, hoping Migi will learn to enjoy more than one favorite dish. Migi loves sweetglazed hog belly sandwiches and comes for lunch when the smokehouse fills with their sweet aroma. Borstan finds a way to honor his parents' request while keeping Migi fed. He crumbles the leftover crispy glazed cracklings into a savory seasoning that can be sprinkled over any dish. Behind Grommash Hold, the topping persuades Migi and his companions to pause their play and share lunch.

quest:97250.text: Wrongly Blamed, Justly Corrected. Along the eastern coast, Wrongly Blamed, Justly Corrected follows rising Horde and Alliance tensions after a roadside tavern is destroyed. The incident warns Alliance forces, while the question of who threatened a vital civilian trade route remains open. Along the eastern coast, Horde and Alliance skirmishes are reaching contested ground. Then a tavern on a major thoroughfare is destroyed. Ordinary travelers now face danger, and the region's stability is at risk. The affair ends in victory for Horde forces in the area, though questions about the tavern remain. The result warns the Alliance that any move into Horde territory along the coast will meet immediate resistance.

quest:97253.text:
Parts and Pieces. In Ratchet, Wrenix's machine lies in pieces after the pirates dismantled it. He sent it to face the raiders after five or six mercenaries failed to return alive. Now its scattered parts lie in the pirates' upper camp. Pirates along the coast south of Ratchet trouble the town's residents and tradesfolk. Wrenix the Wretched wanted to stop them without risking more coin on hired hands. Five or six mercenaries had already gone after the pirates and failed to return alive.

So Wrenix sent an automated machine to deal with the encampment on its own. He hoped the contraption could face the marauders without putting another living soul at risk. The pirates south of Ratchet proved resourceful. They used their curved scimitars as makeshift screwdrivers and pried Wrenix's machine apart before he could send instructions to retreat toward town.

Its delicate components now lie scattered in their upper camp. Wrenix needs someone to slip inside and gather five handfuls of the complicated parts from the dirt.

quest:97257.text: Call of Fire. At Skywall, initiates face the Windshapers’ trial and seek a Fire Totem. They summon spirits of flame, bear the Eternal Flame to Valanaar, and kindle its brazier. Olariaan of the Windshapers guides initiates through a sacred trial at Skywall. They gather at the Brazier of Offering and call to spirits of flame from the Firelands. If their offerings are worthy, the spirits kindle the altar with the Eternal Flame. A worthy initiate may then take up that flame. The Eternal Flame must be caught on a torch and carried across Skywall to Valanaar. In this elemental realm, its power from the Firelands fades in the swirling air. The initiate must reach the Brazier of Eternal Flames before the torch goes dark. When an initiate rekindles the brazier at Valanaar, the Windshapers grant them a Fire Totem. It honors their discipline and respect for the elements. The elders teach that elemental power serves those who respect it, but consumes those who do not.

quest:97263.text: Your Package Has Arrived. A parcel from Aerie Peak lies beside a city mailbox, bound for Ironforge. Marked urgent for Eldrun Stormbreaker, it still waits to be delivered. Several parcels lie abandoned beside a city mailbox. They were left there instead of being carried to their destinations. One urgent parcel came from Aerie Peak, the Wildhammer dwarves’ mountain redoubt in the Hinterlands. Deliveries between distant outposts across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron can go awry. An alert passerby can carry a mislaid package onward. The parcel is addressed to Eldrun Stormbreaker in Ironforge. Its urgent notice marks the shipment as important enough to travel from the Hinterlands to the dwarven capital without delay. The crate still needs to reach Eldrun before it is stolen or forgotten.

quest:97275.text: Whuut's the Rush. Yelmak sends you to carry a tonic to Whuut, whose eagerness has outrun his care. His apprentice reaches for rare herbs before learning what common plants can do. Whuut has a gift for alchemy, and the stirring rod comes naturally to him. Yet impatience leads him to spend the shop’s rarest reagents before he has mastered the basics. He reaches for legendary plants before learning how common herbs must be balanced, treating alchemy as a race. Yelmak answers his apprentice’s haste with a lesson in a vial. He brews a refined tonic from common speargrass and cattail using a quick method. Whuut is daydreaming about Black Lotus and Mountain Silversage when the tonic reaches his hands. Its simple ingredients show how much skill, patience, and respect for everyday plants can matter.

quest:97277.text: Grund and Gozwin. At their camp in the northwestern hills, Grund and Gozwin face a snow leopard’s attack. Grund drives it off with his shotgun, but Gozwin loses his Mechanic's Log in the scramble. You camp with Grund and Gozwin in the snowy hills for the evening. As Grund turns to prepare a boar over the fire, a snow leopard springs from the brush and seizes Gozwin in its jaws. Grund snatches up his shotgun and fires over the beast’s head. Startled, the leopard lets Gozwin go and flees into the cold crags. Gozwin escapes with deep scratches, but the attack scatters the camp. In the scramble, he loses his prized Mechanic's Log, which holds schematics for his mecha-walker. The battered gnome fears someone may find his engineering secrets. He cannot rest until you search the hills northwest of camp for the log and the prowling leopard.

quest:97281.text: A Simmering Storm. In Durotar, the Dull Stormy Orb has caught Rezlak's attention. The goblin tinker sees reason to study the relic, recovered from the Dustwind harpies of Drygulch Ravine. Travelers who contend with the Dustwind harpies of Drygulch Ravine may find the Dull Stormy Orb among their strange trinkets. Its worn surface gives off a steady electrical vibration. Dark mist churns within, split now and then by sharp sparks. The relic shows the harpies have handled storm magic. Rezlak waits at the entrance to Drygulch Ravine, where the orb has caught his eye. Its discovery brings to mind advice from his employer, Chief Engineer Gazlowe of Ratchet. What the harpies meant to do with the miniature storm remains unknown. Now the orb is in goblin hands.

quest:97282.text: Stormy Potential. Near Drygulch Ravine, Rezlak looks for a way to protect his caravan from harpies. He hopes to charge a drained orb with the electrical organs of Durotar's thunder lizards. Near Drygulch Ravine in Durotar, harpies threaten Rezlak's caravan, and a sound magical orb has lost its power. Gazlowe, Ratchet's chief engineer, once advised Rezlak to seize opportunity when it knocks. Now the goblin plans to charge the dormant orb and answer both troubles at once. Rezlak needs strong electricity to restore his drained orb. Thunder lizards live in the gorge west of Drygulch Ravine, and their organs generate and conduct deadly lightning. He asks you to bring him those charged organs. Rezlak hopes to channel their volatile current into the orb and defend his supply wagons from harpy ambushes.

quest:97286.text: Research Access. Your actions have earned you a place in the library. Its doors are open for your study. You have earned access to the library for your studies. Its doors are open to you.

quest:97287.text: Shrewd Negotiations. After your infiltration of the mages' city, Magus Wordeen Voidglare sends you to Dalaran. Carry the arcane mote to Archmage Celindra; Wordeen believes the Kirin Tor will give anything to recover it. Magus Wordeen Voidglare says no order on Azeroth matches the Kirin Tor in arcane knowledge. Even his brilliant work pales beside their ancient wisdom. He believes the Horde should gain access to their exclusive order. So he sends you to Archmage Celindra in Dalaran with the mote you acquired. Wordeen believes the Kirin Tor will give anything to get it back.

quest:97288.text:
Unending Torment. The head of a fallen abomination sets Unending Torment in motion. Its repeated stitching points toward deliberate dark experimentation in the Forsaken capital, and you bring it to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. When the towering abomination falls in battle, its head topples from its shoulders. The neck was severed, stitched, torn away, and reattached many times. Each repair left the seam more fragile, until the head barely clung to its shoulders.

Such persistent patchwork is unusual even for undead constructs. The repeated destruction and reassembly suggest this abomination was rebuilt again and again. Ordinary scavengers could not explain its craftsmanship. Only the skilled flesh-crafters of the Undercity could identify the creature's origins.

quest:97289.text: Unending Torment. In the Undercity, the Forsaken prepare to question a fallen Alliance commander. They mean to give Grand Marshal Othmar Garithos a new body, and learn what he carried to his grave. Deep in the Undercity, Forsaken practitioners stitch abominations from discarded pieces of the dead. Among the preserved skulls lies one with a bitter history: the severed head of Grand Marshal Othmar Garithos. He led the surviving Alliance forces across Lordaeron, until the Dark Lady killed him.

quest:97290.text: Unending Torment. At the Undercity, a defiant subject refuses the Royal Apothecary Society's demands. Master Apothecary Faranell welcomes the news, eager to break a difficult captive. A subject under the Royal Apothecary Society's scrutiny despises you. The captive calls you an abomination and refuses to help. Such hatred is familiar to the Forsaken, for many living beings and captives recoil from Lordaeron's undead. You bring the subject's refusal to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. The head of the Royal Apothecary Society greets the news with wicked delight. To him, resistance makes the subject a challenge, fit for the cruel experiments of the Apothecarium.

quest:97291.text: Unending Torment. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell prepares a brew to bind a captive to the Dark Lady's will. He needs lethal reagents from across the Forsaken capital to finish it. Deep in the Undercity's Apothecarium, Master Apothecary Faranell conducts experiments to strengthen the Forsaken. He has reattached the severed head of a battered captive. Now he needs a special alchemical mixture to crush the creature's remaining resistance and bind its will to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Faranell sends his agent across the Undercity to gather potent ingredients for his brew. A Toxic Skullcap comes from Tawny Grisette in the Trade Quarter. Blisterweed is held by nearby herbalist trainers who owe him a debt, and a poison vendor in the Rogues' Quarter sells Essence of Agony.

quest:97292.text: Unending Torment. Master Apothecary Faranell sets a punishment in motion beneath the Undercity. In the Apothecarium, the Royal Apothecary Society turns Hissing Serum against Othmar’s remains, seeking lasting retribution for crimes against the Dark Lady. In the Undercity’s Apothecarium, Master Apothecary Faranell conducts harsh experiments against the Forsaken’s enemies. He has prepared Hissing Serum, a caustic substance meant to drip without end onto a captive beneath an alchemical apparatus.

quest:973.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, dark cultists lead Delgren the Purifier to Ilkrud Magthrull. He sends you south through Darkshore into Ashenvale to slay the orc warlock at Fire Scar Shrine and recover his tome. Delgren the Purifier traces the dark cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx to Ilkrud Magthrull, an orc warlock. Ilkrud works from Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale. Delgren fears his magic could spread through the elven woodlands, so he sends you to kill the warlock and take his tome. He hopes its contents will reveal his master's designs.

quest:97326.text: Rocks to Rests. Behind Grommash Hold, Thra and friends make room for games in Orgrimmar. They need smooth boulders to use as chairs and tables. Young orcs gather in a dirt clearing behind Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar. There they can play away from the fortress guards. The open ground suits their miniature figures, but with no furniture, they sit in the dust. Thra spots you passing and asks you to carry eight medium-sized, smooth boulders to the clearing. Their flat sides will make sturdy chairs and low tables. Then the youths can arrange their games without sitting in the dirt.

quest:97538.text: Pigments for Paints. Tah Winterhoof needs red pigment for his paints, and you can help him replenish it. The color comes from mirkweed pods gathered in Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Tah Winterhoof has run out of red pigment and cannot continue his work. He lives in Thunder Bluff, and his traveling days are behind him. So he asks you to make the long journey north into the Stonetalon Mountains and gather more coloring. Mirkfallon Lake lies in a mountain pass in the Stonetalon Mountains. Mirkweed grows beneath its waters, and its seed pods turn red when harvested and dried. Gather thirty pods, and Tah will have the raw material he needs to return to his work.

quest:97539.text: Silky Sutures. At Hammerfall, Doctor Gregory Victor is turning to spider silk as infirmary supplies dwindle. Siege damage remains unrepaired, and the outpost's guards and laborers still need care. Hammerfall endures in the Arathi Highlands, though siege damage still mars its defenses. Doctor Gregory Victor, the outpost's physician, sees the neglect as official policy. With little support and crumbling fortifications around him, he keeps the infirmary running. Its care helps laborers and sentinel guards stay on their feet and ready for conflict. Medical supplies are running low at Hammerfall, so Doctor Victor seeks another way to stitch wounds. Tough highland spider silk can be twisted into resilient sutures when bandages and ordinary thread are scarce. Victor jokes that infection is the least of a wounded soldier's worries. The silk gives the infirmary thread to patch up defenders in hostile territory. Doctor Gregory Victor greets travelers with dry jokes about grave prognoses and stitches made from spider silk. His humor masks the hard truth of running a frontline clinic while Hammerfall remains isolated. Regular aid is rare in the highlands, and travelers can help keep the clinic supplied. Victor relies on improvised remedies and determination to care for the wounded as the outpost decays around him.

quest:97583.text: WRIGGLE.. In Undercity, WRIGGLE. dances with travelers, then tires and needs special sludge to recover. After feeding, it follows a new friend. In Undercity, WRIGGLE. joins the dances of friendly travelers. The little slime starts full of energy, but soon tires and needs food to regain its strength. You can buy Nutritious Slime Sludge in Undercity's rancid canals. WRIGGLE. absorbs the foul treat and regains its energy. Then it bonds with the one who fed it and is ready to follow its new friend.

quest:976.text: Supplies to Auberdine. Feero Ironhand carries provisions and messages from Maestra's Post to Auberdine, and the road north needs guards. Trouble near the Tower of Althalaxx and hostile infiltrators make the journey unsafe. Maestra's Post stands on Ashenvale's western frontier, between the forest and Darkshore. After investigations into sinister activity near the Tower of Althalaxx, Delgren the Purifier sends supplies and intelligence to Sentinel Starbreeze in Auberdine. The outpost trusts armed escorts over lone couriers, so Feero Ironhand travels the forest road with guards.

quest:97891.text: Prompt Potion Runner. In Undercity, a runner carries Alessandro’s brew across the slime canal before it spoils. The delivery must reach the Apothecarium in time. Alessandro needs a swift courier in Undercity’s underground corridors. The Forsaken alchemist has made a volatile brew that will soon spoil. His undead joints are too frail for him to cross the toxic slime canal, so you carry it intact before it turns to useless sludge. Doctor Martin Felben waits at the Apothecarium for the brew, which he needs for his ongoing research. He says the six potions Alessandro sent before this one destabilized in transit. A timely delivery lets the doctor continue his shadowy experiments without interruption. The unstable brew and Alessandro’s frail joints show the hazards of Forsaken alchemy and undeath.

quest:97900.text:
Camping 101: Blacksmithing. In Razor Hill, Dwukk can teach you a camp craft suited to your blacksmithing skill. A Sharpening Wheel gives nearby fighters a way to hone their weapons. Dwukk teaches you to craft a Sharpening Wheel once you show skill in blacksmithing. Set it up at a wilderness camp, where nearby fighters and rogues can hone their weapons.

You need a campfire to start your camp. Cooks can teach you how to make one.

quest:97901.text: Camping 101: Enchanting. You can make an Enchanted Lute, but townsfolk dislike camps in town centers. To set up camp in the wilderness, you need a fire. A campfire gives you the basis for your camp. Most cooks can show you how to make one, so seek a cooking trainer if you have not learned the basics.

quest:97903.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At Rawrk's camp in Razor Hill, capable travelers learn to make a First Aid Kit for the wilderness. The lesson covers where to camp and why a fire matters. Rawrk in Razor Hill teaches capable travelers to make a First Aid Kit. With one, you can tend wounds far from an apothecary or infirmary, where help may be hard to find. Rawrk warns you against pitching a tent in the middle of Razor Hill or another settlement. Find an open place in the wild instead. A camp also needs a fire to see you through the night. Learn basic firemaking from a cooking instructor before you set out.

quest:97904.text: Camping 101: Fishing. At your camp, fishing can bring comfort to you and your companions. Near Sen'jin Village, Lau'Tiki can teach you to make a Fish Bowl. Once you have shown skill in fishing, speak with Lau'Tiki near Sen'jin Village. Lau'Tiki can teach you to make a Fish Bowl, a fixture for camp meant to bring joy to you and your fellow adventurers. A happier camp, the giver hopes, makes for stronger fighters.

quest:97905.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. You learn to make incense candles from wild plants in Camping 101: Herbalism. First, though, a proper camp needs a fire, and your campsite belongs in the wilderness beyond town. Herbalism lets you turn gathered plants into incense candles for comfort on the trail. Townsfolk frown on tents pitched in city streets, so these candles are meant for camps beyond guarded settlements. A campfire belongs at the heart of every campsite. Set one before you use an incense candle. Herbalists provide the aromatic burn, while cooking trainers across the land teach travelers the basics of starting a fire.

quest:97907.text: Camping 101: Mining. In Durotar, skilled miners can learn to forge a Lodestone for camps in the wild. Krunn in Razor Hill teaches the craft. Mining yields materials for travel and survival in the wild. With skill in pick and ore, you can learn to make gear for a campsite. In Durotar, Krunn in Razor Hill teaches skilled miners to forge a Lodestone for their travels. At a wilderness camp, a Lodestone gives the gathered fighters greater strength in battle. Set it beside the campfire, and martial fighters around the flames gain an edge. Townsfolk frown on tents pitched in city squares, so you need the open wild to put your craft to use. A sturdy Lodestone needs a fire at the heart of camp. You need a basic campfire before setting up a resting place. If you do not know how to build one, seek a cooking instructor. Cooking teaches the basics for warmth and sustenance on expeditions beyond town walls.

quest:97908.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Orgrimmar, new skinners are sent to Thuwd to learn the craft of camping. You make a Camp Chair from hides and pelts, then carry it beyond the city to open country. In Orgrimmar, Thuwd teaches capable skinners to make a Camp Chair from cured hides. The pelts and hides of fallen beasts can serve beyond armorcraft. A skinner can put them to use in the wild. Thuwd warns that guards and townsfolk frown on camps along busy city streets. A chair belongs in open country, away from settlement walls. A proper campsite needs a warm campfire, too. Cooks across Kalimdor teach the basics of making one.

quest:97916.text: Camping 101: Blacksmithing. In Goldshire, Smith Argus teaches skilled metalworkers to prepare for work in the wild. They learn to forge a portable Sharpening Wheel and to make camp in open country with a proper fire. Smith Argus of Goldshire shows skilled metalworkers how to carry their craft beyond the town anvils. Those ready for the work can learn to forge a Sharpening Wheel, keeping blades keen on long travels. Field gear alone does not make a proper camp. Goldshire townsfolk frown on camps within settlements, so crafters must head into the open frontier to use their equipment. A wilderness camp also needs a warm fire. Visit a local cook to learn the basics of making one.

quest:97917.text: Camping 101: Enchanting. In Stormwind, Betty Quin teaches enchanters to bring a little magic to the campfire. With an Enchanted Lute, they can lift spirits and help travelers rest along the trail. Long roads across Azeroth call for more than steel and rations. Comfort and good spirits matter in the wild, too. Enchanters put their craft to work at camp, turning quiet hours into music and rest before the next stretch of trail. Betty Quin in Stormwind teaches enchanters to make special items for the campsite. Once they have shown skill in enchanting, she can teach them to craft an Enchanted Lute. Its charms lift spirits around the campfire.

quest:97921.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. In Elwynn Forest, Herbalist Pomeroy teaches skilled gatherers a new comfort for camp. They learn to make Incense Candles, whose fragrance lifts the spirits of spellcasters resting in the wild. A herbalist's craft can help a traveling party in more ways than brewing restorative draughts or selling flowers. With skill in gathering, you can help your companions endure the wilds. A camp needs more than a fire and dry bedroll. Weary travelers also need comforts that keep their minds keen. Some plants give off aromas that refresh tired minds, so herbalists can support a party far from civilization. In Elwynn Forest, Herbalist Pomeroy teaches skilled gatherers to make campsite supplies from local plants. She shows them how to shape an Incense Candle, putting herbs to use beyond alchemy flasks. Burned at camp, its fragrance soothes tired travelers and lifts the spirits of companions who rely on mana. With Pomeroy's teaching, herbalists can bring comfort to parties traveling in the wild.

quest:97922.text:
Camping 101: Leatherworking. In Goldshire, Adele Fielder teaches leatherworkers to make a tent for journeys beyond town. It shelters travelers from harsh weather and gives them a place to rest while camping in the wilderness. Beyond the gates of Goldshire, shelter matters as much as armor. In Elwynn Forest, leatherworkers can visit Adele Fielder to learn more than simple belts and tunics. After they show skill with hide and needle, Adele teaches them to make a durable tent for long journeys overland. It is built to withstand harsh weather. A finished tent covers a campsite and guards against the elements. It keeps travelers cool under scorching suns, dry in driving rain, and rested between dangerous encounters.

Goldshire locals and city guards will not allow campsites in the town streets, so you need to head into the open wilderness to camp. Adele also reminds wanderers that a proper camp needs a campfire. A culinary trainer can teach you to make one.

quest:97923.text: Camping 101: Mining. In Stormwind, Gelman Stonehand teaches miners to shape a lodestone for camps in the wild. Set by a campfire, it strengthens the fighters gathered there. Miners in Stormwind can shape the earth’s natural magnetism into a lodestone. At an expedition’s campsite, it bolsters the fighting strength of those gathered there. Gelman Stonehand, Stormwind’s mining instructor, teaches the craft to prospectors who prove their skill with a pickaxe. A lodestone belongs in the wild, far from Cathedral Square and the Trade District. Townsfolk disapprove of travelers camping within city limits, so pioneers must head into the wild to make camp. The stone also needs a campfire. Cooks across the realm teach this basic wilderness skill.

quest:97924.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Elwynn Forest, skinners learn Camping 101: Skinning from Helene Peltskinner in Goldshire. She teaches them to shape harvested hides into a Camp Chair for rests beyond settled towns. You can shape hides taken from beasts into a Camp Chair for rest in the wild. In Goldshire, Helene Peltskinner teaches proficient skinners to make this seat for travelers on long journeys through dangerous lands. Take your gear into the wilderness before making camp, for townspeople often object to camps in the town square. A field camp also needs a campfire. Many skinners learn basic culinary arts to master fire-building.

quest:97925.text: Camping 101: Tailoring. In Elwynn Forest, skilled clothworkers are sent to Eldrin at the Eastvale Logging Camp. He teaches them to weave a Faction Banner that inspires travelers and raises morale at wilderness camps. Eldrin, an artisan at the Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest, guides skilled needleworkers. Tailoring makes garments and bags, but it can also sustain a journey. Those who have proven their skill with thread and loom can learn to make camp accessories for travel through the wilderness. The Faction Banner is the chief craft Eldrin teaches. It stands beside a traveler's fire, where its emblem can hearten those on dangerous journeys and in battle. A banner at camp gives weary travelers a familiar sign of resolve and helps them press on through hostile lands.

quest:97928.text: Camping 101: Blacksmithing. You’re ready to make a Sharpening Wheel and try it in the wilderness. First, you’ll need a campfire to set up camp. You can now craft a Sharpening Wheel. Take it into the wilderness to try it out, where you can set up camp away from the center of town. Bring a campfire along. A cook can teach you how to make one.

quest:97931.text: Camping 101: First Aid. You are ready to make a First Aid Kit, and now you need a place to try it. You can make the kit, but most people would rather not camp in the middle of town. So take it out into the wilderness. Before you set up camp, you need a campfire. Most cooks can teach you how to make one.

quest:97932.text: Camping 101: Fishing. In Mulgore, anglers can turn fishing into a comfort for camps in the wild. Show Uthan Stillwater in Bloodhoof Village your skill with rod and reel, and he teaches you to make a Fish Bowl for travelers resting outdoors. Anglers passing through Mulgore can put their quiet pastime to use around camp. If you have proved your skill with rod and reel, seek out Uthan Stillwater in Bloodhoof Village. He teaches skilled fishermen to make a Fish Bowl, a homely touch for a campsite. A Fish Bowl brings a little cheer to a hard journey. Its calm presence makes a resting place in the wild more pleasant and lifts the spirits of those gathered there. Better spirits mean sharper instincts and greater resilience in battle. A campsite belongs in the open country, not in a settlement like Bloodhoof Village. The Fish Bowl can only be tried in the wilderness. A camp also needs a proper fire, so seek out a culinary trainer to learn basic fire-making before you set one up.

quest:97934.text: Camping 101: Leatherworking. In Bloodhoof Village, leatherworkers can learn to make a tent for shelter on the road. Chaw Stronghide teaches the craft to those ready to handle heavier hides and rugged stitching. Across Kalimdor, leatherworkers who know how to stitch a sturdy tent can shelter from the midday sun and prairie rain. A tent also gives weary travelers a place to rest and recover before crossing the open plains again. At Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, Chaw Stronghide teaches leatherworkers who can handle heavier hides and rugged stitching. Once they prove their skill, he shows them how to make a durable tent for journeys far from civilization. Choose a camp with care and respect for local settlements. Village folk frown on travelers setting up along central paths and thoroughfares, so take your tent into the wild frontier. A proper camp also needs a fire. Ask a skilled cook how to kindle one.

quest:97935.text: Camping 101: Mining. In Thunder Bluff, miners can learn to carry their craft into the wild. Brek Stonehoof teaches them to shape a lodestone that gives strength to those resting by a campfire. Mining may lack the glamour of high arcana, but it is honest work found across Azeroth. Miners draw useful minerals and dense stone from deep rock faces. Those materials make weapons and armor, and now they serve a purpose in the field. A miner can shape stone into sturdy tools for a wilderness camp. Brek Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff teaches miners to put their trade to use in the wild. Once they show skill with a pick, he teaches them to shape a camp lodestone. Set beside an open blaze, the stone lends vigor and an edge in battle to those preparing to wield a blade.

quest:97936.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Mulgore, skinners learn to make a Camp Chair for wilderness rest. Yonn Deepcut teaches the craft in Bloodhoof Village, where skilled hide-gatherers prepare for camps beyond the settlements. Fallen beasts yield hides and pelts that skinners can turn into useful gear. Leather becomes armor, and animal skins can also make comforts for the wild. After long weeks crossing untamed lands, travelers can rest on gear made from those hides and stay sharp in combat. In Mulgore, skinners visit Bloodhoof Village to speak with Yonn Deepcut. Once they show they can harvest beast hides, Yonn teaches them to stitch together a Camp Chair. Towns and villages do not welcome travelers pitching tents in their streets, so the chairs are for wilderness use. A campfire completes the camp, and local cooks teach how to make one.

quest:97938.text: Camping 101: Alchemy. In Dolanaar, Cyndra Kindwhisper teaches alchemists how to tend a campsite. Her lesson joins potion craft with wilderness survival and shows how to make a Mana Well for traveling healers and casters. Alchemists learn to carry their craft beyond the workbench. Cyndra Kindwhisper shows them how to make useful camp fittings that can sustain a traveling party on long journeys through the wild. In Dolanaar, alchemists who know the basics can seek Cyndra Kindwhisper. She teaches them to set up a Mana Well at camp. Its refreshing magic helps healers and spellcasters replenish their mana far from taverns and settlements.

quest:97942.text: Camping 101: First Aid. In Dolanaar, travelers learn to prepare a First Aid Kit for camp. Byancie teaches how to tend wounds far from town healers and find a place to camp. Wild country brings bites from beasts and cuts from jagged ground. Rangers and other travelers may be far from town and its medical supplies. A First Aid Kit lets them tend minor wounds at a roadside camp before they grow grave beneath the open sky. In Dolanaar, Byancie teaches travelers skilled in triage to pack medical supplies for rough trails. Townsfolk do not allow tents and scattered supplies in the center of a settlement. Campers need to head into the forest before making camp. An open flame begins a working camp. Set a campfire before laying out medical kits or bedding; it brings warmth and protection. Building and tending a fire is basic to surviving in the wild. Trainers recommend asking a cook to teach you to kindle one before tending a wilderness camp.

quest:97943.text: Camping 101: Fishing. In Darnassus, anglers are directed to Astaia to learn how a Fish Bowl can brighten a wilderness camp. The craft rewards skilled fishermen with a touch of comfort for life outdoors. Anglers crossing Kalimdor can put quiet hours by the water to use. In Darnassus, Astaia teaches experienced fishermen to turn their catches and skill into campsite comforts. One of these is a Fish Bowl, made to display at camp and bring cheer to weary travelers. A wilderness camp needs more than fishing gear. You cannot pitch one in a crowded city center or urban district, so you must find open ground. Every camp also needs a warm fire. Visit a local cooking trainer to learn basic fire-making before settling down for the night.

quest:97944.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. In Dolanaar, herbalists learn to make camp goods from the plants they gather. Malorne Bladeleaf teaches skilled gatherers to craft Incense Candles, which bolster healers and spellcasters by the campfire. Herbalism can serve a traveler beyond gathering flowers for sale or for alchemists. In the wilderness, harvested plants can become useful camp equipment. Preparing them for survival lets your gathered plants support longer journeys in the field. At Dolanaar, Malorne Bladeleaf teaches skilled herbalists to make an Incense Candle. Its soothing flame creates a focused, high-spirited refuge around the campfire. Healers and spellcasters value its revitalizing presence as they restore their magical energies between perils.

quest:97946.text: Camping 101: Leatherworking. On Teldrassil, leatherworkers can learn to make a shelter for the trail. Find Nadyia Maneweaver on the road between Dolanaar and Darnassus, where she teaches the craft of tents that keep travelers dry and cool. Across Kalimdor, an open sky can bring hard weather. Skilled leatherworkers learn to shape hides and pelts into sturdy shelters, giving travelers a safe place to rest wherever the road leads. A tent lets wanderers find the rest they need far from the inns. Nadyia Maneweaver teaches proficient leatherworkers along the forest road between Dolanaar and Darnassus. She shows them how to stitch a sturdy tent for the trail. A tent needs a campfire to make a proper camp, and cooks teach that craft. Set the shelter in the open wilds, away from town streets.

quest:97948.text: Camping 101: Mining. You’re sent to Auberdine to learn a new use for mining. There, Kurdram Stonehammer teaches skilled miners to craft a lodestone that strengthens allies gathered around a campfire. Mining has uses beyond smelting ingots and hammering armor. Experienced prospectors shape raw earth and magnetic ore into camping gear, so travelers can make well-fortified hearths in the wilderness. This introduction shows miners a practical use for their craft. In Auberdine, the coastal town of Darkshore, promising miners seek out Kurdram Stonehammer. Once a miner proves dedication and skill, Kurdram teaches the method for making a camp lodestone. Set beside a fire, the stone strengthens the martial companions gathered nearby.

quest:97949.text: Camping 101: Skinning. Out in the wilds, you learn to make a Camp Chair and prepare a campsite. You need hides, open ground away from town, and a campfire. Hides gathered on the road can be put to use. With the materials at hand, you learn to make a portable Camp Chair for journeys through Azeroth. Townsfolk object when travelers pitch camp in city centers, so take this craft into the open wilds. A campfire is the first need at a campsite in the wild. Its flames bring warmth and shelter from the elements. If you have not learned basic cooking, visit a cooking trainer to learn how to kindle a fire in the field.

quest:97951.text: Camping 101: Alchemy. At your camp, alchemists can learn to craft a Mana Well. Carolai Anise in Brill teaches the craft once you have shown skill in alchemy. Carolai Anise in Brill teaches alchemists to craft a Mana Well for their camp. Once you know the craft, you can make camp in the wilderness. First, you need a campfire, which cooks can teach you to make.

quest:97953.text: Camping 101: Enchanting. At Brill, Vance Undergloom teaches enchanters to make an Enchanted Lute for camp. First, show proficiency in your skill. At a camp in the wilds, enchanters can learn to make an Enchanted Lute. Bring it along to lend some entertainment to your time away from the trail.

quest:97955.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At wilderness camps, Camping 101: First Aid helps healers prepare for injuries. In Brill, Nurse Neela teaches skilled practitioners to make a First Aid Kit for treating wounds far from settled lands. Beyond guarded settlements, beasts and rival factions put travelers in danger. A healer trained in First Aid can learn to assemble a First Aid Kit for a wilderness camp. With it, travelers can tend wounds far from settled lands. In Brill, Nurse Neela teaches travelers to put their medical skill to work at camp. Those skilled in bandaging and treatment can learn to make a portable First Aid Kit. First, travelers need a wilderness site and a basic campfire. Cooking instructors can teach them how to build one.

quest:97956.text:
Camping 101: Fishing. In Brill, someone hopes your fishing skill will bring cheer to camp. Clyde Kellen can teach you to make a fishbowl for it. Your fishing may brighten the camp. Once you've proved your skill, speak with Clyde Kellen in Brill. He can teach you to make a fishbowl for the camp.

The giver believes cheerful adventurers fight more strongly. They hope the fishbowl will bring joy to you and the others.

quest:97959.text: Camping 101: Mining. You can now make a Lodestone and prepare to camp in the wilderness. You can now craft your own Lodestone. Try it in the wilderness, where folk are less likely to mind a camp. Before you start, you will also need a campfire. A cook can teach you how to make one.

quest:97965.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At Shen'dar Village, you seek care for injuries far from civilization. Naleeia Tattermend teaches skilled practitioners to prepare medical kits for a wilderness camp. A journey across Azeroth can bring violence, wild beasts, and hazards of the land. First Aid lets you bind cuts and broken bones without relying only on spellcraft. A First Aid Kit at a wilderness camp gives you a place to tend injuries and help companions recover. Then you can prepare to travel on. In Shen'dar Village, Naleeia Tattermend teaches practitioners to make durable medical supplies for a campsite. She shares her techniques after you show that you know basic medical care.

quest:97967.text: Camping 101: Fishing. You are learning how fishing can make wilderness camps more welcoming. In Shen'dar Village, skilled anglers can ask Fenn Fairweather to teach them the Fish Bowl craft. A camp in the wild needs comfort along with sharp blades and sturdy armor. Good spirits help companions bear the strain of life in the field. Fishing brings provisions, and skilled anglers can put their craft to work improving a campsite. With live fish and a proper fixture, a traveler can make camp more welcoming. In Shen'dar Village, Fenn Fairweather shares fishing secrets with seasoned anglers who know the patience of rod and reel. Anglers with enough skill can learn to make a Fish Bowl, a simple fixture that brings cheer and rest to weary companions. Good spirits in the wild help a group stay focused and resolute when danger draws near.

quest:97968.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. At camps along the trail, Camping 101: Herbalism points gatherers toward instructors who teach them to make Incense Candles. Herbalists use gathered plants to bring comfort to spellcasters and healers on long journeys. Travelers can put roots and petals to use beyond selling fresh stems or brewing draughts. Gatherers meet instructors who teach them to make Incense Candles from wild aromatic plants. These candles support companions on the trail. Long journeys through hostile country wear down healers and spellcasters. At an active campsite, an Incense Candle gives off a soothing, revitalizing scent that lifts their spirits and helps them recover clarity and strength before danger calls again. Those who wield magic or tend the wounded value that comfort most.

quest:97969.text: Camping 101: Leatherworking. A leatherworker’s travels lead to lessons in making a shelter for the wilds. In Shen'dar Village, Indari Sunseam teaches skilled craftsmen to stitch tents that protect travelers and give them rest on long journeys. Traveling leatherworkers need sturdy gear made from hide and pelt. Once they learn the craft, they are sent to Indari Sunseam in Shen'dar Village. There, she teaches them to make a proper camping tent. It keeps travelers dry in heavy rain and cool beneath a blazing sun, helping them rest on long journeys. Townsfolk object when rough camps clutter their streets, so you pitch your tent in the wild. A campsite needs more than shelter; it also needs a warming campfire. Visit a local cook to learn basic firemaking before you set out.

quest:97971.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Shen'dar Village, Mendalass Tattermend shows skinners how to prepare for rest in the wilds. The lesson joins skinning with survival and a place to sit at camp. You can shape hides from fallen beasts into more than armor. Mendalass Tattermend shows you how to make a portable Camp Chair, so you can rest in the wilds and regain your strength before battle. In Shen'dar Village, Mendalass Tattermend teaches proven skinners to make sturdy seats from collected pelts. Towns forbid camps within their limits. A campsite also needs a campfire, a skill local culinary instructors have traditionally taught.

quest:97973.text: Camping 101: Tailoring. At Shen'dar Village, tailors can learn to make a Faction Banner for wilderness camps. The banner lifts spirits and helps sustain morale. A campsite in the wild calls for more than warm clothes. A well-made banner can give a camp a shared purpose, so clothworkers are urged to carry their craft beyond garments and bags. With further instruction, bolts of woven fabric become a sign of unity and fortitude. In Shen'dar Village, Taleen Shimmerthread teaches camping crafts to tailors with enough skill. She shows them how to fashion a Faction Banner. Stitched with care and planted at camp, it rallies allies and helps keep their spirits up through the trials ahead.

quest:97977.text: Nature's Call. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella seeks the cause of the Gnarlpine's sudden hostility. Their carved totems may tell why they turned against their longtime night elf allies. The dryad Tarindrella asks you to search camps along Shadowglen's western border. The Gnarlpine furbolgs left them in haste, and she cannot believe they would cast aside centuries of friendship with the night elves without cause. Bring back intact engraved totems. Their carvings may tell what changed.

quest:97979.text:
The Goddess Provides. Beneath Teldrassil, young night elves begin a rite that teaches them to know Elune’s gifts. After the Long Vigil, they seek guidance in her radiance and shelter in her shadow. For millennia after the Sundering, the kaldorei kept apart from other peoples. During the Long Vigil, they watched over Kalimdor and guarded the sacred peaks of Mount Hyjal. The Third War brought devastation, and the defense of the World Tree ended their ancient seclusion.

Now the night elves dwell beneath Teldrassil’s boughs and face an unfamiliar world. They reach across the ocean to make allies and take their place among Azeroth’s peoples. Elune, the Mother Moon, remains at the heart of kaldorei faith, though the night elves now dwell in a new home and form new ties. From their earliest days, they learn to call on her gifts. Her radiance guides their strikes and clarifies their purpose. Her shadow hides them from enemy sight.

These inherited blessings bind the kaldorei to their goddess and prepare them for dangers beyond the Great Tree.

quest:97985.text: Thundering Hearts. In Thousand Needles, the researcher seeks Stormheart’s massive heart for work on an abomination. A researcher studying abomination creation believes the work calls for a massive heart. Stormheart, a thunder lizard said to patrol the canyon edge in Thousand Needles, seems large enough. But Stormheart is not docile.

quest:98013.text: Swelling Forces. At the Grove of the Ancients, Arbal sends defenders against the Stormscale naga in the northeast ruins. These cursed former Highborne threaten the surrounding woodlands as their numbers grow. Arbal watches the northeast ruins from the Grove of the Ancients with grave concern. Cursed Highborne have become the serpent-like naga of the Stormscale tribe. They now occupy the remains of their old civilization, and their growing army could spread beyond the ruins into the wider forest.
